disagreements.issue: Community Health Ambassadors Program Funding ($318,244) — Split Vote 4-1
disagreements.summary: The board split 4-1 on allocating $318,244 from the COVID set-aside account for the Recovery and Renewal Task Force's Community Health Ambassadors Program, dividing over program duplication and uncoordinated pandemic spending.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the $318,244 allocation from COVID set-aside funds (while pursuing $89,000 in CRF reimbursement) to address urgent racial disparities and workplace/business COVID clusters.
side_a_arguments: Chair Wendy Jacobs emphasized the proposal emerged directly from minority and immigrant/refugee task force roundtables to reach Latinx and Black businesses and workers lacking resources or trusted health connections.
Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved approval to fund the full-year program immediately while instructing staff to offset eligible expenses with CRF funds.
disagreements.side_b_position: Opposed funding a $318,244 program perceived as duplicating existing county community health workers, masks, and PPE programs without clearer funding and coordination plans.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton questioned why the budget included $60,000 for PPE, $40,000+ for masks, and community health worker positions when the county already employed community health workers and distributed masks.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 4-1 (Jacobs, Carter, Reckhow, Hill Aye; Howerton Nay).

disagreements.issue: Using County Libraries and Piecemeal COVID Reserve Spending for HOPE Learning Centers ($405,600)
disagreements.summary: Prior to voting 5-0 for the six-week $405,600 HOPE Learning Centers allocation, commissioners debated why County libraries remained closed, whether ad-hoc reserve spending lacked a comprehensive plan, and how to guarantee seats reached the neediest students.
disagreements.side_a_position: Fund the 338 ready community seats immediately for six weeks while requiring strict outreach and data tracking for DHA, DSS, and Exceptional Children students.
side_a_arguments: Commissioner Heidi Carter argued the 338 ready seats would otherwise go to fee-paying families rather than the most vulnerable students if the county delayed.

Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow conditioned her Aye vote on immediate outreach to Durham Housing Authority and elementary schools, while Chair Wendy Jacobs questioned why county libraries could not host learning centers like Student U and the YMCA.
disagreements.side_b_position: Caution against ad-hoc spending from the shrinking COVID reserve without a comprehensive county funding strategy and full public health safeguards.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton supported the centers in principle but criticized making piecemeal funding decisions 'on the fly' without giving staff time to build a strategic plan, and pressed for Exceptional Children priority.
General Manager Joanne Pierce and library leadership cited Urban Libraries Council data and rising youth COVID cases to warn against opening libraries prematurely.
disagreements.resolution: Following partner assurances on DHA/DSS outreach and budget staff confirming COVID reserve capacity, the board approved $405,600 unanimously (5-0).

meetings.title: August 10, 2020 BOCC Regular Session Virtual Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the August 10, 2020 virtual BOCC regular session (recorded offline due to a Biamp failure), opening with Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's tribute to Rep. John Lewis and Rev. C.T. Vivian, census mobilization remarks, and unanimous approval (5-0) of four sets of minutes. Commissioners adopted four memorial resolutions honoring Mary Ann Black, Andrea Lynette Harris, Kenneth William Edmonds, and Raymond Eurquhart, celebrated a NACo Achievement Award for DSS/IS&T predictive foster-care analytics, and approved the consent agenda 5-0—including the Longtime Homeowner Tax Deferral Program, Geer Street Cemetery archaeological grant support, and $95,000 for the Back on the Bull campaign after Howerton pressed for M/WBE vendor tracking. Following COVID-19 and Planning Commission updates, the board debated revised Joint Community Safety and Wellness Task Force bylaws, reaching a consensus impasse without a vote as Sheriff Clarence Birkhead, Commissioner Howerton, and Vice Chair James Hill opposed creating a new 24-month task force while Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Heidi Carter favored it (and Commissioner Reckhow raised alarm over emails opposing police in the room). After entering closed session (5-0), the board reconvened and voted unanimously (5-0) to remove and relocate the Confederate monument base to an undisclosed location for public safety and preservation.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Census Update, Civil Rights Tribute, and Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff announced the meeting was being recorded for next-day upload due to a Biamp technical failure, after which Chair Jacobs led the Pledge of Allegiance and discussed mobilizing for the shortened September 30 census deadline (with Durham at 57.7% response). Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton read an A. Philip Randolph Institute tribute to John Lewis and Rev. C.T. Vivian, and the board voted 5-0 to approve four sets of May–June minutes.

agenda_items.title: Memorial Resolutions (Black, Harris, Edmonds, Eurquhart) and NACo Award Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners Reckhow, Howerton, Hill, and Carter read memorial resolutions honoring the lives and legacies of former BOCC Chair and Rep. Mary Ann Black, NCIMED founder Andrea Lynette Harris, Carolina Times publisher Kenneth William Edmonds, and activist/Soil & Water supervisor Raymond Eurquhart. At 00:41:39, DSS Director Ben Rose and IS&T staff were recognized for winning a 2020 NACo Achievement Award for predictive foster-care analytics.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Tax Deferral Program, Back on the Bull, and Geer Street Cemetery)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed the Longtime Homeowner Tax Deferral Program (Item 20-0397) with Tax Administrator Dwane Brinson—discussing financial counseling and a tax-bill check-off fund—and heard from Tom Miller regarding Item 20-0410 supporting Friends of Geer Cemetery's archaeological survey grant. After Commissioner Howerton objected that the $95,000 Back on the Bull media allocation lacked explicit M/WBE contract requirements, staff agreed to report contract vendor details and the board approved the consent agenda 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Health COVID-19 Update and Planning Commission Annual Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported active COVID-19 cases dropping below 400 (to 345, with 79 total deaths) while noting disproportionate Latinx construction-sector cases. Planning staff and Planning Commission representatives then presented the Planning Commission's annual report and attendance records.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Revised Bylaws
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed revised task force bylaws adding a Community Resource Panel of agency and law-enforcement heads and narrowing the county's five appointees to specific boards. Sheriff Clarence Birkhead, Commissioner Howerton, and Vice Chair Hill opposed forming another 24-month study during a spike in gun homicides, Commissioner Reckhow voiced concern over intense emails rejecting police even on the resource panel, and Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Carter defended the task force; the board reached a consensus impasse without a vote.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Action to Remove/Relocate Confederate Monument Base
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to adjourn into closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) and (a)(3) for property/employment negotiations and attorney-client consultation. Reconvening at 02:45:10, commissioners voted unanimously (5-0) to remove and/or relocate the Confederate monument base to an undisclosed location to address public safety concerns and preserve the base until further action, before adjourning.

disagreements.meeting_title: August 10, 2020 BOCC Regular Session Virtual Meeting
disagreements.issue: M/WBE Contracting Commitment on $95,000 'Back on the Bull' Communications Budget Amendment
disagreements.summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton questioned the $264,195 project chart versus the $95,000 consent item and objected that no explicit M/WBE vendor participation requirement appeared in the agenda documentation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require documented M/WBE vendor participation commitments before approving communications funding.
side_a_arguments: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton argued the board committed to M/WBE participation across county contracts and saw no contractual language ensuring African American and minority vendors were hired.
disagreements.side_b_position: Approve the time-sensitive $95,000 budget amendment for Phases 2 and 3 media buys while directing staff to track and report M/WBE vendor contracting.
side_b_arguments: Chair Wendy Jacobs and General Manager Jodi Miller noted 57% of planned buys targeted Latinx media and that no vendor contracts were attached yet to the planning budget amendment.
Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow proposed approving the amendment while instructing staff to push for minority vendors and report back on actual contracts.
disagreements.resolution: Staff agreed to convey the board's M/WBE expectation and report back on actual media contracts, and the consent agenda passed 5-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: August 10, 2020 BOCC Regular Session Virtual Meeting
disagreements.issue: Impasse Over Revised Bylaws for the Joint Community Safety and Wellness Task Force
disagreements.summary: The board deadlocked without a vote on revised bylaws for the Joint Community Safety and Wellness Task Force, splitting over whether a 24-month body duplicated existing agencies during a homicide crisis and whether excluding law enforcement from voting seats—or even the resource room—undermined collaboration.
disagreements.side_a_position: Form the joint task force with the City and School Board using the revised bylaws and Community Resource Panel to engage residents on non-law-enforcement crisis and violence-prevention solutions.
side_a_arguments: Chair Wendy Jacobs argued residents amid the Black Lives Matter movement were clamoring for a community-led voice and suggested shortening the two-year timeline.

Commissioner Heidi Carter warned that county services (public health, CJRC, JCPC, EMS) were central to the work and expressed concern about the county sitting out while City Council and BOE moved ahead.
disagreements.side_b_position: Opposed creating a new 24-month task force that duplicates existing work, diverts exhausted staff, and faced community backlash over law enforcement involvement.
side_b_arguments: Sheriff Clarence Birkhead opposed the task force as a 'waste of time and a waste of resources' repeating prior reports while three homicides occurred in a single day, urging synergy with CJRC and existing community groups.

Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton refused to wait two years while Black and brown children were dying in the streets, argued the plan lacked broad community vetting and diverted 24/7 pandemic staff, and Vice Chair James Hill concurred.

Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow stated she had sought a 'big tent' compromise with the Community Resource Panel, but was sobered by an avalanche of community emails rejecting even police and sheriff participation in the room, concluding the board should not force a split vote.
disagreements.resolution: Chair Jacobs concluded the board had reached an impasse with no vote taken, deferring an update to the August 11 Joint City-County Committee meeting.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-08-03 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the marathon August 3, 2020 work session, the Board of County Commissioners heard 20 citizen comments urging low-income homeowner Tax Assistance Grants, universal COVID-19 testing at the Durham County Detention Center using CARES Act funds, a cop-free Community Safety and Wellness Task Force, and opposition to UDO Text Amendment TC2000003 on development agreements. Because several time-sensitive items required action during a work session, commissioners suspended the rules and voted unanimously (5-0) to approve a $144,000 Robert Half International staffing contract amendment for Board of Elections absentee-ballot processing, a $6,808,956 FAA Airport Improvement Grant for RDU Taxiway F, and removal of a Juvenile Crime Prevention Council member for poor attendance. The board split 3-2 on low-income homeowner property tax relief after County Attorney Brian Wardell warned that Tax Assistance Grants could trigger personal commissioner liability under N.C.G.S. 105-380: Ellen W. Reckhow, James Hill, and Brenda A. Howerton voted Aye to authorize staff's legally defensible long-term tax deferral program (with a 10-year ownership threshold), implement a voluntary tax-bill donation option to offset fees/interest, and explore a Community Land Trust partnership, while Heidi Carter and Wendy Jacobs voted Nay out of preference for direct grants and skepticism that homeowners would accept accumulating deferred tax debt. Commissioners deferred the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force discussion to August 10 and entered a closed session on personnel matters (3-0).

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments on Tax Assistance Grants, Detention Center COVID Testing, Safety Task Force, and Development Agreements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica read portions of 20 submitted citizen comments urging Tax Assistance Grants to prevent foreclosure and displacement, universal COVID-19 testing for ~260 jail detainees and staff out of Durham's $6,239,422 second-round CARES Act allocation, a cop-free Community Safety and Wellness Task Force, and rejection of UDO Text Amendment TC2000003 on development agreements. Chair Wendy Jacobs requested jail testing options for the August 10 meeting and noted an email regarding a Pre-K advisory committee.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review and Rule Suspension for Elections Staffing Contract Amendment (Item 338)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager reviewed consent items including a $402,107 Sheriff's Office licensing contract (Item 292), a $51,500 HIPAA risk assessment contract (Item 314), and Item 338—a $144,000 contract amendment with Robert Half International for temporary Board of Elections staffing amid surging absentee ballot requests. Commissioners discussed absentee drop-box legal constraints with elections staff and suspended the rules (5-0) to approve Item 338 immediately (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Low-Income Homeowner Tax Relief Options: Tax Assistance Grants vs. Tax Deferral Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Tax Administrator Dwayne Brinson, CFO Claudia, and County Attorney Brian Wardell presented three options for low-income homeowners earning ≤30% AMI: a Tax Assistance Grant (TAG) program (~$3.7M total county/city/fire cost, capping taxes at 1% of income), a legally defensible Long-Term Payment Deferral Plan (capping annual payments at 4% of income with remaining taxes deferred plus statutory interest/fees, ~$206K administrative cost), and Community Land Trust expansion. Attorney Wardell warned that TAG constitutes an unauthorized tax compromise carrying personal commissioner liability under N.C.G.S. 105-380. After suspending the rules (4-0+), the board split 3-2: Ellen W. Reckhow, James Hill, and Brenda A. Howerton voted Aye to pursue the 10-year-ownership deferral plan, donation option, and land trust study, while Heidi Carter (favoring TAG) and Wendy Jacobs (fearing homeowners would shun accruing debt) voted Nay.

agenda_items.title: RDU Airport Improvement FAA Grant ($6,808,956) and JCPC Member Removal (Items 20-0350 & 20-0351)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: By consensus, the board postponed discussion of the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force to the August 10 regular meeting. Commissioners then suspended the rules (5-0) and approved accepting a $6,808,956 FAA Airport Improvement Grant for RDU Taxiway F reconstruction (5-0), and suspended the rules (5-0) to remove Leslie Gonzalez from the Juvenile Crime Prevention Council due to poor attendance under Item 20-0351 (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Personnel Matters (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a 30-minute afternoon recess, Chair Jacobs, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Brenda A. Howerton reconvened at 4:00 PM and voted 3-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) regarding a public officer or employee. The board returned at 08:02:01 and adjourned 3-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-08-03 9:00 AM - Work Session
disagreements.issue: Low-Income Homeowner Property Tax Relief: Tax Assistance Grants (TAG) vs. Long-Term Tax Deferral Program
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 3-2 over whether to adopt staff's recommended Long-Term Tax Deferral Program paired with a voluntary donation fund and Community Land Trust partnership, or to pursue direct Tax Assistance Grants (TAG) advocated by the Coalition for Affordable Housing and Transit despite legal risk warnings from the County Attorney.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt staff's legally defensible multi-tool approach: Long-Term Tax Deferral Program (4% income cap with 10-year ownership threshold), voluntary tax-bill donation option to cover interest/fees, and Durham Community Land Trust vetting.
side_a_arguments: County Attorney Brian Wardell advised that North Carolina tax statutes do not authorize local tax-compromise grant programs unless enacted uniformly for all 100 counties, exposing commissioners to personal liability under N.C.G.S. 105-380.

Ellen W. Reckhow, Brenda A. Howerton, and James Hill emphasized their oath to follow state law, avoiding personal legal jeopardy while delivering an immediate relief tool and pursuing future General Assembly reform.
Pairing the deferral plan with private donations and Community Land Trust support avoids the ~$3.7 million annual fiscal impact of TAG during COVID-19 revenue uncertainty.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the tax deferral program and support direct Tax Assistance Grants (TAG) to avoid saddling low-income homeowners with accruing tax debt, interest, and fees.
side_b_arguments: Heidi Carter argued that only TAG meets the urgent financial needs of historically Black neighborhoods facing rapid tax increases while preserving generational home equity, citing UNC School of Government expert Chris McLaughlin's assessment that a legal challenge would be unlikely to succeed.
Carter suggested exploring lower-cost administration through Reinvestment Partners (~$250,000) or a 2%–3% income cap.

Wendy Jacobs doubted low-income residents would enroll in a deferral plan that builds ~$13,000–$25,000 in deferred taxes, interest, and fees over 10 years without any guarantee that private fundraising would cover those charges.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 3-2 (Ayes: Ellen W. Reckhow, James Hill, Brenda A. Howerton; Nays: Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs) authorizing staff to develop the long-term tax deferral program with the 10-year ownership threshold, implement the donation option, and continue vetting a Community Land Trust partnership.

Reckhow and Brenda A. Howerton present while awaiting Vice Chair James Hill, noting that Commissioner Heidi Carter was away on vacation and not expected to join. Once Vice Chair Hill connected, Chair Jacobs read the statutory closed-session motion under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider the qualifications, competence, performance, character, fitness, conditions of appointment, or complaints regarding an individual public officer or employee. On a motion by Commissioner Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Howerton, the Board voted unanimously (with explicit Ayes recorded from Commissioners Howerton, Reckhow, and Chair Jacobs) to enter closed session. After approximately 80 minutes in closed session, the Board reconvened with Chair Jacobs, Vice Chair Hill, and Commissioner Reckhow present and adjourned on a 3-0 voice vote moved by Vice Chair Hill and seconded by Commissioner Reckhow.

meetings.title: July 13, 2020 BOCC Regular Session Virtual Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the July 13, 2020 virtual regular session with all five commissioners present. The board unanimously approved its May 26, 2020 minutes (5-0), the consent agenda excluding pulled Item 20-0309 (5-0), and five land-use items: the South Miami Boulevard/Bruntland Road rezoning (20-0317, 5-0), Historic Properties Local Review Criteria updates (5-0), Neighborhood Protection Overlay revisions (20-0318, 5-0), Affordable Housing Dwelling Unit definition revisions (20-0319, 5-0), and UDO Omnibus 14 changes (20-0320, 5-0). On the Stormwater Utility Fee budget implementation item (20-0309) and the revised Stormwater Utility Ordinance, Chair Wendy Jacobs dissented over insufficient non-digital outreach and fees on 125 agricultural parcels, with both passing 4-1 (Ayes: Heidi Carter, James Hill, Ellen W. Reckhow, Brenda A. Howerton; Nay: Wendy Jacobs). Commissioners postponed action on the Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force bylaws to the August work session after Vice Chair James Hill demanded voting seats for the Sheriff and Police Chief and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton cited late receipt of revised drafts, while later voting 4-1 to extend the meeting past 11:00 p.m. (Ayes: Brenda A. Howerton, James Hill, Ellen W. Reckhow, Wendy Jacobs; Nay: Heidi Carter) before entering a closed session on opioid litigation.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Public Comments, and Approval of May 26, 2020 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the virtual meeting, read the public charge, and shared announcements on nonprofit mask distribution (over 40,000 distributed and 60,000 more available), the 'I Voted' sticker contest, and the Get Back on the Bull campaign. Clerk Monica Toomer read submitted public comments urging redistribution of School Resource Officer funds and adoption of the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force bylaws without law enforcement members. The board unanimously approved the May 26, 2020 minutes.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Item 20-0309)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs pulled Item 20-0309 (Stormwater Utility Fee) for discussion after the stormwater presentation and led review of consent items including the Durham Crisis Response Center / Family Justice Center lease (20-0308, building valued over $1.2 million), detention center window replacements for suicide prevention (20-0311), Vazquez/Elna Media translation and language-equity planning (20-0330), DDI (20-0331), and the Chamber of Commerce economic development contract (20-0332). Staff clarified safety rationale on the jail windows and committed to returning with a translation pilot proposal.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Item 20-0317 — Zoning Map Change (2622 S. Miami Blvd & 2120 Bruntland Rd)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Jamie Sunyak presented applicant Brian Harris's request to rezone approximately seven acres at 2622 South Miami Boulevard and 2120 Bruntland Road from Industrial Light, Commercial Neighborhood, and RS-20 to Industrial Light, noting the Planning Commission's 10-0 recommendation of consistency. With no public speakers signed up or on the line, the board unanimously adopted the consistency statement and zoning map amendment.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Historic Properties Local Review Criteria Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After Item 20-0318 experienced audio feedback issues and was temporarily bypassed, Planner Carla Rosenberg presented two-year updates to the Historic Properties Local Review Criteria, noting City Council's June 15 approval reversing tree-removal allowances for solar installations while the Environmental Affairs Board conducts a one-year review. Commissioners unanimously adopted the revised criteria.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Item 20-0318 — UDO Text Amendment, Neighborhood Protection Overlay Revisions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Michael Stock (relayed by phone through Sarah Young) presented revisions to NPO procedures in Articles 2 and 4 reflecting new state law requiring property-owner or governing-body permission for downzoning, and gave an update on the Forest Hills NPO application. Following an unopposed public hearing, the board unanimously adopted the consistency statement and UDO amendment.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Item 20-0319 — UDO Text Amendment, Affordable Housing Dwelling Unit Definition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock presented UDO revisions to Article 17 updating the Affordable Housing Dwelling Unit definition and addressing Planning Commission member Tom Miller's feedback prior to City Council adoption. With no public comment, commissioners unanimously adopted the consistency statement and ordinance amendment.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Item 20-0320 — UDO Text Amendment, Omnibus Changes 14
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock presented Omnibus Changes 14 incorporating minor revisions across UDO Articles 1–10, 12, and 14–17. After closing the unopposed public hearing, the board unanimously approved the consistency statement and amending ordinance.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Public Health Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported 4,651 cumulative Durham COVID-19 cases (515 active, 4,063 inactive, 72 deaths) with a 7-day moving average declining to 64 and Latinx share of July cases dropping from 76.8% in June to roughly 50%, while zip code 27704 remained highest at 20.88 per 1,000 residents. He highlighted the new Duke/county testing site at Holton Recreation Center, state orders requiring negative-test reporting, and preparation for school reopening.

agenda_items.title: Update on County Food Security Coordinator Position and BOCC Directives
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Cooperative Extension Director Donna Rewalt outlined plans to reclassify a vacant county FTE into a County Food Security Coordinator position, form a cross-departmental County Food Security Team, and develop a food policy network and food security plan. Chair Jacobs and Chief of Staff Drew Cummings also discussed SharePoint glitches affecting access to post-February BOCC directives.

agenda_items.title: Stormwater Utility Outreach Update, Pulled Item 20-0309, and Stormwater Utility Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Stormwater Manager Ryan Eads, McKenzie Myers, and consultant Inga Kennedy presented virtual outreach results and the three-tier residential fee structure ($12/$24/$48 based on a 4,300-square-foot ERU) plus non-residential ERU billing for unincorporated properties to fund Falls Lake and Jordan Lake compliance. Chair Wendy Jacobs objected to taxing 125 non-residential agricultural parcels (~$40,000 total) before establishing BMP credits or conducting non-digital mail/in-person farm outreach and voted against both Pulled Item 20-0309 and the later Stormwater Utility Ordinance, which each passed 4-1.

agenda_items.title: Discussion on Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Bylaws
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Jodi Miller shared Criminal Justice Advisory Committee feedback, and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow presented compromise bylaws developed with Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson dedicating four county seats to representatives from existing health, sheriff advisory, CJAC, and JCPC boards while placing the Sheriff, Police Chief, DA, and Superintendent on a non-voting Community Resource Panel. Commissioner Heidi Carter urged immediate passage, but Vice Chair James Hill insisted the Sheriff and Police Chief be voting task force members and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton cited unreadiness due to late draft changes, leading the board to delay action to the August work session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Deferred to August work session (no formal vote)

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Closed Session (AmerisourceBergen Litigation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Lowell Siler announced appointment results for the ABC Board, Board of Adjustment, CJAC, DSS Board, Durham Convention Center Authority, and Women's Commission. Following a request to add active litigation (Durham County v. AmerisourceBergen, 1:19-cv-00491) under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3), the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session and 4-1 (Carter opposed) to extend the meeting until 11:30 p.m., returning at 04:16:05 to adjourn.

disagreements.meeting_title: July 13, 2020 BOCC Regular Session Virtual Meeting
disagreements.issue: Stormwater Utility Fee Non-Residential Agricultural Parcels and Pandemic Outreach
disagreements.summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs sought to delay adoption of the Stormwater Utility Ordinance and Pulled Item 20-0309 until August to address non-digital outreach and agricultural BMP credits for 125 non-residential farm parcels, while the remaining four commissioners voted 4-1 to enact the fee immediately.
disagreements.side_a_position: Delay implementation of the non-residential stormwater fee until August to conduct mail/non-virtual farmer outreach and offset the ~$40,000 impact on 125 agricultural parcels with BMP credits.
side_a_arguments: Many farmers do not use computers or Zoom and could not participate in virtual outreach while in-person Farm Bureau and Ruritan meetings were suspended due to COVID-19.
Charging agricultural properties that already implement water-quality BMPs contradicts county farmland preservation programs.
disagreements.side_b_position: Enact the Stormwater Utility Ordinance and accompanying budget item now while developing a future credit program and mailed tax-bill outreach.
side_b_arguments: Exempting one landowner class poses legal equity risks and shifts compliance costs onto residential ratepayers, while the fee is already baked into the adopted FY21 budget.
Staff noted 499 of 624 agricultural parcels already pay only residential rates (capped at $48/year) and the remaining 125 parcels have a median fee of $120/year.
disagreements.resolution: Both Pulled Item 20-0309 and the Stormwater Utility Ordinance passed 4-1, with staff directed to return with a credit structure proposal and continue mailed/direct outreach.

disagreements.meeting_title: July 13, 2020 BOCC Regular Session Virtual Meeting
disagreements.issue: Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Bylaws and Law Enforcement Membership
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split over whether to immediately adopt compromise bylaws placing the Sheriff and Police Chief on a non-voting Community Resource Panel or postpone action to resolve demands for voting law enforcement seats and late draft circulation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the revised bylaws immediately, keeping the task force strictly community-led with non-police solutions while engaging the Sheriff and Police Chief on the advisory Resource Panel.
side_a_arguments: Over 100 community residents urged prompt passage aligned with the Beyond Policing report and prior City Council and School Board approvals.
City Council would not approve voting seats for law enforcement on a community task force designed to evaluate alternatives to policing.
disagreements.side_b_position: Postpone approval to the August work session; add the Sheriff and Police Chief as voting members (Hill) or allow adequate time to review late bylaw revisions (Howerton).
side_b_arguments: Vice Chair James Hill stated excluding Durham's African American Sheriff and Police Chief from voting membership was unreasonable and said he would vote No unless they were added.

Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton stated she was unready to vote because revised drafts were emailed too close to the meeting, and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow agreed to pause two weeks rather than split along racial lines over the two African American members' objections.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; Chair Jacobs deferred the bylaws to the August work session.

meetings.title: Durham County Government BOCC Live
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the June 22, 2020 regular session (streamed/archived June 23, 2020) with all five commissioners present, and every formal vote passed unanimously 5-0. The board approved April 27 and May 11, 2020 minutes (5-0), adopted consent agenda items 20-0260 through 20-0299 (5-0) after reviewing pulled items on Wellpath jail healthcare and universal COVID-19 testing, the Sheriff's firing range architectural contract, tax refunds, and a $1.5 million health-benefit fund balance safeguard, and approved a $925,000 performance-based economic incentive for GRAIL, Inc. (5-0). Commissioners also voted 5-0 to commit $1,000,000 to join the City of Durham's Small Business Recovery Fund administered by Carolina Small Business Development Fund, approved a $60,000 match for a $300,000 federal EDA CARES Act grant for the Bulls Initiative Biowork expansion (5-0), adopted the revised FY 2021–2030 Capital Improvement Plan while urging the Museum of Life and Science to increase private fundraising (5-0), and authorized staff to negotiate homeless-housing RFP contracts ahead of the July 8 Marriott RTP expiration (5-0). Following brief discussion of the Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force bylaws—where Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and Sheriff Clarence Birkhead objected to excluding public safety voices and framing county programs negatively—the board deferred the task force item to July 13, approved CARES Act fair-share advocacy letters (5-0), announced 15 boards/commissions appointments, extended the meeting to 11:30 p.m. (5-0), and entered closed session (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustment (Juneteenth), Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the virtual meeting, added a brief discussion on making Juneteenth a county employee holiday at Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's request, and shared announcements on gardening kits. Commissioners unanimously approved the April 27 and May 11, 2020 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Discussion and Approval (Items 20-0260 through 20-0299)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners pulled and examined Item 20-0271 (May 2020 tax releases/refunds district codes), Item 20-0272 (DSS/DFI scope revisions), Item 20-0273 (Wellpath jail medical contract, where Heidi Carter and Ellen W. Reckhow pressed for regular/universal COVID-19 testing in the Detention Center and staff were directed to bring back testing options by July 13), Item 20-0275 (firing range drainage/pre-design vs Northern Durham campus classrooms), and Item 20-0291 ($1.5M fund balance transfer safeguard for Cigna health claims). The board unanimously approved the consent agenda, also recognizing the GoTriangle appointment of Stephanie Williams following Reckhow's decades of transit service.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of Paid Juneteenth Holiday for County Employees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton urged the board to consider making Juneteenth a paid holiday for Durham County employees starting in 2021. Chair Jacobs supported placing the item on the September work session agenda for staff and Racial Equity Officer Quillie Rashid-Henry to develop proposals.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Incentive for GRAIL, Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Officer Andy Miracle presented a $925,000 performance-based award over seven years for GRAIL, Inc. to establish a cancer-screening lab creating 739 jobs and $111 million in capital investment, supported by a state JDIG award. GRAIL representative Michael Myers and Greater Durham Chamber VP Joshua Gunn supported the project, and commissioners amended the motion to bind the briefing paper's workforce-pipeline commitments into the contract.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Public Health Update and County Reopening / Travel Guidelines
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported 3,267 cumulative Durham cases, 62 deaths, and 548 active cases, with 79.5% of June cases in the Latinx community and 16% under age 18, alongside an expected $1.296M DHHS grant and expanded testing at Holton Rec Center and El Centro Hispano. Staff then reviewed internal COVID-19 reopening protocols covering social distancing cohorts, mandatory face coverings, HVAC fresh-air optimization, sanitation, and temporary employee travel/high-risk activity guidelines.

agenda_items.title: Durham Small Business Recovery Fund ($1,000,000 Allocation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Andy Miracle and Carolina Small Business Development Fund CEO Kevin Dick compared partnering with the City/Duke Small Business Recovery Fund (3% interest, 10-year term, no personal guarantee/collateral, <=25 FTEs) against the NC Rural Center loan fund (5%, 5-year, personal guarantee). Despite legal/finance staff cautioning about unsecured loans, commissioners voted unanimously to join the unified City/Duke fund via CSBDF to maximize simplicity and equitable access.

agenda_items.title: Bulls Initiative Update and $60,000 EDA CARES Act Grant Match
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Andy Miracle and Casey Steinbacher presented an 80/20 federal EDA CARES Act grant opportunity for $300,000 in modular aseptic lab equipment to relocate and triple capacity of Durham Tech's Biowork certificate program from Northern Durham to a transit-accessible site. Commissioners unanimously approved the required $60,000 county match while urging increased private biotech sector contributions.

agenda_items.title: Revised FY 2021–2030 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Keith Lane and staff answered follow-up questions on Administration Building 1 HVAC/renovations (floors 2–3), Museum of Life and Science ($36 million in planned requests), Youth Home state partnership talks, and Alliance Behavioral Health space modifications. Commissioners unanimously approved the revised CIP with an added directive encouraging the Museum of Life and Science to step up private fundraising, and tabled Admin Building 1 Phases 3–5 pricing with Robert Sattel to a later date.

agenda_items.title: Homeless Housing Proposals During COVID-19 (Post-Marriott RTP Contract)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Drew Cummings reported that the Marriott RTP shelter contract expires July 8 and Urban Ministries can only reoccupy at half capacity, prompting an RFP that drew three bids: a flexible short-term hotel option and two community-based organization proposals offering permanent homeless-system capacity and potential COVID-positive quarantine beds. The board unanimously authorized staff to negotiate with the bidders and return by July 13 or an earlier special meeting.

agenda_items.title: Discussion on Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners briefly discussed the proposed task force bylaws ahead of a fuller July 13 debate. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow criticized the lack of prior Joint City-County Committee vetting and the bylaws' narrow focus on shortcomings rather than Durham's nationally recognized Stepping Up, CJRC, and specialty court programs, while Sheriff Clarence Birkhead objected that public safety had no representation on the task force.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments, CARES Act Letters, Meeting Extension, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Lowell Siler announced appointments across 15 boards and commissions (with one Women's Commission seat and CJAC business slot needing re-advertisement/follow-up). votes.item_title: Approval of April 27 and May 11, 2020 Regular Session Minutes

disagreements.issue: Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Bylaws and Representation
disagreements.summary: During preliminary review ahead of the July 13 vote, commissioners and Sheriff Clarence Birkhead diverged over whether the City-drafted bylaws fairly involved county leadership, acknowledged existing county criminal justice programs, and included public safety officials.
disagreements.side_a_position: Advance the community-led task force promptly in alignment with City Council and School Board expectations, keeping elected officials and department heads off the voting body.
side_a_arguments: Commissioners Heidi Carter and Wendy Jacobs cited strong public demand and noted the task force was modeled like the Pre-K task force to comprise community representatives rather than elected or department leaders.
Chair Jacobs noted Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson welcomed county bylaw revisions and proposed a joint briefing on existing county programs.
disagreements.side_b_position: Revise the bylaws before approval to ensure equal county partnership, reflect existing county criminal justice successes, and give public safety officials a voice.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow objected that the City bypassed the Joint City-County Committee and wrote bylaws focusing on perceived gaps while ignoring Durham's CJRC, Stepping Up initiative, mental health court, and reduced jail population.
Sheriff Clarence Birkhead objected that a public safety task force excluded public safety representation.
disagreements.resolution: Continued to the July 13, 2020 meeting for bylaw revisions and fuller debate.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-06-22 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 22, 2020 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board unanimously approved the April 27 and May 11, 2020 minutes (5-0) and pulled several consent agenda items for discussion, including a Wellpath jail medical contract (Item 20-0273) where Commissioner Heidi Carter pressed for universal COVID-19 testing and masks for detainees and Chair Jacobs directed staff and Sheriff Clarence Birkhead to return with local testing options. Later in the session, the Board discussed tabling Phases 3–5 of Administration Building I renovations ($1.1M mechanical/HVAC and interior upgrades) due to cost, voted 5-0 to authorize staff to negotiate with bidders on the COVID-19 homelessness housing RFP, and continued discussion of the Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force to July 13 after noting strong community interest and the need for staff feedback and balanced framing of existing Criminal Justice Resource Center work. The Board also approved CARES Act advocacy letters (4-0, with Commissioners Reckhow, Hill, Carter, and Chair Jacobs recorded voting Yes), received boards and commissions appointment results, voted 5-0 to extend the meeting to 11:30 PM, and voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) before adjourning 3-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge, Agenda Adjustments, and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Commissioners agreed to add a brief discussion of Juneteenth as the first item after the consent agenda, and Chair Jacobs shared community announcements regarding Durham Public Schools summer meals, Central Piedmont Community Action CDBG assistance, and virtual 4-H summer camps.

agenda_items.title: Approval of April 27 and May 11, 2020 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill moved to approve the April 27 and May 11, 2020 Regular Session minutes, seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow. After verifying Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's approval while her video connection froze, the Board approved the minutes unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Pulled Items (Tax Report, DSS/DFI Contract, Wellpath Jail Medical Contract, Admin I Project)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners pulled Item 20-0275, Item 20-0273 (Wellpath contract), Item 20-0272 (DSS contract with DFI, approved subject to circulating a revised scope of work), and the tax refunds/releases report. On the Wellpath item, Commissioner Heidi Carter questioned whether funding covered universal COVID-19 testing and masks for detention center detainees; Sheriff Birkhead outlined existing 14-day intake quarantine and screening protocols and noted universal testing would require additional funding, prompting Chair Jacobs to direct staff and the Sheriff to bring back testing partnership options.

agenda_items.title: Administration Building I Renovations (Phases 3–5)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle-of-meeting transcript gap, staff reviewed pricing for Phases 3–5 of Administration Building I renovations, including approximately $1.1M in mechanical/HVAC upgrades for the second and third floors plus carpeting, paint, lighting, and furniture within the $2.7M CIP figure. A participant recommended tabling Phases 3–5 for now because the work would require additional funding beyond already-allocated dollars.

agenda_items.title: Homelessness Housing RFP Negotiations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported that Urban Ministries could house only half its normal population under COVID-19 congregate limits and presented results from an emergency homelessness RFP seeking long-term equity rather than solely temporary hotel payments. Three proposals (one flexible hotel option and two community-based organization bids) were reviewed, and the Board voted 5-0 to authorize staff to enter negotiations with all bidders.

agenda_items.title: Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs noted heavy resident email outreach and majority board support for creating the joint task force, while commissioners requested staff feedback on bylaws and asked that the initiative be framed to highlight successful programs like Durham's Criminal Justice Resource Center alongside areas for reform. Chair Jacobs confirmed members would be community appointees rather than elected officials and continued the item to July 13 for fuller discussion.

agenda_items.title: CARES Act Funding Advocacy Letters
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs presented two letters drafted by staff (Deborah) advocating for Durham County to receive its fair share of CARES Act funding. After allowing commissioners time to review the drafts during board appointments, the Board approved the letters on a 4-0 voice vote moved by Commissioner Reckhow and seconded by Commissioner Carter.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff announced appointment selections including appointments to the Citizen Advisory Committee and other boards, and noted that the Criminal Justice Advisory Committee opening would be re-advertised.

agenda_items.title: Meeting Extension and Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With the 11:00 PM curfew approaching, the Board voted 5-0 to extend the meeting until 11:30 PM. Immediately thereafter, the Board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with the County Attorney, and later reconvened at 04:44:23 to adjourn 3-0.

votes.item_title: Approval of Regular Session Minutes (April 27 and May 11, 2020)
votes.notes: Brenda A. Howerton's video froze during the roll call, and the Clerk confirmed she had given her affirmative approval before calling back in; Chair Jacobs announced the minutes unanimously approved.
votes.discussion_detail: Approval of minutes from the April 27, 2020 and May 11, 2020 Regular Sessions.

votes.item_title: Authorization for Staff to Negotiate Homelessness Housing RFP Proposals
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion authorizing staff to engage in negotiations with all three bidders from the emergency homelessness housing RFP (one flexible hotel option and two community-based organization proposals).

votes.item_title: Approval of CARES Act Fair-Share Funding Letters
votes.notes: Brenda A. Howerton was on the call and briefly asked about adjournment prior to the roll call, and was not called again or recorded voting before Chair Jacobs declared the motion unanimously approved by the four recorded Aye voters.
votes.discussion_detail: Approval of two letters drafted by staff urging fair-share CARES Act funding for Durham County.

votes.item_title: Motion to Extend Regular Session to 11:30 PM
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Procedural motion required to extend the meeting past the 11:00 PM deadline to 11:30 PM to accommodate the closed session.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to adjourn to closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with the County Attorney and preserve attorney-client privilege.

meetings.title: Durham County Government BOCC Live
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the June 8, 2020 regular session (streamed/archived June 9, 2020) with all five commissioners participating. The board unanimously approved its March 2, 2020 work session minutes (5-0), proclaimed World Sickle Cell Awareness Day, adopted/presented the Resolution Declaring Racism as a Public Health Crisis brought by Dr. Wanda Boone, recognized a $50,000 RTP Foundation donation to the EOC, and passed the consent agenda (5-0). On the FY 2020–2021 budget, Commissioner Heidi Carter's motion (seconded by Chair Wendy Jacobs) to pull $3.8 million from reserves/fund balance to immediately fund a $15/hour minimum wage for all Durham Public Schools classified staff failed 2-3 (Ayes: Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs; Nays: James Hill, Ellen W. Reckhow, Brenda A. Howerton); after unanimously adding $42,714 for a state-matched Cooperative Extension agricultural agent (5-0), the board passed the amended FY 2020–2021 budget ordinance 3-2 (Ayes: Brenda A. Howerton, Ellen W. Reckhow, James Hill; Nays: Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs). Commissioners also unanimously approved the $5.48 million Durham County Coronavirus Relief Fund (CRF) plan for submission to NC PRO (5-0), reviewed the revised FY 2021–2030 Capital Improvement Plan ahead of a June 22 vote, and received a COVID-19 public health update.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of March 2, 2020 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the virtual meeting and shared announcements regarding COVID-19 volunteer opportunities (Feed Durham, Durham FEAST), free tax preparation at Northgate Mall, and Census response (55.5%). The board unanimously approved the March 2, 2020 work session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: 11th Anniversary of World Sickle Cell Awareness Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill read the proclamation designating June 19, 2020 as World Sickle Cell Awareness Day, and Duke Sickle Cell Program educator Tiffany Bell discussed the disproportionate impact of COVID-19 and healthcare disparities on Black men and sickle cell patients.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Declaring Racism as a Public Health Crisis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read the resolution authored with Dr. Wanda Boone (Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People), Racial Equity Officer Quillie Rashid-Henry, and Public Health Director Rod Jenkins declaring racism a public health crisis and committing to eight anti-racism policy, training, and reporting actions. Commissioners, Dr. Boone, Rashid-Henry, and Jenkins spoke strongly in support; Chair Jacobs also read letters from the Confederate Monuments Commission co-chairs and Mayor Steve Schewel urging action on the remaining Confederate monument base, prompting Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton to object to raising the monument when the County Attorney advised holding off.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of $50,000 RTP Foundation Donation and Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board recognized the Research Triangle Foundation for contributing $50,000 and coordinating $17,000 in lunches for Emergency Operations Center frontline workers. Commissioners then unanimously approved the consent agenda without pulling any items.

agenda_items.title: Adoption of FY 2020–2021 Budget Ordinance (DPS $15/hr Classified Staff Amendment & Cooperative Extension Position)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter moved (seconded by Chair Wendy Jacobs) to appropriate $3.8 million from fund balance/COVID reserves to fully implement a $15/hour minimum wage for all DPS classified staff in FY21; the motion failed 2-3 after Reckhow, Howerton, and Hill argued the board already added ~$1.9M–$2M by trimming Sheriff positions/vehicles and could not further deplete reserves amid severe pandemic revenue uncertainty and a $2.5M sales-tax split loss. The board unanimously added $42,714 (matched 40% by NC State) for a Cooperative Extension agricultural position (5-0), debated legal limits on countywide property tax relief under the Machinery Act, and adopted the amended FY 2020–2021 Budget Ordinance by a 3-2 vote (Carter and Jacobs opposed).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Amendment Failed 2-3; Extension Position Passed 5-0; Budget Ordinance Passed 3-2

agenda_items.title: Durham County Coronavirus Relief Fund (CRF) Plan ($5.48 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Jodi Miller presented the county's $5.48 million CARES Act CRF spending plan due to NC PRO by June 15, 2020, structured under updated state guidance to pursue 75%/25% FEMA/state reimbursement first while applying CRF funds to testing/Panther lab upgrades ($60k), direct public health expenses ($1.43M), public safety base/hazard payroll, and homeless/senior wraparound support ($2.17M). Commissioners unanimously approved submitting the plan.

agenda_items.title: Revised FY 2021–2030 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Keith Lane presented major CIP revisions including a $162.5M increase for Durham Public Schools (projected to require a 2-cent tax increase in FY 2022–23), deferring half the Public Safety Complex, Youth Home bed-count expansion, Snow Hill pump station escalation ($13M to $19.6M), Admin Building 1 renovations ($11M vs $8M scaled back), and $36M in Museum of Life and Science requests. Commissioners deferred the CIP vote to June 22 for staff follow-up on Admin 1 savings and Museum fundraising.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Public Health Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported Day 94 of EOC operations with 2,247 cumulative Durham cases and 611 active cases, noting the Latinx community accounted for 67% of May cases despite comprising 14% of county population. He reported onboarding 25 CCNC contact tracers (12 bilingual) and requesting 15 more investigators and 25 more tracers while expanding mobile/free testing with Duke and DHHS.

votes.item_title: Approval of March 2, 2020 Work Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Unanimously approved March 2, 2020 work session minutes.

votes.item_title: Budget Amendment Motion: Full $3.8 Million Funding for DPS Classified Staff $15/Hour Minimum Wage
votes.notes: Chair Jacobs stepped in to second Carter's motion when no other commissioner seconded.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to pull $3.8M from fund balance/COVID reserves to lift all DPS classified staff to $15/hour in FY 2020–21 failed 2-3, leaving the ~$1.9M half-step increase in place for potential January 2021 mid-year review.

votes.item_title: Budget Amendment: $42,714 County Match for Cooperative Extension Agricultural Position (0.6 FTE)
votes.discussion_detail: Allocated $42,714 from General Fund fund balance to fund 60% of a permanent Cooperative Extension agricultural agent supporting small/emerging farmers and hemp growers, matched 40% by NC State.

votes.item_title: Adoption of FY 2020–2021 County Budget Ordinance (as Amended with Cooperative Extension Position)
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted FY21 budget ordinance incorporating ~$5M+ in new DPS funding (including $1.9M toward $15/hr classified wages), a full-time Spanish interpreter, broadband study, $1M small business fund, food security coordinator, and the $42,714 Cooperative Extension amendment. Carter and Jacobs voted No solely because full $15/hr DPS classified funding was omitted.

votes.item_title: Approval of $5.48 Million Durham County Coronavirus Relief Fund (CRF) Plan
votes.discussion_detail: Approved submission of the $5.48M CRF spending plan to NC PRO ahead of the June 15, 2020 deadline.

disagreements.issue: Full Immediate Funding ($3.8M) for DPS Classified Staff $15/Hour Minimum Wage and FY 2020–2021 Budget Adoption
disagreements.summary: The board split 2-3 on appropriating $3.8 million from reserves to immediately pay all DPS classified staff $15/hour, and subsequently split 3-2 on adopting the final FY 2020–2021 budget ordinance.
disagreements.side_a_position: Fully fund the $15/hour living wage for all DPS classified staff in FY 2020–2021 now using fund balance/COVID reserves, and reject a budget that leaves those workers below $15/hour.
side_a_arguments: DPS bus drivers, custodians, and cafeteria workers—overwhelmingly Black and brown essential workers—were the only remaining county/city public employees below $15/hour.

With $3.5M remaining in the COVID set-aside, $4.6M in economic uncertainty reserves, and expected FEMA/CARES reimbursements for the $3.67M fund balance spend, the county could fund the $3.8M gap immediately.
disagreements.side_b_position: Limit DPS classified wage increases to the ~$1.9M down payment in the FY21 budget, preserve reserves against pandemic uncertainty, and revisit full funding in January 2021.
side_b_arguments: Commissioners already redirected ~$2M (including $1.25M from Sheriff detention vacancies and vehicles) on top of the manager's $5M DPS increase after DPS's estimate jumped from $1.7M–$1.8M to $3.8M.

County Manager Wendell Davis warned COVID costs already exceeded $7M and DHHS was demanding 10x testing expansion, while the city's sales-tax split change cost the county ~$2.5M and DPS held an $8M fund balance.
disagreements.resolution: Carter's $3.8M amendment failed 2-3, and the amended FY 2020–2021 budget ordinance passed 3-2 with Carter and Jacobs dissenting.

disagreements.issue: Design and City Cost-Sharing of Countywide Property Tax Assistance Program
disagreements.summary: Ahead of the budget vote, commissioners differed over whether the July 13 property tax relief proposal should focus strictly on long-term low-income homeowners alongside a binding City match, or explore broader legally permissible COVID-19 options.
disagreements.side_a_position: Bring forward a model countywide tax assistance program targeting long-term low-income homeowners in time for FY21 tax bills, meeting directly with advocacy groups.
side_a_arguments: Commissioner Heidi Carter emphasized helping long-term low-income homeowners stay in their homes and partnering with the City of Durham.
Chair Wendy Jacobs supported consulting community affordable-housing advocates while also addressing COVID-related mortgage/tax hardship.
disagreements.side_b_position: Restrict options to what is legal under the NC Machinery Act, avoid non-needy recipients, and secure a firm 50%+ financial commitment from the City.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow warned the County Attorney advised outright grant programs could expose commissioners to personal liability, and Vice Chair James Hill cautioned against broad relief echoing federal PPP abuses.
Reckhow and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton noted the Mayor's letter lacked an explicit 50% funding commitment even though the City benefited from $2.5M in reallocated sales tax.
disagreements.resolution: Staff was directed to meet with community groups and present legally viable options on July 13, 2020.

disagreements.issue: Raising Confederate Monument Base Removal During Racism Resolution Discussion
disagreements.summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs read letters calling for removal of the remaining Confederate monument base as a public health hazard, while Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton objected to bringing it up when the County Attorney advised waiting.
disagreements.side_a_position: Connect the Racism as a Public Health Crisis resolution to declaring the Confederate monument base a public health and safety hazard for removal.
side_a_arguments: Confederate Monuments Commission co-chairs and Mayor Steve Schewel wrote urging BOCC to act because white supremacist symbols inflict measurable stress and harm on Black residents.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-06-08 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 8, 2020 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, the Board shared announcements regarding COVID-19 testing resources and mail-in absentee voting via dcovotes.com before beginning a voice vote to approve the March 2, 2020 work session minutes. Vice Chair James Hill read a proclamation declaring June 19, 2020 as World Sickle Cell Awareness Day, followed by the presentation of a Resolution Declaring Racism a Public Health Crisis brought by Dr. Wanda Boone of Durham TRY and the Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People in collaboration with Racial Equity Officer Quaylee Rashid Henry and Public Health Director Rod Jenkins. Following a middle-of-meeting digest gap, the Board reviewed Capital Improvement Program adjustments for Alliance Behavioral Health and Administration Building I (where ground, first, fourth, and 4M floors are under contract while floors two and three retain older mechanical systems) and heard a COVID-19 update from Director Jenkins noting rising cases among Hispanic residents and the onboarding of 25 contact tracers (12 bilingual). The Board adjourned at 10:54 PM on a 4-0 voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs convened the meeting, read the public charge, and shared announcements on COVID-19 testing, federal relief application forms on the county website, and vote-from-home absentee ballot information at dcovotes.com for the 2020 election.

agenda_items.title: Approval of March 2, 2020 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved to approve the March 2, 2020 work session minutes, seconded by Vice Chair James Hill. Commissioners Brenda A. Howerton and Reckhow were recorded voting Yes before a digest gap omitted the remainder of the roll call.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (partial roll call 2-0 recorded before digest gap)

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: World Sickle Cell Awareness Day (June 19, 2020)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill read the proclamation declaring Friday, June 19, 2020 as World Sickle Cell Awareness Day in Durham County. Community representative Ms. Bell spoke on virtual outreach to sickle cell patients and highlighted the disproportionate impacts of COVID-19 and systemic racism on Black men.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Declaring Racism a Public Health Crisis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs introduced and read the Resolution Declaring Racism a Public Health Crisis, developed with Dr. Wanda Boone, Racial Equity Officer Quaylee Rashid Henry, and Public Health Director Rod Jenkins. The resolution commits the County to embedding racial equity across policies, contracting, staff and board training, and periodic progress reporting; Dr. Boone shared personal testimony connecting George Floyd's murder to historical and adverse childhood trauma.

agenda_items.title: CIP Update: Alliance Space and Administration Building I Renovations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a middle-of-meeting transcript truncation, commissioners questioned a 50% cost increase on Alliance workstations and sought clarity on Administration Building I renovations. Staff explained that renovations for the ground, first, fourth, and 4M floors are under contract, whereas floors two and three are excluded from the current phase and will need mechanical, electrical, and plumbing assessments to ensure safe workspaces.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Public Health Update (Director Rod Jenkins)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported that Durham's 7-day moving average of COVID-19 cases rose from 41 to 51, driven heavily by cases among Hispanic residents and close-contact spread (56% of active cases). He announced Durham was the first non-pilot county to onboard 25 contact tracers (12 bilingual) and had requested 15 more investigators and 25 more tracers, while Chair Jacobs pressed for free mobile community testing in partnership with Duke and the state.

agenda_items.title: Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Prior to the 11:00 PM curfew, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved to adjourn, seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow. The motion passed 4-0 with Vice Chair Hill, Commissioner Reckhow, Commissioner Howerton, and Chair Jacobs voting Yes.

votes.notes: Transcript digest omits lines immediately after Brenda A. Howerton and Ellen W. Reckhow voted Yes and Chair Jacobs began calling James Hill; outcome is recorded based on the uncontested start of the voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve the minutes of the March 2, 2020 Work Session.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-06-02 9:00 AM - Budget Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 2, 2020 Budget Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, commissioners reviewed FY2020-21 budget priorities amid COVID-19 fiscal constraints, though Commissioners Heidi Carter and James Hill voiced concern over feeling rushed ahead of the planned June 8 adoption. On a proposed food security coordinator/office, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow recommended against creating a permanent position mid-process and instead favored drawing from the nearly $5.5M COVID-19 recovery reserve once Recovery and Renewal Task Force proposals are vetted, an approach Chair Jacobs and County Manager Wendell Davis noted aligned with the reserve's purpose. In the afternoon, a sharp disagreement emerged over $993,000 in General Fund stormwater and erosion control costs: Commissioner Reckhow threatened to vote against the budget unless the County moved stormwater into an enterprise fund and charged unincorporated residents a $12.24–$48/year impervious-surface fee so city residents stop subsidizing county stormwater costs, while Chair Jacobs opposed acting under an ultimatum without public outreach to affected residents and commercial users. Budget Director Keith Lane concluded by outlining a balancing plan for June 8 adoption—using $1M from the COVID reserve for Duke small business aid and $546,000 in fund balance to cover $1.9M for DPS's $15/hour minimum wage—while deferring CIP and CARES Act discussions to June 8.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks and FY2020-21 Budget Priorities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs framed the budget around COVID-19 response and racial equity, flagging vehicle purchases, DPS's $15/hour minimum wage request, a food security coordinator, a DPS Spanish interpreter, and a northern county broadband study for scrutiny. Commissioner Reckhow requested cost savings from delaying Phase 3 of the Social Services staffing plan, while Commissioners Heidi Carter and James Hill expressed discomfort with the compressed timeline.

agenda_items.title: Food Insecurity Coordinator / COVID-19 Recovery Reserve Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed a late proposal for a food security coordinator or office. Commissioner Reckhow argued against approving new permanent positions in June without thorough vetting, recommending instead that the initiative be funded later from the $5.5M COVID recovery reserve alongside Recovery and Renewal Task Force recommendations and possibly supported by an ICMA intern.

agenda_items.title: Stormwater and Erosion Control Enterprise Fund & Fee Debate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle-of-meeting digest truncation, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow declared she would vote against the budget unless $993,000 in stormwater and erosion control costs were shifted from the General Fund into a utility fund supported by county impervious-surface fees ($12.24–$48/year) so city taxpayers do not subsidize county services. Chair Jacobs resisted enacting a new fee under a budget threat without community outreach, and staff agreed to engage community and commercial groups for feedback.

agenda_items.title: Budget Balancing Framework and Deferral of CIP & CARES Act Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Keith Lane summarized how to close a $1.546M gap for June 8 adoption—supporting $1M for Duke small business aid from the $4.5M COVID reserve and $1.9M for DPS's $15/hour wage using $546,000 in General Fund balance appropriation. Staff noted updated CARES Act/CRF guidance ahead of the June 15 submission deadline, and the Board moved CIP and CARES Act discussions to June 8 before adjourning without a formal vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-06-02 9:00 AM - Budget Work Session
disagreements.issue: Stormwater Utility Fund and County Impervious-Surface Fee Timing
disagreements.summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow threatened to vote against the FY2020-21 budget unless the County created a stormwater enterprise fund and charged county residents an impervious-surface fee immediately, whereas Chair Wendy Jacobs opposed passing a new fee under an ultimatum without prior outreach to impacted residents and commercial users.
disagreements.side_a_position: Transition stormwater and erosion control out of the General Fund into an enterprise/utility fund and enact county impervious-surface fees ($12.24–$48/year) in the FY21 budget.
side_a_arguments: City of Durham residents already pay a municipal stormwater fee and should not have to subsidize $993,000 in General Fund stormwater and erosion control costs for areas outside city limits.
Initial fees of $12.24 to $48 per year are modest compared to future state-mandated compliance costs and can be paired with ongoing outreach.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain temporary General Fund support while conducting public outreach with residential and commercial stakeholders before imposing a new fee.
side_b_arguments: A $48/year fee equates to roughly a 2-cent property tax increase on a $140,000 home and impacts residents during a pandemic.
Passing a new fee under a budget-vote ultimatum bypasses proper community engagement with the people and commercial property owners who will pay it.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken during the work session; staff agreed to conduct outreach with community groups and commercial users to gather feedback ahead of the June 8 meeting.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-06-01 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 1, 2020 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, Vice Chair James Hill read a joint statement on racial equity and social justice condemning prejudice and committing the Board to action in response to recent national events. County Manager Wendell Davis walked the Board through the consent agenda, where Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow questioned 0–3% merit raises in the $779,594.40 Animal Protection Society contract (Item 200) and the $75,000 City-County ICMA fellowship cost (Item 205) during a pandemic downturn, while also noting the Durham Tech Applied Technology Building came in $2M under budget and Chair Jacobs requested a cost-center update on the Rougemont water system (Item 217). Later in the session, commissioners discussed early childhood provider challenges and the status of the reposted Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACES) coordinator position before voting 5-0 by voice vote to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) for economic development incentives. After closed session, the conference line reached its time limit and participants disconnected to restart the call for the afternoon budget session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Joint Board Statement on Racial Equity and Social Justice
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs convened the work session, read the public charge, and delayed citizen comments pending guidance from the County Attorney. Vice Chair James Hill read a joint statement co-authored with Chair Jacobs condemning prejudice and urging the Board to match racial equity rhetoric with concrete action.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (APS Contract, ICMA Fellowship, Utilities, Detention Contract)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis walked through consent items including the $779,594.40 APS shelter contract (Item 200), a $50,000 RTP Foundation donation (Item 202), the ICMA fellowship interlocal agreement (Item 205), manhole inspections ($92,000, Item 216), the local water supply plan (Item 217), and a $98,280 detention center contract (Item 221). Commissioner Reckhow objected to funding merit raises in the APS contract while county staff pay is frozen and questioned the $75,000 ICMA fellowship expense, while Chair Jacobs requested a financial briefing on the water system.

agenda_items.title: Early Childhood Support and ACES Coordinator Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle-of-meeting digest truncation, commissioners discussed pandemic financial pressures on child care centers reopening with fewer children, staffing challenges where unemployment benefits exceeded wages, and coordination with Early Childhood Coordinator Kate Elander. Staff also reported that the selected candidate for the Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACES) coordinator declined the offer, requiring the position to be reposted.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Economic Development Incentives (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read the statutory motion to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss business location or expansion and tentative economic development incentives. Moved by Commissioner Reckhow and seconded by Commissioner Carter, the Board voted 5-0 to enter closed session, and later returned to reset the expiring conference link ahead of the budget work session.

votes.notes: Heidi Carter asked how the closed session would affect the afternoon budget work session before casting her Aye vote; all five commissioners voted Aye.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-05-28 9:00 AM - Budget Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 28, 2020 Budget Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, Durham Public Schools (DPS) presented its $18.9M FY2020-21 funding request versus the County Manager's recommended $3.24M operating increase and $2M capital outlay increase. DPS officials explained that roughly $600,000 of the operating increase passes directly to charter schools (~20% enrollment) and identified a $3.7M shortfall on core obligations—including classified pay, rising 21.86% retirement rates, $1.5M in lost fines/forfeitures, and ESL positions—alongside a separate $15/hour minimum wage request and $11.88M in federal CARES Act funds primarily supporting 1:1 devices. Following a middle-of-meeting digest gap, commissioners requested departmental service-impact details and prioritized Sheriff position rankings, while Budget Director Keith Lane cautioned that trying to digest budget options on June 2 for June 8 adoption left very little turnaround time, prompting Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and Chair Jacobs to weigh postponing CARES Act deliberations. Finally, Commissioner Reckhow pressed for a formal Board vote on a written Capital Improvement Program (CIP) amendment reflecting the >$100M DPS bond commitment and Public Safety Complex reductions, and Lane agreed to prepare a simplified 2–3 page financial roll-up spreadsheet for adoption while deferring the full CIP book until later in the summer.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools (DPS) FY2020-21 Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS finance leadership presented the Board of Education's $18.9M budget request against the County Manager's recommended $3.24M operating increase and $2M capital outlay increase. The presentation detailed a $3.7M shortfall on baseline needs (classified staff pay, retirement increases to 21.86%, charter school pass-throughs, curriculum, and ESL positions), a separate $15/hour minimum wage request, $11.88M in CARES Act funding for 1:1 devices and online instruction, and uncertainty over a projected $1.2B–$2B state shortfall.

agenda_items.title: Departmental Cuts, Sheriff Prioritization, and Budget Adoption Timeline
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a middle-of-meeting digest truncation, Chair Jacobs asked staff for specifics on how department-level cuts would affect direct services and reiterated the request for prioritized Sheriff positions. Budget Director Keith Lane warned that making final dollar choices on June 2 ahead of a June 8 adoption was heavily compressed, leading commissioners to consider deferring CARES Act deliberations to a separate meeting while Manager Wendell Davis urged maintaining momentum so EOC/COVID staff could prepare for reopening.

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Program (CIP) Amendment for DPS Projects
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow emphasized that the Board had committed to DPS in February to formally vote on an amended CIP incorporating over $100M in school capital funding and reductions to projects like the Public Safety Complex. Because producing a complete narrative CIP book by June 8 was not feasible, Budget Director Lane and Manager Davis proposed bringing a simplified 2–3 page financial roll-up schedule for formal Board approval in June and completing the full CIP document later in the summer.
