meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-05-27 9:00 AM - Budget Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 27, 2020 Budget Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, Sheriff Clarence Birkhead presented his FY2020-21 budget request, citing a 40% increase in property crime, 269 inmates in the detention center, and 12% staff turnover while proposing 12 repositioned/detention FTEs (including a mental health sergeant and a second intelligence officer) at a net savings of $23,639. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow raised 911 communications consolidation ('One Durham') and asked the Sheriff to rank-order the 12 positions and provide inmate demographic and quarterly crime data, which Commissioner Heidi Carter and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton echoed. Following a middle-of-meeting transcript gap, staff presented Durham County's $5.48M state Coronavirus Relief Fund (CRF/CARES Act) allocation alongside $875,000 in COVID-19 expenditures to date and ~$21M in projected costs across six federal categories, including food security, Meals on Wheels grants, and the Marriott RTP homeless shelter contract. meetings.title: Durham County Government BOCC Live
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the May 26, 2020 virtual regular session (archived/dated May 27, 2020) with all five commissioners present, and all formal votes passed unanimously (5-0). The board approved its April 13, 2020 regular session minutes (5-0), introduced Durham County's inaugural Racial Equity Officer Quillie Rashid-Henry and Early Childhood Coordinator Kate Elander, and issued proclamations for Older Americans Month and Children's Mental Health Awareness Month. Commissioners reviewed every consent item individually—including over $5 million in post-malware IT and cybersecurity contracts, an Orange County glass-recycling interlocal agreement, and $21,525 in pooled commissioner funds for 50,000 masks—before passing the consent agenda 5-0. The board then held two public hearings under SB 704 rules (leaving comments open 24 hours without voting): one on the FY 2020–2021 County Manager's Recommended Budget featuring 29 written comments largely advocating $15/hour DPS classified wages, school interpreters, and Sheriff budget reallocations, and a second on up to $75 million in Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2020C/2020D) for the 300 E. Main St. parking deck, Snow Hill pump station, Club RTP, DTCC land, and DPS schools; following COVID-19 and malware/SAP recovery updates and board appointments, the board entered closed session (5-0) and adjourned.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of April 13, 2020 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the virtual meeting, noted absentee ballot resources at dcovote.com, and congratulated Clerk Macio Carlton on detailed April 13, 2020 minutes. The board unanimously approved the minutes.

agenda_items.title: Introductions of Racial Equity Officer and Early Childhood Coordinator; Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Joanne Pierce introduced Durham County's first Racial Equity Officer, Quillie Rashid-Henry, and Cooperative Extension Director Donna Rewalt introduced Early Childhood Coordinator Kate Elander, both board-created positions. Chair Jacobs also read proclamations for Older Americans Month (with DSS's Janine Gordon) and Children's Mental Health Awareness Month (noting Alliance Health's Tika Demson).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Item-by-Item Review and Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis walked through each consent item, including IT/cybersecurity contracts (Items 174, 179, 180, 185, 186, 225) following the March 6 malware attack, March and April tax refund reports (191, 192), City-County and Orange County recycling agreements (198, 218 — allowing curbside fee to stay flat if glass is separated at convenience sites), $52,000 for Food Security Task Force contracts (207), and $21,525 in pooled commissioner funds for 50,000 masks via Cover Durham and the Community Health Coalition (242). Commissioners unanimously approved the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2020–2021 County Manager's Recommended Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Toomer read 29 submitted public comments (with duplicates grouped and Spanish-language submissions translated), overwhelmingly from Durham Association of Educators members, teachers, parents, and People's Alliance members urging at least $8.5 million in new DPS funding, a $15/hour minimum wage for DPS classified workers, additional school interpreters, eviction diversion, property tax relief, and reallocating $1.5M for Sheriff vehicles and unspent jail mental-health pod funds. Per SB 704, the hearing remained open for written comments for 24 hours.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Not to Exceed $75 Million Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2020C & 2020D)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director Susan Tezai and Budget Director Keith Lane presented the $75M short-term LOBs resolution covering $15M taxable financing for the 300 E. Main St. parking deck plus tax-exempt financing for Snow Hill pump station, $20M for Club RTP, $2.9M for a central Durham Tech land/building purchase (freeing $2.9M in pay-go reserves for COVID/economic uncertainty), and $18.5M for DPS school projects. Chair Jacobs officially opened the public hearing for 24 hours under SB 704 ahead of a June 1 vote and June 2 LGC review.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Public Health Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported Day 70 of EOC posture with 1,352 Durham cases, 45 deaths, and 408 active cases, highlighting a surge to 48–54% of recent cases in the Latinx community (particularly construction workers), a 1,000+-view Spanish Facebook Live event with ISLA, radio ads on La Ley and Radio One, and delays in receiving total negative-test denominators from NCDHHS.

agenda_items.title: Malware Attack Recovery and SAP Payroll Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CIO Greg Marrow reported completing P0 core IT, P1 citizen-facing, and P2 enterprise/SAP infrastructure restoration 80+ days after the March 6 malware attack, while continuing work on P3 departmental software. Finance Director Susan Tezai detailed manual processing of 2,150 handwritten AP checks, reopening SAP financials countywide, creating COVID disaster pay codes, and truing up payroll for election and part-time workers.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Lowell Siler announced selections for the ABC Board, Animal Welfare Advisory Committee, Board of Health, Durham Cultural Advisory Committee, Farmland Preservation Advisory Board, Industrial Facilities Authority, and Nursing Home CAC, while deferring a Women's Commission seat with only two votes. The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(5) regarding property acquisition/employment terms and returned at 03:41:46 to adjourn.

Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and Chair Jacobs raised strategic concerns over state guidance directing counties to exhaust CRF dollars before seeking FEMA Stafford Act reimbursement—warning that charging major expenses like the RTP homeless hotel contract to CRF could leave little funding for small businesses and recovery task force priorities—and asked staff to confirm options with NCACC and legal counsel. After a middle-of-meeting digest gap, Finance Director Susan Tezai presented fund balance projections comparing the current downturn to the 2008–2011 recession, estimating $3.9M in fund balance use in FY20 and $10.2M in FY21 (reducing unassigned fund balance from 13.25% to roughly 10.18%) before recovering in FY22. Prior to closed session, Commissioner Heidi Carter invoked N.C.G.S. 153A-44 to be excused from voting and participating in closed session, which the Board approved on a motion by Commissioner Reckhow seconded by Vice Chair James Hill (with Reckhow, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, and Chair Jacobs recorded voting Aye before a gap) before later reconvening to adjourn 3-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and CARES Act / Coronavirus Relief Fund Strategy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the 1:00 PM budget work session, read the public charge, and turned to staff for a CARES Act/CRF briefing under Session Law 2020-4. Commissioners Reckhow and Chair Jacobs voiced concern about NC OSBM and School of Government guidance instructing counties to use CRF before FEMA disaster reimbursement, fearing large shelter expenses would crowd out small business and task force relief before the June 1 submission deadline.

agenda_items.title: Fund Balance Overview and Multi-Year Fiscal Projections
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle-of-meeting digest truncation, Finance Director Susan Tezai reviewed FY19 actuals ($211.1M total fund balance; $82.9M or 13.25% unassigned) and modeled FY20–FY22 using 2008–2011 recession recovery benchmarks. She projected using $3.9M of fund balance in FY20 and $10.2M in FY21 (bringing unassigned fund balance to ~10.18%) before narrowing to $3.28M in FY22, while noting CARES Act offsets could ease pressure on FEMA timing.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-05-11 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 11, 2020 virtual Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, the Board unanimously approved the January 6, 2020 work session minutes (5-0) and the consent agenda (5-0), including an Urban Ministries COVID-19 hotel support update (141 residents housed) and a City-County sales tax interlocal agreement resulting in a $2.4 million (transcribed as 'billion') county sales tax revenue loss. County Manager Wendell Davis presented the FY 2021 Recommended Budget amid the dual crises of COVID-19 and the March cyberattack, noting that a projected $12–$15 million natural revenue gain had evaporated and outlining $3.1 million in operating reductions while protecting filled staff positions and Durham Public Schools needs. Later in the meeting, commissioners voted 5-0 by roll call to approve COVID-19 food security program funding—including $56,000 for Meals on Wheels (adjusted from $69,881 to align program timelines through August) alongside End Hunger Durham and El Centro partnerships—and heard an update from Commissioners Brenda A. Howerton and Ellen W. Reckhow on sourcing durable, washable North Carolina-made cloth face coverings in partnership with Duke, the City, DPS, and community health workers.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After confirming all five commissioners, the County Attorney, and the County Manager were on the call, Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the May 11, 2020 virtual Regular Session, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Hearing no agenda adjustments, Chair Jacobs shared announcements including the FY 2021 Durham County work plans remaining open for comment until May 22.

agenda_items.title: Approval of January 6, 2020 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved and Vice Chair James Hill seconded approval of the January 6, 2020 work session minutes. After noting the virtual meeting procedure required an individual roll-call voice vote, all five commissioners voted Aye, and Chair Jacobs reminded staff to incorporate the minutes' directives into the Board's tracking list.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Including Item 20-0151 Urban Ministries Hotel Update and Sales Tax Interlocal)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Under Item 20-0151, Drew Cummings reported that Urban Ministries had reached 141 residents—near full capacity—with hotel rooms still available, and IT staff reported progress toward a 60-day launch. Chair Jacobs thanked staff on the City-County sales tax interlocal agreement while noting it would reduce county sales tax revenue by $2.4 million (transcribed as 'billion'), and Vice Chair Hill confirmed an item aligned with the Durham County Fire and Rescue merger with the City before the Board approved the consent agenda 5-0.

agenda_items.title: County Manager's FY 2021 Recommended Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager presented the FY 2021 Recommended Budget framed around high revenue uncertainty from COVID-19 and recovery from the County's cyberattack. He reported that an anticipated $12–$15 million natural revenue increase evaporated between February and May, leaving no new revenue for over $40 million in requests, and detailed $3.1 million in operating reductions (following $2 million the prior year) while preserving filled employee positions and supporting critical Durham Public Schools needs.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Food Security Programs Funding (Meals on Wheels, End Hunger Durham, and El Centro)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented three food security proposals, noting Meals on Wheels' original $69,881 five-month request was scaled to $56,000 to align timeframes through August alongside End Hunger Durham and El Centro partnerships using local and minority-owned caterers. Commissioner Heidi Carter suggested exploring CARES or realigned funding for a permanent food security coordinator during budget work sessions, and the Board approved the three food security programs 5-0 on a motion by Commissioner Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Carter.

agenda_items.title: Durham Face Covering Initiative Update

Reckhow, joined by partner Isaac and Dr. Hart Brothers, reviewed three washable North Carolina-manufactured cloth mask options (Winston-Salem hosiery Nightingale mask, Barland Fabrics, and Carolina Textile District cooperative) and community health worker distribution plans. meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-05-04 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 4, 2020 virtual Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, early proceedings were marked by a procedural dispute when Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton sought to speak under personal privilege regarding the previous meeting, while Chair Jacobs insisted Howerton first vet her remarks with the County Attorney to avoid violating closed-session confidentiality rules before proceeding to the consent agenda. During consent agenda review, commissioners reached consensus on Item 20-0151—a $100,000 general fund appropriation amending the Urban Ministries COVID-19 hotel support contract—after staff clarified ongoing shelter security and laundry expenses. In the afternoon budget and finance session, the Manager and Finance staff reviewed fund balance projections, cautious July–December budget management principles protecting employee retirement and avoiding furloughs, and $75 million in capital cash flow including $6.5 million already approved by bond counsel and $12 million in additional Durham Public Schools projects, while Chair Jacobs requested written follow-up on CIP delays, AAA bond rating impacts, hazard pay, and payroll tracking. The Board voted 5-0 by roll call to adjourn into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) for personnel matters and later reconvened to adjourn at 08:07:45 after giving direction to staff.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Technical Setup, and Stay-at-Home / Face Covering Task Force Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After troubleshooting Webex camera visibility issues, Chair Wendy Jacobs called the May 4, 2020 virtual Work Session to order at 9:09 AM. She reported that she and the Mayor were assembling a community-leader task force to guide next steps on the stay-at-home order and face coverings.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comment Deferral and Procedural Dispute Over Commissioner Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Lowell Siler requested moving citizen comments later in the agenda while he researched newly surfaced facts. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton asked to make comments as a matter of personal privilege regarding the prior meeting, prompting a dispute with Chair Jacobs over whether her remarks required prior legal vetting to avoid disclosing closed-session personnel issues; Chair Jacobs deferred the request pending attorney guidance and moved to the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review: Item 20-0151 (Urban Ministries $100,000 COVID-19 Support) and Item 20-0160
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager presented Item 20-0151 appropriating $100,000 from the general fund to amend Urban Ministries' contract for COVID-19 hotel operations. After Chair Jacobs questioned the $100,000 figure relative to $74,000 in reported two-month costs and shelter waitlists, staff cited security and laundry expenses and another commissioner backed moving forward so the shelter could pay invoices, yielding board consensus before turning to Item 20-0160.

agenda_items.title: FY 2021 Budget Guiding Principles, Fund Balance Projections, and Capital / DPS Cash Flow
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and commissioners discussed cautious fiscal management from July through December, guiding principles against cutting staff retirement contributions or imposing furloughs, and fund balance projections assuming flat revenue versus a potential 25% Q4 sales tax drop. Finance staff detailed $75 million in capital cash flow—including $6.5 million approved by bond counsel and $12 million more for Durham Public Schools—and Chair Jacobs submitted written-response questions on AAA bond rating impacts, CIP delays, shifting priorities toward food/housing/broadband, hazard pay, and payroll reconciliation.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, the Board voted 5-0 by roll call to adjourn into a 3:30 PM closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) regarding personnel performance, appointments, or complaints. Returning to open session at 08:07:17 with Commissioners Carter, Hill, and Jacobs confirmed on the line, Chair Jacobs reported direction had been given to staff and the Board voted 3-0 to adjourn.

votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 roll-call vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider personnel qualifications, competence, performance, appointment conditions, or an employee complaint or grievance.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-05-04 9:00 AM - Work Session
disagreements.issue: Procedural Dispute Over Commissioner Personal-Privilege Comments and Closed-Session Confidentiality
disagreements.summary: Before the consent agenda, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton and Chair Wendy Jacobs clashed over whether Howerton could make public remarks regarding events from the prior board meeting without first obtaining County Attorney clearance.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require the County Attorney to review whether Commissioner Howerton's planned remarks touch on closed-session personnel matters before allowing public comment.
side_a_arguments: Public remarks referencing events from the prior meeting could implicate confidential closed-session rules.
The County Attorney should advise the Board on what is legally appropriate to discuss in open session before moving off the scheduled agenda order.
disagreements.side_b_position: Allow Commissioner Howerton to speak immediately under personal privilege because her remarks are not closed-session items and have already been discussed with the attorney.
side_b_arguments: The planned remarks were not closed-session comments either at the prior meeting or at the current work session.
Commissioner Howerton stated she had already consulted the County Attorney and objected to Chair Jacobs repeatedly trying to shut down her ability to speak.
disagreements.resolution: Chair Jacobs declined to hold an open-session discussion without the County Attorney's guidance and proceeded directly to the consent agenda.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-04-27 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 27, 2020 virtual Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, Chair Jacobs announced that the County Attorney and Clerk were interviewing independent counsel to conduct two investigations into the County Manager's letter and actions under the ICMA Code of Ethics and state election-interference statutes, sparking a sharp exchange in which Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton objected that she had not been informed of one of the issues and accused Jacobs of hypocrisy for raising it in announcements while cutting off her response. The Board adopted roll-call voting for virtual meetings on County Attorney guidance and approved the March 9, 2020 Regular and Work Session minutes 5-0, then heard Board of Elections officials present a bipartisan resolution supporting State Board of Elections COVID-19 absentee-voting recommendations (with the subsequent vote occurring inside a truncated transcript gap). Later in the session, commissioners reviewed the $28,000 remaining in the Board's discretionary budget for the Durham face-covering effort and received a comprehensive COVID-19 briefing covering 98 Urban Ministries residents housed at the Marriott RTP, a second quarantine host house, Durham Feeds reaching ~8,300 children, detention officer testing, IS&T's post-cyberattack recovery of over 2,000 computers, and countywide broadband equity needs.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Census/Pandemic Announcements, and Dispute Over County Manager Investigations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the virtual Regular Session, read the public charge, led the Pledge of Allegiance, and announced 2020 Census and Pandemic Unemployment Assistance updates. Addressing earlier remarks by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, Chair Jacobs stated the County Attorney and Clerk were interviewing independent counsel for two investigations into the County Manager's letter and potential ICMA ethics or election-interference violations, prompting a pointed exchange after Howerton said she had not been informed of one investigation and called Jacobs hypocritical for raising the topic while refusing open debate.

agenda_items.title: Approval of March 9, 2020 Regular Session and Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter moved and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded approval of the March 9, 2020 Regular Session and Work Session minutes. Following guidance from County Attorney Lowell Siler recommending roll-call votes during remote meetings for clarity, all five commissioners voted to approve the minutes 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting State Board of Elections COVID-19 Voting Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Board of Elections Director Derek Bowens and Board Chair Phil Lehman presented a bipartisan resolution backing State Board of Elections legislative recommendations to expand absentee-by-mail options, launch an online request portal, and waive the 20% (~$2 million) federal match for election PPE and safety supplies. Chair Jacobs began reading the resolution at 00:28:55; any final vote fell within the truncated middle portion of the transcript digest.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Introduced / Vote not shown in transcript digest

agenda_items.title: Durham Face Covering Initiative and BOCC Discretionary Budget Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed allocating unused travel/discretionary funds—confirmed by Budget Director Keith Lane at $28,000 remaining through June 30, with $15,000–$20,000 potentially available—for the Durham face covering effort alongside potential City participation. Chair Jacobs sought a commissioner volunteer to assist Commissioner Howerton ahead of Monday's work session update.

agenda_items.title: Durham County COVID-19 Crisis Update (EOC, Public Health, Housing, Food, Cyber Recovery, Broadband)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Emergency Management Director Jim Groves, Public Health Director Rodney Jenkins, and county staff reported on Latinx community outreach, SNAP online shopping waivers, housing 98 Urban Ministries residents at the Marriott RTP, securing a second quarantine host house, Durham Feeds reaching ~8,300 children, long-term care outbreaks, contact tracing, and Wellpath testing for detention officers. IS&T Director Greg detailed recovery from the March 6 cyberattack across 2,000+ computers, 800 databases, and 300 servers, and Commissioner Heidi Carter emphasized addressing rural broadband gaps and the 3:1 DPS digital divide in the upcoming budget.

agenda_items.title: Board/Commission Appointment Voting Format and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs noted that board and commission appointment votes had been submitted in advance to the Clerk under the County's temporary remote meeting format. The Board then adjourned on a 5-0 roll-call vote moved by Commissioner Reckhow and seconded by Vice Chair Hill.

votes.item_title: Approval of March 9, 2020 Regular Session and Work Session Minutes
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 roll-call vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve the March 9, 2020 Regular Session and Work Session minutes via roll-call vote per County Attorney Lowell Siler's remote-meeting guidance.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-04-27 7:00 PM - Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Disclosure and Open-Session Discussion of Independent Investigations into the County Manager
disagreements.summary: During announcements, Chair Wendy Jacobs and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton clashed over notification and open-session discussion of two independent investigations concerning the County Manager.
disagreements.side_a_position: Implement the Board's prior decision to interview independent counsel for two investigations into the County Manager's letter and conduct, and defer further discussion to a closed session.
side_a_arguments: The County Attorney and Clerk are executing steps the Board already voted on by interviewing independent counsel for two investigations (the letter sent by the County Manager, and his actions relative to the ICMA Code of Ethics, NC General Statutes, and potential election interference).
Discussing personnel and ethics investigation details in open session is improper and should wait for a closed session with the County Attorney at the Monday work session.
disagreements.side_b_position: Object that one of the two investigation issues was not disclosed to Commissioner Howerton and criticize Chair Jacobs for raising the matter in announcements while cutting off questions.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Howerton stated Chair Jacobs had mentioned two investigation issues without informing her of one of them.
Howerton argued it was hypocritical for Chair Jacobs to cite impropriety after raising the investigation details herself during open-session announcements.
disagreements.resolution: Chair Jacobs declined further open-session debate, offered a closed session for the May 4 work session, and moved on to approval of the minutes.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC April 13, 2020
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the April 13, 2020 virtual regular session with all five commissioners participating during dual COVID-19 and malware-recovery operations. The board unanimously approved its February 3 work session and February 24 regular session minutes (5-0), read submitted citizen comments on tax rates and accessible parking decks, and issued proclamations for National County Government Month and Breastfeeding Family Friendly Community. After walking item-by-item through consent items 20-0129 through 20-0139—including a $195,954 state COVID-19 grant, $500,000 in pre-construction/design amendments for the 300 E. Main St. parking deck, a conservation easement option, Elementary School C land acquisition, and a $3.67 million fund balance appropriation for emergency COVID response—the board approved the consent agenda 4-1 (Ayes: Brenda A. Howerton, Heidi Carter, Ellen W. Reckhow, Wendy Jacobs; Nay: James Hill). Commissioners then received extensive COVID-19 response briefings from Public Health Director Rod Jenkins and Emergency Management Chief Leslie O'Connor, an IT malware restoration update from CIO Greg Marrow, and voted 5-0 to enter closed session on economic development incentives before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Minutes, Citizen Comments, and Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the remote meeting, highlighted the unified City-County Stay at Home order, small business resources, and the August 14 census deadline, and led unanimous approval of the February 3 and February 24, 2020 minutes. Written citizen comments from Patrick Nally (tax rate increase) and G. Diane Wilkes (smart accessible parking) were read, followed by proclamations for National County Government Month and Breastfeeding Family Friendly Community (with Love Anderson).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Item-by-Item Review and Approval (Items 20-0129 through 20-0139)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because no work session had been held, Manager Wendell Davis and staff walked through consent items: $195,954 NCDHHS COVID-19 prevention/surveillance grant (129); Chase pre-construction and Little design contracts totaling $500,000 for the 300 E. Main St. parking deck and 414 W. Chapel Hill displacement lot (130, 131); a conservation easement at 514 Harris Mill Rd (137); Durham Public Schools purchase of two parcels for Elementary School C (138); and $3.67 million (~$3.8M) in fund balance for COVID-19 operating costs, Marriott RTP shelter rooms, PPE, and building sanitization (139). After initially hearing no nays, Vice Chair James Hill registered his vote in opposition, resulting in a 4-1 passage.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Crisis Response Briefing (Public Health & Emergency Management)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported 325 Durham COVID-19 cases, one death, and outbreaks at three long-term care facilities, alongside Duke PA contact-tracing support and reduced HHS hours. Emergency Management Chief Leslie O'Connor detailed Day 27 of EOC operations, including moving Urban Ministries residents to the Marriott RTP hotel, pursuing a second quarantine hotel, $1.7M in supplemental SNAP benefits, DPS Foundation feeding partnerships, and FEMA Stafford Act reimbursement tracking, while Jim Groves noted PPE shortages of gowns and masks.

agenda_items.title: IS&T Malware Attack Restoration Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief Information Officer Greg Marrow reported that 38 days after the malware attack, most critical citizen-facing systems (Register of Deeds, Tax, Public Health, DSS, Budget, HR), phones, email, and over 2,000 county laptops and desktops had been cleaned and restored, while IT continued supporting remote work.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Economic Development Incentives)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners voted unanimously to adjourn into closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss industry location/expansion and tentative economic development incentives, returning at 03:44:43 to adjourn.

votes.item_title: Approval of February 3, 2020 Work Session and February 24, 2020 Regular Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Unanimously approved February 3 work session and February 24 regular session minutes.

votes.item_title: Motion to Adjourn into Closed Session (NCGS 143-318.11(a)(4) — Economic Development)
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session to discuss prospective business expansion/location incentives.

disagreements.issue: Opposition Vote on April 13, 2020 Consent Agenda
disagreements.summary: Following item-by-item review of the consent agenda covering COVID-19 state grants, the $3.67 million fund balance appropriation, 300 E. Main St. parking deck contracts, and Elementary School C land acquisition, Vice Chair James Hill registered a dissenting No vote.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the full consent agenda to fund urgent COVID-19 operations, shelter/PPE procurement, school land acquisition, and parking deck pre-construction.
side_a_arguments: County Manager Wendell Davis, EOC staff, and commissioners emphasized the rainy-day fund balance appropriation was critical for hotel shelter, PPE, sanitization, and FEMA reimbursement documentation, alongside needed school and capital projects.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose approval of the consent agenda package.
side_b_arguments: Vice Chair James Hill stated on the record that he wished to vote No without specifying which consent item he opposed.
disagreements.resolution: Consent agenda passed 4-1.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-03-02 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 2, 2020 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, public commenters raised staff parking fees on the 300 block of East Main Street, ICE/Sheriff detainers, and county fund balance reserves. Commissioners reviewed consent agenda items—including E.B. Peterson wastewater positions, jail bed and HVAC capital amendments, a Dry Creek Farm conservation easement, $55,400 in design funding for Lincoln Community Health Center parking lot expansion, and Main Library renovation energy-efficiency grants—and received briefings on the 300/500 East Main Street TDM and parking study as well as the Durham County Memorial Stadium Authority's pilot beer/wine garden policy and $2–$3 million budget ROI tracking. Before entering closed session, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton raised a formal transparency objection after learning a closed session had been arranged the prior Monday night without notifying all commissioners, prompting Chair Jacobs to agree that the County Attorney would attend the next discussion. The Board then voted unanimously by voice vote to adjourn into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5), (a)(6), and (a)(3).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Citizen Comment Period
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the March 2, 2020 Work Session, read the public charge, and heard citizen comments from James Chavis (criticizing employee parking fees at the 300 block of Main Street), Ms. Peterson (questioning City Council citizenship, Sheriff/ICE release practices, and County fund balance reserves), Dr. E.L. Allison, and John Tarantino. Chair Jacobs asked budget staff to follow up on Ms. Peterson's fund balance questions.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Scheduling and Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A commissioner requested adding a closed-session policy discussion and holding closed session at lunch to conclude by 2:00 PM. The County Manager walked through consent items including E.B. Peterson wastewater staff, jail bed/HVAC grille replacements, electro-mechanical services, Dry Creek Farm conservation easement, $55,400 in design funding toward Lincoln Community Health Center's $239,877 parking lot expansion, and Main Library energy-saving renovation grants.

agenda_items.title: 300 and 500 East Main Street Redevelopment: TDM and Staff Parking Assessment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff introduced an update from Little Architectural Design and the project team assessing County staff parking and transportation demand management (TDM) options for the 300 and 500 East Main Street redevelopment. Detailed slides and discussion fell within the truncated middle section of the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Memorial Stadium Authority Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Stadium Manager Zach and Stadium Authority Chair Pam reported progress toward a balanced operating budget, a 15-event pilot beer/wine garden policy for adult-focused Tobacco Road FC and ultimate frisbee events, revised vendor/concession policies, and youth sports camp opportunities. Commissioner Heidi Carter inquired about return on investment given the stadium's $2–$3 million budget, and staff agreed to incorporate ROI data into MFR reporting.

agenda_items.title: Board Directives Follow-Up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported following up directly with responsible department heads on pending ('yellow') board directives from the December work session after those minutes were finalized.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Notification Policy Discussion and Motion to Enter Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton objected that a closed session had been discussed with some board members the prior Monday night without notifying the entire Board, and another member stressed transparency and legal counsel's presence; Chair Jacobs acknowledged the concern and agreed the County Attorney would attend the next discussion. The Board then passed a unanimous voice vote on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Heidi Carter to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5), (a)(6), and (a)(3).

votes.item_title: Motion to Adjourn into Closed Session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5), (a)(6), and (a)(3)
votes.notes: Approved by unanimous voice vote with no opposition voiced; individual roll-call votes were not taken.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to enter closed session to instruct negotiating agents on property acquisition or employment contract terms (a)(5), consider personnel performance/complaints (a)(6), and preserve attorney-client privilege (a)(3).

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-03-02 9:00 AM - Work Session
disagreements.issue: Board-Wide Notification and Legal Counsel Protocol for Calling Closed Sessions
disagreements.summary: Before entering closed session, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton questioned Chair Wendy Jacobs over a closed session arranged the previous Monday night without notifying all commissioners.
disagreements.side_a_position: All commissioners must receive timely board-wide notification whenever a closed session is called, with the County Attorney present for legal guidance.
side_a_arguments: Unlike normal board practice where all commissioners receive email notice, a closed session was initiated with only some members informed, leaving Commissioner Howerton out of the conversation.
Transparency requires informing the entire Board and having legal advice present during such discussions.
disagreements.side_b_position: Acknowledge the concern while explaining that the Chair had been consulting directly with the Clerk, UNC School of Government, and select board members.
side_b_arguments: Chair Jacobs stated she had been working directly with Clerk Monica and conferring with the UNC School of Government while discussing the matter with some board members.
She acknowledged Howerton's point and agreed to ensure the County Attorney is present at the next discussion.
disagreements.resolution: Chair Jacobs acknowledged the concern and committed to having the County Attorney present for the follow-up discussion, after which the Board entered closed session unanimously.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC February 24, 2020
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the February 24, 2020 regular session with all five commissioners present, dominated by an added public comment period and closed session regarding County Manager Wendell Davis's letter alleging racial bias and demeaning remarks by Commissioner Heidi Carter. After voting unanimously to add both a public comment period and a closed session (5-0 each), the board heard emotional testimony from community leaders—including Joshua Gunn, Omar Beasley, Edward Bell, Jackie Wagstaff, Jarvis Martin, Brian Calloway, and Dr. Lavonia Allison—demanding an independent external investigation, while Carter defended her equity and public-school advocacy. Following a 30-minute closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(6) (5-0), Chair Jacobs announced the board unanimously directed the clerk to contact the NC Association of County Commissioners (NCACC), UNC School of Government, and ICMA to recommend outside legal counsel and facilitate a broad independent investigation. In the remainder of the meeting, commissioners memorialized former Commissioner Joe Bowser, honored retiring Interim EMS Director Kevin Underhill, approved December 2, 2019 minutes (5-0), reviewed property tax relief programs, approved the consent agenda (5-0) and pulled items 20-0079 and 20-0087 (5-0), and made board and commission appointments.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Agenda Adjustments (Adding Public Comment & Closed Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order and moved to add a closed session to the agenda, while Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved to add a public comment period and place it prior to the closed session so waiting citizens could address the board. Both adjustments passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Emergency Public Comment on County Manager Wendell Davis's Allegations Against Commissioner Heidi Carter
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Multiple community members and leaders—including Joshua Gunn, Omar Beasley (Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People), Edward Bell, Jackie Wagstaff, Andrea 'Muffin' Hudson, Jarvis Martin, Brian Calloway, and Dr. Lavonia Allison—spoke in support of County Manager Wendell Davis following media reports of his letter alleging racial bias and mistreatment by Commissioner Heidi Carter, calling for an external objective investigation. Commissioner Carter closed the period by rejecting claims of racism, stating she would not apologize for advocating for DPS, pre-K, affordable housing, healthcare, food security, and transit alongside leaders of color.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Personnel Matter (NCGS 143-318.11(a)(6)) and Investigation Directive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session to address the confidential personnel/grievance matter. Upon returning at 01:40:49, Chair Jacobs announced the board unanimously directed the clerk to contact NCACC for outside counsel recommendations and consult UNC School of Government and ICMA regarding a broad investigation, adding that she felt badly Manager Davis was hurt while believing Carter did not intend racist statements.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Tribute to Former Commissioner Joe Bowser, and Resolution for Kevin Underhill
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs paid tribute to former Commissioner Joe Bowser (who passed away February 14, 2020), shared March 3 primary voting and Braggtown Library reopening announcements, and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow recognized Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton and Durham organizations for Think Babies NC awards. The board also presented a retirement resolution honoring Interim EMS Director Kevin Underhill's 26 years of service, including pioneering pre-hospital STEMI ECG protocols and community paramedicine.

agenda_items.title: Approval of December 2, 2019 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After briefly revisiting the skipped minutes item, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow requested a status report on directives from the December 2, 2019 work session at next week's work session and moved approval of the minutes, which passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Tax Relief Program Overview, Consent Agenda, and Pulled Items 20-0079 and 20-0087
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Tax Administrator Dwayne Brinson outlined payment coupons, delinquent payment plans, the online Property Tax Assistance Evaluator, and North Carolina's three primary relief programs (Homestead, Circuit Breaker, Disabled Veteran). The board approved consent items 20-0070 through 20-0081 (excluding 20-0079 and 20-0087) 5-0, heard public comments from Dr. Lavonia Allison and Mr. Leonard on Register of Deeds excise tax refund statute GS 105-228.37, tax revaluations, and Board of Elections voting-site statutes, and then approved items 20-0079 and 20-0087 unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Commuter Rail Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Lowell Siler announced appointment votes for the Board of Health (Roger McDougal, James Miller, Robert Rosenstein, Victoria Orto), Boxing and Wrestling Commission (Maya Bass), and Durham County Women's Commission (Laura Myers). Chair Jacobs noted staff would circulate a summary of strong public turnout at the weekend commuter rail open house before adjourning.

votes.discussion_detail: Added a two-minute-per-speaker public comment period for residents in attendance and sequenced it before closed session.

votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session regarding a confidential personnel complaint/matter; Chair Jacobs later announced the board unanimously directed the clerk to pursue outside counsel via NCACC and consult UNC SOG and ICMA for a broad investigation.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved minutes of the December 2, 2019 work session.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved Register of Deeds statutory tax refund (with Register of Deeds noting he would raise GS 105-228.37 with his state association) and the Board of Elections SouthData contract.

disagreements.issue: County Manager Wendell Davis's Racial Bias Allegations Against Commissioner Heidi Carter and Scope of Investigation
disagreements.summary: Public speakers, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, and Commissioner Heidi Carter clashed over County Manager Wendell Davis's letter accusing Carter of racial bias and demeaning remarks, though all five commissioners ultimately agreed in closed session to seek an independent outside investigation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Validate the County Manager's complaint of racial bias and mistreatment by Commissioner Carter and launch a swift, impartial external investigation.
side_a_arguments: Community speakers (including Joshua Gunn, Omar Beasley, Jackie Wagstaff, and Dr. Lavonia Allison) cited Davis's seven-year exemplary audit record and accused Carter of racial insensitivity and disrespectful remarks ('you work for the board; grin and bear it').
Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton insisted on holding the public comment session before closed session so community voices would be heard.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject allegations of racist intent while agreeing to an independent outside review to address all underlying issues fairly.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Heidi Carter stated she would not apologize for advocating for DPS, pre-K, affordable housing, and transit alongside leaders of color, and joined the vote to enter closed session.
Chair Wendy Jacobs apologized that Davis's feelings were hurt while stating she did not believe Carter intended racist remarks and supporting outside counsel.
disagreements.resolution: After a 30-minute closed session, the board unanimously directed the clerk to contact NCACC for outside counsel recommendations and consult UNC School of Government and ICMA regarding a broad investigation.

meetings.title: BOCC Feb 10 2020 ENTIRE meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the February 10, 2020 regular session with all five commissioners present. The board unanimously approved its January 27, 2020 minutes (5-0) and consent agenda items 20-0032 through 20-0067 (5-0)—including $76,700 in Open Space and Trails matching grants, $2 million+ for bus stops, a revised Economic Development Incentives Policy with community benefits, a Sports Commission interlocal agreement, and $3 million in school capital reallocations. Following a public hearing, commissioners voted 5-0 to approve a $2,550,000 seven-year economic development incentive for Eli Lilly and Company's $440 million, 462-job biopharmaceutical manufacturing facility. During BOCC directives review, commissioners sparred over whether to evaluate paid employee parking in county decks as part of Transportation Demand Management, with Ellen W. Reckhow and Wendy Jacobs urging options while James Hill and Brenda A. Howerton opposed charging county workers. On the Triangle Trails Initiative resolution, the board voted 4-1 to endorse multi-county trail planning (Ayes: Heidi Carter, Ellen W. Reckhow, Wendy Jacobs, James Hill; Nay: Brenda A. Howerton, who cited unclear accountability), before entering closed session (5-0) and granting Vice Chair Hill an excused absence for March 2 (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of January 27, 2020 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting (noting building construction disrupted video livestreaming, leaving audio active), shared March 3 primary early-voting and same-day registration information, and announced a $701,101 JCPC funding RFP and Golden Leaf Award nominations. Commissioners unanimously approved the January 27, 2020 minutes.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review and Approval (Items 20-0032 through 20-0067)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners highlighted key consent items including $76,700 in Open Space & Trails matching grants, Youth Home comprehensive center planning, expanded Veterans outreach, over $2 million for bus stop amenities, and the revised Economic Development Incentives Policy incorporating community benefits. Staff also clarified $352,000+ in annual Urban Ministries support after public comment from Mr. Chavis, reviewed the new Sports Commission interlocal agreement, and confirmed reallocating $3M from Northern High School 2016 GO bond funds would not delay Northern High or Elementary School C before approving the consent agenda 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Item 20-0065 — $2,550,000 Economic Development Incentive for Eli Lilly and Company
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Officer Andy Miracle presented a $2.55M seven-year incentive for Eli Lilly's $440 million facility creating 462 jobs (half accessible with associate/vocational degrees starting around $50,000+) and generating $5.3M in new property tax revenue over five years, plus childcare, TDM, MWBE, and second-chance hiring commitments under the new policy. Chamber representative Brian Foxx supported the grant, while CJ Broderick urged upfront anti-displacement planning; commissioners approved the incentive 5-0.

agenda_items.title: BOCC Directives Follow-Up (TDM/Paid Parking, Planning Split, Sheriff Jail Data, Sales Tax ILA)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed outstanding directives, sparking debate over Transportation Demand Management and paid employee deck parking ahead of 300/500 E. Main St. agreements, with Reckhow and Jacobs seeking options and Hill and Howerton opposing employee parking fees. Commissioners also queried Engaged Durham consultant spending, DPS pre-K Title I data, unspent Sheriff female mental health pod funds and jail data, the 70/30 city-county planning workload vs 50/50 cost split, DSS building DFI plans, the sales-tax ILA, and the 100% clean energy RFQ.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting the Triangle Trails Initiative
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow presented a resolution endorsing multi-county regional greenway planning led by Chuck Flink (Greenways Inc.) using privately raised funds at no cost to Durham County, incorporating Chair Jacobs's added 'whereas' clause on commuting access and climate/carbon reduction and Heidi Carter's request for equitable engagement. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton opposed the resolution, citing insufficient background on who holds accountability, resulting in a 4-1 passage.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Excused Absence for Vice Chair James Hill
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(4) on economic development incentives, returned at 02:08:22, unanimously granted Vice Chair James Hill an excused absence for the March 2 work session to attend the NACo conference, and adjourned.

disagreements.issue: Triangle Trails Initiative Resolution Governance and Accountability
disagreements.summary: Four commissioners supported endorsing the privately funded multi-county Triangle Trails Initiative with added climate and commuting-equity language, while Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton voted No due to unclear organizational accountability.
disagreements.side_a_position: Endorse the Triangle Trails Initiative resolution to establish regional greenway connections for commuting, health, economic development, and climate benefits at no cost to Durham County.
side_a_arguments: Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow, Wendy Jacobs, and Heidi Carter noted the initiative required no county funds, leveraged private philanthropy through a regional foundation, and supported transportation equity and carbon reduction.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the resolution until leadership, organizational governance, and county responsibility are clearly explained.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton stated the agenda packet lacked sufficient background on the proposed foundation and which entity would be accountable, saying she 'didn't get the essence of it.'
disagreements.resolution: Resolution passed 4-1, with Reckhow tasked with following up on equitable community engagement and governance questions.

disagreements.issue: Transportation Demand Management and Charging County Employees for Deck Parking
disagreements.summary: During directives review, commissioners clashed over whether staff should evaluate charging county employees to park in county decks ahead of the 300 and 500 East Main Street parking decisions.
disagreements.side_a_position: Bring forward TDM options including potential employee parking fees to manage parking demand and right-size downtown parking decks.
side_a_arguments: Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow and Wendy Jacobs noted City of Durham employees pay tiered parking rates and the Environmental Affairs Board urged cutting parking supply in the 300/500 block projects.
disagreements.side_b_position: Protect free employee parking as a matter of workforce fairness and economic equity.
side_b_arguments: Vice Chair James Hill argued charging county workers—many single mothers—for parking when Durham transit cannot reliably get parents from schools to downtown work is regressive.
Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton called taking back hard-won competitive employee compensation through parking fees 'inhumane.'
disagreements.resolution: No vote taken; County Manager Wendell Davis agreed to present TDM options and updates at the March work session.

meetings.title: Joint BOCC and BOE Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 4, 2020 Joint Board of County Commissioners and Durham Public Schools Board of Education (BOE) meeting presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the joint boards adjusted the agenda to hear Morehead Montessori updates first and unanimously approved the prior joint minutes by voice vote with a correction from 'GEO' to 'GO' (General Obligation) bonds. Morehead Montessori Principal Cynthia Webb and DPS COO Julius Monk reported that failing heat exchangers in 7 of 11 HVAC units had displaced students and staff to the Staff Development Center and Eno Valley Elementary at an estimated $100,000 emergency repair cost; a BOE member requested a $100,000 county fund-balance appropriation at BOCC's next meeting, which Chair Jacobs deferred to comprehensive budget discussions alongside carbon monoxide detector needs. Subsequent presentations reviewed DPS's $17+ million FY 2020–21 budget request, its $9.3 million combined unrestricted fund balance, teacher salary supplement comparisons with Wake County, emergency collaboration during the McDougall Terrace evacuation at Burton Elementary, Durham Pre-K's 44-site braided funding model, and a new contract with East Durham Children's Initiative / Durham Children's Initiative to develop a countywide Early Childhood Action Plan.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustment, and Approval of Joint Minutes

Reckhow seconded by BOE member Natalie, the joint boards unanimously approved the minutes by voice vote with a page-5 typo corrected from 'GEO' to 'GO' (General Obligation) bonds and a reminder to revisit Northern High School stadium plans.

agenda_items.title: Morehead Montessori Elementary HVAC Failure, Displacement, and $100,000 Repair Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Principal Cynthia Webb and DPS Chief Operating Officer Julius Monk reported that 7 of 11 HVAC units at Morehead Montessori required emergency heat-exchanger replacements shipped from three countries, displacing students and staff to the Staff Development Center and Eno Valley Elementary at an estimated $100,000 cost including duct cleaning and burn-off. agenda_items.title: DPS FY 2020–21 Budget Request, Fund Balance, and Teacher Salary Supplements

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-02-03 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 3, 2020 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, public commenters Brian Fox and Carl Rist (Durham People's Alliance) weighed in on the draft Economic Development Policy, with Rist praising clawbacks and justice-involved hiring priorities while urging an online incentives dashboard, expanded public-hearing notice, and a $15/hour living-wage floor for all incentivized jobs. Staff briefed commissioners on the first CMAR phase for the new 36-bed Youth Home facility (planned for Fall 2022 to accommodate 16- and 17-year-olds under Raise the Age), though Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton questioned whether neighboring counties would contribute funding. Later in the session, transit officials noted upcoming GoTriangle and MPO briefings on Treyburn service and BRT routes, and commissioners debated revisions to the Economic Development Policy—including MWBE RFP notices, annual reporting, staff capacity, and avoiding formulaic revenue-percentage caps (such as 50%) that could weaken county negotiating leverage—before holding the draft off Monday's agenda for legal review by Thursday. The Board then voted unanimously by voice vote on a motion by Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded by Vice Chair James Hill to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) for economic development negotiations and subsequently adjourned.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Citizen Comments on Economic Development Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the February 3, 2020 Work Session and read the public charge. Brian Fox endorsed the draft Economic Development Policy codifying workforce, education, diverse purchasing, and sustainability practices, while Carl Rist of the Durham People's Alliance praised clawback and justice-involved hiring provisions while urging an annual dashboard, broader public-hearing outreach, and a $15/hour living-wage requirement or bonus incentive for all incentivized jobs.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review: New 36-Bed Youth Home CMAR Phase and Item 34
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff member Jody presented the first-phase Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) contract for the new 36-bed Youth Home (targeted for Fall 2022) serving 16- and 17-year-olds under Raise the Age, noting outreach to the Durham legislative delegation, NC Department of Public Safety, and five catchment counties (three interested). Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton cautioned that neighboring counties might view the expense as a state obligation, and staff began reviewing Item 34 before the transcript middle gap.

agenda_items.title: Transit Update: Proposed BRT Routes, Treyburn Service, and Triangle Greenways Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transit staff noted that proposed Treyburn bus service remained subject to GoTriangle Board approval at its February meeting and that proposed BRT routes would go before the MPO Board the following week. Chair Jacobs stated that board directives and the Triangle Greenways resolution would be placed on Monday night's Regular Session agenda.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Policy Revisions Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic development staff Andy presented policy revisions requiring companies to notify MWBE vendors of capital RFPs, adding pre- and post-hearing project briefing sheets, supporting an annual report/dashboard, and requesting an additional staff position. Commissioners including Heidi Carter debated avoiding formulaic award ceilings (such as 50% of revenue) or fixed checklist bonuses that could undermine negotiation leverage toward lower one-third or one-fourth incentive shares, and agreed to delay Monday action unless revised language cleared legal review by Thursday.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded by Vice Chair James Hill, the Board voted unanimously by voice vote to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) regarding industry location/expansion and tentative economic development incentives. Upon reconvening at 05:30:52 after giving direction to staff, the Board adjourned unanimously on a motion by Commissioner Carter seconded by Commissioner Reckhow.

votes.notes: Approved unanimously by voice vote without roll call.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC January 27, 2020
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the January 27, 2020 regular session with all five commissioners present, passing every formal vote unanimously (5-0). The board approved its November 4, 2019 work session and January 13, 2020 regular session minutes (5-0), welcomed new Public Health Director Rodney Jenkins and a deploying 91st Civil Affairs Battalion delegation from Fort Bragg, and approved consent items 20-0019 through 20-0039 (5-0) after reviewing a NACo early-childhood policy resolution tied to the Pritzker grant. Following a public hearing on UDO Text Amendment TC19-0002—a privately initiated request on behalf of Topgolf at Page Road and I-40 allowing extended outdoor recreational lighting hours (up to 3:00 a.m. Sun–Thu and 5:00 a.m. Fri–Sat) in industrial zoning districts via a quasi-judicial Minor Special Use Permit—commissioners questioned lighting glare, neighborhood notice, public interest, and service-worker wages before adopting both the consistency statement (5-0) and the ordinance amendment (5-0). The meeting concluded with appointments across six boards and commissions and a brief manager update awaiting Durham Public Schools' revised capital cash-flow plan.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting, announced the Youth Listening Project, new GoDurham high-frequency/night routes, March 3 primary election rules (no photo ID required), and county tax payment plans. Commissioners unanimously approved the November 4, 2019 work session and January 13, 2020 regular session minutes and noted directives follow-up for the February work session.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Welcomes: Public Health Director Rodney Jenkins and 91st Civil Affairs Battalion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board formally welcomed new Public Health Director Rodney Jenkins, who expressed pride in joining Durham County's 250+ public health professionals, and hosted Captain Juan Cruz and soldiers from Fort Bragg's 91st Civil Affairs Battalion studying local governance ahead of their deployment to West Africa.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 20-0019 through 20-0039)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's request, Marcia and Linda explained Item 20-0039, a resolution submitting Durham's birth-to-three and early-childhood workforce priorities to NACo's national policy agenda in alignment with the Pritzker grant ahead of a January 29 deadline. Commissioners unanimously approved consent items 20-0019 through 20-0039.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC19-0002 — Outdoor Lighting Applicability
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Pat Young and Senior Planner Carl Kolosna presented privately initiated text amendment TC19-0002 enabling recreational venues in Industrial, Industrial Light, and Industrial Park districts to operate outdoor lighting until 3:00 a.m. (Sun–Thu) and 5:00 a.m. (Fri–Sat) if granted a quasi-judicial Minor Special Use Permit by the Board of Adjustment with 600-foot neighbor notice. Applicant attorney Keith Burns confirmed the site is a proposed Topgolf facility at Page Road and I-40 requiring late-night outfield maintenance lighting; after Commissioners Carter and Howerton pressed Burns on paying $15/hour living wages and commissioners praised Planning Commission feedback, the board unanimously adopted the consistency statement and ordinance amendment.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and DPS Capital Cash-Flow Inquiry
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board appointed members to the Board of Health (Eric Ireland), Boxing and Wrestling Commission (Jonathan Leach), City-County Appearance Commission (Bettina/Latina Rogers), DOST (William Aiken and Reynolds Smith), Farmland Protection Advisory Board (Talmadge Layton), and Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (DeWarren Langley). Before adjourning, Manager Wendell Davis responded to a commissioner inquiry that staff was still awaiting Durham Public Schools' workable cash-flow version of its long-term facility master plan.

votes.item_title: Approval of November 4, 2019 Work Session and January 13, 2020 Regular Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Unanimously approved November 4, 2019 work session and January 13, 2020 regular session minutes.

votes.item_title: TC19-0002 Statement of Consistency (NCGS 153A-341) — Outdoor Lighting Applicability
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted statutory consistency statement for UDO text amendment TC19-0002.

votes.item_title: Adoption of UDO Text Amendment TC19-0002 — Article 7 Design Standards (Outdoor Lighting)
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted UDO Article 7 revisions permitting extended late-hour recreational lighting in industrial districts subject to Board of Adjustment Minor Special Use Permit approval.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-01-13 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 13, 2020 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners active, the Board began with a unanimous voice vote to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) on economic development incentives before reconvening at 7:00 PM. In open session, the Board unanimously approved the November 25 and December 9, 2019 minutes, presented ceremonial proclamations for Durham Tech's 35th Martin Luther King Jr. celebration, National Mentoring Month (Charles Hamilton Houston Foundation), and a County MLK resolution, and unanimously adopted the consent agenda (Items 19-0621 through 20-0028)—highlighting the 300 and 500 East Main Street parking/workforce-housing MOU and North Carolina's first county Early Childhood Action Plan. Following three separate public hearings with no public opposition, the Board unanimously approved non-emergency ambulance transport franchises for Jan-Care, Life Star Emergency Services, and North State Medical Transport after each provider agreed to Commissioner Heidi Carter's request to extend non-discrimination practices to sexual orientation and gender identity. Finally, external auditors Scott Duda and Leanne presented an unmodified FY 2019 CAFR and Single Audit accepted by the LGC with no comments, noting one repeat compliance finding and a positive $5.6 million interest rate swap valuation.

agenda_items.title: Pre-Meeting Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4)) and Reconvening
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before the 7:00 PM public session, the Board voted unanimously by voice vote on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Heidi Carter to adjourn into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) regarding economic development incentives. Reconvening at 01:13:53, Chair Wendy Jacobs reported direction had been given to staff, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance.

agenda_items.title: Approval of November 25, 2019 and December 9, 2019 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Vice Chair James Hill seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, the Board unanimously approved the November 25 and December 9, 2019 regular session minutes by voice vote. A commissioner asked staff to follow up on outstanding directives in both sets of minutes, including regular updates on sentenced felons held in the jail.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations: Durham Tech MLK Anniversary, National Mentoring Month, and MLK Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners honored Durham Technical Community College's 35th anniversary celebrating Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.'s legacy, proclaimed National Mentoring Month alongside Charles Hamilton Houston Foundation Executive Director Warren Langley (highlighting its Young Men of Excellence program), and adopted/read a BOCC resolution honoring Dr. King ahead of community MLK events.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 19-0621 through 20-0028: 300/500 East Main MOU & Early Childhood Action Plan)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before approving Items 19-0621 through 20-0028, Chair Jacobs asked the County Manager to highlight the MOU with private partners for parking structures and workforce/affordable housing on the 300 and 500 East Main Street blocks, and invited Barker French and David to highlight Durham launching North Carolina's first county Early Childhood Action Plan. The consent agenda passed unanimously by voice vote on a motion by Commissioner Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Carter.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Non-Emergency Ambulance Franchise Renewal — Jan-Care
agenda_items.discussion_summary: EMS staff presented a multi-year non-emergency interfacility ambulance franchise renewal for Jan-Care, recommended by the EMS peer review committee. Commissioner Heidi Carter asked applicants to include sexual orientation and gender identity in non-discrimination practices (with County Attorney Lowell Siler agreeing to review statutory limits following HB 2/HB 142), and the Board approved the franchise unanimously after a public hearing with no speakers.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Non-Emergency Ambulance Franchise — Life Star Emergency Services, LLC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following confirmation from Life Star Emergency Services representative Mike Coates that the company would adjust its application/practice to include sexual orientation and gender identity protections, and with no public speakers during the hearing, the Board unanimously approved the franchise on a motion by Commissioner Carter seconded by Commissioner Howerton.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Non-Emergency Ambulance Franchise — North State Medical Transport
agenda_items.discussion_summary: North State Medical Transport representative Alex agreed to incorporate the expanded non-discrimination language, while County Attorney Lowell Siler noted he would check whether HB 142 sunsetting affected local non-discrimination ordinances. With no public speakers, the Board unanimously approved the franchise on a motion by Commissioner Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Howerton.

agenda_items.title: Presentation of FY 2019 Annual Financial Audit (CAFR) and Single Audit & Compliance Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance staff and auditors Scott Duda and Leanne presented the FY 2019 CAFR and Single Audit, submitted ahead of the December 1 extended deadline and accepted by the Local Government Commission with no comments. Auditors noted one repeat case-file compliance finding from early in the fiscal year and reported a $5.6 million positive June 30 valuation on the County's interest rate swap (generating over $1.7 million annually) before the Board adjourned unanimously.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2020-01-06 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 6, 2020 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board opened with an emergency update on the McDougall Terrace evacuation—commending DSS, EMS, Public Health, and the County Manager for coordinating with the City, Durham Housing Authority, and Durham Public Schools—and heard public comments urging Durham County as an RDU property co-owner to file an amicus brief and pass a resolution opposing the Wake Stone quarry lease and 8.3-mile fence on the Odd Fellows tract. Later in the session, partners presented a 12–18 month Early Childhood Action Plan proposal led by East Durham Children's Initiative (EDCI) with shared private-public investment, and commissioners endorsed developing a zero-waste reusable dishware policy for board meetings. The Board also reviewed staff parking, transportation demand management (TDM), and the sizing of the 500 East Main Street parking deck: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow urged early budget-cycle action on employee parking fees and GoTriangle-recommended transit incentives, while Vice Chair James Hill supported transit incentives but cautioned that single-parent schedules and current transit service gaps must be considered before closing with staff directives and unanimous adjournment.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, McDougall Terrace Evacuation Update, and Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the January 6, 2020 Work Session, praised DSS, EMS, Public Health, and the County Manager for assisting McDougall Terrace residents alongside the City, Durham Housing Authority, and DPS, and asked Emergency Management Director Jim Groves about state coordination and mandatory evacuation criteria. Citizen speakers including an Umstead/RDU speaker and Umstead Coalition Chair Jean Spooner urged the County to file an amicus brief and pass a resolution opposing the Wake Stone quarry and 8.3-mile barbed-wire fence on RDU's Odd Fellows tract, followed by John Tarantino on his campaign and George Roberson requesting legal review regarding the Confederate monument and the 13th Amendment.

agenda_items.title: Early Childhood Action Plan Proposal (East Durham Children's Initiative)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion, presenters briefed commissioners on a 12-to-18 month Early Childhood Action Plan led by East Durham Children's Initiative (EDCI) and aligned with the ACEs task force. Speakers explained that alongside a county funding request, EDCI would invest its own resources to attract philanthropic partners for implementation.

agenda_items.title: Zero-Waste Reusable Dishware Policy for County Board Meetings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented cost estimates for reusable plates, cups, and utensils for board meetings and new library facilities. Commissioners expressed strong support for modeling waste reduction at board meetings immediately, noting no formal action vote was scheduled at the work session.

agenda_items.title: Staff Parking, TDM Plan, 500 East Main Parking Deck Sizing, and Treyburn Transit Pilot
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow urged bringing parking and Transportation Demand Management (TDM) options into the upcoming budget cycle well ahead of the summer decision on sizing the 500 East Main Street parking deck, citing City parking fees, lower single-occupancy vehicle rates, and GoTriangle's recommendation to pay employees to use transit. Another member stressed $30,000+ per-space deck costs and filling the transportation position, while Vice Chair James Hill supported transit incentives while noting single-parent childcare duties and current transit service limitations; Chair Jacobs closed by summarizing directives on TDM, the 500 deck, and a holistic Treyburn pilot before unanimous adjournment.
