meetings.title: Durham County BOCC December 9, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the December 9, 2019 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners, with all five commissioners present. The board unanimously approved the October 28 and November 12, 2019 minutes (5-0), honored Southern High School football players for organizing the 'Guns Down, Lives Up' anti-gun-violence rally, and heard a presentation from the Eno River Association's new executive director. After pulling consent item 19-0608 ($1.9 million to design a 780-space downtown parking deck) due to a resident's climate-related objection, the board unanimously approved both the remainder of the consent agenda (5-0) and item 19-0608 (5-0), emphasizing the deck's mixed-use integration with affordable housing, commercial space, and a daycare facility. Following a public hearing, the board also unanimously approved a $950,000 economic development incentive for Q2 Solutions (5-0), expected to create 749 jobs and $84.2 million in investment, before adjourning to a closed session on pending litigation (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and North Carolina Solar Schools Initiative
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Announcements covered the DCHC MPO regional plan to reduce single-occupancy vehicles, the Hub Pop-Up youth resource event, the Durham Holiday Parade, open enrollment at healthcare.gov, and the launch of the North Carolina Solar Schools Initiative by 34 elected officials partnering with Duke Energy to install no-cost solar on public schools.

agenda_items.title: Approval of October 28, 2019 and November 12, 2019 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved approval of the October 28 and November 12, 2019 meeting minutes and commended the clerk's office on the improved formatting. Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded the commendation and motion, which passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Eno River Association Calendar, 'Guns Down, Lives Up' Resolution, and Youth Safety
agenda_items.discussion_summary: New Eno River Association Executive Director Jessica Sheffield presented the organization's annual calendar. Vice Chair James Hill read a resolution honoring Southern High School football team members and Durham Athletes United Against Gun Violence for organizing the November 'Guns Down, Lives Up' rally, followed by discussion of Durham youth violence/bullying statistics and a request for Congress to revoke the Medicaid Inmate Exclusion Policy.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 19-0560 through 19-0618, excluding 19-0608)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed a $1.2 million pay-as-you-go interfund reimbursement resolution, state 'Raise the Age' juvenile crime prevention allocations ($4.2 million in FY 2019-20 and $6.6 million in FY 2020-21), and two conservation easements. The board unanimously approved items 19-0560 through 19-0618 with item 19-0608 pulled for public comment.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 19-0608: $1.9M Design Appropriation for 780-Space Downtown Parking Deck
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Nick Doty objected to appropriating $1.9 million to design a $22 million, 780-space downtown parking deck on public land, arguing it subsidizes gasoline vehicles in a transit-rich area during a climate crisis. Commissioners and staff noted the site is part of a mixed-use 300 block plan incorporating affordable housing, commercial space, a daycare facility, library overflow, and shared employee/resident parking, before unanimously approving the item.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: $950,000 Economic Development Incentive for Q2 Solutions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Officer Andy Miracle presented a $950,000 incentive request for Q2 Solutions (a joint venture of IQVIA and Quest Diagnostics) to establish a clinical trial lab facility at 2400 Ellis Drive in RTP, creating 749 jobs (all meeting the county Living Wage Policy) and $84.2 million in investment over seven years. Following public hearing remarks from Chamber representative Brian Fox and company attorney David Eford, commissioners urged staff to build a biotech workforce continuum with Durham Public Schools and Durham Tech and unanimously approved the incentive.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Rodriguez v. Michael Andrews et al.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to adjourn into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with counsel regarding Rodriguez v. Michael Andrews et al. (Case No. 18-CVS-12). Upon returning at 02:12:07, Chair Jacobs reported that direction was given to staff and the board adjourned.

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Minutes for the October 28, 2019 and November 12, 2019 meetings were approved along with a commendation of the clerk's office for improved formatting.

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2019-12-02 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 2, 2019 Work Session, the Board of County Commissioners opened its annual organizational proceedings by unanimously re-electing Wendy Jacobs as Chair and James Hill as Vice Chair by 5-0 voice votes, followed by unanimous 5-0 approval of the annual public official bonds. During citizen comments, resident Lee Mortimer disputed a four-year-old $200 EMS ambulance debt-collection notice due to a vendor transition and lack of an appeal process, while two community speakers criticized the Bull City United program (Item 19-0605) for failing to hire former offenders with street credibility. Later in the work session, the Board reviewed Durham Pre-K utilization at Whitted School ($1.5 million base plus local per-child supplementation) and pushed staff to refine the scope of work before authorizing a $100,000 Durham County Early Childhood Action Plan, requested the complete county-wide classification and compensation pay-band results during directives review, and voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and appoint Daniel Edwards and Fran Kale Scott to the Alcohol and Beverage Control (ABC) Board.

agenda_items.title: Annual Election of Chair and Vice Chair and Chair's Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Conducted by the Clerk, the Board unanimously elected Wendy Jacobs as Chair by voice vote. Heidi Carter then nominated James Hill for Vice Chair, seconded by Brenda A. Howerton, and the nomination passed unanimously 5-0. Chair Jacobs reflected on the Board's three years together—highlighting Ellen W. Reckhow's 31 years of community service, Durham Pre-K, and the 300 and 500 East Main Street mixed-use projects.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Public Official Bonds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In accordance with the statutory requirement to approve public official bonds on the first Monday of December each year for recording with the Register of Deeds and safekeeping by the Clerk of Superior Court, Ellen W. Reckhow moved approval, seconded by Heidi Carter. The motion carried unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comment Period: EMS Billing Appeal & Bull City United (Item 19-0605)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Lee Mortimer described receiving a debt-collection notice for a $200 patient balance from a June 2015 EMS ambulance transport that surfaced during a third-party billing vendor transition, prompting Heidi Carter to ask the County Attorney when the Board has authority to hear citizen appeals. Two subsequent speakers, including Rafique Zayedi, criticized Bull City United (Item 19-0605) as ineffective and urged the County and City to hire ex-offenders with lived street experience rather than operating what they described as a giveaway program.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs asked the County Manager to walk through the lengthy consent agenda item by item. The middle portion of the consent review and mid-meeting items is omitted in the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Durham Pre-K Update and Proposed Early Childhood Action Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported that Whitted School is fully subscribed—combining six local pre-K classrooms, two federal exceptional children classrooms, and $1.5 million in direct DPS funding supplemented to reach $1,250 per child per month—and noted an upcoming child-level evaluation RFP. Staff also proposed spending up to $100,000 ($50,000 in the current year and $50,000 in FY2021) to develop a Durham County Early Childhood Action Plan, but commissioners requested a clearer scope of work and definition of the Early Childhood Systems Coordinator role before returning in January.

agenda_items.title: BOCC Directives Review: Classification and Compensation Plan Data
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During the directives review, commissioners noted that while the Board had previously received salary survey results and proposed pay bands for executive-level employees, it had still not received the complete classification and compensation pay-band comparisons across all general employee classifications requested during budget season. Staff agreed to review prior minutes and compile the full data.

agenda_items.title: Suspension of Rules and ABC Board Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by James Hill, the Board voted unanimously to suspend the rules in order to vote on appointments to the Alcohol and Beverage Control (ABC) Board. Following ballot voting, the Clerk announced that the Board selected Daniel Edwards and Fran Kale Scott for the two seats.

votes.notes: Conducted by the Clerk; nominator not identified by name in the transcript digest, and no nays were cast.
votes.discussion_detail: Nomination of Wendy Jacobs to serve as Chair of the Board of County Commissioners for the upcoming year.

votes.item_title: Election of James Hill as Board Vice Chair
votes.notes: All five seated commissioners were present at the organizational session.
votes.discussion_detail: Heidi Carter nominated James Hill for Vice Chair, seconded by Brenda A. Howerton, and Chair Jacobs announced the vote was unanimous.

votes.item_title: Approval of Annual Public Official Bonds
votes.notes: Chair Jacobs announced the bonds were unanimously approved.
votes.discussion_detail: Statutory annual approval of public official bonds on the first Monday of December for recording with the Register of Deeds and safekeeping by the Clerk of Superior Court.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend the Rules for ABC Board Appointments
votes.notes: Transcript records unanimous approval.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to suspend work session rules so the Board could vote on appointments to the Alcohol and Beverage Control Board.

votes.item_title: Appointments of Daniel Edwards and Fran Kale Scott to the ABC Board

votes.discussion_detail: Following suspension of the rules, commissioners cast written/recorded selections for two ABC Board seats; the Clerk reported that the Board selected Daniel Edwards and Fran Kale Scott.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC November 25, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the November 25, 2019 regular session, with Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton excused absent (4-0) and four commissioners present. The board approved the October 7 work session minutes (4-0) and adopted a consent agenda (4-0) that included $6.5 million in limited obligation bonds capital funding for Durham Public Schools deferred maintenance and a $145 million installment financing and refunding package yielding roughly $5 million in net present value savings. During the public hearing on UDO Text Amendment TC190001 (Omnibus Changes 13), neighbors raised urgent complaints about non-compliant fill sites, concrete debris, and DOT diamond-grinding dumping near Falls Lake. An initial combined motion by Ellen W. Reckhow (seconded by Heidi Carter) to approve the proposed regulations along with monitoring and enforcement recommendations passed 3-1, with Ellen W. Reckhow and Heidi Carter voting aye and one of the remaining two present commissioners (Wendy Jacobs or James Hill, not identified by name in the audio transcript) voting nay; the board then unanimously passed the required statutory consistency statement (4-0) and adopted the UDO text amendment with a task force directive to the Environmental Affairs Board and Soil and Water Conservation Board (4-0) before entering closed session (4-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excused Absence for Commissioner Howerton, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting, read the public charge, and removed closed session adjustments before the board voted 4-0 to excuse Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's absence. Announcements highlighted the Durham Homicide and Victims of Violent Death Memorial Quilt, a Durham Local Reentry Council simulation, community anti-violence collaboration (Project Build and Bull City United), and public comment on single-occupancy vehicle reduction.

agenda_items.title: Approval of October 7, 2019 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved approval of the October 7, 2019 work session minutes and praised staff for thorough documentation of a long, complex session. Vice Chair James Hill seconded, and the motion passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: National Radon Action Month and Refugee Welcome Letters
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board proclaimed National Radon Action Month 2019 with state program director Phillip Gibson, highlighting EPA grant participation and radon's role as a leading cause of lung cancer in non-smokers. Commissioners also discussed letters affirming Durham County as a welcoming community for refugees alongside the City of Durham.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 19-0535 through 19-0574): DPS Capital Funding & $145M Financing/Refunding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter questioned item 19-0535 ($6.5 million in limited obligation bonds for Durham Public Schools deferred maintenance) and item 19-0574 (authorizing a $145 million installment financing amendment including $10.029 million for Administration One renovations, EMS Station 1 draw takeout, and a taxable refunding projected to save $5 million net present value). disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the pending TC190001 regulations now (matching the City) while commissioning a task force with the Soil and Water Conservation Board, Environmental Affairs Board, and NC State to bring back enforcement and legislative amendments.

Reckhow and Heidi Carter moving/seconding in favor, and one unidentified present member between Wendy Jacobs and James Hill opposed); when prompted for formal statutory votes, the board unanimously approved both the consistency statement (4-0) and the ordinance with the task force directive (4-0).

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC November 12, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the Tuesday, November 12, 2019 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners, shifted from Monday due to Veterans Day, with all five commissioners present. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow took a point of personal privilege to reflect on her 31 years of service on the board, and Commissioner Heidi Carter introduced a joint local-official letter urging Duke Energy to deploy no-upfront-cost solar plus battery storage on North Carolina public schools. The board received a $10,000 Duke Energy donation for City-County Emergency Management, accepted the second installment of a $1.2 million contribution from the Durham Library Foundation for the new main library, and adopted resolutions supporting Durham becoming a Medicaid Healthy Opportunities Community and urging the General Assembly to end the FY 2019-2020 state budget impasse with a 5% public school employee raise and Medicaid expansion. Formally, the board unanimously approved the October 14 minutes (5-0), the consent agenda items 19-0488 through 19-0556 including the library item (5-0), and closed session entry under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)-(4) (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Ellen W. Reckhow 31-Year Service Reflection
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the Tuesday session (rescheduled for Veterans Day) and shared announcements on the 300/500 East Main Street developer open house and a vaping/smoking public health forum. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow took a point of personal privilege reflecting on 31 years on the board and thanking voters across 24 primary and general elections, and Commissioner Heidi Carter circulated a clean-energy letter urging Duke Energy to partner on no-upfront-cost solar plus battery storage at public schools.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Duke Energy Donation, National Adoption Month, Healthy Opportunities, and State Budget Impasse Resolutions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board recognized a $10,000 Duke Energy donation to Emergency Management and proclaimed November 2019 as National Adoption Awareness Month (noting 166 adoptions since January 2014). Commissioners also presented a resolution supporting Durham's six-county Medicaid Healthy Opportunities social determinants of health RFP and a resolution urging the North Carolina General Assembly to resolve the 2019-2020 budget impasse, enact a 5% raise for public school employees and retirees, and expand Medicaid.

agenda_items.title: Durham Library Foundation $1.2 Million Contribution Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Library Foundation President Annie Cravar presented the second installment of contributions totaling $1.2 million ($800,000 committed in June plus $400,000 raised over the past year) for enhancements to the new main library. Commissioners expressed gratitude and incorporated the library business item into the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Approval of October 14, 2019 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs noted the minutes had been briefly overlooked after ceremonial items. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved approval of the October 14, 2019 regular session minutes, seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, and the motion passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 19-0488 through 19-0556, plus Library Item 19-0529)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board added library item 19-0529 to consent items 19-0488 through 19-0556 and unanimously approved the package (5-0). Chair Jacobs highlighted a conservation easement on a minority-owned farm, an added full-time nutrition educator for the DINE program in Durham Public Schools, and funding for the Formerly Incarcerated Transitions (FIT) health program.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Economic Development & Attorney-Client Privilege)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) for economic development incentive negotiations and N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client privilege. Upon reconvening at 02:30:41, Chair Jacobs acknowledged a staff binder on the DPS MOU data and the board adjourned.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2019-11-04 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 4, 2019 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board heard public comments criticizing Saturday outreach timing on the 300 and 500 East Main Street projects and opposing RDU Airport Authority's quarry lease on the Odd Fellows Tract. Staff reviewed consent agenda items (including DINE program recognition, Century Farm status for the Douglas Day farm, and wastewater plant BNR upgrades) and proposed a $69,000 midyear county match alongside the City of Durham and $77,000 in federal funds for street outreach to replace the transitioning Nehemiah Center. Following a presentation on transitional parking and Transportation Demand Management (TDM) for 300 and 500 East Main Street—where commissioners debated paid parking versus transit incentives—the Board unanimously voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and authorize staff to move forward with a seven-level, 780-space parking deck on the 300 block while returning with a parking assessment for the 500 block. Commissioners also discussed a resolution brought forward by Heidi Carter urging the North Carolina General Assembly to pass a state budget and expand Medicaid, deferring action to the upcoming regular session.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge and Citizen Comments: 300/500 East Main Outreach and RDU Quarry Opposition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs opened the work session with the public charge and citizen comments. James Chambers raised concerns about public outreach meetings for the 300 and 500 East Main Street parcels being scheduled on Saturday mornings when many residents cannot attend. Dr. Jean Spooner, Chair of the Umstead Coalition, urged the Board to adopt a resolution matching Raleigh City Council's September 17 statement opposing a rock quarry on the publicly owned Odd Fellows Tract near Umstead State Park.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (Items 488–556)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager walked through consent items 488 through 556. Commissioners asked about donor thank-you protocols for gifts such as a Duke Energy donation, praised the DINE nutrition program, clarified state Century Farm designation rules for the Douglas Day farm, and questioned engineering contract amendments for wastewater treatment plant BNR train resilience upgrades and annual sewer incident benchmarks.

agenda_items.title: Midyear Allocation for City-County Street Outreach Collaboration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presenters Drew and Hanalea outlined a low-barrier street outreach partnership with the City of Durham to bridge the gap left by the Nehemiah Center transition, requiring $69,000 each from the City and County for the remainder of FY2020 (paired with $77,000 in federal funds) and $250,000 annually thereafter under an Interlocal Agreement. Ellen W. Reckhow expressed support while asking staff to check whether Alliance Health could cover the $69,000 midyear share given the stalled state budget.

agenda_items.title: 300 and 500 East Main Street Parking Deck Design and TDM Strategies
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Consultants presented phased parking logistics requiring 300 remote spaces during construction and comparing a six-level versus seven-level deck on the 300 block, while commissioners debated whether employee Transportation Demand Management should use parking fees ('sticks') or transit subsidies and carpool incentives ('carrots'). The Board unanimously suspended the rules and voted 5-0 to authorize staff to proceed with a seven-level, 780-space parking deck on the 300 block and return with a further assessment of parking counts for the 500 block.

agenda_items.title: Directives Recap and Resolution Urging General Assembly Budget Passage and Medicaid Expansion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff confirmed three follow-up information requests from the first agenda item, and Heidi Carter introduced a resolution requested by the District Attorney urging the General Assembly to pass a state budget and supporting Medicaid expansion. Because the legislature was expected to return November 13 solely for redistricting and not reconvene on budget matters until January, commissioners agreed to verify with the DA whether the request remained active and consider it at the regular session.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend the Rules for 300 Block Parking Deck Authorization
votes.notes: Chair Jacobs announced the rules were suspended unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to suspend work session rules in order to vote immediately on authorizing the 300 East Main Street parking deck configuration.

votes.item_title: Authorization of 7-Level, 780-Space Parking Deck on 300 East Main Street and 500 Block Assessment
votes.notes: Approved unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion stated by Chair Jacobs authorizing staff to move forward with plans for a seven-level, 780-space parking deck on the 300 block and to return with an assessment regarding parking space counts for the 500 block.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC October 28, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the October 28, 2019 regular session, with Vice Chair James Hill excused absent (4-0) and four commissioners present. After approving the September 23 minutes (4-0), recognizing Bull City United outreach worker Keisha Gray and the Made in Durham work-based learning campaign, and passing single-item consent agenda 19-0500 (4-0), the board conducted four consecutive land-use public hearings. Commissioners unanimously approved zoning map change Z1900020 for Leesville Road Boat and RV Storage with a proffered Section 9.7 screening standard (4-0 across consistency and ordinance votes) and adopted UDO Text Amendment TC190003 updating FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Maps (4-0 across both votes). Following extensive discussion of stormwater and environmental impacts on the county's previously referred Expanding Housing Choices text amendment (TC180007), the board unanimously adopted the consistency statement (4-0), the UDO amendment (4-0), and a county substitute monitoring resolution requiring a three-year review (4-0), and likewise approved Tree Coverage and Landscaping UDO amendment TC180005 (4-0 across both votes) before making advisory board appointments.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Minutes, and Excused Absence for Vice Chair Hill
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting, announced the Durham County Recycles app, the Homicide Memorial Quilt display at Human Services, and Healthcare.gov open enrollment. The board approved the September 23, 2019 regular session minutes (4-0), granted an excused absence to Vice Chair James Hill (4-0), and confirmed with the County Manager that the employee compensation study implementation would be retroactive.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions: Bull City United Award and Made in Durham Work-Based Learning Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board honored Bull City United violence interruption worker Keisha Gray for winning the 2019 Willis Young Memorial Award and reviewed a video and resolution supporting the Made in Durham work-based learning collaborative campaign.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Item 19-0500
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the single-item consent agenda (19-0500) on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and second by Commissioner Heidi Carter.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change Z1900020 (Leesville Road Boat & RV Storage)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented applicant Warren Mitchell's request to rezone nearly 14 acres at 4615 Leesville Road from Rural Residential (RR) to Commercial General with a text-only development plan (CG-D) limited to boat and RV storage. After Commissioner Reckhow requested enforceable screening guarantees, the applicant proffered compliance with UDO Section 9.7 perimeter screening, and the board unanimously approved the consistency statement and rezoning ordinance (4-0 each).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC190003 (FEMA FIRM Updates)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock and Ryan Eaves presented TC190003 to incorporate outstanding FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map panels resolved after neighboring-county challenges prior to the December 6, 2019 deadline required for National Flood Insurance Program eligibility. Commissioners discussed 1% future-conditions floodplain mapping and watershed education before unanimously adopting the consistency statement and ordinance (4-0 each).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC180007 (Expanding Housing Choices, County Jurisdiction)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Pat Young reintroduced Expanding Housing Choices (TC180007) for the county jurisdiction following the board's September 23 referral back to staff. Commissioners examined how stormwater/environmental impacts from accessory dwelling units and small-lot infill would be tracked alongside tree planting, ribbon driveways, and the upcoming affordable housing bond, then unanimously adopted the consistency statement (4-0), ordinance (4-0), and a substitute metrics and three-year review resolution (4-0).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC180005 (Tree Coverage and Landscaping)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock presented TC180005 to prioritize preservation of existing trees over replacement, widen buffers where mass grading is used, and increase urban-tier tree coverage, while deferring broad suburban right-of-way street tree mandates pending a joint pilot with TreesDurham. meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2019-10-07 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 7, 2019 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, citizens addressed dental care and follow-up at Lincoln Community Health Center as well as chronic HVAC failures and ADA accessibility barriers at Durham School of the Arts ahead of the 2020 school bond. Commissioners reviewed FY2019 sales tax rollover figures (clarifying that Article 39 general fund sales tax came in near 92% of budget while dedicated capital Article 40 over-realized), adjusted the 2020 meeting calendar around the March 3 primary election, and received an update on the 300 and 500 East Main Street redevelopment goals—including housing affordable at 80% AMI and below, selection of outside legal counsel Anthony Fox of Parker Poe, and November 'Meet the Developer' public sessions. During policy discussions, commissioners pressed economic development staff to disclose negotiated company community-benefit commitments publicly in hearing memos and ads under Section 6 and launch a public incentives tracking website, reviewed county-city funding splits ($1.3 million county, $681,000 city) for the Whitted School interlocal agreement, agreed to bring back revised Expanding Housing Choice resolution language for a vote, and voted unanimously 5-0 to enter closed session on economic development incentives and attorney-client privilege.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge and Citizen Comments: Healthcare Quality and Durham School of the Arts Bond Needs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Elois Johnson raised concerns about dental care supplies at Lincoln Community Health Center and unanswered public health follow-up questions. Betsy Steiclether, chair of the 2020 bond committee for the Durham School of the Arts PTSA, detailed weekly air conditioning failures in the Academy Building, loud window units disrupting instruction, second-floor stair-only access, and cracked sidewalks outside Weaver Auditorium, urging support for the 2020 school bond. A third speaker praised a school board member's responsiveness to Durham Public Schools families.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Sales Tax Rollover Review and 2020 Board Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reviewing Item 436, commissioners questioned why sales tax appeared over-realized; budget staff explained that dedicated capital Article 40 exceeded budget while Article 42 under-collected and general-fund Article 39 ended around 92% of budget. Commissioners also adjusted the draft 2020 meeting calendar to keep the March 2 work session despite conference conflicts with the March 3 primary, trim June 2 budget work session by 30 minutes for a Durham leadership meeting, and add a second session for June elected/appointed official evaluations.

agenda_items.title: 300 and 500 East Main Street Redevelopment Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff outlined four objectives for 300 and 500 East Main Street: multimodal connectivity near future light rail, downtown affordable housing at or below 80% AMI, ground-floor commercial uses, and efficient public-private leverage. Staff noted the County Attorney selected Anthony Fox of Parker Poe as project counsel and announced Meet the Developer public outreach sessions on November 2 at Holton Career and Resource Center and November 12 at the Human Services Facility.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Policy Disclosure and Tracking Website
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners voiced concern that specific company commitments on internships and workforce engagement discussed in closed session are not always placed on the public record at the time of the public hearing. Chair Jacobs and commissioners directed staff to amend Section 6 of the economic development policy so negotiated community benefits are enumerated in public hearing ads and memos, and asked when the public-facing incentive tracking website would go live.

agenda_items.title: Whitted School Interlocal Agreement and Expanding Housing Choice Resolution Next Steps
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners sought clarification on the agenda action form for the Whitted School interlocal agreement showing $1.3 million from the County and $681,000 from the City. They then confirmed with staff Drew that the Expanding Housing Choice resolution (distinct from the text amendment itself) would return to the Board for both discussion and a formal vote once commissioners finalized their proposed resolution language.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by James Hill, the Board voted unanimously 5-0 to enter closed session to discuss tentative economic development incentives and negotiations and to consult with the County Attorney. Returning at 04:48:54, Chair Jacobs reported direction was given to staff before adjourning.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2019-09-23 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 23, 2019 session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board welcomed a 30-member Neighborhood College cohort and conducted an in-depth review of the general-employee Classification and Compensation Study with MAG consultants Carolyn Long and Russell Campbell. Consultants explained their 14-jurisdiction market benchmark methodology and told commissioners Durham County's recruitment and retention issues—such as social worker turnover—stemmed more from pay administration and lacking cost-of-living adjustments than pay structure, while commissioners pressed for full pay-band tables and clarity on when budgeted October raises would be implemented. Later in the meeting, commissioners divided over the Expanding Housing Choice (EHC) zoning text amendment for unincorporated county areas following Raleigh/Durham City Council's September 3 adoption: supporters emphasized legalizing modest-income housing options near jobs and transit, whereas Ellen W. Reckhow objected to adopting the post-March draft as-is (citing the 25-foot vs. 35-foot small-lot change) and other commissioners raised equity, displacement, and joint city-county coordination concerns. On a motion by Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by Brenda A. Howerton, the Board voted 4-1 by voice vote to refer the EHC item back to administration for re-advertisement—with Ellen W. Reckhow and Brenda A. Howerton recorded in the Aye majority alongside two unnamed Aye commissioners and one unnamed commissioner voting Nay.

agenda_items.title: Welcome and Recognition of Neighborhood College Cohort
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the special session by welcoming members of the 30-person Neighborhood College cohort (selected from roughly 100 applicants) and inviting participants to introduce themselves and share their neighborhoods. She noted that Heidi Carter and Mayor Schewel had also attended the cohort's opening night.

agenda_items.title: Classification and Compensation Study Review with MAG Consultants
agenda_items.discussion_summary: MAG consultants Carolyn Long and Russell Campbell reviewed their 14-jurisdiction benchmark survey methodology following Phase 1 public safety implementation (2.5%). Consultants advised that Durham County's retention challenges—such as social worker turnover—were driven by pay administration lagging behind peers like Wake County and Raleigh (which offered 3% COLAs and up to 6.5% pay-for-performance) and recommended a 2.7%–3% market adjustment, while Brenda A. Howerton and other commissioners demanded complete pay-band comparisons and a firm date for budgeted October increases.

agenda_items.title: Expanding Housing Choice (EHC) Text Amendment and Referral Back to Administration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners debated the Expanding Housing Choice ordinance for unincorporated Durham County after the City Council's September 3 adoption (scheduled to take effect October 1). Supporters argued EHC enables modest-income market-rate housing in the urban tier near transit and jobs, whereas Ellen W. Reckhow opposed adopting it as-is—citing neighborhood support for the March draft's 35-foot small-lot standard before later edits—and commissioners sought to amend the monitoring resolution and discuss concerns at the October 2 JCCPC meeting; on a motion by Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by Brenda A. Howerton, the Board voted 4-1 to refer the item back to administration.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments Scheduling
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Immediately after the EHC referral vote, Chair Jacobs asked whether boards and commissions appointments could be delayed given the late hour. The Clerk indicated the appointments would be straightforward to complete.

votes.item_title: Motion to Refer Expanding Housing Choice (EHC) Item Back to Administration
votes.notes: Chair Jacobs announced 'four in favor, one opposed' on a voice vote; Ellen W. Reckhow (mover) and Brenda A. Howerton (seconder) are confirmed Ayes in the transcript, while the two additional Aye commissioners and single Nay commissioner (among Wendy Jacobs, James Hill, and Heidi Carter) were not identified by name in the voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: After closing the public hearing and debating whether to adopt EHC, amend the accompanying monitoring resolution, or request a City implementation delay for JCCPC review, Ellen W. Reckhow moved to refer the item back to the administration (requiring 10–25 days re-advertisement before rescheduling), seconded by Brenda A. Howerton.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2019-09-23 7:00 PM - Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Immediate Adoption vs. Referral Back to Administration of Expanding Housing Choice (EHC)
disagreements.summary: Following City Council's September 3 adoption of Expanding Housing Choice, commissioners split 4-1 over whether to move forward with the unincorporated-area EHC text amendment or refer it back to administration for further review, JCCPC consultation, and re-advertisement.
disagreements.side_a_position: Refer EHC back to administration rather than adopting as-is, pending equity/displacement safeguards, JCCPC discussion, and resolution amendments.
side_a_arguments: Ellen W. Reckhow objected to post-March changes that reversed the neighborhood-supported 35-foot small-lot standard back toward narrower lots without sufficient public awareness.
Commissioners raised displacement and equity concerns raised by community coalitions and wanted the monitoring resolution strengthened and aligned with the Engage Durham comprehensive plan process.
A majority favored seeking City-County dialogue at the October 2 Joint City-County Planning Committee meeting and re-advertising the item after administrative referral.
disagreements.side_b_position: Support EHC zoning reforms without referring the item back to administration.
side_b_arguments: Allowing smaller lots and additional housing types in the urban tier makes market-rate housing accessible to modest-income households near jobs, transit, and existing infrastructure.
Zoning reforms are an essential long-term component of addressing Durham's housing affordability crisis.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-1 by voice vote to refer the EHC item back to administration (Ellen W. Reckhow moved, Brenda A. Howerton seconded; the two other Aye voters and the single Nay voter were not named in the transcript).

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2019-09-09 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 9, 2019 Regular Session, Vice Chair James Hill presided with Brenda A. Howerton and Heidi Carter present while Chair Wendy Jacobs and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow had excused absences to attend a transportation conference in Vancouver, Canada. The three-member Board unanimously approved the June 11 and August 12 meeting minutes (3-0), recognized Emergency Management preparedness following Hurricane Dorian and the downtown gas explosion, issued a Durham Senior Hunger Awareness Week proclamation highlighting food insecurity among 12,600 local seniors, and approved the consent agenda (3-0), including Item 19-0439 honoring a community leader's legacy. Following a public hearing with remarks from Greater Durham Chamber of Commerce representative Brian Fox and Policygenius Head of Finance Kevin Fusick, the Board voted 3-0 on a motion by Heidi Carter and second by Brenda A. Howerton to approve a performance-based $188,500 economic development incentive over seven years for Policygenius Inc.'s second headquarters (projected to invest $6 million and create 377 jobs averaging $72,000), before hearing one public comment on the public art resolution and adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Absence Notice, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill opened the meeting, read the public charge and September National Recovery Month and Durham 150 announcements, and noted that Chair Wendy Jacobs and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow were attending a transportation conference in Vancouver, Canada. The three commissioners present approved the June 11 budget work session and August 12 regular session minutes unanimously 3-0.

agenda_items.title: Emergency Management Update and Durham Senior Hunger Awareness Week Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Emergency Management staff highlighted recent responses to hurricanes including Hurricane Dorian, winter snow events, and the downtown Durham gas explosion. The Board then presented a proclamation for Durham Senior Hunger Awareness Week 2019, noting that North Carolina ranks second worst nationally and roughly 12,600 Durham County residents age 60 and older are at risk of food insecurity.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Including Item 19-0439)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before moving approval, a commissioner highlighted consent Item 19-0439 honoring a prominent community leader's life and legacy and noting Smithsonian recognition. The Board approved the entire consent agenda unanimously 3-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Incentive Award to Policygenius Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic development staff Andy Miracle presented a $188,500 local incentive spread over seven years—serving as the local match for an approximately $5 million state JDIG grant—for Policygenius Inc. to establish its second headquarters, invest $6 million, and create 377 jobs averaging $72,000 (entry-level starting at $49,000). Brian Fox of the Chamber/Downtown Durham Inc. and Policygenius Head of Finance Kevin Fusick spoke in support, highlighting workforce training, DPS CTE internships, and entry-level opportunities; Heidi Carter moved approval contingent on contract performance criteria, seconded by Brenda A. Howerton, passing 3-0.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comment on Public Art Program Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen General Bernstein spoke regarding the public art program resolution and First Amendment concerns. Immediately following his remarks, the Board voted to adjourn.

votes.item_title: Approval of June 11 Budget Work Session and August 12 Regular Session Minutes
votes.notes: Wendy Jacobs and Ellen W. Reckhow were absent (excused in Vancouver, Canada); mover and seconder were not identified by name in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion and second among the three commissioners present to accept the June 11, 2019 budget work session minutes and August 12, 2019 regular session minutes.

votes.item_title: Allocation of $188,500 Economic Development Incentive to Policygenius Inc.
votes.notes: Wendy Jacobs and Ellen W. Reckhow were absent; passed unanimously among the three present commissioners.
votes.discussion_detail: Following a public hearing, Heidi Carter moved to accept the County Manager's recommendation to allocate $188,500 over seven years to Policygenius Inc., contingent upon meeting performance criteria for 377 jobs and $6 million capital investment laid out in the contract, seconded by Brenda A. Howerton.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2019-09-03 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 3, 2019 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board noted upcoming September 9 excused absences for Jacobs and Ellen W. Reckhow and reviewed consent agenda items including Youth Home capital ($19 million) and Raise the Age operating negotiations with the N.C. Department of Public Safety stalled by the state budget impasse, Moseley design work, solar-ready roof standards for new facilities and the Judicial Annex, an open-space planning grant, and a $125,000 appropriation cover-memo clarification. Later in the work session, commissioners reviewed the draft Public Art Program resolution and work plan—requesting clearer language confirming Board policy-approval authority, ongoing board reporting, and deaccessioning procedures ahead of paired City Council action—and reported out of an earlier 1:21 PM closed session that direction had been given to staff. The Board then suspended the rules (5-0) on a motion by Heidi Carter and second by James Hill and voted unanimously 5-0 to approve an involuntary commitment transportation agreement resolution (with commissioners noting the LME's planned CIT mental-health training for transport staff), before reviewing outstanding BOCC directives and adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge, September 9 Absence Notice, and Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs noted that she and Ellen W. Reckhow would have excused absences on September 9 for a conference, leaving Vice Chair James Hill to preside. Reviewing the consent agenda, staff briefed the Board on Youth Home funding ($19 million capital request and Raise the Age operating templates modeled on Madison County stalled by the state budget impasse), Moseley's youth home design contract, solar-ready roof construction including the Judicial Annex, an open space planning grant, and clarifying a $125,000 vs. $150,000 cover-memo figure.

agenda_items.title: Public Art Program Resolution and Work Plan Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the draft Public Art Program resolution and operational work plan, highlighting local Durham artists David Wilson and Stephen Hayes mentoring early-career artists and existing deaccessioning procedures. Commissioners requested explicit wording stating that the Board of County Commissioners approves Public Art Program policies and clarified ongoing reporting to the Board ahead of City Council's work session and September 16 adoption cycle.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Report-Out
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs noted she had omitted reporting out of the Board's earlier afternoon closed session (adjourned at 1:21 PM) and stated for the record that the Board adjourned from closed session and gave direction to staff.

agenda_items.title: Involuntary Commitment Transportation Agreement Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney staff presented an involuntary commitment transportation agreement resolution imposing minimal operational disruption while awaiting the LME's finalization of Crisis Intervention Team (CIT) training for transport personnel. On a motion by Heidi Carter, seconded by James Hill, the Board voted 5-0 to suspend the rules, and then unanimously 5-0 approved the resolution on Heidi Carter's motion after discussing past safety incidents when transporters lacked training.

agenda_items.title: BOCC Directives Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget staff member Drew reviewed pending and completed directives, including updates on the SNAP resolution, federal poverty guidelines resolution, Treburn transportation coordination with Brian Fox of the Chamber, NC Public Schools Day of Action, and gender-identity items discussed in closed session, plus follow-up correspondence with a constituent.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend the Rules for Involuntary Commitment Transportation Agreement
votes.notes: Chair Jacobs announced the rules were suspended unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion by Heidi Carter, seconded by James Hill, to suspend work session rules to act immediately on the involuntary commitment transportation agreement resolution.

votes.item_title: Approval of Resolution Regarding Involuntary Commitment Transportation Agreement
votes.notes: Seconder was not identified by name in the transcript digest; Chair Jacobs announced the resolution was unanimously approved.
votes.discussion_detail: Heidi Carter moved approval of the resolution regarding the involuntary commitment transportation agreement; commissioners discussed ensuring transport staff receive CIT mental-health training from the LME before voting unanimously in favor.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC August 26, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the August 26, 2019 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners with all five commissioners present. Following emotional remarks and a Project Build update addressing recent gun violence—including the fatal shooting of a nine-year-old boy—the board approved prior minutes (5-0) and proclaimed National Recovery Month 2019. Commissioners unanimously approved the unpulled consent agenda (5-0) and then approved pulled consent items 0396 ($12.6 million Snow Hill capital project amendment and $2.1 million design-build phase), 0406 (Chamber of Commerce contract), and 0407 (Downtown Durham Inc. contract) (5-0) after discussing gap tax billing, local workforce pipelines, MWBE participation, and downtown panhandling outreach. After a public hearing on item 19-0395, the board unanimously adopted the Compact Suburban Design District UDO text amendment, consistency statement, and future street network resolution for Patterson Place (5-0 across all three votes), heard a reproductive rights presentation from the Durham County Women's Commission, made board appointments, and entered closed session (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Gun Violence Remarks, and Project Build Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting and addressed recent shootings in Durham, including the fatal shooting of a nine-year-old boy and wounding of an eight-year-old child. Project Build staff described newly funded outreach workers, a six-week Phoenix conflict-resolution curriculum at Lakeview School, trauma support, and the Fatherhood of Durham initiative.

agenda_items.title: Approval of June 24, July 11, and August 5, 2019 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the June 24, July 11, and August 5, 2019 work session and regular session minutes on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and second by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Item: National Recovery Month 2019 Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Representatives from the Criminal Justice Resource Center (CJRC) and Durham's recovery community received a National Recovery Month 2019 proclamation highlighting fentanyl-driven overdose deaths, suicide rates, mental health treatment gaps, and stigma reduction.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda and Pulled Items 19-0396, 19-0400, 19-0406, and 19-0407
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved consent items 19-0382 through 19-0407 minus four pulled items (5-0), then reviewed the pulled items: the $12.6 million Snow Hill capital project ($2.1 million initial design-build contract), tax settlement report showing gap-billing impacts (0400), the Greater Durham Chamber contract (0406, focusing on Treyburn transit and local hiring pipelines), and the Downtown Durham Inc. contract (0407, noting a panhandling best-practices study). Commissioners then unanimously approved items 0396, 0406, and 0407 (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Compact Suburban Design District Text Amendment & Patterson Place (Item 19-0395)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Lisa Miller presented the form-based Compact Suburban Design District text amendment and Patterson Place future street network, incorporating affordable housing density bonuses, prohibited payday lending, New Hope Creek environmental buffers, and suspended sidewalks. Following discussion of transit frequency without light rail, Go Triangle height comments, and school/sewer capacity (Gethin lift station), the board unanimously approved the consistency statement, text amendment ordinance, and future street network resolution (5-0 each).

agenda_items.title: Durham County Women's Commission Presentation on Reproductive Healthcare & Maternal Mortality
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Women's Commission representatives Vivian Slade, Sarah Bausch, and Patty Black urged the board to pass a resolution affirming reproductive healthcare access and supporting federal legislation (the Women's Health Protection Act and EACH Act). Commissioners requested a draft resolution incorporating Black maternal mortality, volunteer doula access (MAAME), and county public health programs.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The clerk announced board appointments to the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee, Board of Adjustment, Appearance Commission, and Durham-Wake Research and Production Service District. The board then voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)-(4), returning at 03:45:14 to adjourn.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC August 12, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the August 12, 2019 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners with all five commissioners present. The board opened with a joint statement condemning recent mass shootings in Gilroy, El Paso, and Dayton as well as large-scale ICE raids, approved May and June meeting minutes (5-0), and signed onto the Paris Declaration on Fast-Track Cities to End the AIDS Epidemic alongside IAPAC leader Dr. Jose Zuniga and Ace Robinson. Commissioners also adopted a Purple Heart resolution, endorsed a resolution opposing proposed USDA restrictions on SNAP broad-based categorical eligibility, recognized Durham County IT's second-place national ranking in the 2019 Digital Counties Survey, and unanimously approved consent agenda items 19-0214 through 19-0368 (5-0). Following a public hearing, the board unanimously approved a $3 million economic development incentive for Merck's $650 million Durham plant expansion creating 391 new jobs (5-0) before adjourning to closed session (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Statement on Mass Shootings and ICE Raids, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting and delivered a board statement condemning mass shootings in Gilroy, El Paso, and Dayton and large-scale federal ICE arrests, followed by comments from commissioners on federal inaction and gun violence. The board also added a closed session to the agenda and shared announcements including City Hall Selfie Day and a local history exhibit at the Health Department.

agenda_items.title: Approval of May 21, May 29, and June 10, 2019 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter moved approval of the May 21 and May 29 budget work session minutes and June 10 regular session minutes, noting their detailed directives. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded, and the motion passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Fast-Track Cities Paris Declaration, Purple Heart, SNAP Eligibility Resolution, and Digital Counties Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County signed the Paris Declaration on Fast-Track Cities to End the AIDS Epidemic with Dr. Jose Zuniga and Ace Robinson, adopted a Purple Heart recognition resolution, and endorsed a resolution presented with DSS Director Ben Rose opposing federal USDA restrictions on SNAP broad-based categorical eligibility that threaten child nutrition. The board also introduced newly promoted staff and recognized IT Director Greg Marrow for tying for second place nationwide in the 2019 Digital Counties Survey.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 19-0214 through 19-0368)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a brief question on item 19-0365, the board unanimously approved consent items 19-0214 through 19-0368. Chair Jacobs highlighted a grant for a sensory-inclusive space at the main library and doubling county electric-vehicle charging stations.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: $3 Million Economic Development Incentive for Merck
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Director Andy Miracle presented a $3 million incentive for Merck's $650 million expansion of its Durham vaccine manufacturing plant, adding 391 new jobs averaging roughly $73,000 (including operations and support jobs starting at $61,000-$80,000 without advanced degree requirements). Following public hearing testimony from Greater Durham Chamber VP Brian Fox and commissioner inquiries regarding net job growth after 150 prior positions and workforce pipeline access for Durham residents, the board unanimously approved the $3 million award.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Attorney-Client Privilege and Criminal Investigation Reports)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(7) for attorney-client consultation and reports concerning investigations of alleged criminal misconduct. Upon returning at 02:35:52, Chair Jacobs reported direction was given to staff and the meeting adjourned.

votes.item_title: Approval of May 21, May 29, and June 10, 2019 Minutes
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the May 21 and May 29 budget work session minutes and June 10, 2019 regular session minutes.

votes.notes: Mover was not identified by name in the audio transcript; seconded by Vice Chair James Hill.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved $3M in economic development funds for Merck's $650M Durham facility expansion and 391 new jobs.

votes.item_title: Adjourn to Closed Session (Attorney-Client Privilege & Criminal Investigation Reports)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2019-08-05 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 5, 2019 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, citizen speakers advocated allowing solar panels on rooftops in the Moorhead Hill local historic district and urged commissioners to attend a September community forum addressing shootings and safety concerns around Franklin Village and Hooper Road. On the consent agenda, commissioners reviewed an inclusive sensory playroom at the library, connected EV charging stations (noting a new state law allowing cost recovery for electricity) and early-voting library parking impacts, and an addiction treatment contract reducing daily cost to $6 and expanding capacity from 40 to 80 slots. The Board then reviewed a joint City-County Fast-Track Cities HIV/AIDS resolution (adding Durham-specific housing and jail metrics) and updated ABC Board qualification and appointment descriptions, voted 5-0 on motions by Ellen W. Reckhow and James Hill to suspend the rules and delegate signing authority for an urgent $10 million FAA grant for RDU Runway/Taxiway B reconstruction, and voted 5-0 to enter closed session on attorney-client privilege matters including Rodriguez v. Michael Andrews et al. (18-CVS-3012) before returning and adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: Historic District Solar Rooftops and Community Safety
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A Moorhead Hill homeowner requested a resolution allowing solar rooftops and obstructive tree removal on contributing and non-contributing homes in local historic districts ahead of a Joint City-County Planning Committee presentation. A subsequent community speaker urged Brenda A. Howerton and James Hill to attend a September forum regarding shootings and neighborhood concerns at Franklin Village and Hooper Road.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review: Library Sensory Space, EV Charging, and Substance Use Treatment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and Sustainability Director Tobin discussed a library inclusive sensory room, grant-funded connected electric vehicle charging stations (noting a newly enacted state law allowing EV station owners to recover electricity costs), and Ellen W. Reckhow's concern over parking overflow at Southwest and North Regional Libraries during early voting. Commissioners also praised a new addiction treatment contract lowering per-day costs to $6 and doubling capacity from 40 to 80 individuals within budget.

agenda_items.title: Fast-Track Cities HIV/AIDS Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Gail Harris and commissioners reviewed the Fast-Track Cities HIV/AIDS resolution ahead of joint City-County action, noting that individuals with undetectable viral loads are not subject to communicable disease enforcement. Commissioners asked to add Durham-specific whereas clauses highlighting DSS's HOPWA housing program, jail HIV treatment, and budget-book performance measures.

agenda_items.title: ABC Board Description, Vacancy Qualifications, and Board Appointment Rules
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff member Maseo and Clerk Lowell presented a two-part profile for the ABC Board—a general description and a detailed recruitment advertisement listing desired business and financial skill sets—and confirmed with legal counsel whether designated skill-set slots could be used across the County's 43 boards and commissions alongside Board of Adjustment quasi-judicial standards.

agenda_items.title: Pritzker Children's Initiative Invitation and $10 Million FAA Grant Delegation for RDU
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A commissioner reported an email from NACo recommending Durham County for an invitation-only Pritzker Children's Initiative grant. County Manager staff then presented an urgent $10 million FAA grant for RDU Taxiway B / runway reconstruction requiring acceptance signatures from all four airport-owning governments; on motions by Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by James Hill, the Board voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and 5-0 to delegate signing authority.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) Attorney-Client Privilege)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deferring BOCC directives to August 12 due to Drew's absence, the Board voted 5-0 on a motion by Ellen W. Reckhow to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) regarding Rodriguez v. Michael Andrews et al. (Case No. 18-CVS-3012) and a related legal matter. Returning at 03:35:50, Chair Jacobs reported direction was given to staff and the Board adjourned.

votes.notes: Chair Jacobs announced the rules were suspended unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to suspend work session rules so the Board could immediately delegate signing authority for a $10 million FAA grant for RDU runway/Taxiway B reconstruction.

votes.notes: Chair Jacobs announced the motion was unanimously approved.
votes.discussion_detail: Delegation of signature authority on behalf of Durham County (as one of the four airport owners) to accept the $10 million FAA grant for RDU Taxiway B / runway reconstruction.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC July 8, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the July 8, 2019 regular session following an initial closed session, with all five commissioners present. Immediately upon reconvening, the board voted 4-1 on a motion by Ellen W. Reckhow and second by James Hill to set the County Manager's salary at $226,011—with Ellen W. Reckhow, James Hill, and two of the other three commissioners (Wendy Jacobs, Brenda A. Howerton, and Heidi Carter) voting aye, and one of those three commissioners casting the lone nay (whose name was garbled/unidentified in the audio transcript). Commissioners then unanimously approved the June 3 work session minutes (5-0) and the consent agenda (5-0), including funding for main library and cooperative extension after-hours security. In other business, the board received an update from the UNC School of Government's Development Finance Initiative (DFI) on selecting Laurel Street for 305 affordable housing units at 300 and 500 East Main Street, endorsed staff's post-light-rail transit planning framework with GoTriangle (including Commissioner Howerton's call for representative board diversity), approved ABC Board language (5-0), made advisory board appointments, and entered closed session (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Post-Closed Session Action: County Manager Salary Adjustment ($226,011)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reconvening from a pre-meeting closed session, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved and Vice Chair James Hill seconded setting the County Manager's salary at $226,011. The motion passed 4-1 with one unidentified commissioner voting nay.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Minutes, and Consent Agenda (Item 19-0337)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs shared announcements on Durham Neighborhood College, Engaged Durham, Innovate Durham, and the Eno-Haw Regional Hazard Mitigation Plan. The board unanimously approved the June 3, 2019 work session minutes (5-0) and the consent agenda (5-0) after clarifying that item 19-0337 transfers funds for after-hours security at Cooperative Extension and additional security at the new main library.

agenda_items.title: Update on 300 and 500 East Main Street Development Partner Selection (305 Affordable Units)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Marcia Perritt of UNC's Development Finance Initiative (DFI) updated the board on selecting Laurel Street's proposal for 300 and 500 East Main Street, which exceeds the solicitation's 277-unit target by providing 305 affordable units at 80% AMI and below alongside community meet-the-developer sessions. Commissioners praised the county's milestone entry into affordable housing development and discussed shared parking and street-level design over a six-to-nine-month predevelopment period.

agenda_items.title: Post-Light-Rail Durham County Transit Plan Update & Framework Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning and GoTriangle staff outlined a 12-month process to update the 2017 Durham County Transit Plan following cancellation of the Durham-Orange Light Rail project, including an FY 2020 pipeline assessment and budget reconciliation by November 1. Commissioners discussed bus and commuter-rail priorities, multi-directional commuter patterns, and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's demand for greater racial diversity on the GoTriangle Board of Directors; staff confirmed no formal resolution was needed to endorse the process.

agenda_items.title: ABC Board Language Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a brief introduction with the county attorney regarding proposed language for the ABC Board, the board approved the motion by unanimous voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The clerk announced selections for the Board of Adjustment (one of two vacancies filled) and other advisory posts including Natalia Rice. The board then voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) on economic development incentives, returning at 02:41:52 to adjourn.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC June 24, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the June 24, 2019 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners with all five commissioners present. After approving May minutes (5-0), celebrating the J. Robert Havlick Innovation Award, and passing consent items 19-0108 through 19-0331 minus pulled item 19-0236 (5-0), the board unanimously adopted the FY 2019-2020 Budget Ordinance (5-0). The adopted budget set a 71.22-cent tax rate (2.3 cents above revenue-neutral), boosted Durham Public Schools funding by $7.25 million (adding $250,000 above the manager's $7 million recommendation, bringing DPS operating funds near $146 million), funded Durham Pre-K at $5.1 million, invested $4.8 million in justice diversion/reentry programs, and allocated $3.1 million for employee compensation equity. The board also unanimously approved the continued Rougemont Commercial rezoning Z1800037 (5-0 across both votes), endorsed the City-County Response Policy Regarding Encampments on Public Property (5-0), updated the Northern Durham convenience site plan, adopted the Downtown County-Owned Property Evaluation Framework with equity and transit-oriented language (5-0), and voted 5-0 on anniversary-date salary increases for five appointed/elected officials.

agenda_items.title: Pre-Meeting Closed Session Salary Announcement, Announcements, and May Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs announced salaries following an early closed session for the Sheriff, Register of Deeds, Acting Tax Administrator, Clerk to the Board, and County Attorney, and shared announcements on summer meals, the USATF Youth Outdoor Championship, and 2020 Census jobs. The board unanimously approved the May 13, May 28, and May 18, 2019 minutes (5-0) and recognized the J. Robert Havlick Innovation Award.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 19-0108 through 19-0331, excluding 19-0236)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed Urban Ministries items (19-0291 and 19-0317) and requested a future briefing on computer stations before pulling item 19-0236 (the FY 2019-2020 budget ordinance). The remainder of the consent agenda passed unanimously (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 19-0236: FY 2019-2020 Budget Ordinance ($7.25M DPS Increase & 71.22-Cent Tax Rate)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter introduced the updated budget ordinance adding $250,000 above the manager's $7 million recommendation for Durham Public Schools—providing a $7.25 million increase (nearly $146 million total)—alongside $5.1 million for Durham Pre-K, $1.4 million in Durham Tech scholarships, $4.8 million for Bull City United/FIT/Project Build/reentry, doubled eviction diversion funding, $3.1 million for employee pay equity, and a 71.22-cent property tax rate. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton noted a procedural concern that the $250,000 addition arose after the last work session, while all five commissioners voted aye to adopt the budget (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Continued Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change Z1800037 (Rougemont Commercial)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Emily Struthers presented supplemental analysis on the 2014 Village of Rougemont Plan and rural pedestrian connectivity for continued rezoning case Z1800037. Commissioners noted that Rougemont residents had previously prioritized local commercial retail access over restrictive design guidelines and unanimously approved the consistency statement and rezoning ordinance (5-0 each).

agenda_items.title: City-County Response Policy Regarding Encampments on Public Property
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Homeless Project Manager Analia Hoberman presented the formalized City-County encampment response policy developed with homeless service providers after visible encampments along Highway 147, establishing public health, safety, and mobility assessments alongside outreach. Commissioners asked about Homeless Services Advisory Committee progress reporting and unanimously endorsed the policy (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Northern Durham Convenience Site Project Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services and Solid Waste staff presented plans to replace the gravel Bahama/Northern Durham convenience site (over 100,000 annual visitors) with a four-bay paved layout, cardboard compactors, shared fire-station driveway access, and a multi-purpose two-story building incorporating Sheriff observation/substation access and youth environmental education.

agenda_items.title: Downtown County-Owned Property Evaluation Tool / Framework
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the revised downtown property evaluation tool incorporating acquisition history, current tenants, opportunity costs, human capital, affordable housing, and partners such as DHA and DPS, while awaiting a joint city-county consultant study on additional parcels including 315 Holland Street. At Chair Jacobs's request, the motion to adopt the framework (5-0) directed staff to incorporate explicit equity and transit-oriented development language.

agenda_items.title: Official Salary Adjustments Vote and Boards & Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Recognizing that the closed-session salary adjustments required a formal open-session vote, the board unanimously approved anniversary-date salary adjustments for the Sheriff ($144,654 as read in the motion; $150,602 noted earlier), Register of Deeds ($105,541), Interim Tax Administrator ($107,054), Clerk to the Board ($85,000), and County Attorney ($209,931) (5-0). The clerk then read board appointment results for 12 advisory bodies before adjournment.

votes.item_title: Approval of May 13, May 28, and May 18, 2019 Minutes
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the May 13 regular session, May 28 regular session, and May 18 minutes.

votes.item_title: FY 2019-2020 Budget Ordinance Adoption (Item 19-0236)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the FY 2019-2020 budget ordinance at a 71.22-cent property tax rate, including a $7.25M funding increase for Durham Public Schools (adding $250,000 above the manager's recommendation), $5.1M for Durham Pre-K, and $3.1M for employee pay equity.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change Z1800037 (Rougemont Commercial) Consistency Statement
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the statutory consistency statement for Rougemont Commercial rezoning Z1800037 pursuant to N.C.G.S. 153A-341.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change Z1800037 (Rougemont Commercial) Ordinance Adoption
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the UDO rezoning ordinance for Rougemont Commercial (Z1800037) in the Little River District B watershed overlay.

votes.item_title: Endorse City-County Response Policy Regarding Encampments on Public Property
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Endorsed the joint City-County response policy for assessing and addressing encampments on public property with outreach and mitigation protocols.

votes.item_title: Adopt Downtown County-Owned Property Evaluation Framework (with Equity and Transit-Oriented Language)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the downtown county-owned property evaluation framework while directing staff to add explicit equity/inclusiveness and transit-oriented development wording.

votes.item_title: Official Salary Adjustments for Sheriff, Register of Deeds, Interim Tax Administrator, Clerk, and County Attorney
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved anniversary-date salary adjustments for the Sheriff ($144,654 stated in motion; $150,602 read earlier), Register of Deeds ($105,541), Interim Tax Administrator ($107,054), Clerk to the Board ($85,000), and County Attorney ($209,931).
