meetings.title: Durham County BOCC June 10, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the June 10, 2019 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners, adjusting the agenda to recognize the Friends of the Library Foundation for furnishing the Main Library and proclaiming June 19, 2019 as the 10th Anniversary of World Sickle Cell Awareness Day. The board unanimously approved meeting minutes (5-0), excused upcoming September 9 absences for Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow (5-0), and adopted the consent agenda (5-0), which included conveying five county surplus properties—including a 3.5-acre parcel—to the City of Durham for $10 each for affordable housing and accepting NC Biotech and NIH grants. Following a public hearing on $120,500 in economic development incentives for ParExcel International Corporation (to add 264 jobs and establish a second U.S. headquarters) and community budget remarks, the board held a public hearing and voted 5-0 to approve merging Durham County ACCESS paratransit operations with the City of Durham. Commissioners also heard from DSS Director Ben Rose regarding a proposed federal Office of Management and Budget rule change shifting poverty guidelines to Chained CPI and discussed submitting a comment letter opposing the change before holding a unanimous closed session on three pending litigation matters (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustment, and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order following a closed session, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. She adjusted the agenda to move Item 19-0284 to the start of ceremonial items and announced the Durham County Summer Reading Program, Board of Elections voter photo ID sessions, and the County Manager's Durham This Week newsletter.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes and Excused Absences for September 9, 2019 Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs noted a pending excused absence request with Clerk Monica Toomer for the September 9 meeting. The board voted unanimously (5-0) to approve the minutes and then voted unanimously (5-0) to excuse Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow from the September 9 regular meeting.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions: Friends of the Library Foundation (Item 19-0284) and World Sickle Cell Awareness Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board recognized Friends of the Library Foundation Board Chair Lou and foundation representatives for fundraising and furnishing the Main Library's communal space. Chair Jacobs then read a proclamation recognizing Wednesday, June 19, 2019 as the 10th anniversary of World Sickle Cell Awareness Day with Tiffany Bell and community partners.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Items 19-0185 through 19-0305)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved consent items 19-0185 through 19-0305 (5-0). Chair Jacobs highlighted Item 19-0280 conveying five county surplus parcels—including a 3.5-acre site—to the City of Durham at $10 each for affordable housing, and Economic Development's Andy Miracle highlighted NC Biotech-funded awards with community benefits and an NIH library health programming grant.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Incentives for ParExcel International Corporation and Budget Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Andy Miracle presented a proposal to allocate $120,500 in economic development funds to ParExcel International Corporation to support a $1.7 million investment, 264 new jobs, retention of over 600 North Carolina employees, and a second U.S. headquarters in Durham County. Later in the session, commissioners thanked the large community audience for attending and weighing in on upcoming budget decisions.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Approval of Durham County ACCESS Merger with City of Durham
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation staff member Linda Wallace Thomas presented the interlocal merger transferring administrative functions of Durham County ACCESS demand-response paratransit to the City of Durham to achieve cost and operational efficiencies while maintaining FY18-19 funding and service levels under First Transit management. Chair Jacobs asked staff to pursue continuing the Transportation Heroes recognition ceremonies, and after closing the public hearing with no speakers, the board approved the merger 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of Proposed Federal OMB Poverty Guidelines Rule Change
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DSS Director Ben Rose briefed the board on the federal Office of Management and Budget proposal to calculate poverty guidelines using the Chained Consumer Price Index rather than the traditional CPI, warning it would lower thresholds over time and reduce SNAP and social services eligibility. Commissioners discussed having the County Manager send a comment letter supporting continued use of CPI with copies to the congressional delegation.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Litigation Matters (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session to consult with legal counsel regarding Marquita Welton v. Durham County et al. (17-CV-258), Julia Graves v. Durham County et al. (19-CV-316), and Durham County v. AmerisourceBergen Drug Corporation et al. (1:19-CV-0041). Upon returning to open session, Chair Jacobs reported that staff was given direction and the board adjourned.

votes.notes: ASR transcribed Commissioner Reckhow as 'Rec out' and Commissioner Howerton as 'Howardton'.
votes.discussion_detail: Unanimous approval of the minutes presented by Clerk Monica Toomer.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved excused absences for Chair Wendy Jacobs and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow for the September 9, 2019 regular meeting.

votes.notes: ASR transcribed Commissioner Reckhow as 'rec'.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the interlocal merger of Durham County ACCESS with the City of Durham following a public hearing with no opposition.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2019-06-03 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 3, 2019 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, citizen speakers urged the County to oppose the RDU Airport Authority's rock quarry lease on the Odd Fellows Tract under N.C.G.S. 63-56(f) (citing a competing $6.5 million Conservation Fund offer), requested a joint City Police and Sheriff task force along the Swansboro boundary, and proposed a local property-tax circuit-breaker deferral for low-income homeowners at 30%–80% AMI. After re-ordering the agenda for a Comprehensive Land Use Plan presentation, commissioners reviewed proposed updates to the Economic Development Incentive Policy with staff Andy Miracle—discussing public deliverable tracking, 'but-for' and clawback language, green building and transit/TDM criteria, agricultural economics, and a proposed smaller 50-job / $50,000 startup incentive tier for firms growing out of local incubators like The Frontier and BioLabs. The Board then voted unanimously 5-0 to suspend the rules (Ellen W. Reckhow moving, Heidi Carter seconding) and 5-0 to approve the Fourth Amendment to the Convention Center Management Agreement (Heidi Carter moving, Ellen W. Reckhow seconding) before concluding work session directives and recessing for budget hearings.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: RDU Quarry Lease, Boundary Enforcement, and Low-Income Tax Deferral
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Umstead Coalition representatives Gil Johnson, Matt Thompson, and legal counsel argued RDU's mineral lease on the Odd Fellows Tract violates N.C.G.S. 63-56(f) and municipal sale rules compared to the Conservation Fund's $6.5 million cash offer, urging the County to oppose it or file a declaratory action. Mr. Noble sought a joint City Police/Sheriff task force along a Swansboro boundary (referred to County Attorney and Curtis Massey), and Jim presented a Coalition for Affordable Housing and Transit / People's Alliance proposal for a local property-tax circuit-breaker deferral capped at 1%–3% of income for households up to 80% AMI.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustment for Comprehensive Land Use Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs asked to move the Comprehensive Land Use Plan presentation ahead of the consent agenda to accommodate the presenters' travel schedules. The middle portion of the meeting covering the presentation and consent agenda is omitted in the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Policy Revisions and Startup Tier Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic development staff Andy Miracle presented draft policy updates covering transparent deliverable tracking, clawback and 'but-for' clauses, green building/LEED standards, non-monetary infrastructure options, agricultural economics realignment in Soil and Water, and TDM incentives such as GoPasses and vanpools. Staff also floated a smaller-scale incentive tier (e.g., 50 new jobs over two years for a $50,000 award or incubator facility upfits with partners like The Frontier and BioLabs), receiving positive feedback to return in August.

agenda_items.title: Fourth Amendment to the Convention Center Management Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained that the Fourth Amendment to the Convention Center management agreement had been delayed after the May work session. On a motion by Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by Heidi Carter, the Board unanimously suspended the rules 5-0, and on a motion by Heidi Carter, seconded by Ellen W. Reckhow, unanimously approved the amendment 5-0.

agenda_items.title: BOCC Directives Update and Transition to Budget Hearings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff member Drew reported progress clearing outstanding directives from yellow to white on the tracking sheet with Clerk Monica's draft minutes. Chair Jacobs closed the work session for a five-minute agenda prep ahead of 1:30 PM budget hearings.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend the Rules for Convention Center Management Agreement Amendment
votes.notes: No opposition voiced on the motion to suspend the rules.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to suspend work session rules in order to vote immediately on the Fourth Amendment to the Convention Center management agreement.

votes.item_title: Approval of Fourth Amendment to the Convention Center Management Agreement
votes.notes: Chair Jacobs announced the amendment was approved without opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Approval of the Fourth Amendment to the management agreement for the Durham Convention Center, which had carried over from the May work session.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC May 28, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 28, 2019 regular session, Chair Wendy Jacobs and the Durham County Board of Commissioners unanimously approved prior meeting minutes (5-0) and consent agenda items 19-0239 through 19-0273 (5-0). Ceremonial items included an Older Americans Month proclamation presented with DSS Director Ben Rose and a special recognition honoring Amia Mitchell for using Stop the Bleed training to save gunshot victim Aria Hackney's life. During a public hearing on the Rougemont Commercial text-only rezoning (Item 19-0257), commissioners questioned staff on prohibited uses such as tobacco shops, sidewalk requirements, water utilities, and Rougemont Rural Village Plan consistency, while a resident expressed opposition to a rumored Dollar General; the board voted unanimously (5-0) to continue the hearing to June 24, 2019 for a supplemental staff report. The board also announced appointments to the Dangerous Dog Appeal Board and Workforce Development Board, welcomed summer Strategic Initiatives interns Sabrina Davis and Kelly Warren, and voted 5-0 to enter closed session on economic development incentives.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. She announced Board of Elections voter ID seminars (including Spanish-language sessions), the June 1 property tax relief deadline for seniors and disabled veterans, the FY19-20 budget portal and June 10 public hearing, Alert Durham, and the Community Health Coalition's 30th anniversary.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (PAC 4 Feb 9, PAC 2 April 8, Regular Sessions April 8 and April 22, 2019)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved minutes from the February 9 PAC 4 meeting, April 8 PAC 2 meeting, April 8 regular session, and April 22 regular session.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Older Americans Month Proclamation and Recognition of Amia Mitchell
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill read the Older Americans Month proclamation alongside DSS Director Ben Rose, who noted Durham County's 65-and-older population is projected to rise from roughly 32,000 to nearly 90,000 by 2037. Chair Jacobs then presented a recognition to Amia Mitchell for using Stop the Bleed training to save Aria Hackney after a gunshot wound.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Items 19-0239 through 19-0273)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled for separate discussion, the board unanimously approved consent agenda items 19-0239 through 19-0273.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Rougemont Commercial Text-Only Rezoning (Item 19-0257)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Emily Struthers presented a text-only development plan rezoning to Commercial Neighborhood (CN) prohibiting drive-throughs, dry cleaning, payday lenders, taxi dispatch, and animal kennels, which the Planning Commission recommended 8-3. Commissioners raised questions about tobacco shops, malt beverage sales, UDO restrictions on proffering sidewalks in text-only plans, utilities, and Rougemont transit, and after public comment opposing a rumored Dollar General, voted 5-0 to continue the hearing to June 24, 2019 for a supplemental report on the Rougemont Rural Village Plan.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board conducted ballots and announced appointments to county advisory bodies, including Michelle Bixby to the Dangerous Dog Appeal Board and Anthony Nelson to the Workforce Development Board.

agenda_items.title: Introduction of Summer Interns and Closed Session on Economic Development (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session regarding business location and economic development incentives under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4), after which Chair Jacobs introduced Strategic Initiatives summer interns Sabrina Davis (Duke MPP) and Kelly Warren (NC State MPA). Upon returning from closed session, Chair Jacobs announced direction had been given to staff and the meeting adjourned.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (PAC 4, PAC 2, April 8 and April 22, 2019 Regular Sessions)
votes.discussion_detail: Unanimous approval of four sets of prior work/PAC and regular session minutes.

votes.item_title: Continue Rougemont Commercial Rezoning (Item 19-0257) to June 24, 2019 with Public Hearing Open
votes.notes: Motion deferred final action to June 24, 2019.
votes.discussion_detail: Continued the Rougemont Commercial text-only rezoning public hearing to June 24, 2019 so planning staff can prepare a supplemental report addressing the Rougemont Rural Village Plan and commissioner questions.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4))
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session to discuss economic development incentives and business location negotiations.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC May 13, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: During the May 13, 2019 regular session, the Durham County Board of Commissioners unanimously approved April 1, 2019 work session minutes (5-0) and issued ceremonial proclamations for National Drug Treatment Court Month, EMS Week (honoring responders to the April 10 downtown Durham incident), and Foster Care Month alongside DSS Director Ben Rose. The board also presented a resolution supporting North Carolina's working families—advocating for paid family leave, a $15 state employee minimum wage, Medicaid expansion, and public-sector collective bargaining rights. Following the County Manager's FY19-20 recommended budget presentation, public speakers Brian Calloway and Carl Kenney urged competitive pay and a $15 minimum wage across Durham Public Schools and Durham County, and the board unanimously adopted consent agenda items 19-0168 through 19-0248 (5-0), including a milestone ground-floor restaurant lease at Admin II. After a unanimous personnel closed session (5-0), the board voted 5-0 to appoint Monica Toomer as Clerk to the Board ($85,000 salary) and Timothy Dwayne Brinson as Tax Administrator ($165,000 salary).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of April 1, 2019 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order, read the public charge, and shared announcements covering Board of Elections voter ID seminars, FY2020 transit work plans public comment through May 20, the Foster Care Fair, Aging Well in Durham, and the FY19-20 budget portal. The board then unanimously approved the April 1, 2019 work session minutes (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations: National Drug Treatment Court Month, EMS Week, and Foster Care Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter read the National Drug Treatment Court Month proclamation, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow read the EMS Week proclamation with Sheriff Clarence Burkhead honoring April 10 first responders, and the board recognized Foster Care Month (313 children in care and 104 licensed foster homes). DSS Director Ben Rose and commissioners discussed flat state foster reimbursement rates, $800,000 in mid-year local foster funding ($3.8 million total), and shifting toward prevention and Durham Pre-K.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting North Carolina's Working People and Their Families
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read a board resolution urging the North Carolina legislative delegation to support paid family leave, a higher minimum wage and $15/hour for all state employees, Medicaid expansion, and repealing 'right to work' restrictions to allow public-sector collective bargaining. Commissioners noted Durham County already provides a $15/hour minimum wage and 12 weeks of paid family leave.

agenda_items.title: FY19-20 Recommended Budget Remarks and Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the County Manager's FY19-20 budget presentation (which noted five upcoming budget work sessions totaling 26 hours and honored retiring staff member Gail), two public speakers addressed compensation and capital planning. Brian Calloway criticized the DPS budget for omitting a $15 minimum wage while raising administrator salaries and commended the manager's bond approach to DPS capital requests, while Carl Kenney urged market-competitive pay for county workers.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Items 19-0168 through 19-0248)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs highlighted Item 19-0216, a milestone ground-floor retail lease in the Admin II building for Neighbors restaurant incorporating board-requested community benefits. The board voted unanimously (5-0) to approve consent items 19-0168 through 19-0248.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Personnel (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider public officer appointments and employment conditions.

agenda_items.title: Appointments of Clerk to the Board (Monica Toomer) and Tax Administrator (Timothy Dwayne Brinson)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After returning from closed session, the board voted 5-0 to appoint interim clerk Monica Toomer as Clerk to the Board effective May 14, 2019 at an annual salary of $85,000. The board then voted 5-0 to appoint Orange County Tax Administrator Timothy Dwayne Brinson as Durham County Tax Administrator effective July 1, 2019 (succeeding retired Kimberly Simpson) at a salary of $165,000, approving his appointment, salary, and contract.

votes.item_title: Approval of April 1, 2019 Work Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Unanimous approval of the April 1, 2019 work session minutes.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session to consider qualifications, conditions of appointment, and employment for public officers.

votes.discussion_detail: Appointed Monica Toomer (serving as interim clerk since December) as Clerk to the Board effective May 14, 2019 at a salary of $85,000.

votes.item_title: Appointment of Timothy Dwayne Brinson as Tax Administrator ($165,000 Salary and Contract)
votes.discussion_detail: Appointed Timothy Dwayne Brinson as Durham County Tax Administrator effective July 1, 2019 at a salary of $165,000, succeeding retired Tax Administrator Kimberly Simpson, and approved his contract.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2019-05-06 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 6, 2019 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with four commissioners present (the Board voted 4-0 to grant an excused absence to James Hill due to illness), speakers included SBA Disaster Assistance specialist Julie Garrett promoting low-interest working-capital loans up to $2 million for businesses affected by the April 10 downtown gas explosion, and Mr. Gibson urging greater hiring of qualified professionals of color in planning and zoning departments. During consent agenda review (Items 19-0168 through 19-0204), commissioners examined manager contract-signing thresholds ($40,000 for original contracts vs. board review of all amendments), a fund-balance transfer covering the 2.5% public safety pay increase for county-employed staff at Lebanon Volunteer Fire Department, utility contracts, and Detention Center elevator cost increases. The Board then refined and advanced two items to its upcoming consent agenda—a Local Progress resolution supporting North Carolina's working families (amended to specify a $15/hour state-employee minimum wage, Medicaid expansion, and Durham volunteer leave after Brenda A. Howerton confirmed it would not conflict with the county compensation study) and written board appointment rules on unexpired terms and tie-vote reporting—before reviewing directives and voting 4-0 to enter closed session on economic development incentives, personnel, and attorney-client matters.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge, Excused Absence for James Hill, and Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After reading the public charge, the Board voted 4-0 (Ellen W. Reckhow moving, Heidi Carter seconding) to grant an excused absence to James Hill, who was ill. Julie Garrett of the SBA Office of Disaster Assistance announced a Chesterfield Building center offering 4% disaster working-capital loans up to $2 million for businesses hurt by the April 10 gas explosion, and Mr. Gibson urged hiring qualified professionals of color in local planning, zoning, and architectural offices.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (Items 19-0168 through 19-0204)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed consent items including Slater Road pump station closeout (19-0168), the policy requiring board approval of any amendment to a contract whose original value exceeded the $40,000 manager threshold (19-0177), a fund-balance transfer for the 2.5% public safety compensation increase for 12 county-staffed positions at Lebanon Volunteer Fire Department (19-0185), biosolids/polymer and Triangle Wastewater collection system contracts (19-0199, 19-0200, 19-0202), and Detention Center elevator cost increases above an original $312,000 estimate (19-0204).

agenda_items.title: Resolution in Support of North Carolina's Working People and Their Families
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed a Local Progress resolution tailored with Durham County employee benefits. Ellen W. Reckhow proposed specifying a minimum wage of at least $15 per hour for all state employees alongside raising the minimum wage for all workers, Brenda A. Howerton sought confirmation that the resolution would not preempt or undercut Durham County's compensation study, and commissioners added Medicaid expansion language and Durham County employee volunteer leave.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Policy: Mid-Term Appointments and Vote Reporting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and the Clerk presented written rules clarifying that appointees filling mid-term vacancies (such as a prior Audit Committee question) serve the remainder of the unexpired term plus eligibility for a full term, and that the Clerk will report top vote-getters to the Board if nominees tie at two votes. Commissioners agreed to place the policy on the next consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: BOCC Directives Review and Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4), (a)(6), (a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed pending 2019 directives—requesting updates on the economic development policy, foster care, and a JCCPC item on NPOs and historic-district housing affordability—before voting 4-0 on a motion by Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by Heidi Carter, to enter closed session on economic development incentives, personnel evaluations/complaints, and attorney-client privilege. Returning at 04:56:11, Chair Jacobs reported direction was given to staff and the Board adjourned.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Vice Chair James Hill
votes.notes: James Hill was absent; all four remaining commissioners voted Aye.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve an excused absence for Vice Chair James Hill due to illness.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4), (a)(6), and (a)(3)
votes.notes: James Hill was absent; Chair Jacobs announced the motion passed unanimously 4-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to adjourn into closed session to discuss tentative economic development incentives (a)(4), individual personnel qualifications/performance/complaints (a)(6), and attorney-client privileged matters (a)(3).

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC April 22, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: On April 22, 2019, the Durham County Board of Commissioners approved work session and March 25 regular session minutes (5-0) after clarifying that prior work-session discussion on participating in a post-light-rail transit feasibility study reflected informal consensus rather than formal action. Ceremonially, Commissioner Heidi Carter read a Children's Mental Health Awareness Month proclamation and Chair Wendy Jacobs read a resolution supporting the May 1, 2019 Day of Action for North Carolina Public Schools, calling for state-funded support staff, a $15 school minimum wage, 5% employee and retiree raises, Medicaid expansion, and reinstated retiree health benefits. The board unanimously passed consent items 19-0179 through 19-0195 (5-0), received a report from the Adult Services Advisory Committee regarding volunteer retention and training, and announced appointments to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission, Child Protection/Fatality Prevention Team, Criminal Justice Advisory Committee, City-County Appearance Commission, and Durham County Hospital Corporation Board of Trustees. Commissioners then entered a closed session on personnel and attorney-client matters (5-0) before giving staff direction and adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The meeting opened with the public charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and announcements including a non-medication pain management workshop at the Durham Center for Senior Life, GoTriangle Get On Board Day free passes (April 22–26), and an Expanding Housing Choices community conversation on April 27 at Walltown Park Recreation Center.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Work Session and March 25, 2019 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Responding to Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's concern about whether work-session consensus on joining a transit feasibility study (evaluating options instead of light rail if four partner entities participated) constituted formal action, commissioners clarified no motion or rule suspension occurred at the work session. The board then voted 5-0 to approve both the work session and March 25 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Children's Mental Health Awareness Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter, the board's representative to Alliance Behavioral Healthcare, read the proclamation for Children's Mental Health Awareness Month and presented it to Tika Dempson, who provided a brief update on local System of Care initiatives.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting May 1st Day of Action for North Carolina Public Schools
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read a resolution signed by all five commissioners backing Durham Public Schools educators ahead of the May 1, 2019 rally. The resolution urged the General Assembly to fund national ratios for school nurses, social workers, psychologists, counselors, and media coordinators, enact a $15 minimum wage and 5% raises/retiree COLA, expand Medicaid, and restore state retiree health benefits; staff was directed to send copies to the school board, superintendent, governor, and legislative delegation.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Items 19-0179 through 19-0195)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled for separate consideration, the board voted unanimously (5-0) to approve consent agenda items 19-0179 through 19-0195.

agenda_items.title: Adult Services Advisory Committee Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Adult Services Advisory Committee Chair Sue Roth, Earl Kirby, and Jeff Austin delivered the committee's annual report. Commissioners discussed board orientation, training, and member retention challenges.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After correcting a ballot typo noting four selections (two citizen, two health system) for the Durham County Hospital Corporation Board of Trustees, the board announced appointments across five advisory bodies including Trisha Smart (BPAC), Keith Helmer (Child Protection/Fatality Prevention), Andrew Jennings (CJAC), three Appearance Commission appointees, and four Hospital Corporation Trustees.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC April 8, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 8, 2019 meeting, the Durham County Board of Commissioners approved the February 11 and March 11 regular session minutes (5-0) and presented seven ceremonial proclamations and resolutions, including Week of the Young Child, Child Abuse Prevention Awareness Month, Reentry Week, and a 2020 Census resolution targeting an 82% or higher county response rate. Following discussion of the 1% public art allocation process across capital projects, the board held a major deliberation on the termination of the Durham-Orange Light Rail cost-sharing agreement, citing North Carolina General Assembly funding cuts from 25% to 7.7% (which required $57.6 million in extra county transit funds), rigid legislative deadlines, the federal shutdown, and unexpected environmental assessment requirements. Commissioners voted unanimously (5-0) to approve disbanding the light rail cost-sharing agreement while committing to a 12-to-15-month Durham Transit Plan update, evaluating how to repurpose corridor investments, advancing commuter rail planning ($800,000 committed), and expanding public transit budget transparency online. The board concluded with a unanimous closed session on pending litigation (18-CVS-312) before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order at 7:01 PM, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Announcements included a Tax Administration Homestead exemption seminar for seniors, the FY19-20 online budget comment portal, the Kids Voting Durham youth survey, Microsoft Man Code Camp at NCCU, and board/commission vacancies.

agenda_items.title: Approval of February 11, 2019 and March 11, 2019 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the minutes of the February 11, 2019 and March 11, 2019 regular sessions.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations and Resolutions (Early Childhood, Child Abuse Prevention, Reentry Week, and 2020 Census)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board presented proclamations for Week of the Young Child (with Durham Partnership for Children and Durham Tech), Child Abuse Prevention Awareness Month (with DSS Director Ben Rose), and Reentry Week (read by Vice Chair James Hill). Chair Jacobs also read a resolution supporting the 2020 Census with Deborah Craig-Ray, setting an 82% response goal (up from 75% in 2010) and launching a Complete Count Committee for hard-to-count communities.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of 1% Public Art Allocation Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed how the 1% public art policy is applied across county capital projects. Vice Chair James Hill asked for clarification on project-by-project eligibility and noted that artistic selection should remain with arts professionals rather than becoming politicized.

agenda_items.title: Durham-Orange Light Rail Cost-Sharing Disbanding and Transit Plan Next Steps
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed why the Durham-Orange Light Rail project could no longer move forward under statutory deadlines after General Assembly funding cuts reduced state participation from 25% to 10% and then 7.7%—requiring $57.6 million in additional county transit funds—compounded by the six-week federal shutdown and an unexpected environmental assessment. The board voted 5-0 to approve disbanding the cost-sharing agreement, while committing to evaluate repurposing corridor investments, conduct a 12–15 month Durham Transit Plan update, publish transit spending data online, and advance regional commuter rail planning ($800,000 committed).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Litigation (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel regarding Francisco Rivera-Rodriguez v. Michael Andrews, Paul Aiken, Durham County, and Travelers Casualty and Surety Company (18-CVS-312). The board returned from closed session and adjourned.

votes.discussion_detail: Unanimous approval of the February 11 and March 11, 2019 regular session minutes.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2019-04-01 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 1, 2019 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, citizen commenters clashed over Confederate memorials, with Matthew McQuinn alleging harassment and urging compliance with state monument law while George Robeson announced an impending federal lawsuit challenging Confederate symbols on public property. During consent agenda review, commissioners scrutinized Item 19-0154 (Little Diversified Architectural's parking-deck programming contract, noting references to the canceled light-rail project and pressing staff to incorporate parking charges, carpool/vanpool preferences, and rooftop solar collectors toward the County's 80% greenhouse gas reduction target by 2030) and Item 19-0164 (CJRC roof replacement change order), urging the Manager to expedite hiring the climate-resolution feasibility consultant rather than waiting for the new fiscal year. Later in the session, staff briefed the Board on Falls Lake nutrient-reduction rules (existing-development Stage 1 targeted for 2024 and Stage 2 around 2041), commissioners reviewed a national prenatal-to-three resolution brought by Brenda A. Howerton (debating staffing needs and half-funding of a joint youth position versus early childhood coordination), and the Board voted unanimously 5-0 to enter closed session on real property acquisition and economic development before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge and Citizen Comments: Confederate Memorials
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs opened the session with the public charge and two citizen speakers. Matthew McQuinn said Confederate veterans' descendants had experienced harassment and asked the Board to follow state law regarding memorial restoration, whereas George Robeson distributed documents and announced he would file a federal U.S. District Court lawsuit challenging Confederate displays on public property.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review: Parking Deck Programming (19-0154), CJRC Roof (19-0164), and Climate Action
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners pulled Items 19-0148, 19-0154, and 19-0164. On Item 19-0154 (Little Diversified Architectural's single-bid RFQ for 300/500 East Main parking deck programming), commissioners noted outdated light-rail references and urged incorporating paid parking, carpool/vanpool spaces, and solar panels to meet the County's 2030 80% greenhouse gas reduction resolution; on Item 19-0164 (CJRC roof change order), commissioners pressed staff for solar-ready roof standards and asked the Manager to expedite the greenhouse gas feasibility consultant before FY2020.

agenda_items.title: Falls Lake Stormwater Rules and Nutrient Reduction Implementation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Stormwater staff (including Ryan) explained that Durham County enforces Falls Lake new-development rules and that the state's model program for Stage 1 existing development was due in 2020 with estimated implementation in 2024 (and Stage 2 around 2041). Staff outlined compliance tools including new stormwater control measures, retrofits, and land conservation credits.

agenda_items.title: Prenatal-to-Three Early Childhood Resolution and Staffing Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Brenda A. Howerton introduced a national Pritzker prenatal-to-three resolution. Commissioners discussed adding Durham child poverty statistics (26% overall, 37% Black, 36% Hispanic, 8% white) and whether to redirect half-funding from a City youth position toward early childhood or ACEs coordination, ultimately agreeing to check whether Durham-specific whereas edits would affect eligibility and place the item on Monday's agenda.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5)(i) and (a)(4))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by James Hill, the Board voted 5-0 to enter closed session regarding price and material terms for real property acquisition and business location/expansion negotiations. Following closed session at 06:50:14, the Board adjourned on a motion by Heidi Carter, seconded by Brenda A. Howerton.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5)(i) and (a)(4)
votes.notes: Chair Jacobs initially misspoke the mover's name before correcting to Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by James Hill; passed unanimously 5-0.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC March 25, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 25, 2019 meeting, Chair Wendy Jacobs delivered the 2019 State of the County Address, highlighting county investments exceeding $150 million (over one-third of the budget) in public education, Durham Pre-K, Durham Tech College Promise, and upcoming capital needs for Northern High School and a new South Durham elementary school. Her address also reviewed the ACEs task force, AARP Age-Friendly Community certification, Youth Home and Detention Center facility planning, surplus property transfers for affordable housing, a 2050 100% renewable energy goal, the Data DCoNC dashboard, and a record 99.8% tax collection rate. Ceremonial recognitions honored National Service Recognition Day (AmeriCorps), County Government Month, and Women in Public Office Day. The board unanimously approved the consent agenda (Item 19-0113, February 2019 property tax releases and refunds, 5-0), approved the $50,000 Aetna-funded Durham Pre-K mini-grant program (5-0), heard budget comments from resident Michael Harris, and made appointments to four boards and commissions including the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority and Library Board of Trustees.

agenda_items.title: 2019 State of the County Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs delivered the 2019 State of the County Address after postponing a technical intro video. She emphasized shared prosperity across affordable housing, transit, and job training; over $150 million in education funding and upcoming CIP needs for Northern High School and a South Durham elementary school; the ACEs task force and AARP Age-Friendly certification; Youth Home and Detention Center upgrades; affordable housing surplus land transfers; the 2050 renewable energy resolution; and a 99.8% tax collection rate.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations: National Service Recognition Day, County Government Month, and Women in Public Office Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board proclaimed National Service Recognition Day 2019 with Conservation Trust for North Carolina AmeriCorps representatives (noting six local AmeriCorps members and over $700,000 in federal funding), recognized County Government Month and the NACo 'Connecting the Unconnected' initiative, and proclaimed Women in Public Office Day 2019 with Vice Chair James Hill honoring women's leadership on the suffrage centennial.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Item 19-0113: Property Tax Releases and Refunds)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the single consent agenda item, Item 19-0113 covering property tax releases and refunds for February 2019.

agenda_items.title: Durham Pre-K Mini-Grant Program ($50,000 Aetna Grant)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the Durham Pre-K mini-grant program utilizing a $50,000 grant from Aetna alongside capacity-building and outcome indicator requirements for local organizations. Commissioners noted the agenda text should explicitly clarify the Aetna grant source rather than general fund dollars, then voted unanimously (5-0) to approve the funding item.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Public Comment on Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Michael Harris addressed the board regarding taxpayer funding and urged commissioners to exercise frugality in county spending. Chair Jacobs thanked him for waiting to speak and explained that the regular budget public hearing had taken place earlier in the agenda.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After circulating the AARP Age-Friendly Community certification, the board announced appointments including Edward Rezuto (Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission), Camilla Mique (Library Board of Trustees), Edwin Bryson Jr. (Memorial Stadium Authority), and Patrick Hannah and David Morgan (Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority).

votes.discussion_detail: Approved the $50,000 Aetna-funded Durham Pre-K mini-grant program after clarifying the grant source in the agenda item.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC March 11, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 11, 2019 regular session, the Durham County Board of Commissioners postponed Item 19-0115 (My Brother's Keeper mini-grant program) to March 25 and unanimously approved the corrected January 28 regular session minutes (5-0) and February 4 work session minutes (5-0). Ceremonially, Vice Chair James Hill sponsored a Colorectal Cancer Awareness Month proclamation highlighting screening at age 45, and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton presented a resolution supporting Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (JCPC) allocation expansion to address nine years of flat base funding and the December 1, 2019 Raise the Age implementation, which staff was directed to send to NCACC, the Durham legislative delegation, and Public Safety Secretary Hooks. Staff also demonstrated the interactive Data DCoNC and Power BI Strategic Plan and Budget dashboards, including 10-year longitudinal NCACC peer-county tax and school spending comparisons. Following a unanimous closed session under attorney-client privilege (5-0), the board voted 5-0 to approve a Memorandum of Agreement with the State of North Carolina and voted 5-0 to authorize Chair Wendy Jacobs to execute the agreement.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustment (Item 19-0115 Postponed), and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order, postponed Item 19-0115 (My Brother's Keeper mini-grant program) to March 25, and shared community announcements including Sheriff's Office $10 rabies clinics, safe internet exchange zones at the courthouse parking lot, LIEAP energy assistance through March 31, National Track & Field Championship registration, Alert Durham, and 43 county advisory boards.

agenda_items.title: Approval of January 28, 2019 Regular Session and February 4, 2019 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved the January 28, 2019 regular session minutes with a minor correction (5-0) and subsequently approved the February 4, 2019 work session minutes (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Colorectal Cancer Awareness Month 2019
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill read the Colorectal Cancer Awareness Month proclamation emphasizing early screening starting at age 45, noting colorectal cancer is the second leading cause of cancer death for men and women combined. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow shared her family history and urged residents to get screened.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (JCPC) Allocation Expansion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton read a resolution urging the state to expand JCPC funding—unchanged for nine years—to support early intervention programs and the December 1, 2019 Raise the Age Juvenile Justice Reinvestment Act expansion to 16- and 17-year-olds. The board directed staff to transmit the resolution to NCACC's Kevin Leonard, the Durham legislative delegation, and NC Department of Public Safety Secretary Hooks.

agenda_items.title: Presentation: Data DCoNC Power BI Strategic Plan, Budget, and NCACC Comparison Dashboards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff demonstrated interactive Power BI visualizations embedded on the county budget page, including the Strategic Plan Dashboard across five goal areas, real-time adopted general fund expenditures (66% spent at 69.5% of the year across $228 million operating and $138 million personnel), and 10-year longitudinal NCACC Budget & Tax Survey comparisons of per-pupil school spending and tax rates across peer counties. Staff committed to emailing direct dashboard links to commissioners and improving homepage visibility.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)) and Memorandum of Agreement with the State of North Carolina
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the request of County Attorney Lowell Siler, the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session for attorney-client consultation under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3). Returning to open session at 02:38:44, the board voted 5-0 to approve a Memorandum of Agreement with the State of North Carolina and voted 5-0 to authorize Chair Jacobs to execute the agreement.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2019-03-07 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the Thursday, March 7, 2019 Work Session (rescheduled from Monday due to the NACo conference in Washington, D.C.), Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting and heard public comments including a 162-household petition presented by Phil Post urging an independent financial review, a spending cap, and no county funding for GoTriangle donation shortfalls on the Durham-Orange Light Rail project after an FTA risk report projected costs up to $3.3 billion–$3.6 billion, alongside competing comments from John Flora, James Ward, and George Roberson regarding the Confederate monument. During consent agenda review, commissioners flagged Items 19-0095 and 19-0103, questioning facilities contractor wages (reported at minimum wage to $10/hour versus the county's $15/hour rate), potential in-house staffing ahead of the budget report, and furnishings for the 170,000-square-foot Admin II building. Later in the session, following a community survey update, staff and commissioners discussed a comprehensive, equity-centered approach to county-owned properties—particularly six parcels along East Main Street including 907 East Main adjacent to Durham Housing Authority and City of Durham holdings—and directed staff to return with a consulting contract. After reviewing the 2019 OneDrive directives tracking sheet with staff, the Board adjourned unanimously on a voice vote with no contested votes or formal substantive votes taken during the work session.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks and Public Comment (Light Rail Costs and Confederate Monument)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs noted the session was held Thursday because commissioners attended the NACo conference in D.C. on Monday and read the public charge. Phil Post presented a petition signed by 162 Southwest Durham households near Creekside Elementary School asking the County to hire an independent financial consultant on light rail, adopt a spending cap, and decline to cover GoTriangle donation shortfalls, citing an FTA risk report estimating $3.3 billion at 50% confidence and $3.6 billion at 80% confidence. Three additional speakers—John Flora, James Ward, and George Roberson—addressed the Confederate monument, with Roberson calling it unconstitutional under the 13th Amendment and stating he was pursuing action in district court.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review: Items 19-0095 (Facilities Contracting/Wages) and 19-0103 (Admin II Furnishings)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's request to expedite the consent agenda, the Board focused discussion on flagged items 19-0095 and 19-0103. On Item 19-0095, staff noted the RFP fell within the $1.00–$1.15 per square foot range with a WBE contractor, while discussing high turnover even at $15/hour and noting most contractors pay minimum wage to $10/hour ($11–$12 for management); a commissioner expressed concern about being unable to mandate a contractor living wage and favored reviewing a forthcoming budget report on bringing services in-house. On Item 19-0103, discussion addressed furnishings for the 170,000-square-foot Admin II building across the street and recouping investment by selling surplus items.

agenda_items.title: Community Survey Update and Comprehensive County-Owned Property Planning (East Main Street)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a 2019 community survey briefing noting overall resident satisfaction and challenges achieving diverse participation comparable to random sampling, staff led a strategic discussion on county-owned properties including the Civic Center parking lot, Admin II/old bank building under the facility master plan, and 907 East Main Street. Commissioners explored balancing property sales to reduce capital debt against retaining land to advance inclusiveness and human-capital goals across racial, health, education, and economic equity. Commissioners favored a comprehensive, holistic approach across six highlighted East Main Street properties—including potential RFQ coordination with the Durham Housing Authority and City of Durham—and gave staff direction to return with a consulting contract.

agenda_items.title: 2019 Board Directives Tracking and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After one commissioner stepped out for an Alliance meeting, staff member Drew reviewed the 2019 directives tracker with Clerk Monica and assisted commissioners in locating the updated SharePoint/OneDrive link rather than older 2018 files. With no further comments on directives, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved to adjourn, seconded by Vice Chair James Hill, and the motion passed unanimously by voice vote.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC February 25, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 25, 2019 regular session, the Durham County Board of Commissioners shared announcements on Tax Administration property reappraisal consultations, pre-K registration, and the upcoming National Track & Field Championship before unanimously approving work session minutes (5-0) and scheduling a future Gang Reduction Steering Committee report. Ceremonial items included the 2018 Champions in Transportation Awards and proclamation presented by Durham County ACCESS Director Linda Thomas, recognition of Interim Cooperative Extension Director Dr. Deborah Crandall, and a recognition of Bull City YouthBuild's 21 recent graduates. The board unanimously approved the consent agenda (5-0), appointed members to the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee, Animal Services Advisory Committee, Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee, and Women's Commission, and entered a unanimous attorney-client closed session (5-0) before giving direction to staff and adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting and announced remaining Tax Administration individual reappraisal meetings at Southwest and East Regional Libraries, pre-K registration appointments through May 16, the June 25–30 National Track & Field Championship at Durham County Memorial Stadium, Alert Durham, and board/commission openings. The board voted 5-0 to approve the work session minutes, and Chair Jacobs confirmed a Gang Reduction Steering Committee report requested by Commissioner Heidi Carter would be scheduled.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions: Champions in Transportation Awards, Dr. Deborah Crandall, and Bull City YouthBuild
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Director Linda Thomas presented the 2018 Champions in Transportation Awards and proclamation recognizing Durham County ACCESS riders (including Leroy and Mary Cropper) and advocacy leaders. The board then recognized Dr. Deborah Crandall for her service as Interim Director of Durham Cooperative Extension, followed by Corey Wallinson and graduates from Bull City YouthBuild's 21-member second cohort sharing personal writings.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no questions or items pulled for separate discussion, the board unanimously approved the consent agenda (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a brief recess to tally ballots, staff announced the board's appointments: Jennifer Melvin Eiffher to the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee, Mary Ann Bond to the Animal Services Advisory Committee, Marilyn Cash to the Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee, and Patty Black to the Women's Commission.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Attorney-Client Privilege (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session to consult with the county attorney pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3). Upon returning to open session at 01:46:22, Chair Jacobs reported direction was given to staff and the meeting adjourned.

votes.discussion_detail: Unanimous approval of the 2019 work session minutes, followed by Chair Jacobs confirming a Gang Reduction Steering Committee report would be scheduled.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC "Resolution to Protect FNS from Impact of Federal Government Shutdowns"
meetings.executive_summary: This standalone video excerpt from the February 11, 2019 regular session features Chair Wendy Jacobs and DSS staff member Rhonda Stevens (speaking on behalf of DSS Director Ben Rose) presenting the Durham Board of County Commissioners' Resolution to Protect Food and Nutrition Services (FNS) from Impact of Federal Government Shutdowns. Chair Jacobs read the full resolution noting that over 36,000 Durham County residents across 17,000+ households (including 60% with children under 18 and 27.4% with adults 60 and older) depend on $4.5 million per month in SNAP benefits, and that local nonprofits meet only about 5% of food insecurity needs during normal operations. The resolution, signed by all five commissioners (Wendy Jacobs, James Hill Jr., Heidi Carter, Brenda A. Howerton, and Ellen W. Reckhow) on February 11, 2019, urged Senators Burr and Tillis and Representatives Butterfield and Price to designate SNAP as an essential service exempt from federal shutdowns and maintain federal funding. No formal floor vote appears in this excerpt.

agenda_items.title: Resolution to Protect Food and Nutrition Services (FNS/SNAP) from Federal Government Shutdowns
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs thanked DSS Director Ben Rose and DSS staff member Rhonda Stevens for preparing the resolution following a community stakeholder meeting, and Stevens emphasized that food and nutrition assistance is an essential service. Chair Jacobs read the full text citing 1.3 million North Carolina and 36,000+ Durham County SNAP recipients ($4.5 million monthly economic impact) and urging federal lawmakers to exempt SNAP from future government shutdowns; the resolution bore the names of all five seated commissioners dated February 11, 2019.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC February 11, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 11, 2019 regular session, Chair Wendy Jacobs read a formal board statement condemning recent ICE enforcement actions in Durham affecting at least six families and affirming support for Sheriff Clarence F. Birkhead's policy refusing to honor ICE detainers or facilitate immigration apprehensions. The board unanimously approved the January 14, 2019 meeting minutes (5-0), presented the Resolution to Protect Food and Nutrition Services (SNAP) from Impact of Federal Government Shutdowns alongside DSS staff Rhonda Stevens, and fielded a pre-consent inquiry on Item 19-0079 (Durham Crisis Response Center grant extension and the Lethality Assessment Program). Later in the meeting, commissioners discussed partnering on state RAD advocacy and county land availability—while cautioning against cash commitments—for a $566 million public housing redevelopment effort addressing 60% unemployment among work-able public housing adults. Staff also briefed the board on Durham Pre-K expansion ($1,250/child/month reimbursement, 18 quality-improvement 'pipeline' classrooms, and 5 new classrooms starting in March) and the 2019 property reappraisal (showing 19.5% value growth excluding 3.5% natural growth and explaining the statutory revenue-neutral rate calculation in response to taxpayer concerns).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Board Statement Condemning ICE Actions, and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting and read a board statement condemning recent ICE enforcement actions affecting at least six Durham families, noting they undermine trust in local law enforcement, and affirming the board's support for Sheriff Clarence F. Birkhead's policy not to honor ICE detainers. Announcements covered the Feb 12 DPS Town Hall at Neal Middle School, the Hayti Heritage Film Festival, the Durham YouthWork goal of 300+ paid summer internships, and recognition of Durham employers on a regional workplace list.

agenda_items.title: Approval of January 14, 2019 Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously (5-0) to approve the minutes of the January 14, 2019 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Resolution to Protect FNS/SNAP from Impact of Federal Government Shutdowns
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DSS staff member Rhonda Stevens spoke on behalf of Director Ben Rose, and Chair Jacobs read the resolution signed by all five commissioners urging federal lawmakers (Senators Burr and Tillis and Representatives Butterfield and Price) to classify SNAP as an essential service exempt from federal shutdowns, citing over 36,000 Durham County recipients and $4.5 million in monthly food and nutrition benefits.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (Item 19-0079: Durham Crisis Response Center Grant Extension)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During consent agenda review, a commissioner requested an offline explanation of the Lethality Assessment Program referenced in Item 19-0079 (a Memorandum of Understanding supporting the Durham Crisis Response Center grant extension).

agenda_items.title: Public Housing Redevelopment Partnership and Land Collaboration Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A housing presenter outlined a $566 million redevelopment plan ($400 million+ in construction) and workforce efforts with Durham Tech to address a 60% unemployment rate among work-able public housing adults. Commissioners offered to assist with state-level advocacy on RAD expansion and explore county land availability, while cautioning that county cash funding would be constrained by competing priorities such as universal pre-K.

agenda_items.title: Durham Pre-K Program Expansion Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported on Durham Pre-K expansion, noting programs are reimbursed at $1,250 per child per month, 18 classrooms (from 30+ applicants) were selected for intensive quality improvement technical assistance, and 5 new classrooms (from 19 applicants) would begin in March alongside coordination with NC Pre-K, El Centro Hispano, Book Harvest, and DPS.

agenda_items.title: 2019 Property Reappraisal Update and Revenue-Neutral Tax Rate Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Tax Administration staff (including Ryan Vincent) reported 19.5% value growth from the 2019 general reappraisal (excluding 3.5% annual natural growth, up from 14% over the 2008–2016 eight-year cycle) and explained the statutory requirement to include a revenue-neutral tax rate in the County Manager's recommended budget. Resident Mr. Walker raised concern that homeowners face March appeal deadlines before learning the adopted June tax rate, and commissioners encouraged residents to schedule staff appointments and file appeals as needed before adjourning.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2019-02-04 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 4, 2019 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, citizens addressed food insecurity following the 35-day federal government shutdown—with End Hunger Durham coordinator Betsy Kites urging a resolution against future shutdowns—and offered opposing views on restoring versus removing the Confederate monument. During consent agenda review, the Board discussed a $263,438 general fund balance amendment to upgrade computer-aided dispatch (CAD) systems, technical changes to the Environmental Affairs Board interlocal agreement with the City of Durham, updated 10-year property tax breakout charts, and a roughly $800,000 mid-year Social Services foster care shortfall driven by 14% annual cost growth and extended care for 18-year-olds. Commissioners also discussed replacing the county's administrative alcohol policy with a misdemeanor-enforceable ordinance across 54 county facilities—including libraries, the Human Services Complex courtyard, Admin II restaurants/catering, and future parking-deck commercial spaces—and reviewed OneDrive access and staff capacity for board directives. The Board voted unanimously by voice vote (moved by Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by James Hill) to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) on economic development incentives, later returning to report staff direction and adjourn unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks and Citizen Comments (Federal Shutdown Food Aid and Confederate Monument)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Chair opened the session with the public charge and heard from four citizens. Betsy Kites of End Hunger Durham warned that the 35-day federal shutdown pushed tens of thousands of Durham residents closer to hunger and urged the Board to pass a resolution demanding Congress and the President avoid future shutdowns. Subsequent speakers split over the Confederate monument: one recommended following state law by restoring the statue or a facsimile with agreed contextual plaques, while another cited the 13th Amendment and civil rights law to demand permanent removal, threatening litigation up to the U.S. Supreme Court.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review: CAD Upgrade, Environmental Affairs Board ILA, and Foster Care Shortfall
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed a $263,438 general fund balance budget ordinance amendment to upgrade computer-aided dispatch (CAD) systems, technical amendments to the Environmental Affairs Board interlocal agreement with the City of Durham, and updated 10-year revenue and property tax breakout charts. Social Services staff reported an FY 2018-19 foster care shortfall exceeding $800,000 after an earlier $1.2 million request was deferred to mid-year, citing roughly 14% annual cost growth since 2012 and about 35 youth aged 18+ remaining in or returning to care beyond 304 base cases. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow emphasized expanding preventive System of Care efforts, and staff noted North Carolina's expected 2020–2021 opt-in to the federal Families First Prevention Act would unlock federal prevention dollars.

agenda_items.title: County Facility Alcohol Policy and Proposed Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners and staff discussed converting the county's administrative alcohol policy into a formal ordinance modeled on the City of Durham's ordinance to enable misdemeanor enforcement and designate permitted areas across 54 county facilities, including downtown and regional libraries, the Human Services Complex courtyard, Admin II restaurant/catering spaces, and commercial spaces in two upcoming parking decks. Commissioner Heidi Carter supported moving to an ordinance and framed the remaining policy question as use versus sales. Commissioners expressed openness to event alcohol use while weighing whether to restrict events to beer and wine or cautiously allow full pours for occasions such as weddings.

agenda_items.title: Board Directives Spreadsheet Access and Staff Work Plan Capacity
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff member Drew and IS&T Director Greg Mero walked commissioners through OneDrive/SharePoint link issues that prevented some members from seeing the updated directives spreadsheet amid older shared files. Commissioners also discussed protecting staff capacity for budget-endorsed work plan items and clarifying how directives bolded in Clerk Monica's minutes are tracked.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Economic Development Incentives (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4)) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board moved into closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss the location or expansion of businesses and tentative economic development incentives and contracts, on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Vice Chair James Hill that passed unanimously by voice vote. After roughly 44 minutes in closed session, the Board returned to open session, reported giving direction to staff, and adjourned unanimously on a motion by Commissioner Reckhow.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC January 28, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the January 28, 2019 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners, which began with a unanimous agenda addition (5-0) for R.N. Harris Elementary School third-grade students to thank Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton for providing free county-government educational booklets, followed by approval of the December 3, 2018 minutes as amended (5-0) and Consent Agenda Item 19-0019 (5-0). Ceremonial items honored Durham County Library staff members Hotoko Burke and Mark Donnelly for NCPLDA awards, recognized Higher Orbits and Team Orion students whose fungal radiation-absorption experiment launched to the International Space Station, and proclaimed February 2019 as Together for Resilient Youth (TRY) Prevention Month. Following a substantive policy debate over a proposed Comprehensive Plan policy evaluating the net impact of Neighborhood Protection Overlays (NPOs) and local historic districts on affordable housing—in which Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow favored severing or broadening the language while Commissioner Heidi Carter and Chair Wendy Jacobs supported retaining it—the board unanimously adopted the 2017 Evaluation and Assessment Report (5-0) after planning staff agreed to consider broader language when reporting back on methodology. The board also unanimously adopted a $50 million General Obligation Refunding Bond order and resolution (5-0), completed advisory board ballot appointments, and met in closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(6) (5-0) before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Pledge of Allegiance, Agenda Adjustment, and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the January 28, 2019 meeting to order, delivered the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The board voted 5-0 to add a student presentation from R.N. Harris Elementary School to the announcements section, and Chair Jacobs highlighted GoTriangle fare relief for federal workers, the LEAP heating assistance program, Golden Leaf Award nominations, Durham YouthWorks summer internships, the My Brother's Keeper Boys of Color Conference, Durham's 150th anniversary kickoff, Alert Durham, and 43 active advisory boards. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton then welcomed R.N. Harris Elementary students, parents, teachers, the principal, and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga to read thank-you letters for 3,000 free county-government educational booklets she distributed to third graders.

agenda_items.title: Approval of December 3, 2018 Meeting Minutes (As Amended)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton requested a correction to the December 3, 2018 minutes noting that she had been delayed roughly 10 minutes by traffic and was not present for the board's first vote. Chair Jacobs directed the clerk to insert the arrival time and explanation, and the board unanimously approved the minutes as amended. Commissioner Howerton also asked staff to implement a more systematic process for tracking and following up on directives issued during board meetings.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions: Durham County Library NCPLDA Awards and Higher Orbits Go For Launch! Team Orion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Library Director Tammy Baggett recognized graphic designer and photographer Hotoko Burke for winning the NCPLDA Public Relations Award for chronicling the Main Library renovation, and East Regional librarian Mark Donnelly for winning the NCPLDA Children's Programming Award for Bike Month free helmet and bike-rodeo events. The board also recognized IT Manager Matt Lowbridge, Higher Orbits founder Michelle Lucas, the Durham Library Foundation, and Team Orion high school students whose fungal radiation-shielding experiment from a free library STEAM camp was launched to the International Space Station.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Together for Resilient Youth (TRY) Prevention Month (February 2019)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs read a proclamation declaring February 2019 as Together for Resilient Youth (TRY) Prevention Month in Durham County, citing 2017 Youth Risk Behavior Survey figures on youth vaping, cigarette, alcohol, marijuana, and prescription drug use as well as suicide ideation. TRY leader Wanda Boone highlighted declining substance-use trends, compliance checks across nearly 450 Durham alcohol outlets that earned a national CADCA Got Outcomes award, risks from high-potency marijuana and fentanyl, and school bullying prevention, with commissioners praising her work on the county ACEs Task Force.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Item 19-0019)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs returned to the skipped consent agenda containing a single item, 19-0019. On motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and second by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, the board approved Item 19-0019 unanimously with no discussion.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Adoption: 2017 Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) of the Durham Comprehensive Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Laura Woods presented the 2017 Evaluation and Assessment Report (previously approved 7-0 by Durham City Council), which rectifies nine 2017 City-adopted Future Land Use Map (FLUM) amendments, updates demographic and land-use demand data, reclassifies three conservation-easement parcels near Eno River State Park and Valley Springs Park to Recreation and Open Space, and adds a policy requiring staff to evaluate net impacts on housing affordability and supply for proposed Neighborhood Protection Overlays (NPOs) and local historic districts. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow expressed concern that the new policy unfairly singled out NPOs and historic districts rather than evaluating broader rezoning impacts, while Commissioner Heidi Carter and Chair Wendy Jacobs defended the targeted NPO evaluation; after staff agreed to consider broader language when reporting back on evaluation methodology to JCCPC, the public hearing closed with no speakers and the board unanimously adopted the resolution.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Adoption: $50 Million General Obligation Refunding Bonds (Series 2019)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director Susan Tezai presented a $50 million General Obligation refunding bond order and authorizing resolution to refund 2017 Bond Anticipation Notes (BANs) representing the first drawdown under the 2016 $170 million bond referendum, noting a second draw program would come before the board within a month. Following a public hearing with no speakers, the board voted unanimously to adopt both the refunding bond order and the bond issuance resolution.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners cast ballot votes for county advisory board and commission vacancies, with staff clarifying notation for board-recommended and incumbent candidates. The clerk announced selections of Catherine Thomas (Durham County Hospital Corporation), William Aiken and Ledana Summers (Open Space and Trails Commission), Almond Spencer Curtis, Rosemary Jackson, and Victoria Revel (Public Health Board), and Beverly Thor (Transportation Advisory Board).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(6)) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session to consult with its attorney under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and to consider qualifications, performance, or conditions of appointment or employment of an individual public officer or employee under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6). Upon returning to open session at 02:57:10, Chair Jacobs stated the board gave direction to staff and entertained a motion to adjourn, which passed unanimously.

disagreements.issue: Scope of Proposed Comprehensive Plan Policy Evaluating Affordable Housing Impacts of NPOs and Local Historic Districts
disagreements.summary: During consideration of the 2017 Evaluation and Assessment Report, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow objected to singling out only Neighborhood Protection Overlays (NPOs) and local historic districts for housing affordability impact evaluations and asked to sever or broaden the wording, whereas Commissioner Heidi Carter and Chair Wendy Jacobs argued the targeted policy was an appropriate informational step prompted by City Council's Old West Durham NPO debate.
disagreements.side_a_position: Sever the policy back to the Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) or broaden its wording to evaluate housing affordability impacts across all major land-use changes, not just NPOs and historic districts.
side_a_arguments: Citing Planning Commissioner Tom Miller's comments and National Trust/CityLab research, older smaller buildings in historic districts and NPOs often preserve naturally occurring affordable housing and prevent teardowns.
Targeting only NPOs and historic districts casts an unfair cloud over neighborhood preservation while ignoring rezonings (such as residential-to-commercial) that also affect housing affordability.
The proposed policy had not been discussed at JCCPC and lacked context in the report.
disagreements.side_b_position: Retain and approve the policy as drafted so planning staff evaluates the net impact of proposed NPOs and local historic districts on housing affordability and supply.
side_b_arguments: The policy grew directly out of City Council's Old West Durham NPO deliberations, where restrictions on accessory dwelling units and duplexes raised long-term housing supply concerns.
Planning staff already removed the earlier directive requiring staff to recommend denial, leaving only a neutral informational analysis that could also show positive affordability impacts.
Overlay districts impose broad area-wide restrictions distinct from individual parcel rezonings, and Durham City Council had already approved the report 7-0.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved by compromise without a split vote: planning staff agreed to consider proposing broadened policy language covering other land-use categories when returning to JCCPC with the evaluation methodology, after which Commissioner Reckhow moved adoption of the 2017 EAR resolution and it passed unanimously 5-0.
