meetings.title: Durham County BOCC January 14, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the January 14, 2019 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners, opening with remarks by Jacobs and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton mourning recent gun and domestic violence—including the fatal shooting of a 22-year-old mother and her 10-month-old infant—alongside ceremonial proclamations for National Mentoring Month and Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. The board unanimously approved the December 20, 2018 minutes (5-0), reordered business items after public hearings (5-0), approved Consent Agenda items 18-1133 through 19-0030 (5-0), and approved pulled Item 18-1191 as amended (5-0) to rename the 'Durham-Orange fund' reference to 'Durham Transit Fund'. In three public hearings, the board unanimously approved UDO Text Amendment TC1800002 (Omnibus Changes 12, 5-0 on consistency and 5-0 on the ordinance), UDO Text Amendment TC1800008 (Text-Only Development Plans, 5-0 on consistency and 5-0 on the ordinance), and a $750,000 economic development incentive allocation for gene-therapy company AveXis (Project Bengal, 5-0) tied to a $60 million investment and 200 jobs. The board also reviewed a clean FY2018 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) audit from Cherry Bekaert, debated neighborhood-character versus aggressive housing-supply trade-offs during an Expanding Housing Choices briefing, outlined 2019 General Assembly legislative priorities, and entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) (5-0) before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Remarks on Gun and Domestic Violence, and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the January 14, 2019 meeting, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance before addressing recent gun violence and the fatal shooting of a 22-year-old mother and her 10-month-old baby, citing local domestic violence support resources and a third-year federal first-responder training grant on the agenda. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton shared a personal connection to the victims' family and urged the community to confront violence, after which Chair Jacobs announced the Jan. 15 MLK observance, Jan. 21 holiday closures, LEAP heating assistance, Golden Leaf Awards, Durham YouthWorks internships, Durham's 150th anniversary, and Alert Durham.

agenda_items.title: Approval of December 20, 2018 Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On motion by Commissioner Heidi Carter and second by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, the board unanimously approved the minutes from its December 20, 2018 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: National Mentoring Month (January 2019)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs read a proclamation declaring January 2019 as National Mentoring Month in Durham County, noting a minor text correction from 'more likely' to 'less likely' regarding school truancy statistics. Charles Hamilton Houston Foundation Executive Director Dewarren Langley and representatives from more than a dozen local mentoring, school, workforce, and violence-interruption organizations gave brief remarks on coordinating youth mentorship, with Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow and Brenda A. Howerton linking the work to the county's ACEs Task Force.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustment: Move Regular Business Items After Public Hearings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved to adjust the agenda to place the three regular business items (18-1198, 19-0002, and 19-0033) after the three public hearings, recommending that order as standard practice going forward. Seconded by Vice Chair James Hill, the motion carried unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring the Life and Service of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill read the board's resolution honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and recounting his 1960–1964 civil rights addresses in Durham. MLK Steering Committee Chair Reverend Lucas and committee members thanked commissioners for funding 12 student scholarships and outlined the week's commemorative schedule including the wreath-laying, prayer breakfast, unity march, Book Harvest Day of Service, Jubilee Home workday, and religious service.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 18-1133 through 19-0030) and Pulled Item 18-1191 (Transit Cost-Share Amendment)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before voting, commissioners highlighted Bull City 150 sponsorship, a housing-rehab grant study (Item 0022) showing half of Durham households are housing- and transit-cost burdened, the updated firearm discharge ordinance (Item 19-0029), federal shutdown impacts on DSS food-assistance funding (secured through February), and continuation funding for the Durham Integrated Violence Response System grant (Item 0006). The board unanimously approved Consent Agenda items 18-1133 through 19-0030 excluding pulled Item 18-1191 (5-0), then unanimously approved Item 18-1191 as amended (5-0) to replace a reference to the 'Durham-Orange fund' with 'Durham Transit Fund' on page 1 of the contractor-change amendment.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Adoption: UDO Text Amendment TC1800002 (Omnibus Changes 12)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Michael Stock presented UDO Text Amendment TC1800002 containing technical corrections and minor policy updates—including removing parking minimums on very narrow infill lots and expanding the affordable housing density bonus from 1:1 to 2:1—noting that Neighborhood Protection Overlay process changes (Section 8) were removed by Planning Commission and referred back to staff. After brief questions and a public hearing with no speakers, the board unanimously adopted both the Statement of Consistency (5-0) and the ordinance amendment (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Adoption: UDO Text Amendment TC1800008 (Text-Only Development Plans)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Michael Stock presented UDO Text Amendment TC1800008 establishing a limited text-only development plan option for zoning map change requests to allow proffers limiting permitted uses under Article 5, previously recommended 12-0 by the Planning Commission. Chair Wendy Jacobs praised the streamlined option as user-friendly and less costly for applicants, and following a public hearing with no speakers, the board unanimously adopted the N.C.G.S. 153A-341 Statement of Consistency (5-0) and the ordinance amendment (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Approval: $750,000 Economic Development Incentive for AveXis (Project Bengal)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Director Andy Miracle presented a $750,000 economic development investment allocation for gene-therapy firm AveXis (Project Bengal), contingent on a minimum $60 million investment and 200 new jobs averaging ~$76,000 in annual wages alongside workforce partnerships with Durham Public Schools CTE, Durham Tech, and NCWorks and MWBE purchasing commitments. Greater Durham Chamber of Commerce representative Jeff Durham spoke in support during the public hearing, commissioners commended the binding community-benefit and living-wage provisions while confirming the final contract will return to the board, and the board voted 5-0 to approve the allocation.

agenda_items.title: Presentation: FY2018 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) and External Audit
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Susan Tezai introduced Cherry Bekaert engagement partner Scott Duda, who reported unmodified ('clean') financial statement and Yellow Book audit opinions for FY2018, no management letter or material weaknesses, four internal control significant deficiencies across grant compliance testing (including one repeat finding from 2017), and timely Local Government Commission submission with zero LGC comments. Commissioners questioned retiree health benefit increases under GASB 75, >10% budget underspending variances in General Administration and Economic/Physical Development, and a $16 million DSS general fund amendment reduction, requesting dedicated CAFR review time at the upcoming budget retreat.

agenda_items.title: Presentation and Discussion: Expanding Housing Choices (Missing Middle UDO Proposals)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Patrick Young and Senior Planner Michael Stock briefed the board on the Expanding Housing Choices initiative ahead of a February 12 Planning Commission hearing and spring BOCC vote, outlining urban-tier proposals for infill lot-width reductions, larger Accessory Dwelling Units (up to 800 sq. ft.), duplexes across urban-tier residential districts, and small-house/small-lot and 12-foot flag-lot options while deferring triplexes, quads, and cottage courts. Commissioners debated the trade-offs extensively: Ellen W. Reckhow raised concerns about overriding Neighborhood Protection Overlays and small-lot rows tearing neighborhood fabric; Heidi Carter urged aggressive supply expansion over preserving neighborhood fabric; James Hill warned against absentee investors accelerating gentrification in lower-income areas; and Chair Wendy Jacobs highlighted ADU design/financing pilots, transit access, and revisiting the three-unrelated-occupant cap.

agenda_items.title: Discussion: 2019 NC General Assembly Legislative Priorities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County legislative staff briefed commissioners ahead of the January 22 legislative breakfast with Durham's General Assembly delegation—noting newly seated Representatives Zack Hawkins and Robert Reives II and the end of the legislative supermajority—and outlined initial priorities across criminal justice, education, human services, and transportation. Commissioners requested adding or emphasizing funding for Raise the Age youth detention/home facilities, drug and mental health treatment courts, additional Assistant District Attorneys, City-backed expungement legislation, K-3 class-size flexibility, a $1.3B statewide K-12 school construction bond, authority to convey school property for teacher housing, Medicaid expansion, opioid funding, tenant eviction reform, and increasing state transit funding above 4%.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4)) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss economic development incentives and the location or expansion of industries or businesses. Returning at 04:14:23, Chair Jacobs reported that the board gave direction to staff and entertained a motion to adjourn, which passed unanimously.

disagreements.issue: Neighborhood Character Protection vs. Aggressive Missing-Middle Housing Supply in Expanding Housing Choices
disagreements.summary: During the Expanding Housing Choices briefing, commissioners diverged on how aggressively to loosen urban-tier zoning rules: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and Vice Chair James Hill emphasized neighborhood fabric, Neighborhood Protection Overlays (NPOs), and gentrification/absentee-investor risks, while Commissioner Heidi Carter urged prioritizing maximum housing supply and future affordability over existing neighborhood preservation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Prioritize protecting existing neighborhood fabric, honoring Neighborhood Protection Overlays, and guarding against speculative investor conversions and displacement in lower-income neighborhoods.
side_a_arguments: Overriding NPO provisions undermines extensive community work put into overlays like Old West Durham and Tuscaloosa-Lakewood.
Dividing a block face into six small lots in a row would create a tear in the fabric of established neighborhoods; clustered cottage courts or zero-lot-line designs would be more context-sensitive.
Without owner-occupancy rules, outside investors in less affluent neighborhoods could buy properties solely to maximize units without caring about neighborhood character, compounding gentrification.
disagreements.side_b_position: Pursue missing-middle housing supply and urban-tier density as aggressively as possible to address Durham's affordability crisis for future and current residents.
side_b_arguments: Expanding housing options and missing-middle supply should be the board's primary driver rather than preserving existing neighborhood fabric through overlays.
With 160,000 new residents projected over 25–30 years, failing to expand in-town supply will drive worse unaffordability, sprawl, and climate/infrastructure costs.
Suburban neighborhoods should also be examined for duplex and townhome opportunities where covenants do not prohibit them.
disagreements.resolution: Informational work-session discussion with no formal vote; Planning Director Patrick Young committed to refining context-sensitive standards with neighborhood groups ahead of the February 12, 2019 Planning Commission public hearing and April/May 2019 board vote.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2019-01-07 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 7, 2019 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, citizen speaker Matthew Mick Wiker urged restoration of the Confederate Soldiers Memorial ahead of a City-County committee report, and County Attorney Saller introduced new Risk Manager Janelle Owens. Reviewing consent items individually, Commissioner Heidi Carter, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, and other commissioners questioned staff on Item 1133 (a parking deck contract amendment) regarding low utilization, safety concerns, and uncaptured DPAC/Durham Bulls event revenue prior to a March RFP, and examined Item 1193 regarding restricted fund balance re-appropriations for unspent grant and state partnership dollars. In the afternoon, interim tax leaders Risa and Ryan presented the 2019 general reappraisal timeline and three-step appeals process (with the Board of Equalization and Review meeting April 3–May 3), while Vice Chair James Hill and Commissioner Howerton highlighted recent Roxboro Road and countywide gunshot injuries to urge legislative action on gun violence alongside discussion of incorporating renewable energy vehicle goals into February budget planning. The Board voted unanimously by voice vote (moved by Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by James Hill) to enter closed session on economic development incentives, subsequently reporting direction to staff and adjourning unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks, Citizen Comment on Confederate Memorial, and Risk Manager Introduction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the work session with the public charge and invited citizen speaker Matthew Mick Wiker, who noted the City-County Committee on the Confederate Memorial would issue its report the next day and argued state law and county insurance required restoring the memorial. Following public comment, County Attorney Saller introduced Janelle Owens as Durham County's new risk manager, noting her prior experience with the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority alongside former risk manager David English.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review: Item 1133 (Parking Deck Contract) and Item 1193 (Restricted Fund Balance)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because commissioners had questions on nearly every consent item, the Board walked through items individually. On Item 1133, Commissioner Heidi Carter questioned paying for an added position and higher salary in a delayed parking-deck contract amendment; staff cited an added 24-hour call service and an upcoming March RFP, while commissioners raised safety concerns in the nearly empty deck during events and demanded FY 2018 revenue figures and an action plan ahead of baseball season to pursue DPAC and Bulls Stadium partnerships, with Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seeking clarification on the item's three parts. On Item 1193, Finance staff explained that appropriating restricted fund balance (including JAG, sheriff, museum, public health, and social services dollars) reflects standard GAAP year-end rollovers without penalty.

agenda_items.title: FY 2019 General Reappraisal Update and Appeals Timeline
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim tax leaders Risa and Ryan presented the 2019 general reappraisal (effective January 1, 2019), detailing property characteristic verification, sales analysis, and application of the Board-approved schedule of values. They outlined the notice mailing schedule, a two-week informal review period, and the three-step appeal process culminating with the Board of Equalization and Review convening April 3 and closing real-property appeals on May 3 at 5:00 PM. Commissioners urged staff to highlight the revenue-neutral rate and property-value-versus-tax-rate distinction in brochures and press releases so residents remain informed and calm.

agenda_items.title: Gun Violence Discussion, Regular Meeting Scheduling, and Renewable Energy Budget Considerations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill addressed a shooting the prior day on Roxboro Road that injured a 13-year-old girl waiting at a fast-food restaurant, calling for reasonable gun control from the General Assembly and community changes to reject violence; Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton cited Herald Sun reporting on 180 people injured in 160 gun incidents and recent multi-victim shootings. Commissioners also discussed scheduling an item for a regular January meeting and raised whether the Board's renewable energy resolution (including vehicle purchasing practices) should inform February budget retreat discussions versus awaiting a formal implementation plan.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Economic Development Incentives and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board moved into closed session regarding industry/business location or expansion and tentative economic development incentives (referencing N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) in the transcript) on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Vice Chair James Hill, passing unanimously by voice vote. Upon returning to open session, the Chair reported direction had been given to staff, and the Board adjourned unanimously on a motion by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Reckhow.

votes.item_title: Motion to Adjourn to Closed Session on Economic Development Incentives
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote with all five commissioners confirmed participating in the meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to adjourn to closed session to discuss business location/expansion and tentative economic development incentives (citing N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) in the transcript).

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC Dec 20 Live
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the December 20, 2018 Durham County Board of Commissioners regular meeting, held at 2:00 p.m. after Monday's session was rescheduled due to a snowstorm. The board unanimously approved adding an Eno River Association presentation (5-0), approved the November 26, 2018 minutes (5-0), and passed all consent agenda items except Item 18-1124 (5-0), highlighting eight grant-funded items across departments including the Sheriff's Office and Public Health. After amending the 2019 board calendar (Item 18-1124) to correct NCACC Legislative Goals Conference dates, reschedule a June 13 budget work session, and add an August 13 joint city-county meeting, the board approved the calendar (5-0) and authorized moving forward with a $35,000 Age-Friendly Durham Master Aging Plan following an update from the Durham Center for Senior Life (5-0). Following commissioner comments on surplus property marketing and delinquent tax foreclosure policies, Open Space and Trails Commission appointments, and a closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6), the four remaining commissioners unanimously appointed Teresa Harrison as Interim Tax Administrator (4-0; Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton had departed prior to closed session).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Pledge of Allegiance, Agenda Adjustments, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the rescheduled December 20, 2018 meeting to order at 2:00 p.m., read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The board voted 5-0 to add an Eno River Association presentation to ceremonial items, followed by announcements on FEMA disaster rental assistance, the Welcome Baby coat drive, and LIEAP energy bill assistance.

agenda_items.title: Approval of November 26, 2018 Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered the minutes from the November 26, 2018 meeting. Commissioner James Hill moved approval, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded, and the motion passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Presentations: Eno River Association and Transportation Champions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Eno River Association Executive Director Robin Jacobs and Milo Pyne addressed the board during the annual ceremonial presentation. Chair Jacobs also recognized Durham County ACCESS transit users and transportation champions for providing critical mobility to work and medical care.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 18-1124)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners pulled Item 18-1124 (the 2019 board calendar) for separate edits and highlighted Item 18-1180 and eight grant-funded consent items benefiting departments including the Sheriff's Office and Public Health, as well as a private-sector Credit Suisse grant. The board unanimously approved all remaining consent agenda items through 18-119D.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 18-1124: 2019 Board Calendar and Excused Absence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners corrected the 2019 calendar dates for the NCACC Legislative Goals Conference (January 10-11), removed the June 13 six-hour budget work session for rescheduling due to Commissioner Reckhow's absence, fixed the Monday August 12 regular session label, and added an August 13 joint city-county meeting. The board approved the amended calendar 5-0 and granted Commissioner Reckhow an excused absence for a January 9 joint meeting 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Durham Center for Senior Life Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Judy Kinney presented an update on the Durham Center for Senior Life, detailing its downtown center, adult day program, and congregate meal sites on Fayetteville Street, JFK Towers, North Roxboro, and Little River. She noted an annual budget just under $1,650,000, with 70% derived from government contracts and relatively flat funding over the prior four years.

agenda_items.title: Age-Friendly Durham Master Aging Plan Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented plans to develop an Age-Friendly Durham Master Aging Plan following the prior livability assessment, outlining a $35,000 project budget largely for contractor facilitation of roughly 25 meetings and steering committee coordination with Partnership for Seniors. The board voted unanimously to approve moving forward with the plan.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Comments, Boards and Commissions Appointments, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Reckhow raised accelerating surplus property marketing with Joint City-County Planning and DFI and asked for a report on tax foreclosure policy for properties delinquent more than a year. The board announced the selection of Dave Connolly and Tisha Wymore to the Open Space and Trails Commission, after which Commissioner Howerton stated she was leaving and would not stay for closed session; the board then entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6).

agenda_items.title: Appointment of Interim Tax Administrator
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Upon returning from closed session and reporting that staff had been given direction, Chair Jacobs entertained a motion to appoint Teresa Harrison as Interim Tax Administrator. The four remaining commissioners approved the appointment unanimously before adjourning.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-12-13 8:30 AM - Special Meeting (Thursday Meeting Date)
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 13, 2018 Special Meeting presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board of County Commissioners convened to reschedule its cancelled December 10, 2018 regular meeting following inclement weather in accordance with N.C.G.S. 153A-40. With Commissioners Brenda A. Howerton and James Hill not yet present at the start of the morning session, Chair Jacobs, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, and Commissioner Heidi Carter voted 3-0 to amend the 2018 meeting calendar to hold the rescheduled regular session at 2:00 PM on Thursday, December 20, 2018, accommodating schedules and avoiding an evening session for staff. The three commissioners then voted 3-0 to adjourn into closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to discuss personnel matters involving the tax administrator. Following closed session, with Vice Chair James Hill present, the Board reported giving direction to staff and adjourned unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Amendment of 2018 Meeting Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the special meeting to order at 8:40 a.m., read the public charge, and explained that under N.C.G.S. 153A-40 the Board needed to formally reschedule its December 10, 2018 regular meeting cancelled due to inclement weather. With Commissioners Brenda A. Howerton and James Hill noted as absent at the start, Chair Jacobs, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, and Commissioner Heidi Carter discussed calendar conflicts and agreed on a 2:00 p.m. afternoon meeting on Thursday, December 20, 2018 to avoid requiring staff at night. On motion of Commissioner Reckhow, seconded by Commissioner Carter, the Board amended the 2018 calendar 3-0.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) (Tax Administrator Personnel Matter)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs noted at the outset that the Board would discuss the tax administrator and read the statutory citation for closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) regarding the qualifications, competence, performance, conditions of appointment, or complaints involving an individual public officer or employee. On motion of Commissioner Carter, seconded by Commissioner Reckhow, the Board voted 3-0 to enter closed session.

agenda_items.title: Report Out of Closed Session and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning to open session after approximately 94 minutes, Chair Jacobs reported that the Board had adjourned from closed session and given direction to staff. With Vice Chair James Hill now present alongside Commissioners Reckhow and Carter, the Board voted unanimously by voice to adjourn.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC Work Session Dec 3 LIve
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 3, 2018 organizational work session, County Attorney Lowell Siler presided over receipt of Soil and Water Conservation District Supervisor election certificates for Natalie Murdock and David Harris and the unanimous re-election of Chair Wendy Jacobs (5-0), after which Chair Jacobs presided and Vice Chair James Hill was unanimously re-elected (5-0). The board approved public official bonds (5-0), witnessed the swearing-in of Murdock and Harris by District Court Judge Jaretta Walker, and voted unanimously to suspend the rules (5-0) and set the salary of the incoming sheriff (5-0). During work session review, commissioners disagreed over the proposed 2019 meeting calendar—Commissioner Heidi Carter declined to approve past June and proposed adding a second monthly work session on Thursday afternoons, whereas Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton urged approving at least through August for advance scheduling—leaving the calendar deferred to January. Commissioners also questioned capital cost overruns on Item 1130 ($2.7M over budget note), Item 1156 (over $4M total for Admin II 7th floor upfit), and Item 1158 (Detention Center HVAC grille and bunk bed safety modifications), directed the County Attorney to bring back the updated firearms ordinance, and entered closed session (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Organizational Business: Election Certificates, Selection of Chair and Vice Chair, Public Official Bonds, and Oaths
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Lowell Siler presided for the annual receipt of election certificates for Soil and Water Conservation District Supervisors Natalie Murdock and David Harris and conducted the election of Wendy Jacobs as Chair (5-0). Chair Jacobs then presided over the election of James Hill as Vice Chair (5-0), approval of public official bonds (5-0), and oaths administered by Judge Jaretta Walker.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident John Tarantino of 515 North Hyde Park spoke regarding traffic congestion and difficulties navigating NC-147 construction.

agenda_items.title: Suspend Rules and Set Salary of Incoming Sheriff
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs entertained a request to suspend the rules and act immediately on setting the salary of the incoming sheriff. The board voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and then voted 5-0 to approve and set the incoming sheriff's salary.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of 2019 Board Meeting Calendar and Second Monthly Work Session Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners debated the draft 2019 meeting schedule, with Commissioner Heidi Carter declining to vote past June and renewing her proposal to move work sessions to the Thursday afternoons following Monday regular meetings and add a second monthly work session. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton asked to approve at least through August so commissioners could plan ahead, and the board deferred action until January.

agenda_items.title: Review of Capital Budget Overruns, Admin II 7th Floor Upfit, and Detention Center Safety Upgrades
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners questioned Item 1130 ($65,000 addition and a $2.7 million over-budget reference), Item 1156 (Admin II 7th floor LOBs-funded upfit pushing total project cost over $4 million), and Item 1158 (Detention Center HVAC grilles, bunk bed safety modifications, and pod staff desks with C2 Wilson targeted for October 2019 completion). Commissioner Reckhow pressed staff to avoid letting surplus property sales languish so one-time revenues could help offset capital overruns.

agenda_items.title: Directives Follow-Up (Firearms Ordinance) and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners asked the County Attorney to bring back clarifications to the firearms ordinance—citing a Rougemont complaint dating back to early 2017 and preempted provisions—for the next regular meeting. Rather than recessing until 2:00 p.m., the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and (a)(3).

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC Nov 26 Live
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the November 26, 2018 regular meeting of the Durham County Board of Commissioners. The board unanimously moved the ACEs Task Force resolution from regular business to ceremonial items (5-0), approved the October 22, November 5, and November 13, 2018 meeting minutes (5-0) while requesting future minutes record adjournment times, and honored the late Dr. Brenda Estelle Armstrong ('Coach Doc') and Captain Aleem for rescuing a mother and two children on I-85. Later in the session, the board unanimously approved submitting two amended NCACC legislative goals—on resiliency and volunteer firefighters—along with previously passed SNAP farm bill language (5-0), declining to draft a new Medicaid expansion goal due to the end-of-month deadline. Commissioners also received the County Manager's updated Power BI quarterly management report under the Managing for Results framework, clarified advisory board attendance rules, and appointed members to four boards and commissions.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustment, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the November 26, 2018 meeting, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The board voted 5-0 to move the ACEs Task Force resolution to ceremonial items, shared community announcements including the November 30 light rail draft EIS comment deadline, and approved the October 22, November 5, and November 13 minutes 5-0 while requesting that future minutes include adjournment times.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Resolution Honoring Dr. Brenda Estelle Armstrong and Recognition of Captain Aleem
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board presented a resolution honoring the life and legacy of Dr. Brenda Estelle Armstrong ('Coach Doc'), a pioneering Duke pediatric cardiologist and 37-year Durham Striders coach and team physician who passed away on October 7, 2018, accepted by Durham Striders Director Frank Davis. Commissioners also recognized Captain Aleem for rescuing two children and their mother from an overturned vehicle on I-85.

agenda_items.title: NCACC Legislative Goals Submission (Resiliency, Volunteer Firefighters, and SNAP Farm Bill Resolution)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following discussion of NCACC legislative goal submissions before the end-of-November deadline, Commissioner Heidi Carter suggested adding SNAP benefits and Medicaid expansion. Because time did not permit drafting a new Medicaid expansion proposal, the board voted 5-0 to submit the two amended goals on resiliency and volunteer firefighters together with previously adopted SNAP farm bill language.

agenda_items.title: Quarterly Management Report (Managing for Results / Power BI Rollout)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager presented the second evolution of the quarterly management report powered by Power BI under the Managing for Results strategy. The dashboard enables drill-downs into five-year expenditure and revenue trends, adopted budgets, departmental FTEs, and strategic plan performance metrics.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Comments and Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners offered brief remarks on a recent D.C. trip and transit/zoning articles and clarified with County Attorney Lowell Siler that advisory board removal thresholds require exceeding 50% absences, three consecutive unexcused absences, or five total absences. The board appointed Deidre Thornlow (Nursing Home CAC), David Morgan (Planning Commission), Hannah Horn, Fred Mayak, and Natalie Murdock (Transportation Advisory Board), and Elizabeth Morel (Women's Commission).

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-11-26 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 26, 2018 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board of County Commissioners opened by entering a closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) before reconvening in open session, moving the ACES Task Force resolution to ceremonial items (5-0), and approving October and November 2018 minutes (5-0) with a request from Commissioner Heidi Carter to log adjournment times in future minutes. The Board honored the life and legacy of Dr. Brenda Estelle Armstrong ('Coach Doc')—received by Durham Striders Director Frank Davis—and recognized Captain Aleem for a highway crash rescue on I-85. Later in the session (with the middle portion of the transcript truncated), the Board voted 5-0 to advance federal legislative priorities on resiliency, volunteer firefighters, and a previously adopted SNAP resolution, reviewed County Manager Wendell Davis's second-generation Power BI Quarterly Management Report, discussed regional hurricane resiliency planning and Moody's credit considerations, and completed appointments to three advisory boards before adjourning unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the start of the evening, the Board voted unanimously by voice to adjourn into closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) regarding personnel qualifications, performance, conditions of appointment, or complaints. Returning around 00:53:50, Chair Jacobs reported the Board had given direction to staff.

agenda_items.title: Open Session Call to Order, Agenda Adjustment, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs opened the public session, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. On motion of Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by Commissioner Heidi Carter, the Board voted 5-0 to move the ACES Task Force resolution from regular business to ceremonial items. Chair Jacobs then shared announcements including the John W. Hatch Health Lecture at Shaw University, downtown tree lightings, the GoTriangle light rail Draft EIS supplemental assessment comment deadline (Nov. 30, 2018), National Adoption Awareness Month, and Innovate Durham demo day.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (Oct. 22, Nov. 5, and Nov. 13, 2018)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered minutes from the October 22 regular session, November 5 work session, and November 13 regular session. Commissioner Carter requested that future minutes record the adjournment time so commissioners could track meeting-length trends, and Chair Jacobs commended Clerk staff Monica and Terry for bringing the minutes completely up to date. Moved by Commissioner Reckhow and seconded by Vice Chair James Hill, the minutes passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Resolutions: Dr. Brenda Estelle Armstrong and Captain Aleem
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read a special resolution honoring the life and service of Dr. Brenda Estelle Armstrong ('Coach Doc'), the Duke pediatric cardiologist, diversity dean, and Durham Striders coach who passed away October 7, 2018, with Durham Striders Director Frank Davis accepting on her behalf. The Board then recognized Captain Aleem and his family for rescuing a motorist involved in a rollover crash on I-85. (The middle portion of the transcript between 01:28:34 and 03:13:12 was truncated in the digest.)

agenda_items.title: Federal Legislative Goals (Resiliency, Volunteer Firefighters, and SNAP)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed federal legislative goals ahead of an end-of-November deadline, discussing incorporating past SNAP resolution language alongside Medicaid expansion, transportation funding, and medication-assisted treatment proposals. Because time and staff input were insufficient to finalize new items before the deadline, Commissioner Reckhow moved and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded advancing the two amended goals on resiliency and volunteer firefighters along with the existing SNAP resolution, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Quarterly Management Report Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis, recognizing Chief of Staff/team member Dionne Hines and general managers, presented the second evolution of the County's Quarterly Management Report. He highlighted online project hyperlinks and Power BI dashboards enabling drill-downs into five-year expenditure and revenue trends, adopted budgets, personnel FTEs, and department-level roll-ups to support data-driven decision-making.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Comments: Work Sessions and Regional Resiliency
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Carter reiterated interest in continuing discussions about adding a second monthly work session to shorten regular meetings. Another commissioner reported on a joint Metropolitan Planning Organization (MPO) resiliency briefing noting that Moody's will factor resiliency planning into municipal credit evaluations and citing Hurricane Florence's $17 billion statewide impact—leaving an estimated $9 billion gap uncovered by federal/state aid or insurance to fall on local counties.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a brief question to Clerk Terry and County Attorney Siler regarding the attendance policy for board appointees, the Board voted by ballot and announced selections: David Morgan (Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee), Tiana Horn, Fred Myett, and Natalie Murdoch (Transportation Advisory Board), and Elizabeth Morel (Women's Commission). The Board then adjourned unanimously on motion of Commissioner Carter, seconded by Commissioner Howerton.

meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the November 13, 2018 regular meeting of the Durham County Board of Commissioners, shifted to Tuesday due to the Veterans Day holiday. The board unanimously approved five sets of September and October 2018 minutes (5-0), proclaimed the Durham NC Chapter of The Links, Incorporated Day, and adopted a solemn resolution honoring Lewis McCallen, a founding member of the Bull City United violence prevention program who died October 28, 2018. Commissioners unanimously approved Consent Agenda items 18-1025 through 18-1113 (5-0)—highlighting the affordable housing policy, surplus property, and a renewable energy resolution—and received briefings on comprehensive OB clinic ACEs screenings and Durham Pre-K integration into NC Pre-K ahead of its winter 2019 launch. Concluding a public hearing with no speakers, the board voted unanimously to adopt a statement of consistency (5-0) and an ordinance approving Unified Development Ordinance text amendment TC1800006 allowing private streets in cross-county developments (5-0).

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-11-05 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 5, 2018 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board of County Commissioners heard extensive public comment supporting a proposed 2050 100% renewable energy resolution, advocating for Plan B affordable housing commitments (including 3-bedroom units and deeper AMI levels), and raising traffic and tree-clearing concerns along Ephesus Church Road near Creekside Elementary and the proposed GoTriangle rail maintenance facility; commissioners voted 5-0 to extend citizen comment time to 9:40 AM. Later in the work session (after a truncated middle section), commissioners reviewed draft surplus property disposition procedures—recommending routing properties to county departments and schools for 10-year capital needs before affordable housing transfer and capping city resale reimbursement at the actual sale price—along with a study of 706 Rigsbee. The Board also reviewed a draft quarterly management report for email feedback, deferred commissioner comments to November 13, and voted 5-0 to enter a multi-hour closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4), (a)(5), and (a)(6) before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Citizen Comments (Climate Resolution, Affordable Housing, and Ephesus Church Rd Traffic)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs opened the work session and read the public charge. Speakers Dale Ebertz, Tom Campbell, Daniel Parkhurst (Clean Air Carolina), and Richard Harkrader urged adoption of the 100% clean renewable energy by 2050 resolution. Additional residents advocated for Plan B affordable housing (offering more 80%, 60%, and 30% AMI units and three-bedroom apartments) and raised traffic, tree-clearing, and development concerns along Ephesus Church Road near Creekside Elementary, 130 townhomes, a daycare, and the proposed GoTriangle rail operations maintenance facility. At 00:28:09, the Board voted 5-0 to suspend its 30-minute comment limit until 9:40 a.m. to hear the final speaker, Heather. (The middle portion from 00:28:35 to 04:31:00 was truncated in the digest.)

agenda_items.title: Surplus Property Policy and Inventory Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed proposed policy language governing real property acquired through tax foreclosure, donation, or deed in lieu of foreclosure prior to affordable housing disposition. Board members suggested reorganizing the text chronologically, explicitly requiring departments and Durham Public Schools to evaluate 10-year future capital needs during routing, capping any city resale compensation to the county at the actual sale price rather than full prior tax/investment value, and setting clear policy goals for parcels such as the Civic Center parking lot and 706 Rigsbee (already under internal team study).

agenda_items.title: Draft Quarterly Management Report and Board Directives Follow-Up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis distributed a draft of the first quarterly report for commissioners to review and submit feedback by email over the following week prior to online publication, noting the County was building a unified web portal for Managing for Results reports and community indicators. Commissioners also checked on pending September directives, including follow-ups from Tobin, completed CDBG public hearings, and Piedmont's scheduled return on November 26.

agenda_items.title: Deferral of Commissioner Comments and Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4), (a)(5), (a)(6))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Due to the late hour, Chair Jacobs recommended moving commissioner comments to the November 13 meeting. On motion of Vice Chair James Hill, seconded by Commissioner Heidi Carter, the Board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) (economic development incentives), (a)(5) (real property acquisition negotiating position), and (a)(6) (personnel). Upon returning at 08:35:29, Chair Jacobs reported direction had been given to staff and the meeting adjourned.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC Oct 22 Live
meetings.executive_summary: Vice Chair James Hill presided over the October 22, 2018 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners while Chair Wendy Jacobs had an excused absence to attend the Rail-Volution conference. The four present commissioners unanimously approved seven sets of May through August 2018 meeting minutes (4-0) and approved the consent agenda (4-0) after discussing contract phase structures and work session scheduling. Ceremonial items included proclaiming November 11, 2018 as Bells Across Durham Day for the World War I centennial—accepted by former City Council member Eddie Davis—and honoring the late Dr. Brenda Estelle Armstrong. The board held a public hearing with no speakers on the 2019 Reappraisal Schedule of Values (no action required until November), heard a 2020 Census Complete Count Committee briefing in which County Manager Wendell Davis pledged a marketing budget amendment, and made appointments to six advisory boards and commissions.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of May-August 2018 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill called the October 22, 2018 meeting to order at 7:02 p.m., read the public charge, led announcements including encouraging citizens to vote, and presided over approval of seven sets of minutes (May 22, May 24, May 31, June 4, and June 14 budget work sessions; July 23 regular session; and August 6 work session). The board passed the minutes unanimously 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Bells Across Durham Day Proclamation and Tribute to Dr. Brenda Estelle Armstrong
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow read a proclamation designating November 11, 2018 as Bells Across Durham Day to mark the 100th anniversary of the World War I Armistice, with former City Council member Eddie Davis speaking on the simultaneous bell-ringing initiative. The board also presented a tribute honoring Duke pediatric cardiologist and Durham Striders co-leader Dr. Brenda Estelle Armstrong following her passing on October 7, 2018.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners questioned why a contract listed eight service phases while the county was paying for a smaller portion and reiterated support for adding a second work session so consent items can be vetted in advance. The board then voted 4-0 to approve the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: 2019 Reappraisal Schedule of Values
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Hill opened and closed the public hearing on the 2019 Reappraisal Schedule of Values with no speakers signed up or rising to comment. Staff noted two citizen emails had been received and answered and stated that no board vote was required until adoption in November.

agenda_items.title: 2020 Census Complete Count Committee and Recruitment Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: U.S. Census Bureau representatives Laura McCready and regional recruitment staff requested county participation in a Complete Count Committee with liaison Ms. Hines, marketing funds, and outreach to count underserved and homeless populations ahead of opening a local census office in Durham needing at least 348 applicants. County Manager Wendell Davis committed to returning with a budget amendment for census outreach.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff announced the board's voting results appointing Tamario Alston and Vicky Winters to the Adult Care Home CAC, Charles Douglas to the City-County Appearance Commission, Jessica Uba to the Dangerous Dog Appeal Board, Amanda Wire and Eric Zog to the Nursing Home CAC, Milton Gilder to the Transportation Advisory Board, and Michelle Laws to the Women's Commission.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC Oct 8 Live
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the October 8, 2018 regular meeting of the Durham County Board of Commissioners, opening after a closed session with an apology to guests for the 15-minute delay. The board adjusted the agenda to move pulled consent items after regular business (5-0) and postponed Item 18-1021 (the 2019 Reappraisal Schedule of Values public hearing) to October 22 (5-0), approved March 2018 minutes while asking the clerk for a catch-up plan (5-0), honored the Bouncing Bulldogs world-champion jump rope team, and paid tribute to the late Dr. Brenda Armstrong. After receiving an update on Durham-Orange Light Rail operations and maintenance facility rezoning and public workshops, commissioners unanimously adopted Item 18-1063 establishing an Enterprise Fund Capital Reserve Fund for sewer System Development Fees in compliance with state law (5-0). At the County Manager's request to ensure clarity following pulled items, the board re-affirmed all consent agenda items including $6.5 million for multiple capital projects (5-0) and granted Chair Jacobs an excused absence for October 22 (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, Announcements, and Approval of March 2018 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning from closed session, Chair Jacobs apologized for the delay, led the Pledge of Allegiance, and presided over unanimous votes to move pulled consent items after regular business (5-0) and delay Item 18-1021 (2019 Reappraisal Schedule of Values public hearing) to October 22 (5-0). Following announcements including free GoDurham/GoTriangle Youth GoPasses, the board approved March 2018 minutes 5-0 and asked Clerk Monica Toomer for a plan to catch up on remaining old minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Resolution Honoring the Bouncing Bulldogs and Tribute to Dr. Brenda Armstrong
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow presented a resolution honoring the Bouncing Bulldogs jump rope team and founder Ray Frederick Jr., celebrating their 2018 Double Dutch Contest World first-place victory in Tokyo in the 12-and-under Fusion category. Vice Chair James Hill and commissioners also paid tribute to Dr. Brenda Armstrong following her passing and requested a formal memorial resolution.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (Late Additions and DPS Laptop/Chromebook Item)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter flagged multiple late consent items not reviewed in advance, including a Durham Public Schools request regarding laptops and Chromebooks that lacked lease amounts and quantities in the amendment backup. The remaining consent items were subsequently confirmed later in the meeting.

agenda_items.title: Durham-Orange Light Rail Project Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff provided an update on GoTriangle's rail operations and maintenance facility site acquisition, Planning Commission and City Council rezoning/annexation steps for water service, workforce development alignment, and public design workshops scheduled for November 3, 5, and 8. Commissioner Howerton also flagged transit stop conditions at Phoenix Square and Fayetteville Street.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Item 18-1063: Enterprise Fund Capital Reserve Fund for System Development Fees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained that following 2017 legislation (N.C.G.S. 162A Article 8), a W.R. Martin fee study, and UNC School of Government guidance, the county must establish a Capital Reserve Fund within the Sewer Enterprise Fund before collecting and expending System Development Fees adopted in the FY2019 budget. agenda_items.title: Excused Absence, Agenda Order Discussion, and Re-affirmation of Consent Agenda

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-10-08 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 8, 2018 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board of County Commissioners opened by voting 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and (a)(3) for personnel and attorney-client matters, reconvening at 1:48 into the recording with apologies to the Bouncing Bulldogs for the delay. The Board unanimously adjusted the agenda (5-0) to discuss items pulled from consent immediately after consent, delayed Item 18-1021 (2019 Reappraisal Schedule of Values public hearing) to October 22 (5-0), approved minutes (5-0), honored the Bouncing Bulldogs jump rope team, and paid tribute to the late Dr. Brenda Estelle Armstrong. After receiving a GoTriangle light rail update on the Farrington Road rail maintenance facility and affordable housing alignment, the Board voted 5-0 to adopt Item 18-1063 establishing a capital reserve fund for water/sewer system development fees under N.C.G.S. 162A Article 8, excused Chair Jacobs's October 22 absence (5-0), and reaffirmed 5-0 approval of the consent agenda including Item 091 ($6.5 million for multiple capital projects).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and (a)(3)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On motion of Vice Chair James Hill, seconded by Commissioner Heidi Carter, the Board voted 5-0 to adjourn into closed session to address individual personnel matters under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and consult with legal counsel under (a)(3). Returning at 01:48:21, Chair Jacobs reported giving direction to staff and apologized to audience guests for running late.

agenda_items.title: Open Session Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read the public charge and entertained agenda adjustments. The Board voted 5-0 on Commissioner Carter's request to place items pulled from consent immediately after the consent agenda rather than at the end of the meeting, and voted 5-0 on the County Attorney's request to remove Item 18-1021 (2019 Reappraisal Schedule of Values public hearing) and defer it to October 22, 2018. Announcements included the October 13 Reuse Rodeo e-waste/shredding event, Duke Game Days, Kids Voting Durham, and free GoDurham/GoTriangle youth bus passes.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes, Ceremonial Resolution (Bouncing Bulldogs), and Tribute to Dr. Brenda Armstrong
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After requesting a clerk's plan to clear remaining historical minutes, the Board approved the minutes 5-0 on motion of Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton. Commissioner Reckhow read a resolution honoring Coach Ray Frederick Jr. and the Bouncing Bulldogs jump rope team, after which Vice Chair Hill, Chair Jacobs, and Commissioner Howerton paid tribute to recently deceased pediatric cardiologist Dr. Brenda Estelle Armstrong and asked staff to prepare a memorial resolution. (Consent agenda discussion between 02:18:56 and 03:27:42 was truncated in the digest.)

agenda_items.title: GoTriangle Light Rail and Transit Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: GoTriangle staff briefed commissioners on the Rail Operations and Maintenance Facility (ROMF) site off Farrington Road across I-40, noting the future land use map amendment and rezoning would go before the Planning Commission the next evening and City Council later in the year alongside an annexation request for water service. Staff also highlighted alignment with guaranteed affordable housing stock and public outreach via goforwardnc.org, while Commissioner Howerton asked staff to check bus stop improvements at Phoenix Square and Fayetteville Street.

agenda_items.title: Item 18-1063: Capital Reserve Fund Resolution for Enterprise System Development Fees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained that under N.C.G.S. 162A Article 8 (enacted after Town of Carthage v. Quality Built Homes), Durham County completed a W.R. Martin fee study, held a May 29, 2018 public hearing, and adopted FY 2019 system development fees (replacing capital recovery fees), but learned from the UNC School of Government that a dedicated capital reserve fund was legally required before collecting or spending those fees. On motion of Commissioner Reckhow, seconded by Commissioner Howerton, the Board voted 5-0 to adopt the resolution, capital improvement plan, and supplemental information.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence Request, Agenda Workflow Discussion, and Consent Agenda Reaffirmation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On motion of Commissioner Reckhow, seconded by Vice Chair Hill, the Board voted 5-0 to excuse Chair Jacobs's absence for the October 22, 2018 meeting so she could attend the Rail~Volution conference in Pittsburgh. Commissioners then discussed keeping advertised public hearings before regular business and adding a second work session to avoid late additions to consent agendas. At Manager Davis's request to ensure clarity for Item 091 ($6.5 million for multiple capital projects), Commissioner Carter moved and Commissioner Reckhow seconded reaffirming approval of all consent agenda items 5-0 before adjourning unanimously.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-10-01 9:00 AM - Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 1, 2018 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, County Attorney Siler introduced new attorney Larissa Williamson, and resident Jim Svara (speaking for the Coalition for Affordable Housing and Transit, Durham CAN, St. Philip's, and First Presbyterian) voiced concern over delaying the East Main parking lots redevelopment report until November while noting 71% of public input respondents preferred Option B on affordable housing. Commissioners reviewed upcoming consent items—including Triangle Wastewater Treatment Plant aeration system and sluice gate items (18-0994 and 18-1041)—and heard an update on the Minority and Women Business Enterprise (MWBE) program showing $20 million of $81 million (25%) diverse spend in 2017 and $11 million of $70 million in 2018 alongside increased subcontractor participation. Later in the session (after a truncated middle portion), commissioners debated proposals to shorten lengthy meetings and add a second monthly work session, reviewed board directives tracking, and shared comments on economic equity, school food pantries, and GoTriangle no-smoking signage before adjourning unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Staff Introduction, and Citizen Comments (East Main Parking Lots Redevelopment)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the work session and read the public charge, after which County Attorney Siler introduced Larissa Williamson (formerly Special Deputy Attorney General at the NC Attorney General's office) as a new addition to the County Attorney's Office. Citizen Jim Svara expressed disappointment that the East Main Street parking lots redevelopment report was postponed to November, noted that 71% of public input forms favored Option B on affordable housing compared to 15% for Option A, and Chair Jacobs asked staff to fix online access to the September 4 DFI presentation.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Preview: Triangle Wastewater Treatment Plant Items (18-0994 and 18-1041)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis reviewed upcoming consent items ahead of the next regular session, focusing together on Items 18-0994 and 18-1041 for Triangle Wastewater Treatment Plant improvements, aeration system services, and sluice gates purchase. Commissioners commended staff for consistently completing bid and sole-source documentation.

agenda_items.title: Minority and Women Business Enterprise (MWBE) Program Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and consultants from The Institute reviewed the 2016 MWBE ordinance establishing a 25% aspirational goal and dedicated purchasing positions. Presenters reported $20 million of $81 million total spend (~25%) went to diverse businesses in 2017 and $11 million of $70 million in 2018 while reaching a larger pool of second-tier subcontractors (citing prime/subcontractor examples such as Holt Brothers and CT Wilson), and recommended adopting predictive spend modeling tied to departmental budgets. (The middle portion of the transcript from 00:41:40 to 04:00:52 was truncated in the digest.)

agenda_items.title: Board Meeting Structure and Second Work Session Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners debated options to reduce meeting lengths and late consent additions, including Commissioner Heidi Carter's proposal to add a second monthly work session (potentially Thursdays or split morning/afternoon sessions), moving informational presentations to regular meetings, polling consent items at the outset so staff can depart, and enforcing item time allotments. County Manager Davis defended reviewing consent items at work sessions before regular meetings as a process improvement, and commissioners asked staff/the clerk's office to research member board conflicts and NCACC schedules.

agenda_items.title: Board Directives Follow-Up, Commissioner Comments, and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed a new workflow of checking draft minutes ahead of adoption to keep the board directives tracker updated, while commissioners noted items prior to August were missing from the document. During commissioner comments, members highlighted economic equity and job access, the Child Food Hub grand opening supporting school food pantries, and GoTriangle's appreciation for county staff collaboration on no-smoking bus stop signs, before adjourning unanimously.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC Sept 24 LIve
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the September 24, 2018 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners after returning from closed session. The board thanked first responders and emergency staff for Hurricane Florence preparedness, approved the August 27, 2018 minutes as amended (5-0), and issued proclamations for Minority Enterprise Development Week, National Community Planning Month (marking the 30th anniversary of the merged City-County Planning Department), and domestic/care workers. After pulling Item 18-0995 to reconcile a 75% advisory board attendance requirement, the board approved Consent Agenda items 18-1036 through 18-1049 (5-0) and heard Tax Administrator Kim Simpson introduce the 2019 Reappraisal Schedule of Values. Following a public hearing with no speakers on UDO Text Amendment TC1800003—updating FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) panels effective October 19, 2018 to preserve National Flood Insurance Program eligibility—the board unanimously adopted the statement of consistency (5-0) and the UDO Article 8 ordinance (5-0), and appointed residents to five advisory boards and commissions.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Emergency Preparedness Announcements, and Approval of August 27, 2018 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After adjourning from closed session, Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the September 24, 2018 meeting, praised county first responders and emergency management for Hurricane Florence response during National Preparedness Month, and shared announcements including the Inter-Faith Food Shuttle Child Food Hub opening and Alert Durham. The board approved the August 27, 2018 minutes as amended 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations: MED Week, National Community Planning Month, and Domestic Workers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board proclaimed October 1-5, 2018 as Minority Enterprise Development Week (highlighting the county's MWBE ordinance), October 2018 as National Community Planning Month (celebrating the 30th anniversary of the merged City-County Planning Department), and honored domestic and care workers in the legacy of Dorothy Bolden.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 18-0995) and 2019 Reappraisal Schedule of Values Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Item 18-0995 was pulled for wording clarification on an advisory board's 75% attendance requirement, and the board voted 5-0 to approve Consent Agenda items 18-1036 through 18-1049. meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-09-04 9:00 AM - Work Session (Tuesday Meeting date)
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 4, 2018 Work Session (held on Tuesday after Labor Day) presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board heard citizen comment from city public historian Eddie Davis proposing 'Bells Across Durham County' on November 11, 2018 for the World War I Armistice centennial and reviewed upcoming consent items including jail behavioral health reporting, Library Foundation and literacy symposium grant budget amendments ($155,229 and $14,000), a McFarland Farm agricultural easement grant (Item 1001), and MWBE bid tabulation form wording. Later in the lengthy work session (following a truncated middle section), commissioners reviewed draft state/federal legislative goals—such as a $1.9 billion school capital bond, state transit funding levels, EMS Medicaid cost reporting, and pharmaceutical buying-club constraints—and held in-depth discussions on Youth Home replacement planning under North Carolina's 'Raise the Age' law and Federal PREA sight-and-sound separation rules at the Detention Center. At the close of the session, the Board took a unanimous 5-0 voice vote moved by Commissioner Heidi Carter and seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow regarding recording a commissioner's incomplete Planning Commission ballot.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Citizen Comment (Bells Across Durham Proposal)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the Tuesday work session following Labor Day and read the public charge. Citizen Eddie Davis—serving as public historian for Durham's 2019 sesquicentennial—proposed 'Bells Across Durham County' on November 11, 2018 to mark the 100th anniversary of the end of World War I, and Chair Jacobs asked Clerk Terry to prepare a resolution.

agenda_items.title: Work Session Agenda Format and Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners raised concerns about confusing online agenda blocks (listing lunch at 9:45 a.m.) and reviewed upcoming consent items: jail mental health visit tracking, Item 978 ($155,229 Library Foundation revenue budget amendment), Item 979 ($14,000 library symposium scholarship grant), and Item 1001 (McFarland Farm agricultural land easement grant). Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton flagged that a bid form categorized 'white females' rather than all women under MWBE tracking, and commissioners asked staff to verify with Purchasing. (The middle portion from 00:45:00 to 07:24:21 was truncated in the digest.)

agenda_items.title: State and Federal Legislative Goals Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff walked through proposed legislative goals including support for a $1.9 billion statewide school capital bond, Youth Home priorities (with Director Angela Dunn and General Manager Jody Miller), maintaining state transit funding above FY 2017–18 levels, preserving EMS Medicaid cost-report supplemental reimbursements (unique to North Carolina and California), and clarifying FDA distribution-license limits on hospital pharmaceutical buying clubs.

agenda_items.title: Youth Home Replacement Planning ('Raise the Age') and Detention Center PREA Assessment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners and staff (Angela Dunn and Jody Miller) discussed concept planning, Engineering's RFQ, and potential state cost-sharing (following a spring 2018 meeting with Billy Lassiter) to replace the Youth Home in light of Raise the Age legislation adding 16- and 17-year-olds; staff noted the state law shifted the original project scope, while a commissioner emphasized that Durham's youth remain the County's responsibility. Colonel Pregnano then briefed the Board on federal PREA sight-and-sound separation rules versus North Carolina's separate-sleeping standards and adult detention population trends (roughly 405–480), with staff asked to return with data.

agenda_items.title: Planning Commission Ballot Record and Wrap-Up Vote
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the close of the work session, a commissioner noted having mistakenly voted for only one instead of all three candidates on a Planning Commission appointment ballot and sought to clarify the record even though it did not alter the outcome. On motion of Commissioner Heidi Carter, seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, the Board passed a procedural voice vote 5-0.

meetings.executive_summary: At the August 6, 2018 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board heard citizen comments from John Tarantino regarding the Confederate monument committee report (which Jacobs noted was expected around December) before reviewing upcoming consent agenda items placed at the start of the session to minimize staff wait times. Chair Jacobs replied that the committee's work would run until around December and its report would be posted on the county website.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review: Financing Collateral, Vendor Location Tracking, and Library/Health Grants
agenda_items.discussion_summary: To avoid keeping staff waiting all day, the Board reviewed consent agenda items first, with Commissioner Heidi Carter proposing that commissioners pull only flagged items at future work sessions. Discussions covered a port authority grant (952), a $43.5M project financing collateral swap between the building across the street and the judicial building annex under the 2018 financing corporation, an NC Housing Finance Agency water-project loan disclosure, tracking bidder locations on bid tabs to boost Durham businesses, the LSTA library grant (870), Sheriff's grant amendments (917, 902), and the NIH 'All of Us' research partnership at the library (908).

agenda_items.title: County Firearms Discharge Ordinance Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners and Sheriff's/county staff examined possible updates to Durham County's firearms discharge ordinance, noting enforcement difficulties under the current 'predominant residential district' rule and discussing whether the 600-foot setback should measure from property lines or residential structures. Commissioners asked staff to combine Mecklenburg County's clearer distance, private firing-range, and juvenile supervision provisions with Durham's existing protections addressing automatic weapons and magazine capacity.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC July 23, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At the July 23, 2018 regular session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Durham County Board of Commissioners approved the March 8 work session and June 11 and June 25 regular session minutes (5-0), adopted consent agenda items 18-0897 through 18-0916 after deferring item 18-0887 to the August work session (5-0), and recognized community matriarchs Mrs. Peggy Johnson Tapp (posthumously) and Mrs. Cora Jones Boothe McCloy on her 100th birthday. Following joint public hearings with Economic Development Director Andy Miracle and Greater Durham Chamber of Commerce CEO Geoff Durham, the board unanimously approved (5-0) local match allocations for Job Development Investment Grant awards to AveXis, Inc. ($175,000 match donated by Clarion Partners), LabCorp ($220,000 match donated by Karlin Real Estate), and Sensus USA ($50,000 match), along with a completion-date amendment to January 1, 2019 for Austin Lawrence Partners East LLC. After making appointments to eight advisory boards and committees and returning from closed session, the board approved a motion moved by Ellen W. Reckhow and seconded by Heidi Carter setting the County Attorney's salary at $204,811 effective on his anniversary date by a 4-1 voice vote (Ayes: Ellen W. Reckhow, Heidi Carter, and two other commissioners; Nay: one unidentified commissioner not named in the audio record).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustment, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order at 7:05 p.m. following a closed-session recess, noted the board would return to closed session later in the evening, and shared announcements on the Complete Streets workshop, East Main Street 300/500 parking lot mixed-use/affordable housing input sessions, Durham Neighborhood College, summer reading, and the City-County Planning zoning survey. The board unanimously approved the March 8, 2018 work session minutes and the June 11 and June 25, 2018 regular session minutes, while flagging follow-up on the Park Center agreement.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comment Period: ABC Board Reappointment Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen Jackie Wagstaff addressed the board requesting reappointment to a second term on the Durham Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) Board, noting that reappointment was necessary for her to remain in line to sit on the state ABC Board of Directors.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Resolutions: Mrs. Peggy Johnson Tapp and Mrs. Cora Jones Boothe McCloy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board presented a resolution honoring the late Mrs. Peggy Johnson Tapp, co-operator of the Chicken Hut restaurant and community gathering place, followed by Vice Chair James Hill reading a resolution celebrating the 100th birthday of longtime Durham resident and entrepreneur Mrs. Cora Jones Boothe McCloy.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Items 18-0897 through 18-0916; Item 18-0887 Deferred)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs removed item 18-0887 from the agenda for consideration at the August work session. The board then unanimously approved consent agenda items 18-0897 through 18-0916.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearings: Economic Development Local Match Grants (18-0909, 18-0910, 18-0911) and Austin Lawrence Partners East Amendment (18-0914)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Director Andy Miracle and Chamber of Commerce CEO Geoff Durham presented four items: JDIG local match recognitions for AveXis, Inc. ($175,000 Clarion Partners donation; $55 million investment and 100 jobs), LabCorp at Parmer RTP ($220,000 Karlin Real Estate donation; $30 million investment and 422 jobs), and Sensus USA at Keystone Park ($50,000 match; $4 million investment and 301 jobs), plus a contract amendment extending Austin Lawrence Partners East LLC's completion date from July 1, 2018 to January 1, 2019 due to a mechanical contractor failure. Commissioners questioned job qualifications and inclusive local workforce outreach through Durham Tech before unanimously approving all four items in separate motions.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Prior to announcing ballot results, a commissioner raised concern about low Durham residency among primary and secondary recommendations for an advisory body. Results were announced for appointments to the ABC Board, Convention Center Authority, Criminal Justice Advisory Committee, Dangerous Dog Appeal Board, Durham-Wake Counties Research and Production Service District, Environmental Affairs Board, Library Board of Trustees, and Sports Commission.

agenda_items.title: Post-Closed Session Action: County Attorney Salary Adjustment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a closed-session recess beginning at 01:16:54, the board returned to open session and considered setting the County Attorney's salary at $204,811 effective on his anniversary date. The motion carried on a 4-1 voice vote, with one unidentified commissioner voting in opposition.
