meetings.title: Durham County BOCC June 25, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: With Commissioner Heidi Carter absent on an excused absence previously approved on June 11, the four attending members of the Durham County Board of Commissioners unanimously adopted the FY 2018-19 Budget Ordinance (4-0) after reducing the County Manager's proposed property tax increase from 1.9 cents to 1 cent. Before voting on the budget, Chair Wendy Jacobs, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Brenda A. Howerton delivered an extensive board statement responding to June 11 public hearing testimony on Detention Center safety and suicide prevention, detailing 16 years of CIP and operating allocations ($137,000 for HVAC security vents, $90,000 for window fixes, $1.5 million for Durham Youth Home expansion, and over $3.5 million annually for inmate physical and mental healthcare). The board also unanimously (4-0) approved consent items 18-0848 through 18-0892 (including the southern Durham fire consolidation ILA with the City and a Durham Pre-K expansion contract), installment financing and reimbursement resolutions under G.S. 160A-20 (refinancing $43.5 million for Admin II and funding jail, emergency communications, and fire district capital projects), and post-closed-session salaries for Tax Collector/Administrator Kim Simpson ($145,306) and Register of Deeds Sharon Davis ($100,515).

agenda_items.title: Adjournment from Pre-Meeting Closed Session, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 4-0 to adjourn from closed session, read the public charge, and shared announcements covering the 15-501 corridor study, JCPC community conversation, HIV testing, summer reading, Durham Neighborhood College, and the zoning choices survey. Commissioner Howerton raised an NC AFL-CIO petition regarding Kroger's closure of 14 Triangle stores (4 not converting to Harris Teeter or Food Lion), and the board approved April 2 work session and May 29 regular session minutes 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognition: Durham County EMS AHA Mission: Lifeline Gold Plus Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim EMS Director Kevin Underhill and staff were recognized for receiving the American Heart Association Mission: Lifeline Gold Plus award, the highest EMS recognition level. Underhill highlighted 256 STEMI transports out of 1,700+ acute coronary syndrome dispatches in 2017 and a 17% cardiac arrest survival rate compared to the 10.4% national average.

agenda_items.title: Board Statement on Durham County Detention Center Safety, Suicide Prevention, and Youth Home Planning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs delivered a detailed statement on behalf of the board addressing June 11 public hearing concerns over inmate safety in the Detention Center. Staff's review back to 2002 found that $40,000 window and $1.23 million air vent grille proposals in the 2004–2013 CIP were never brought forward as capital project amendments, while the county subsequently funded $137,000 for HVAC security vents (80+ cells completed by March 2017), $90,000 for completed cell window fixes, $87,600 and $1.5 million toward expanding the Durham Youth Home to 24 beds ahead of Raise the Age, $544,542 for jail mental health services, and over $3 million for inmate physical health care; Commissioners Reckhow and Howerton expressed regret for not responding directly to the mother at the June 11 hearing.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review and Approval (Items 18-0848 through 18-0892, Excluding Pulled Item 18-0881)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Reckhow highlighted the fire service consolidation ILA with the City of Durham (18-0848), the Child Care Services Association Pre-K expansion contract (18-0866; 13 new and 25 enhanced classrooms), and requested follow-up on Greater Durham Chamber of Commerce workforce readiness resources (18-0877); Chair Jacobs highlighted the Student U MOU for W.G. Pearson School. Commissioner Howerton pulled item 18-0881 (FY 2018-19 budget ordinance) for citizen comment, and the remaining consent items passed 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Installment Financing Agreement (G.S. 160A-20) and CFO Reimbursement Authority Resolutions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Jay Gibson and CFO Susan Tezai presented two resolutions to refinance $43.5 million for Administration Building II renovations and finance detention center pod renovations, a portion of Admin II, the emergency communications center in the new police headquarters, emergency radio equipment, detention center elevators, and three Durham County Fire and Rescue vehicles, while authorizing the CFO to handle reimbursement actions under IRS/Treasury rules. No citizens spoke during the public hearing, and both resolutions passed 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 18-0881: FY 2018-19 Budget Ordinance Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Ricky Hart questioned confusing language in the recommended budget displaying $2.5 million for 27 school resource officers and $300,000 transitional SRO funds on the DPS page; Budget Director Keith Lane and commissioners clarified the SROs are in the Sheriff's budget, the $300,000 request was rescinded, and the adopted budget text would be clarified. Bull City Community Schools executive director Nicholas Graber-Grace thanked the board, and commissioners highlighted full DPS funding ($138M+), two community schools coordinator positions, $2.15 million for Pre-K, $300,000+ for eviction diversion and supportive housing, law enforcement pay raises, a female mental health jail pod, expanded community paramedicine, and cutting the property tax increase from 1.9 cents to 1 cent before adopting the budget 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Motion to Enter Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The four present commissioners made appointments to 13 advisory boards and commissions, deferring a tied Sports Commission vote until July when all five members would be present. The board then voted 4-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(6).

agenda_items.title: Post-Closed Session Salary Adjustments for Tax Collector and Register of Deeds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Upon returning from closed session, the board voted 4-0 to set Tax Collector/Administrator Kim Simpson's salary at $145,306 and Register of Deeds Sharon Davis's salary at $100,515, effective on their anniversary dates.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC June 11, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 11, 2018 meeting, the Durham County Board of Commissioners approved the May 14 minutes (5-0), recognized awards for Best Workplace for Commuters and the Sedimentation & Erosion Control program, approved consent agenda items 18-0743 through 18-0851 (5-0), and held an extensive public hearing on the FY 2018-19 recommended budget. Dozens of speakers addressed Detention Center safety and the 2017 suicide of 17-year-old Niecy Fennell, Inmate Welfare Fund commissary/phone fees and money bail, funding five Community Schools coordinator positions, custodial living wages, eviction diversion rental assistance, and Durham Tech accountability. Following a closed-session personnel evaluation, the board split 4-1 to set County Manager Wendell Davis's FY 2018-19 salary at $221,579 (Ayes: Wendy Jacobs, James Hill, Ellen W. Reckhow, Heidi Carter; Nay: Brenda A. Howerton), with Howerton objecting that the 2% increase was unfair compared to peer counties and the board's own 3% adjustment and protesting same-day distribution of evaluation materials.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of May 14, 2018 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order and announced the June 25 budget adoption date, the online budget comment portal, a June 16 Dolly Parton's Imagination Library enrollment event, and the relaunch of Durham Neighborhood College. The board unanimously approved the May 14, 2018 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions: Best Workplace for Commuters and Sedimentation & Erosion Control Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sustainability Officer Tobin Freid presented the Best Workplace for Commuters recognition highlighting employee GoPasses, vanpool subsidies, bike lockers, flex schedules, and GoTriangle's Emergency Ride Home program. State officials also presented an award recognizing Durham County's Sedimentation & Erosion Control program for rebounding from 2016 probation and enacting UDO alignment updates.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Scheduling Objection and Approval of Consent Agenda (Items 18-0743 through 18-0851)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton objected to taking up a closed-session personnel item whose packet materials were circulated at 6:00 p.m. that evening and asked to postpone it to June 25; Chair Jacobs noted other commissioners wished to hold the closed session that night while offering an additional session if needed. The board then unanimously approved consent agenda items 18-0743 through 18-0851.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on FY 2018-19 County Manager's Recommended Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Under a two-minute per speaker limit, residents and advocates testified on four major budget themes: (1) jail safety, federal PREA sight-and-sound separation for minors, inmate mental healthcare, ending money bail, and removing detainee phone/commissary fees from the Inmate Welfare Fund (including attorneys Ian Mance and Whitley Carpenter representing Julia Graves, mother of Niecy Fennell); (2) funding five Community Schools coordinator positions, custodial living wages, universal Pre-K, and Durham Tech outcome tracking (opposed on tax/outcomes grounds by Antonio Jones and Friends of Durham chair Dick Ford); (3) adding $200,000 in county emergency rental assistance and a coordinator for eviction diversion plus renewing Durham Habitat's $40,000 repair grant; and (4) funding a Memorial Stadium hammer throw cage for the 2019 USATF National Youth Outdoor Championships.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Personnel Evaluation (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the public hearing, the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to conduct an individual public officer evaluation.

agenda_items.title: Post-Closed Session Vote and Debate on County Manager FY 2018-19 Salary ($221,579)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning from closed session, the board voted 4-1 to set County Manager Wendell Davis's FY 2018-19 salary at $221,579. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton opposed the figure and read a formal dissent citing the manager's achievements and arguing he deserved a 3%–6% raise, while Commissioners James Hill, Wendy Jacobs, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Heidi Carter defended the ~2% increase as consistent with a 'meets expectations' rating under the board's mutually adopted evaluation instrument and placing Davis third in base pay and second in total compensation ($324,968.07) among peer NC counties.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Heidi Carter Excused Absence Request for June 25, 2018
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter requested and received unanimous approval for an excused absence from the June 25, 2018 budget adoption meeting to accompany her husband on an award trip to Hawaii.

votes.item_title: Approval of May 14, 2018 Regular Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Routine approval of the May 14, 2018 regular session minutes.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session for individual public officer evaluation.

votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the audio transcript after Chair Jacobs entertained the motion.
votes.discussion_detail: Sets County Manager Wendell Davis's FY 2018-19 salary at $221,579 (~2% increase). Brenda A. Howerton dissented and read a prepared statement; James Hill, Wendy Jacobs, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Heidi Carter spoke in support of the figure and evaluation process.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Commissioner Heidi Carter (June 25, 2018 Meeting)
votes.discussion_detail: Grants excused absence for June 25, 2018 regular session.

disagreements.issue: County Manager Wendell Davis FY 2018-19 Salary Increase and Evaluation Process
disagreements.summary: The board divided 4-1 over setting County Manager Wendell Davis's FY 2018-19 salary at $221,579 (an increase of over $4,000, or roughly 2%), as well as over holding the vote the same night evaluation materials were circulated at 6:00 p.m.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve a 2% salary increase to $221,579 based on the board's mutually adopted evaluation instrument and peer county benchmarks.
side_a_arguments: James Hill noted that peer county managers received 0% to 2% raises (contradicting claims of a 3%–6% floor) and that 48% of county employees received the same 2% 'meets expectations' increase.

Wendy Jacobs cited benchmark data showing $221,579 ranked third highest in base pay behind only Mecklenburg and Wake counties and second highest statewide in total compensation ($324,968.07 including benefits).
Ellen W. Reckhow and Heidi Carter emphasized that the manager co-drafted and agreed to the evaluation instrument, which the entire board—including Howerton—had unanimously adopted the prior year.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject limiting the County Manager's increase to ~$4,000 (~2%) and defer the vote to June 25 to allow proper review of same-day materials.
side_b_arguments: Brenda A. Howerton argued the manager exceeded expectations—citing the AAA bond rating, clean audit, 15+ awards, Managing for Results, Pre-K, gun violence reduction, and southern fire consolidation—and deserved 3%–6% rather than less than the board's own 3% budget adjustment.
Howerton protested voting on information distributed at 6:00 p.m. the same evening instead of postponing action until the June 25 meeting.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 4-1, setting the County Manager's FY 2018-19 salary at $221,579.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-06-04 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 4, 2018 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board heard citizen comments from John Tarantino and received an in-depth presentation on economic development strategy, social equity, and North Carolina constitutional constraints on local business incentives—including prohibitions on local tax abatements and local-hire mandates, and lawful alternatives such as subordinate lending, commercial pre-leasing, workforce development, and business retention. In reviewing work-session directives ahead of budget adoption, a commissioner raised strong concerns that My Brother's Keeper (MBK) and Public Allies work plans requested in May were delayed until June 28 (after the budget vote) and questioned an unbriefed $55,000 mini-grant program in the County Manager's budget; staff pledged to provide answers before budget approval. Commissioners also discussed an NCACC legislative brief concerning state budget provisions and bills enabling municipalities to fund public schools, reviewed upcoming consent items (jail food-service training, relocating the budget public hearing out of consent, and ICMA Fellows staffing), and noted a September 17 event placeholder before transitioning to FY 2018-19 budget hearings with no formal votes taken.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Citizen Comments (John Tarantino)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the June 4, 2018 work session, read the public charge, and received citizen comments from John Tarantino of Durham Satire.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Strategy, Incentives Law, and Downtown Business Parity
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic development policy and legal presenters briefed the Board on business recruitment, business retention and expansion (BRE), workforce development, and North Carolina constitutional rules barring local property tax abatements and local-hire mandates while permitting interstate-competition cash grants, subordinate loans, and commercial pre-leasing. Later discussion touched on five-year profitability projections and ensuring county-assisted ventures do not create an uneven playing field for existing downtown restaurants.

agenda_items.title: Work Session Directives Review: MBK / Public Allies Deliverables and Mini-Grant Questions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reviewing the monthly directives tracker, a commissioner objected that My Brother's Keeper (MBK) and Public Allies work plans and deliverables requested in May were scheduled for June 28—after budget adoption—and questioned a $55,000 mini-grant program listed in the Manager's budget response without prior Board briefing or a formal process like Durham Open Space and Trails matching grants. Staff committed to meeting with Edmund and delivering answers prior to the budget vote.

agenda_items.title: NCACC Legislative Brief on Municipal School Funding Bills
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners and Chair Wendy Jacobs discussed an NCACC legislative brief regarding provisions in the state budget and two separate bills enabling municipalities to fund public schools, clarifying discrepancies in whether NCACC had requested commissioner input.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review, Calendar Placeholder, and Transition to Budget Hearings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners briefly reviewed consent agenda items—including a directive request on detainee food-preparation certification under the jail food service contract, correcting the Clerk's placement of the budget public hearing under consent instead of public hearings, and ICMA Fellows staffing—and noted a September 17 morning/evening calendar placeholder before transitioning to afternoon budget hearings ahead of a 4:30 PM hard stop.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-06-04 9:00 AM - Worksession
disagreements.issue: Timing and Transparency of My Brother's Keeper (MBK) Deliverables and $55,000 Mini-Grant Proposal
disagreements.summary: During the directives review, a commissioner objected to receiving My Brother's Keeper (MBK) and Public Allies work plans after the budget vote and questioned an unbriefed $55,000 mini-grant program in the Manager's proposed budget.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require MBK/Public Allies work plans, deliverables, and formal criteria for the proposed $55,000 mini-grant program before approving the FY 2018-19 budget.
side_a_arguments: The Board requested MBK and Public Allies work plans and deliverables in May, and June 28 is after budget adoption.
The City's youth coordinator delivered a detailed work plan since starting in December, whereas MBK staffing has been in place since September without a work plan.
Other county grant programs such as the $70,000 Durham Open Space and Trails Matching Grants follow rigorous processes, unlike an unbriefed $55,000 mini-grant line item.
disagreements.side_b_position: Staff noted prior conversations with the chair/staff scheduling issues and committed to gathering answers before budget adoption.
side_b_arguments: County administration had scheduled a meeting with Edmund that could not take place and was still catching up on tape notes from the prior meeting.
Staff pledged to follow up this week and provide full answers prior to final budget approval.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; County Manager's office agreed to meet with Edmund and deliver the requested MBK/Public Allies information and mini-grant details before budget adoption.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC May 14, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 14, 2018 regular session, County Manager Wendell Davis presented his FY 2018-19 Recommended Budget totaling $644.5 million (+1.8%, including a $435.5 million general fund) and proposing a 1.9-cent countywide property tax increase plus a 2-cent Durham County Fire and Rescue Service District tax increase to support southern Durham fire consolidation with the City. Key budget recommendations included $137 million in operating funding for Durham Public Schools (+$3 million), $5.2 million total for Pre-K expansion ($3.7 million as a challenge grant), 20 new Sheriff's Office positions (5 school resource officers replacing city-funded SROs, 2 domestic violence deputies, and 13 detention officers for a female mental health unit), $3 million to begin implementing the compensation and classification study, and transitioning 53 county fire positions to the City of Durham. The board also issued proclamations for Foster Care Awareness Month, National Drug Court Month, and Older Americans Month, approved the April 21 minutes (5-0), and unanimously adopted consent agenda items 18-0673 through 18-0810 (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of April 21, 2018 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order and announced the third annual Aging Well in Durham Summit on May 19, the June 9 Summer Reading kickoff at Northgate Mall, and a May 17 maintenance closure at a county solid waste convenience site. The board unanimously approved the April 21, 2018 meeting minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations: Foster Care Awareness Month, National Drug Court Month, and Older Americans Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board read proclamations for Foster Care Awareness Month (with DSS Director Ben Rose and Sharon Flatt highlighting the need for more locally licensed foster homes), National Drug Court Month (with Judge Brad Battaglia and CJRC's Roshana Parker noting restorative justice outcomes), and Older Americans Month (with commissioner remarks on pedestrian fatalities and waitlists for Meals on Wheels and in-home care).

agenda_items.title: County Manager's Recommended FY 2018-19 Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis presented the recommended $644.5 million FY 2018-19 budget ($435.5 million general fund), proposing a 1.9-cent property tax rate increase and a 2-cent fire district tax increase to fund southern fire consolidation (transferring 53 positions to the City). Major priorities included $137 million for DPS (+$3M; $3,400 per pupil), $5.2 million for Pre-K expansion, $7.5 million for Durham Tech, 20 new Sheriff/Detention positions (5 SROs, 2 DV deputies, 13 detention officers for a female mental health pod), EMS training and 5 replacement ambulances, $3 million to begin implementing the compensation/classification study, and a 2%–4% pay-for-performance range; commissioners confirmed the May–June budget work session schedule and asked to review the resident survey on May 22.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-05-07 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 7, 2018 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board heard citizen comments from Jim Savar (advocating expanding housing choices and revisions to the County's surplus property conveyance policy for rental housing and city transfers) and George Roberson (opposing the Confederate statue), and welcomed the new Clerk to the Board. Planning Director Patrick Young, Assistant Director Sarah Young, and Policy Supervisor Scott Whiteman briefed the Board on the merged Planning Department's 30th anniversary and FY 2018-19 work program, emphasizing Expanding Housing Choice (ADUs, tiny houses, potential teacher housing near schools), updating the 13-year-old Comprehensive Plan, and industrial land inventory. During commissioner comments, Commissioner Heidi Carter highlighted System of Care community awards, another commissioner advocated jail data-analytics software and misdemeanor citation tools, and a commissioner questioned Chair Jacobs over whether county budget or staff resources were committed to the Monument Committee's reception and security without prior Board discussion. Following consent agenda review—covering sole-source fire gear, enterprise sewer contracts, fire apparatus maintenance, and $485,633 in Medicaid cost-settlement funds—and a request for GoTriangle minority-vendor contracting data, the Board adjourned without taking substantive votes.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: Surplus Property Conveyance Policy and Confederate Monument
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jim Savar of the Coalition for Affordable Housing and Transit endorsed the Planning Department's Expanding Housing Choice initiative (ADUs and tiny houses) and urged amending the County's draft real-property conveyance policy to allow rental housing, apply the $10 nonprofit fee to City transfers, and broaden floodplain suitability rules. George Roberson spoke against the Confederate monument on county property under the 13th Amendment.

agenda_items.title: Introduction of New Clerk to the Board and FY 2018-19 Planning Department Work Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following introductory remarks from the new Clerk to the Board, Planning Director Patrick Young, Assistant Director Sarah Young, and Scott Whiteman presented the Planning Department's FY 2018-19 work program marking the merged City-County department's 30th anniversary. Key discretionary initiatives included Expanding Housing Choice (ADUs, tiny houses, lot-size flexibility, and potential school-site teacher housing), launching an extensive community-engaged Comprehensive Plan update aligned with capital budgeting, evaluating light-industrial land supply, and addressing state statute-of-limitations constraints on zoning enforcement.

agenda_items.title: Directives Capture Procedure and Commissioner Comments (System of Care, Monument Committee, Jail Data)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed summarizing explicit directives aloud at the end of work sessions with Drew before turning to Commissioner Comments (noting four commissioners were present). Commissioner Heidi Carter recognized System of Care award recipients, commissioners debated whether the Monument Committee's reception, facilitation, and Sheriff's security were arranged without prior Board resource approval, and a commissioner reported on a national jail data conference recommending data-analysis software and misdemeanor citation risk tools to reduce jail bookings.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review and GoTriangle Minority Vendor Report Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed consent items including sole-source Viking fire protective gear, Item 18-0751 library grant funds, Item 18-0752 enterprise-funded wastewater collection/treatment contracts, Item 18-0795 ($27,000 fire apparatus repairs), and Item 18-0798 ($485,633 Medicaid cost-settlement funds explained by Gail). Before adjourning on a motion by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, a commissioner requested a report from GoTriangle on minority/HUB vendor participation on light-rail contracts.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-05-07 9:00 AM - Worksession
disagreements.issue: Board Consultation and Resource Support for the Confederate Monument Committee's Swearing-In Meeting
disagreements.summary: During Commissioner Comments, a commissioner questioned Chair Wendy Jacobs over whether staff time, reception funding, live-streaming, and Sheriff's security for the Monument Committee's May meeting had been committed without prior Board discussion.
disagreements.side_a_position: Any use of County staff, commissioners' budget funds, or security resources for the Monument Committee should first be discussed by the full Board.
side_a_arguments: Emails referenced a 6:30 PM reception, website, and live-streaming without the Board having finalized a budget figure or discussed it collectively.
Whenever County resources or commissioners' budget funds are used, the Board should hold an explicit discussion beforehand.
disagreements.side_b_position: No dedicated staff or Board budget funds were assigned; committee members arranged external communications independently and Sheriff's deputies volunteered.
side_b_arguments: The committee is building its own website and Facebook page with zero dedicated County staff support, similar to other advisory committees.
Nothing is coming out of the commissioners' budget; staff facilitators were simply connected as a resource and Sheriff's Department personnel volunteered for security.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; Chair Wendy Jacobs clarified the resource boundaries and confirmed commissioners would attend to administer the oaths of office.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC April 23, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 23, 2018 regular session, the Durham County Board of Commissioners surprised retiring Clerk to the Board Michelle Parker-Evans with a resolution honoring her 31 years of local government service and issued proclamations for Durham Reentry Week, National Correctional Officers and Employees Week, and Children's Mental Health Awareness Month. The board unanimously approved consent agenda items 18-0745 through 18-0782 (5-0), including a Triangle Wastewater Treatment Plant contract achieving 100% minority- and women-owned business participation, a letter supporting state legislation for Durham Public Schools teacher housing with CASA and SECU, and a resolution advocating a 2018 statewide North Carolina School Construction Bond. Following a public hearing with no speakers, the board unanimously adopted Unified Development Ordinance Text Amendment TC17-007 allowing alternative streetscape designs in Downtown and Compact Design districts (5-0), and after a closed session covering litigation (*Milton v. Durham County*) and personnel, unanimously appointed Terry Huggy (transcribed) as Clerk to the Board effective May 7, 2018 at an $85,000 salary (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Farm Bill SNAP Alert, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order and shared announcements regarding a utility/lead poisoning comment period ending May 27 and bike-share operations, while Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton circulated an NEA alert urging opposition to SNAP cuts in the federal Agriculture and Nutrition Act. The board unanimously approved the April 9 regular session and April 14 PAC 4 meeting minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Clerk Michelle Parker-Evans Retirement and Reentry, Correctional Officers, and Children's Mental Health Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board surprised Clerk to the Board Michelle Parker-Evans with a resolution celebrating her 31-year career in local government ahead of her May 1 retirement. Commissioners also presented proclamations for Durham Reentry Week (April 23–27), National Correctional Officers and Employees Week (with Sheriff Mike Andrews), and Children's Mental Health Awareness Month.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 18-0745 through 18-0782) and NC School Construction Bond Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before the consent vote, Chair Jacobs highlighted 100% MWBE participation on the Triangle Wastewater Treatment Plant project (18-0764) and a letter supporting DPS teacher housing legislation with CASA and SECU. The board unanimously approved consent items 18-0745 through 18-0782, and Commissioner Howerton read aloud the adopted resolution calling for a 2018 statewide North Carolina School Construction Bond to address a five-year school capital backlog.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment — Design District Streetscape Alternatives (TC17-007)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Michael Stock presented privately initiated text amendment TC17-007 creating alternative streetscape amenity design standards in the Downtown Design and Compact Design districts, noting 14-0 Planning Commission approval and City Council adoption. After a public hearing with no speakers, the board unanimously adopted the statement of consistency and the UDO text amendment ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Motion to Enter Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board completed advisory board appointment balloting and then voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1), (a)(3) regarding *Milton v. Durham County et al.* (MDNC file 17-CV-258), and (a)(6) regarding personnel.

agenda_items.title: Post-Closed Session Appointment of Clerk to the Board
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Upon returning from closed session, the board voted unanimously to appoint Terry Huggy (as transcribed in audio) as Clerk to the Board effective May 7, 2018 at an annual salary of $85,000.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC April 9 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 9, 2018 regular session, the Durham County Board of Commissioners unanimously approved minutes for three prior meetings (5-0), honored retiring Soil and Water Conservation Director Eddie Culberson, and issued proclamations for Child Abuse Prevention Month and National County Government Month. IT Director Greg Marrow, Criminal Justice Resource Center Director Gudrun Parmer, and Dr. Shannon Tufts of the UNC School of Government recognized item 18-0647—Durham County's Local Government Federal Credit Union innovation award for its open-source court date text reminder system (`courtreminders.dconc.gov`) that sharply curtailed failure-to-appear jailings. The board unanimously approved consent agenda items 18-0647 through 18-0753 (5-0), including a landmark Resolution to Support Women's Health (read aloud by Heidi Carter) calling for repeal of the federal Hyde Amendment and comprehensive reproductive healthcare and abortion insurance coverage, and unanimously approved an excused absence request for May 23–29, 2018 (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order and announced the April 17 Kids Voting Durham youth candidate forum, April 16 NC 98 corridor study open house, Pre-K/Head Start enrollment, an April 23 NCDOT roundabout meeting, NCACC school construction bond advocacy (noted by Brenda A. Howerton), and Veterans Services limited hours. The board unanimously approved minutes for the February 8 work session, March 26 regular session, and March 16 legislative breakfast.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions: Eddie Culberson, Child Abuse Prevention Month, and National County Government Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Jay Gibson introduced a surprise recognition honoring Eddie Culberson for his water quality, stream restoration, and stormwater work in Soil and Water Conservation. The board also presented proclamations for Child Abuse Prevention Month (with DSS Director Ben Rose and Prevent Child Abuse NC's Sharon Hirsch) and National County Government Month.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Item 18-0647: UNC School of Government Award for Court Date Reminder System
agenda_items.discussion_summary: IT Director Greg Marrow, CJRC Director Gudrun Parmer, and UNC School of Government's Dr. Shannon Tufts presented the Local Government Federal Credit Union innovation award for Durham County's open-source court date text reminder system (`courtreminders.dconc.gov`). Officials noted that over 2,000 residents had signed up and only two recipients missed court out of several thousand reminders sent over a recent 20-day period, helping reduce failure-to-appear incarcerations, fines, and fees.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 18-0647 through 18-0753) and Resolution to Support Women's Health
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved consent agenda items 18-0647 through 18-0753. Commissioner Heidi Carter then read aloud the adopted Resolution to Support Women's Health—calling for repeal of the federal Hyde Amendment and urging President Trump and Governor Cooper to protect reproductive healthcare and abortion insurance coverage—which Chair Jacobs noted made Durham the 14th locality nationally and first in North Carolina to pass such a resolution.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence Request (May 23–29) and Grant Acknowledgements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved an excused absence for meetings from May 23 to May 29, 2018. Chair Jacobs also highlighted numerous grants and community donations included on the consent agenda (Aetna, UNC FIT, Shift NC, Watts Street Baptist Church, Wake EMC, and an anonymous CJRC donation), with Vice Chair James Hill emphasizing that the board's gratitude applied on behalf of all five commissioners.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-04-02 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 2, 2018 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board heard citizen comments from Tara Romano (NARAL Pro-Choice North Carolina) urging a county resolution supporting repeal of the federal Hyde Amendment, and received a briefing from Alliance Behavioral Healthcare on supportive housing programs including HUD's DASH shelter-plus-care initiative, the Duke Health housing pilot, and North Carolina's Transitions to Community Living Initiative (TCLI). Commissioners expressed concern that the state earmarks no housing funds outside the DOJ settlement TCLI population and had cut state mental health funding that forced Alliance to end a 10-person RHD subsidized housing program. During consent agenda review, commissioners refined draft language and exhibit references for Item 18-0721 (the county's opioid public nuisance litigation declaration), reviewed Item 18-0724 ($14,000+ Senior Center transportation rate realignment), Item 18-0730 (debt service adjustments for three fire and rescue vehicles), and Item 18-0733 ($247,000 GoTriangle grant amendment), and heard a brief Pre-K working group update from Commissioner Heidi Carter. The Board then voted unanimously by voice vote to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1), (a)(3), and (a)(6).

agenda_items.title: Public Charge and Citizen Comments (Tara Romano, NARAL Pro-Choice NC)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the work session, read the public charge, and heard from Tara Romano of NARAL Pro-Choice North Carolina, representing a 14-organization coalition requesting a Board resolution calling on the federal government to repeal the Hyde Amendment. Chair Jacobs noted the Board would discuss the request later during commissioner comments.

agenda_items.title: Supportive Housing Briefing and State Mental Health Funding Gaps (Alliance Behavioral Healthcare)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Alliance Behavioral Healthcare staff presented supportive housing models emphasizing 'housing as the platform for recovery,' detailing the HUD-funded DASH shelter-plus-care program, the Duke Health housing pilot, and the state DOJ-settlement Transitions to Community Living Initiative (TCLI). Commissioners criticized the lack of state-earmarked housing funds outside TCLI and questioned how state budget cuts forced the closure of a 10-person RHD subsidized housing program, noting the acute shortage of deeply affordable units in Durham.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review: Opioid Nuisance Declaration, Senior Transit, Fire Vehicles, and GoTriangle Grant
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed consent agenda items including Item 18-0721 (declaring the opioid epidemic a public nuisance, requesting grammatical corrections and clearer exhibit labeling for the Health Department white paper), Item 18-0724 (Durham Center for Senior Life $14,000+ realignment correcting the $45.71 adult day health transportation reimbursement rate), Item 18-0730 (debt service adjustments for three fire and rescue vehicles), and Item 18-0733 (recognizing $247,000 in GoTriangle grant revenue and clarifying Orange/Durham packet attachments).

agenda_items.title: Pre-K Working Group Update and Work Session Agenda Sequencing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter reported that the Pre-K working group had met twice with Durham Public Schools, confirming DPS's commitment as a partner and ongoing alignment with Board direction. Commissioners also discussed scheduling outreach with Senator Thom Tillis's office and agreed to place commissioner comments after consent agenda review on future work session agendas.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Adjourn to Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1), (a)(3), (a)(6))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously by voice vote to adjourn into closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1) (confidential/privileged records), (a)(3) (attorney-client privilege), and (a)(6) (individual personnel matters).

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC March 26
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 26, 2018 regular session (indexed under March 27, 2018), Chair Wendy Jacobs delivered the 2018 State of the County Address highlighting Durham's 27.9% job growth, cradle-to-career and early childhood priorities, opioid response, court-reminder and reentry initiatives, Durham-Orange Light Rail and Durham-Wake Commuter Rail progress, and 3.54% property tax base growth tempered by slowing sales tax revenues. Following budget public comments, approval of the February 26 minutes (5-0), and recognitions for National Service Recognition Day, EMS Corporal Chris Langdon, and IS&T analyst Bert White, the board unanimously approved consent agenda items 18-0687 through 18-0741 (5-0), including resolutions opposing offshore oil/gas drilling and seismic blasting (18-0722) and supporting youth-led advocacy for gun violence prevention legislation (18-0741). After a public hearing with no opposition, the board unanimously approved the Future Land Use Map amendment (Office to Industrial), consistency statement, and Industrial Light rezoning for the 2.187-acre Long Beverage expansion along Page Road (5-0 each) and appointed three members to the Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and 2018 State of the County Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs delivered the 2018 State of the County Address, citing 3.8% unemployment and 27.9% job growth alongside a 17.4% poverty rate and only 38% kindergarten readiness as drivers for a cradle-to-career system. She also highlighted law enforcement Narcan deployment, the court reminder and Local Reentry Council programs, Durham-Orange Light Rail ($1.25 billion federal funding eligibility) and Durham-Wake Commuter Rail progress, interim affordable housing density bonuses, and 3.54% tax base growth offset by slowing sales tax collections.

agenda_items.title: Budget Public Comment, Announcements, NCACC Report, and Approval of February 26 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Carolina Arbors residents commented on the upcoming May opening of co-located Fire Station 17, neighborhood speeding, and prioritizing education funding, while staff publicized the online FY 2018-19 budget comment portal. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton reported on her NCACC '100 Counties Helping All Children Thrive' summit, and the board unanimously approved the February 26, 2018 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions: National Service Recognition Day, EMS Corporal Chris Langdon, and IS&T Analyst Bert White
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board proclaimed April 3, 2018 as National Service Recognition Day with NCCU Eagle Corps director Colleen Herbert and Durham Tech RSVP coordinator Paula Rife. Commissioners then witnessed EMS Operations Chief Rodney Medlin present the Meritorious Intervention Commendation to Paramedic Corporal Chris Langdon for saving a crash victim's life off-duty with a tourniquet, and recognized IS&T's Bert White as HDI IT Analyst of the Year for the Triangle/Eastern NC region.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 18-0687 through 18-0741), Offshore Drilling Opposition (18-0722), and Youth Gun Violence Resolution (18-0741)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved consent agenda items 18-0687 through 18-0741. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow then read Resolution 18-0722 opposing offshore oil/gas drilling and seismic airgun blasting off North Carolina's coast, and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton read Resolution 18-0741 supporting youth-led advocacy for universal background checks, waiting periods, an assault weapons ban, and extreme risk protective orders while rejecting arming teachers.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Long Beverage Expansion Plan Amendment and Rezoning (A1700015 / Z1700037)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Jamie Sunyak and Planning Director Sara Young presented Patrick Byker's application to amend the Future Land Use Map from Office to Industrial and rezone four parcels (2.187 acres along Page Road) from Rural Residential to Industrial Light (IL) for future Long Beverage expansion, noting a 13-0 Planning Commission recommendation. After the applicant testified that employee shifts occur outside peak hours and no opponents spoke, the board unanimously approved the plan amendment resolution, consistency statement, and IL rezoning ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted by ballot to appoint Sylvia Alston, Northy Justice, and Brenda Bram (as transcribed) to the Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee before adjourning.

votes.discussion_detail: Routine approval of the February 26, 2018 regular session minutes.

votes.discussion_detail: Amends Future Land Use Map designation from Office to Industrial for 2.187 acres adjacent to Long Beverage on Page Road.

votes.discussion_detail: Adopts statutory consistency statement for the Long Beverage plan amendment and rezoning.

votes.discussion_detail: Rezones four Page Road parcels totaling 2.187 acres from Rural Residential to Industrial Light.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-03-26 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 26, 2018 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, Jacobs delivered the 2018 Durham State of the County Address highlighting a 3.8% unemployment rate, rising child poverty (22.2% to 26%), a new cradle-to-career initiative, Criminal Justice Resource Center reentry programs, $1.25 billion in federal light-rail funding eligibility and the Durham-Wake commuter rail study, 3.54% property tax-base growth tempered by slowing sales tax revenues, and over $134 million in county funding for Durham Public Schools plus $1.5 million for Pre-K. The Board announced the FY 2018-19 budget calendar (scheduled for May 14 presentation through June 25 adoption), took advance budget public comments, and issued a resolution signed by all five commissioners supporting youth-led gun violence prevention advocacy and urging state and federal leaders to enact gun-safety legislation. Following a public hearing on Case A1700015 / Z1700037 (Long Beverage Expansion at 3719 Page Road), the Board voted unanimously by voice vote on three motions to amend the Future Land Use Map to Industrial, adopt a N.C.G.S. 153A-341 consistency statement, and rezone 2.187 acres from Rural Residential to Industrial Light. The meeting concluded with ballot appointments of Sylvia Alston, Dorothy Justice, and Brenda Brown to the Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee.

agenda_items.title: 2018 Durham State of the County Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs delivered the 2018 State of the County Address reviewing county progress across education, economic equity, criminal justice reentry (including court reminder texts and the Local Reentry Council), opioid response, regional light-rail and commuter-rail transit, and digital service tools. She noted 3.54% tax-base growth alongside slowing sales tax revenues and highlighted over $134 million for Durham Public Schools, $4.3 million for school health/SROs, and $1.5 million for Pre-K.

agenda_items.title: FY 2018-19 Budget Calendar and Advance Public Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs reviewed the FY 2018-19 budget schedule—Manager's recommended budget on May 14, five work sessions from May 22 to June 14, public hearing on June 11, and budget ordinance adoption on June 25, 2018—and opened the floor for advance budget public comments beginning with James Briggs.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting Youth-Led Action on Gun Violence Prevention
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A March 26, 2018 Board resolution signed by Chair Wendy Jacobs, Vice Chair James Hill, and Commissioners Heidi Carter, Brenda A. Howerton, and Ellen W. Reckhow was read aloud supporting youth-led advocacy and calling on state and federal leaders (Senators Richard Burr and Thom Tillis, Rep. David Price, Gov. Roy Cooper, Sen. Valerie Foushee, and the Durham legislative delegation) to enact sensible gun control legislation. Commissioners also noted ensuring the resolution would be sent to the congressional delegation.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Adopted by Board resolution (signed by all 5 commissioners)

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Long Beverage Expansion FLUM Amendment and Rezoning (A1700015 / Z1700037)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Jamie Sunyak presented Case A1700015 / Z1700037 (applicant Patrick Byker of Morningstar) to amend the Future Land Use Map from Office to Industrial and rezone 2.187 acres at 3719 Page Road from Rural Residential (RR) to Industrial Light (IL) without a development plan, noting a 13-0 Planning Commission recommendation. Commissioners praised the new PowerPoint presentation format and asked about neighboring Office/Institutional parcels, which staff explained would be addressed in the upcoming FY19 Comprehensive Plan; after hearing from the applicant supporting the 60-year Durham family business, the Board unanimously approved the FLUM amendment, consistency statement, and IL rezoning across three separate voice votes.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following written balloting, the Clerk announced the appointments of Sylvia Alston, Dorothy Justice, and Brenda Brown to the Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee. The Board then adjourned by unanimous voice vote.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC March 12
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 12, 2018 regular session, the Durham County Board of Commissioners approved the January 2, 2018 work session minutes (5-0), reviewed the FY 2018-19 budget calendar while requesting additional work sessions to match the prior year's 28+ hours of deliberations, and unanimously adopted a time-sensitive Joint Resolution with the Social Services and Public Health boards opposing 2018 Farm Bill cuts or cost-shifts to SNAP (5-0). The board proclaimed April 3, 2018 as National Service Recognition Day and March 25, 2018 as Durham CROP Hunger Walk Day (honoring the late Baba Chuck Davis), and unanimously approved consent agenda items 18-0603 through 18-0676 (5-0), highlighting five new Open Space and Trails Matching Grants and a $140,000 Incredible Years parenting program grant. No closed session was held, and officials noted inclement weather could delay the next morning's Joint City-County Committee meeting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of January 2, 2018 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs confirmed the addition of the Joint SNAP Resolution to the agenda and announced JCPC DJJ grant deadlines (March 19), the 16th Annual Women's Forum (March 22), and a water resources legal forum (March 22). The board unanimously approved the January 2, 2018 work session minutes while discussing keeping future minutes concise alongside tracking staff directives.

agenda_items.title: Item 18-0685: Advance Public Comments and FY 2018-19 Budget Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no citizens signed up to speak—likely due to inclement weather and limited advance notice—staff agreed to carry forward an advance budget comment period to the next meeting. Commissioners requested polling for additional budget work sessions beyond May 24, May 31, June 4, and June 14 so the board could reach at least the 28+ deliberation hours held the prior year ahead of the June 11 public hearing and June 25 adoption.

agenda_items.title: Joint Resolution Supporting SNAP and Federal Nutrition Programs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter read a joint resolution with the Durham County Social Services Board and Board of Public Health urging North Carolina's congressional delegation to reject 2018 Farm Bill cuts, cost-shifts, or benefit reductions to SNAP (noting NC's $119 average monthly household benefit and 1.5 million+ recipients). The board unanimously approved the resolution.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations: National Service Recognition Day and Durham CROP Hunger Walk Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Recognition of IS&T analyst Bert White was deferred due to his absence. Chair Jacobs read proclamations declaring April 3, 2018 as National Service Recognition Day (AmeriCorps, Senior Corps, and NCCU Eagle Corps) and March 25, 2018 as Durham CROP Hunger Walk Day, joined by organizers Karen Johansson, Bob Newlin, and Marge Clemens highlighting the 44th annual walk's dedication to Baba Chuck Davis and Kenyan Safe School Zone fundraising.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Items 18-0603 through 18-0676)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners highlighted five new Open Space and Trails Matching Grants (bringing the 26-year program past 100 projects and $1.5 million awarded, including an Eno River canoe launch, Ellerbe Creek land, Lakewood Elementary improvements, Scrap Exchange open space, and 21 acres by Triangle Greenways Council) and a $140,000 grant expanding the Incredible Years program from birth to age eight. The board unanimously approved consent items 18-0603 through 18-0676.

agenda_items.title: Closing Updates: Federal SNAP Protection, Inclement Weather, and Remote Meeting Participation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners noted Senate federal budget updates protecting SNAP-related funding, the County Manager stated staff would decide after a 9:00 p.m. call whether freezing temperatures required delaying the next morning's Joint City-County Committee meeting, and members clarified non-voting remote phone participation procedures for the upcoming legislative breakfast.

votes.item_title: Approval of January 2, 2018 Work Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Approved with discussion on keeping future work session minutes briefer while ensuring staff directives are circulated.

votes.item_title: Joint Resolution Supporting SNAP and Federal Nutrition Programs
votes.discussion_detail: Joint resolution with Social Services and Public Health boards opposing 2018 Farm Bill cuts or cost-shifts to SNAP.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-03-08 9:00 AM - Worksession (Thursday Meeting date)
meetings.executive_summary: At the Thursday, March 8, 2018 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, citizens offered competing perspectives on the Confederate monument case and committee membership before Research Triangle Park (RTP) Foundation leadership presented phased master plans for Park Center featuring a 22-story hotel/conference tower ('The Archie'), rental housing, a Davis Drive grocery store, and dark-fiber connectivity. A sharp disagreement arose over the second County-RTP financial agreement (previously approved with two commissioners absent): a commissioner criticized the agreement as 'very loose' and opposed front-loading $15–$20 million without binding development commitments, prompting County leadership to commit to renegotiating county protections with RTP staff. Staff also alerted commissioners to upcoming construction fencing around the 200 E. Main Street courtyard where the Confederate monument stands, and reviewed consent items including Open Space matching grants (18-0604), general reappraisal visits, a $47,000 aging grant (18-0666), a $100,000 public art budget/policy update, a HIPAA risk assessment (18-0671), and an $80,000 Duke Endowment grant for Welcome Baby's Incredible Years expansion. No formal substantive votes were taken, and commissioners agreed to target a 2:00 PM hard stop for future work sessions.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Citizen Comments (Confederate Monument and Local Farming)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the special Thursday work session and read the public charge. George Roberson spoke on behalf of Defend Durham thanking Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Heidi Carter and urging removal of the remaining Confederate monument base, speaker Nicole provided a local farm progress update, and a 10-year military infantryman criticized the statue's tearing down and sought appointment to the monument committee.

agenda_items.title: RTP Park Center Redevelopment Presentation and County Funding Agreement Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: RTP Foundation representatives presented phased redevelopment plans for Park Center—including 1.1 million square feet of office/retail, two hotels including the 22-story 'The Archie' conference hotel, mid-rise rental housing, a Davis Drive grocery store, and MCNC dark fiber. Commissioners questioned mixed-income/affordable housing options and paid parking feasibility, and one commissioner sharply criticized the second County-RTP funding agreement (passed when two commissioners were absent) for front-loading $15–$20 million without back-loaded county protections, prompting staff and the Chair to schedule renegotiations with RTP staff.

agenda_items.title: 200 E. Main Street Courtyard Construction and Fencing Notification
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff alerted the Board to an impending news release regarding the building construction contract across the street and the planned courtyard redesign at 200 E. Main Street where the monuments sit. Because construction firms would soon erect fencing in a sensitive public area, staff briefed commissioners in advance for full transparency.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review and Work Session Time-Limit Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed consent items including Admin II Phase 2, Item 18-0604 (Open Space and Trails Matching Grants), general reappraisal property visit requirements, Item 18-0666 ($47,000 Home and Community Care Block Grant and electronic Aging Plan request), the $100,000 public art project ($65,000 fabrication/installation) and revised arts policy, Item 18-0671 (HIPAA gap analysis), disparity study reporting consistency, and an $80,000 Duke Endowment amendment for Welcome Baby / Incredible Years. disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-03-08 9:00 AM - Worksession (Thursday Meeting date)
disagreements.issue: County-RTP Park Center Funding Agreement: Front-Loading $15–$20M vs. Back-Loaded Protections
disagreements.summary: Following the RTP Park Center redevelopment briefing, a commissioner challenged the second County-RTP funding agreement as overly loose and opposed committing $15–$20 million upfront without firm development milestones.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require back-loaded county incentives tied to actual construction and binding commitments rather than front-loading $15–$20 million under a loose agreement.
side_a_arguments: Durham County's standard practice has been to verify development first and pay incentives on the back end.
The second agreement—approved when two commissioners were absent—lacks adequate county protections and is overly loose.
The County cannot spend $15–$20 million upfront merely hoping development materializes without coincident commitments.
disagreements.side_b_position: Some front-end infrastructure investment is needed for Park Center, and staff should meet with RTP leadership to clarify front-end vs. binding obligations.
side_b_arguments: Some degree of front-loading is required to enable Park Center's initial infrastructure and commercial momentum.
County staff and RTP Foundation leadership can review the second agreement's obligations and return to the Board with clarified protections.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; the Chair and County Manager directed staff to meet with Scott and RTP Foundation staff to work through front-end obligations and strengthen county protections.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-02-26 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 26, 2018 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board unanimously approved past meeting minutes (requesting a work-session accounting of pending directives), heard testimony from Triangle Literacy Council / Durham YouthBuild participants, and unanimously approved the consent agenda (Items 18-0638 through 18-0664). Planning staff presented UDO Text Amendment TC16-0005 proposing density, height, and zero-parking bonuses for affordable housing in compact neighborhood transit tiers (at least 15% of units at 60% AMI or below), and the Board later took up a contested zoning map change from Rural Residential (RR) to Industrial Light (IL) without a development plan for a timber/log transshipment operation. On the consistency statement required under N.C.G.S. 153A-341, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded an affirmative motion per staff procedure so opponents could vote it down, resulting in a failed 1-4 voice vote (the transcript digest records the 1-4 voice tally without identifying which single member voted Aye versus the four Nays, amid brief procedural confusion over voting on an affirmative motion). On the subsequent motion by Reckhow seconded by Howerton to adopt the Industrial Light rezoning ordinance, all five seated commissioners—Wendy Jacobs, James Hill, Ellen W. Reckhow, Brenda A. Howerton, and Heidi Carter—voted Nay in a 0-5 (5-0 opposed) defeat. The Board then made ballot appointments to four advisory boards and adjourned unanimously into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) for economic development negotiations.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Approval of Minutes (Dec. 4, 2017 and Feb. 12, 2018)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs announced the March 3 Summer Work Youth Job Expo at Holton Career and Resource Center and NCDJJDP grant applications. On a motion by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, the Board unanimously approved the December 4 and February 12 work and regular session minutes while requesting an accounting of unresolved work-session directives.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Presentation: Durham YouthBuild / Bull City YouthBuild
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Corey Rawlinson of the Triangle Literacy Council and Durham YouthBuild introduced program participants—including Kevin Sims and a young participant sharing his journey from gun charges to probation and community service—highlighting the program's blend of education, hands-on construction training, and past funding challenges.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 18-0638 through 18-0664)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered Consent Agenda Items 18-0638 through 18-0664 with no items pulled. On a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, the consent agenda passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC16-0005 — Compact Neighborhood Interim Affordable Housing Bonuses
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Hannah Jacobson presented TC16-0005, proposing administrative density bonuses (up to 75 units/acre), height bonuses (up to 90 feet), and zero minimum parking in compact neighborhood tiers where at least 15% of units serve households at or below 60% AMI, alongside technical Section 6.6 updates from Omnibus 11 (TC17-05). Planning Commission recommended approval 12-1 and City Council approved it the previous week; Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow inquired about the interim timeline (Patterson Place rezoning within one year) before the public hearing opened (final vote omitted in digest truncation).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Public hearing opened (vote omitted in truncated digest)

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing (Resumed): Zoning Map Change from Rural Residential (RR) to Industrial Light (IL) — Timber/Log Transshipment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming mid-hearing on a rezoning request from Rural Residential (RR) to Industrial Light (IL) without a development plan for timber and log storage/transshipment, commissioners objected to 18-wheeler traffic, noise externalities, and residential incompatibility despite the Industrial Future Land Use designation. After briefly reopening the public hearing to weigh a 30-day continuance and declining to delay, the Board rejected the N.C.G.S. 153A-341 consistency statement on a 1-4 voice vote (with one commissioner noting confusion over voting down an affirmative motion) and then defeated the Industrial Light rezoning ordinance 0-5 (5-0 opposed).

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following written balloting, the Clerk announced appointments to four boards: Mary Delahunt Andrews and Jonathan Leach (Environmental Affairs Board), Donald Abdul (Firefighters Relief Fund Board of Trustees), Jeffrey Wolf, Mary Braywhite, and Stephen Derek (Public Health Board), and Quirias Anderson (Women's Commission).

agenda_items.title: Motion to Adjourn to Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Vice Chair James Hill, the Board voted unanimously by voice vote to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss industrial/business location or expansion and tentative economic development incentives.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-02-26 7:00 PM - Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Rural Residential to Industrial Light Rezoning Without a Development Plan (Timber/Log Transshipment Site)
disagreements.summary: During a public hearing on rezoning a Rural Residential parcel to Industrial Light without a development plan for timber/log transshipment, commissioners debated the mismatch between the Future Land Use Map's Industrial designation and surrounding residential growth, leading to a 1-4 failed consistency-statement vote and a 0-5 defeat of the rezoning.
disagreements.side_a_position: The Future Land Use Map designates the corridor Industrial, and storage/transshipment of logs without on-site processing is technically permissible under Industrial Light zoning.
side_a_arguments: Planning staff noted the site falls within an Industrial land-use designation on the Comprehensive Plan's Future Land Use Map.
Without on-site timber processing (which would require Heavy Industrial), log storage and transshipment fits Light Industrial standards, and site-plan rules still apply.
disagreements.side_b_position: Deny the rezoning because Industrial Light without a development plan permits heavy 18-wheeler traffic and noise incompatible with growing nearby residential uses.
side_b_arguments: Without a binding development plan, any Industrial Light use could locate on the parcel.
Unloading and moving large timber/logs with 18-wheelers creates noise and traffic externalities inappropriate next to residential homes.
Growing residential development in the surrounding area makes Industrial Light inconsistent with on-the-ground neighborhood conditions.
disagreements.resolution: After declining a 30-day continuance, the Board rejected the N.C.G.S. 153A-341 consistency statement 1-4 by voice vote (with one commissioner noting procedural confusion on the affirmative motion) and voted 0-5 (5-0 opposed) to defeat the rezoning ordinance.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-02-12 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 12, 2018 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved the January 22, 2018 regular session minutes, the consent agenda (Items 18-0599 through 18-0649), and a motion to enter closed session on economic development incentives, personnel, and attorney-client privilege matters by voice votes, with no split or contested votes. Chair Jacobs corrected the rescheduled date of the Youth Summer Work Expo to Saturday, March 3 at Holton Career and Resource Center (noting 800 youth applied for roughly 200 summer internships the prior year), announced the 2018 primary candidate filing period through February 28, and promoted upcoming February 17 and February 22 public input sessions and multilingual online surveys on the 300 and 500 blocks of East Main Street redevelopment. The Board held a ceremonial recognition honoring Durham County Library staff (led by Director Tammy Baggett and interim Main Library manager Faith Burns) and the Friends of the Durham Library (co-chairs Carol Ann Walters and Jane Goodrich) for receiving the North Carolina Public Library Directors Association Service Innovation Award and Library Friend of the Year Award for the 'Downtown Library Without Walls' initiative, which maintained services during Main Library closure through Northgate Mall leased space, bookmobile expansion, Criminal Justice Resource Center digital access, and Maker Lab tutoring.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting at 7:01 p.m., read the public charge, led the Pledge of Allegiance, and confirmed no agenda adjustments. She corrected the rescheduled Youth Summer Work Expo date to March 3 (10 a.m. to noon at Holton Career and Resource Center) and urged local businesses to host summer interns after 800 youth applied for about 200 spots the previous year. Chair Jacobs also announced the 2018 candidate filing window (February 12–28) and upcoming public input sessions (February 17 and February 22) plus English and Spanish online surveys for the 300 and 500 blocks of East Main Street redevelopment.

agenda_items.title: Approval of January 22, 2018 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered the minutes from the January 22, 2018 regular session. On a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, the minutes were unanimously approved by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognition: Durham County Library and Friends of the Durham Library Awards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recognized the Durham County Library and the Friends of the Durham Library for winning the North Carolina Public Library Directors Association Service Innovation Award and Library Friend of the Year Award. Library Director Tammy Baggett, interim Main Library manager Faith Burns, grant writer Annie Mountcastle, and Friends board president Carolyn highlighted the 'Downtown Library Without Walls' initiative—including Northgate Mall leased space for the North Carolina Collection, Maker Lab, and book sales, expanded bookmobile stops, over 1,000 community members served at the Criminal Justice Resource Center digital access center, and Duke/teen tutoring for over 40 pre-K–6 students. Chair Jacobs presented a Board proclamation honoring Friends book-sale co-chairs Carol Ann Walters and Jane Goodrich.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 18-0599 through 18-0649)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs asked whether commissioners wished to pull any items from consent agenda items 18-0599 through 18-0649. With no items pulled, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved approval and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded, passing unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Adjourn to Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read three statutory bases for entering closed session: business location/expansion and tentative economic development incentives (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4)), personnel performance/employment/complaint matters (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6)), and attorney-client consultation (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)). On a motion by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, the Board unanimously voted to adjourn to closed session.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-02-08 8:30 AM - Worksession (Thursday Meeting date)
meetings.executive_summary: At its February 8, 2018 Worksession presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Durham Board of County Commissioners voted unanimously by voice vote to suspend the rules and approve the framework for a City-County Committee on Confederate Monuments and Memorials, with no split or contested votes taken. Jason Morado of ETC Institute presented results from 609 completed 2017 resident surveys showing over 60% of residents felt Durham County was moving in the right direction (15% disagreed), public school operations remained the top area for tax willingness, and public health and wellness rose by at least 5%, while commissioners examined survey wording around pre-K and noted 22% of residents had lived in the county fewer than five years. Following an HR update on the Classification and Compensation Study RFP (which drew only one bid after a two-week December window) and a truncated middle segment, the Board approved the focused Confederate monuments committee framework with the understanding that Chair Jacobs would return with her suggested co-chair appointment for Board approval. Commissioners also reviewed a Department of Social Services (DSS) staffing and retention proposal from Director Ben Rose and a $107,000 annualized Health and Human Services (HHS) building security screening contract amendment prompted by weapons and altercation incidents, as well as staff materials on evaluating a potential opioid lawsuit.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Schedule Constraints
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the worksession, read the public charge, and confirmed no citizens were signed up for public comment. She reminded attendees that the agenda was tight because commissioners were departing for the Chamber luncheon.

agenda_items.title: Presentation of 2017 Resident Survey Data
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County staff introduced Jason Morado of ETC Institute, who presented findings from 609 randomly sampled mail, online, and phone resident surveys (with new questions added on 24/7 emergency information and elections). Over 60% of respondents believed Durham County was moving in the right direction compared to 15% who disagreed, and public school operations remained the top priority for tax willingness while public health and wellness increased at least 5% (with 24% the prior year opposing any higher taxes). Commissioners discussed how 'subsidies' phrasing may have lowered pre-K support and noted Vice Chair James Hill's observation that 22% of residents had lived in Durham under five years; staff also previewed an interactive cross-tabulation data tool for the March worksession.

agenda_items.title: Classification and Compensation Study RFP Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Human Resources staff updated the Board on the FY 2017-18 Classification and Compensation Study (last implemented in 2014 and recommended every three to four years). After a minimum two-week December RFP window yielded only one response because surrounding jurisdictions were conducting concurrent studies and two prior bidders had merged, staff interviewed Management Advisory Group. Commissioners questioned why the RFP went out so late after budget approval and asked about response rates.

agenda_items.title: City-County Committee on Confederate Monuments and Memorials Framework
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, commissioners discussed narrowing the proposed joint City-County committee's scope specifically to Confederate monuments, memorials, and symbols while fostering broad community participation, with County Attorney Lowell Siler noting outside legal expert Adam Lovelady had agreed to assist while reserving formal legal decisions for the City and County Attorneys. After a commissioner sought assurance on appointment process transparency, the Board first voted unanimously to suspend the rules and then voted unanimously to approve the framework with the understanding that Chair Wendy Jacobs would bring back her suggested co-chair appointment for Board approval.

agenda_items.title: Department of Social Services (DSS) Staffing Request and Retention Strategic Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DSS Director Ben Rose, accompanied by Social Services Board Chair Tara Fikes and staff, presented a request for additional FTEs—funded in the current year and sought in the upcoming budget—citing caseload capacity, state performance measures, and staff turnover. Chair Jacobs praised Rose's accompanying retention strategic plan and confirmed with the County Manager that the item was slated for Monday's consent agenda, though a commissioner noted she had not realized this specific item was on the agenda.

agenda_items.title: Health and Human Services (HHS) Building Security Contract Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a $107,000 annualized security contract amendment to add walkthrough screening, hand-carried bag checks, and exit-only door monitoring at the HHS building using three officers plus morning part-time coverage during peak hours. Chair Jacobs, citing her Social Services Board role, noted ongoing incidents involving weapons and fights inside the building, while Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and another commissioner noted they had not received full background context beforehand. Vice Chair James Hill asked about ADA access for strollers and wheelchairs (which staff confirmed was built into the plan) and whether visitors would be escorted as in the former Duke Street building (staff confirmed visitors would proceed freely after screening).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Process, Opioid Litigation Follow-Up, and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Due to time constraints before the Chamber luncheon, Chair Jacobs suggested directing any Monday consent agenda questions directly to the County Manager. A commissioner distributed staff follow-up materials on calculating opioid-related costs and legal considerations for a potential opioid lawsuit, and the Board adjourned on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Vice Chair James Hill.
