meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-01-22 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its January 22, 2018 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved (5-0) the January 8, 2018 minutes, an amended resolution opposing changing North Carolina's election of judges to appointment or subdividing Durham judicial districts, and an economic development incentive for Corning, while also approving board and commission appointments by ballot, with no split or contested votes recorded. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow amended the judicial-elections resolution—which Chair Jacobs had reviewed with Rep. Marcia Morey—to replace 'selection' with 'appointment' and direct copies to the local legislative delegation and all 100 North Carolina county boards. Chair Jacobs also presented a draft National Association of Counties (NACo) interim resolution prepared with Durham Housing Authority CEO Anthony Scott urging Congress to lift the federal Rental Assistance Demonstration (RAD) cap and preserve supportive services funding, agreeing to remove the County Board header so it remained a draft NACo committee proposal. Following public hearings, the Board approved the Corning manufacturing and logistics incentive (~269–317 jobs, with workforce coordination involving Durham Tech, DPS CTE, NCWorks, and Made in Durham) and heard a presentation and motion on Item 18-0616 for Braeburn Pharmaceuticals' opioid-treatment facility funded via a Longfellow Real Estate pass-through donation, while deferring Women's Commission appointments to the February worksession.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting at 7:02 p.m., read the public charge, led the Pledge of Allegiance, and highlighted two time-sensitive resolutions added to the agenda regarding the election of judges and a NACo public housing resolution. Announcements included DCHC MPO public feedback, GoTriangle's February 6 Connecting to Opportunity Summit, and a rescheduled March 10 community event.

agenda_items.title: Approval of January 8, 2018 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed the minutes of the January 8, 2018 regular session. On a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, the minutes passed 5-0 by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognition: Soil and Water Conservation District Award & CHIP Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recognized Soil and Water Conservation staff alongside Chris Hogan of the North Carolina Association of Soil and Water Conservation Districts for county conservation and grant achievements. Following the presentation, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton noted that when she missed the January 8 meeting she had been in Washington, D.C. advocating with members of Congress for the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP), which had just received a six-year federal extension.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Opposing Change from Election to Appointment of Judges
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs introduced a Beaufort County draft resolution revised with input from Rep. Marcia Morey (former Chief District Court Judge) opposing any North Carolina constitutional amendment eliminating judicial elections or dividing Durham into judicial sub-districts. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow proposed substituting 'appointment' for 'selection' in the third whereas clause along with minor wording corrections and removing a middle initial from Vice Chair James Hill's name. Moved as amended by Commissioner Heidi Carter and seconded by Commissioner Reckhow, the resolution passed 5-0 with instructions to send it to the local delegation and all 100 county clerks.

agenda_items.title: Draft NACo Interim Resolution on Public Housing (RAD Program) and Supportive Services
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presented a draft interim resolution prepared with Durham Housing Authority CEO Anthony Scott for her work on the National Association of Counties (NACo) Community, Economic and Workforce Development Steering Committee. The draft urged lifting the federal cap on the Rental Assistance Demonstration (RAD) program—critical to Durham's mixed-income public housing redevelopment plans—and protecting supportive services funding for job placement and financial management. After a truncated middle segment, commissioners voiced support while confirming the County Board header would be removed so it served strictly as a draft NACo committee resolution.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Economic Development Incentive for Corning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the truncated middle portion, commissioners and staff discussed aligning Durham's workforce pipeline—including the Office of Economic and Workforce Development, NCWorks, Durham Public Schools career and technical education, Durham Tech, Made in Durham, and the Chamber—to support Corning's hiring of roughly 269 to 317 manufacturing and logistics workers. Staff confirmed to Commissioner Heidi Carter that mutually agreed performance targets, budget amendments, and contract execution authorization would return to the Board in writing. After closing the public hearing, the Board approved the incentive 5-0 on a motion by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow.

agenda_items.title: Item 18-0616: Public Hearing and Economic Development Investment Funds for Braeburn Pharmaceuticals
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Director Jay Gibson and Chamber representative Ted Connor presented Item 18-0616 for Braeburn Pharmaceuticals, a New Jersey-founded developer of 3-to-6-month injectable treatments for opioid addiction and chronic pain, noting the incentive would be funded through a private pass-through donation from Longfellow Real Estate vetted by County Attorney Lowell Siler and a written North Carolina Attorney General opinion. Chair Jacobs highlighted that Braeburn and Corning together bring about 360 manufacturing jobs requiring Durham Tech training partnerships. After the public hearing closed, a commissioner moved approval of the incentive at 01:16:49, though the transcript digest does not record the second or final vote call before transitioning to board appointments.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Motion made; vote outcome not captured in transcript

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments and Deferral of Women's Commission
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners agreed to hold the Women's Commission appointments until their February worksession because applications had been added over the weekend. At 01:27:20, the Clerk announced the results of the Board's ballot votes selecting four members to the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee (Christopher Fisher, Jennifer Melvin, Christopher Jones, Kimberly Robertson), five members to the GoTriangle Citizen Advisory Committee (Philip Azar, Nicholas Norbaj, Monique Velasquez, Ed Woodsey Harrison, Jacob Rogers), and one member to the Historic Preservation Commission (Matt Bouchard).

votes.item_title: Approval of January 8, 2018 Regular Session Minutes
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote; all five seated commissioners were confirmed present during the meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the minutes of the January 8, 2018 regular session without amendment.

votes.item_title: Resolution Opposing Change from Election to Appointment of Judges (As Amended)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote; Chair Jacobs requested distribution to the local legislative delegation and clerks of all 100 NC counties.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the resolution opposing any North Carolina constitutional amendment changing judicial elections to appointment or dividing Durham into sub-districts, incorporating Commissioner Reckhow's wording edits ('appointment' for 'selection', 'supports', 'ensures') and removing middle initial 'A' from James Hill's name.

votes.item_title: Approval of Economic Development Incentive for Corning
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote; staff noted mutually agreed targets, budget amendments, and formal contract authorization would return to the Board in writing.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the economic development incentive for Corning following the public hearing and workforce readiness discussion.

votes.item_title: Appointments to Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee, GoTriangle Citizen Advisory Committee, and Historic Preservation Commission
votes.notes: Individual commissioner ballot tallies were not read into the transcript; only the final selected appointees were announced.
votes.discussion_detail: Clerk read the Board's ballot voting results: Christopher Fisher, Jennifer Melvin, Christopher Jones, and Kimberly Robertson (Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee); Philip Azar, Nicholas Norbaj, Monique Velasquez, Ed Woodsey Harrison, and Jacob Rogers (GoTriangle Citizen Advisory Committee); and Matt Bouchard (Historic Preservation Commission). Women's Commission appointments were deferred to the February worksession.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-01-08 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 8, 2018 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton absent (excused at the January 2 worksession while in Washington, D.C.), the four attending commissioners unanimously approved (4-0) all action items by voice vote, with no split or contested votes. The Board approved the November 6 and December 11, 2017 minutes (commending detailed directive tracking), the consent agenda (Items 18-0516 through 18-0591), an ambulance service franchise award to Medix Medical Transport following a public hearing with Interim EMS Director Kevin Underhill and Medix COO Jeff White, and a motion to enter closed session on attorney-client privilege matters including Marcheta Welton v. Durham County et al. The Board also recognized county staff and federal/state collaboration on the Rougemont water line project, highlighted Information Services and Technology's (IS&T) national effectiveness award alongside a regional Complex Coordinated Terrorist Attack (CCTA) preparedness grant partnered with Wake and Orange counties, and adopted ceremonial resolutions supporting youth mentoring (including County employee volunteer leave) and honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. alongside the Durham MLK Steering Committee.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Board Recruitment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m., read the public charge, and confirmed no agenda adjustments. Announcements promoted GoTriangle's February 6 Connecting to Opportunity Summit at DPAC around the $2 billion-plus light rail project, GoTriangle light rail appearance workshops, the January 11 City-County MLK Jr. Program, an early childhood community input session (100 Counties / Pathways to Grade-Level Reading / 2017 Pre-K Task Force Report), and a call for volunteers on a county board.

agenda_items.title: Approval of November 6, 2017 and December 11, 2017 Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered the November 6, 2017 worksession and December 11, 2017 regular session minutes. On a motion by Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded by Vice Chair James Hill, the minutes passed 4-0 by voice vote. Chair Jacobs praised staff's detailed capture of Board directives and asked staff to distribute minutes and follow up on directives.

agenda_items.title: Rougemont Water Line Project and Staff Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presenters recounted the multi-year Rougemont water line project originating with 2009 ARRA funding and intergovernmental coordination with Person County, culminating in completion through federal, state, and local collaboration. Staff member Drew was recognized in connection with the Atlanta Federal Executive Board's Employee of the Year public service awards program.

agenda_items.title: IS&T National Award and Complex Coordinated Terrorist Attack (CCTA) Grant Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a national effectiveness award earned by the Information Services and Technology department, highlighting Durham County's continuously updated jurisdiction-wide technology plan. Officials also briefed the Board on the Complex Coordinated Terrorist Attack (CCTA) grant awarded in September in regional partnership with Wake and Orange counties, covering work plans, budgets, family and friend assistance centers, crisis communications, resource management, and suspicious activity reporting.

agenda_items.title: Youth Mentoring Resolution and Community Partnership Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs read a Board resolution promoting youth mentoring outcomes and highlighted a county employee policy permitting one hour of paid time per week for school or nonprofit mentoring, suggesting county government could recruit 31 mentors. Community mentors and youth advocates (including Mr. Lewis, Mr. Thomas, and Edmund) spoke extensively on reaching vulnerable youth and strengthening collaboration across local mentoring groups.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Celebrating and Honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill read the Board's resolution celebrating and honoring the life and civil rights legacy of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Durham MLK Steering Committee Chairman William Lucas, committee member Grace Wilson, and other subcommittee representatives thanked the Board and invited the community to upcoming MLK holiday observances.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 18-0516 through 18-0591)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: No items were pulled from consent agenda items 18-0516 through 18-0591. On a motion by Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, the consent agenda passed 4-0 by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Ambulance Service Franchise Award to Medix Medical Transport
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim EMS Director Kevin Underhill and Medix Medical Transport COO Jeff White presented an application to award an ambulance service franchise to Medix, starting with 10 vehicles in Durham County (out of 62 regional units) to handle non-critical, critical care, and bariatric transports and reduce call volume on 911 paramedics. With no other speakers at the public hearing, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved approval and Vice Chair James Hill seconded, passing 4-0 by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Adjourn to Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read two closed session items under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to preserve attorney-client privilege—one concerning Marcheta Welton v. Durham County, Durham Board of County Commissioners, Wendell Davis, and Kathy Everett-Perry, and a second general attorney-client consultation (confirming a crossed-out first item was omitted). On a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Heidi Carter, the Board voted 4-0 by voice vote to enter closed session.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2018-01-02 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 2, 2018 Worksession presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously voted (5-0) to suspend the rules and excuse Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton from the January 8, 2018 regular meeting, with no split or contested votes taken. During citizen comments, speakers addressed the 300 block of East Main Street mixed-use housing/parking concept—urging formal architect engagement with nearby churches, the library, Durham Housing Authority, and the City—and opposed proposed Sheriff protest rules at the Durham County jail following the toppling of the Confederate monument. Associate Director Christie Raleigh and Sarah Odio of the UNC Development Finance Initiative (DFI) presented pre-development market and housing-affordability analysis for the county-owned 300 and 500 East Main Street surface parking lots, highlighting naturally occurring affordable housing losses and high cost burdens among single non-elderly under-62 households and small families under 80% AMI. Following a truncated middle segment, commissioners discussed decoupling a proposed public art policy (covering capital percentages, ongoing O&M costs, and Main Library sculptures) from June budget workshops into an April or May worksession, questioned MWBE/WBE procurement on consent item 566, and directed staff to prepare a briefing on recent chemical findings at the Triangle Wastewater Plant.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Citizen Comment Period
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the worksession, read the public charge, and moderated citizen comments. Jim Savar (representing St. Philip's and First Presbyterian) cited architect Jared Martinson's feasible 75–80-unit mixed-use housing, retail, and parking concept on the 300 block of East Main Street and criticized the architect RFQ for omitting explicit public engagement with neighborhood churches, the library, Durham Housing Authority, and the City. Another speaker from Inside-Outside Alliance criticized proposed Sheriff protest rules on county property at the Durham County jail in the wake of the Confederate monument removal.

agenda_items.title: Development Finance Initiative (DFI) Pre-Development Update on 300 and 500 Blocks of East Main Street
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DFI's Christie Raleigh and Sarah Odio, joined by Jay Gibson and Deputy Engineering Director Perry Manns, outlined the delayed pre-development timeline, architect massing-diagram scope for financial pro formas, and guiding public goals for the 300 and 500 East Main Street parking lots. Presenters defined naturally occurring affordable housing (NOAH), noted that all downtown projects under construction carry rents above current market rates, and showed that single non-elderly under-62 households and small families below 80% AMI account for the largest shares of cost-burdened households, while Chair Jacobs noted small locally owned shops struggle with current market retail rents.

agenda_items.title: Public Art Policy, Capital/Operating Budget Linkage, and Directives Tracking
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, staff discussed creating a county public art policy—addressing whether to dedicate a percentage of major capital project budgets, factoring ongoing O&M lifecycle costs and certificate-of-occupancy timelines, and supporting outdoor sculptures planned for the Main Library—alongside Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's note on updating the county's Arts Committee/Commission. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow requested decoupling the policy discussion from congested June budget workshops into an April or May worksession, which staff agreed would still inform upcoming capital and operating budgets; officials also confirmed Clerk tracking of a running directives list.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Comments and Excusal of Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners thanked organizers of the Week of Peace, noted upcoming early childhood meetings with Partnership for Children and Child Care Services Association, invited items for upcoming federal advocacy, and paid tribute to late civil rights pioneer Leroy Frazier (who helped integrate UNC-Chapel Hill in 1955). Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved to suspend the rules (seconded by Commissioner Heidi Carter) and then moved to excuse Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton from the January 8 regular meeting (seconded by Vice Chair James Hill), with both motions passing 5-0 by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review, Procurement Questions, and Triangle Wastewater Plant Follow-Up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager summarized upcoming consent agenda items including ~$14,000 in grant funds (item 562), a moving consultant contract, procurement item 566, and office systems for the building across the street. Commissioners Brenda A. Howerton and Heidi Carter questioned why lower-priced contender Hillards was not selected on item 566 and whether MWBE/WBE firms were evaluated; staff cited quality-based legal selection rules and prior manhole damage issues with that vendor. Chair Jacobs also requested a staff briefing/white paper (added to the directives list) on recent news regarding chemicals found in water at the Triangle Wastewater Plant before the Board adjourned.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend the Rules
votes.notes: Passed unanimously (5-0) by voice vote; all five seated commissioners were confirmed present during the worksession.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended Board rules to allow a motion excusing a commissioner's upcoming regular-meeting absence.

votes.item_title: Motion to Excuse Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton from January 8, 2018 Regular Meeting
votes.notes: Passed unanimously (5-0) by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Excused Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton from attending the Monday, January 8, 2018 regular Board meeting.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-12-11 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Vice Chair James Hill in Chair Wendy Jacobs' excused absence, the Durham County Board of Commissioners approved the October 2 work session and November 27 regular session minutes and adopted Consent Agenda Items 17-0500 through 17-0556 by unanimous 4-0 voice votes. The Board held ceremonial recognitions for Champions in Transportation Week, UNC-Chapel Hill's 2BEAT HIV Cure Research project, community organizer Umar Muasah Muhammad, and retiring CFO George Kenneth Quick after 16 years of service. Commissioners Heidi Carter and Ellen W. Reckhow presented a joint resolution urging the North Carolina General Assembly to fully fund and slow implementation of state-mandated K-3 class size reductions (S.L. 2017-9) during a January special session, coordinating with the Durham Board of Education and other counties statewide. Auditor Scott Duda (Cherry Bekaert) presented the FY 2016-17 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR), reporting Local Government Commission approval without recommendations, a recurring eligibility compliance finding, and fund balance growth driven primarily by departments underspending budgets by more than 10%.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and Winter Fire Safety Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill called the meeting to order at 7:02 PM, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Announcements highlighted winter home fire prevention, safe spacing for heaters and fireplaces, annual chimney inspections, and carbon monoxide detector installation.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (October 2, 2017 Work Session and November 27, 2017 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered the minutes for the October 2, 2017 Work Session and the November 27, 2017 Regular Session. The minutes were approved unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Champions in Transportation Week and Champion Transportation Awards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board proclaimed December 11-18, 2017 as Champions in Transportation Week in Durham County to raise awareness of demand-response transit services. The Chair of the Durham County Transportation Advisory Board presented the Durham County Access Champion Transportation Awards recognizing riders and community partners.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation and Recognition: UNC-Chapel Hill HIV Cure Research and 2BEAT HIV Project
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recognized UNC-Chapel Hill's HIV Cure clinical trials research, which brought over $40 million in federal funding, and the 2BEAT HIV project's Health Equity Impact Award from the NC Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities. Speakers noted that North Carolina also officially proclaimed HIV Cure Research Day.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Umar Muasah Muhammad
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board read a memorial resolution honoring community leader Umar Muasah Muhammad following his passing on July 17, 2017. The resolution highlighted his advocacy with All of Us or None NC, the Ban the Box movement, Clean Slate clinics at the Southern Coalition for Social Justice, Forward Justice, and the Criminal Justice Advisory Committee.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Recognizing Retirement of Chief Financial Officer George Kenneth Quick
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board read a resolution honoring George Kenneth Quick upon his retirement after more than 16 years as Durham County's Chief Financial Officer. The resolution credited Quick with strengthening and growing Durham County's fund balance reserves and financial operations.

agenda_items.title: Joint Resolution Regarding K-3 Class Size Reduction Implementation (S.L. 2017-9)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow and Heidi Carter jointly read a resolution requesting that the North Carolina General Assembly fully fund small classes and slow the 2018-19 K-3 class size mandate during a January special session, warning of teacher shortages and forced budget trade-offs before May. Commissioners discussed circulating the resolution to all 100 NC counties, NCACC, NCSBA, and the Durham Board of Education ahead of its Thursday vote.

agenda_items.title: FY 2016-17 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) and Audit Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Managing partner Scott Duda of Cherry Bekaert presented the FY 2016-17 audit, reporting two passed adjustments related to construction-in-progress, LGC approval prior to October 31 without recommendations, and a recurring compliance finding on eligibility. Commissioners questioned why several departments underspent budgets by more than 10-15% and discussed using mid-year budget amendments and Management's Discussion and Analysis, which noted Durham MSA per capita income rose 3.92% in 2015 to $44,507.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 17-0500 through 17-0556)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered Consent Agenda Items 17-0500 through 17-0556 without pulling any items for separate discussion. The Consent Agenda passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following ballot voting, the results were announced to Vice Chair James Hill and the Board. Katie Hamilton was appointed to the Historic Preservation Commission, and Keith Bryant and John (surname untranscribed) were selected for two seats on the Open Space and Trails Commission.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-12-04 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 4, 2017 Work Session, Vice Chair James Hill opened the annual organizational election, in which the Board unanimously re-elected Wendy Jacobs as Chair (5-0) and James Hill as Vice Chair (5-0) before Chair Jacobs assumed the gavel. The Board unanimously suspended the rules (5-0) and approved annual public official bonds (5-0) ahead of Finance Director George Quick's January 1 retirement and successor Susan Tezai's incoming appointment. Public commenters including graduate student researchers (such as Gary Bush) presented survey findings on the Confederate Soldiers Monument at the Old Courthouse and the Unity Monument at Bennett Place, while staff briefed commissioners on the Main Street building project staying on schedule and within its $47 million overall budget. Following a middle portion omitted from the digest, commissioners discussed drafting a K-3 class size reduction resolution, reviewing the October 2016 RTP Foundation Park Center contract amendment, refining Chair Jacobs' monument public-input commission proposal, approving excused absences for Jacobs (Dec 11) and Hill (Jan) via unanimous 5-0 votes, and adjourning 5-0 into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Annual Election of Chair and Vice Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill read the public charge and opened the floor for the annual December election of Board Chair. Wendy Jacobs was nominated and unanimously elected Chair (5-0), after which she took the chair seat and presided over the unanimous election of James Hill as Vice Chair (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Approval of Public Official Bonds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented annual public official bonds protecting the public and officials in their duties, noting Finance Director George Quick's January 1 retirement and incoming Finance Director Susan Tezai (transcribed 'Susan T. Sy') requiring a subsequent bond. The Board voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and 5-0 to approve the bonds.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments (Confederate Monuments Survey and Detention Center Food Service)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public administration graduate students including Gary Bush presented survey research on Durham's Confederate monuments, recommending no public funds for maintenance or restoration, leaving the Old Courthouse sale to George Lawson/Larson unchanged, and establishing a permanent diverse community outreach task force. Other speakers commented on the Mariah Woods case and criticized ABL detention center food service.

agenda_items.title: Main Street / County Facility Construction, Budget, and Public Art Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Project staff presented interior and exterior construction progress on the Main Street building, confirming the project remained on schedule and within its overall budget of just over $47 million (approximately $38.9-$39 million in construction with contingencies, comparable to the library). Commissioners discussed the structural engineering review and questioned whether the public art selection committee was sufficiently inclusive across community organizations.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Updates (K-3 Resolution, Grown in Durham, RTP Foundation Amendment, and Monument Commission)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle portion omitted from the transcript digest, commissioners discussed Guilford County's Camp Hope youth trauma program, preparing a K-3 class size and school construction bond resolution for a January legislative special session, scheduling community forums on Grown in Durham, and requesting a staff memo on the October 10, 2016 RTP Foundation contract amendment affecting Park Center scope and 2018 payment exposure. Chair Jacobs also circulated revisions to her draft Confederate monument public-input commission proposal and flagged a second grant MOU.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absences for Chair Wendy Jacobs (Dec 11) and Vice Chair James Hill (Jan)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously suspended the rules and granted Chair Wendy Jacobs an excused absence for the December 11, 2017 Regular Session (with Vice Chair James Hill set to preside), and then suspended the rules and granted Vice Chair Hill an excused absence for the January meeting. Chair Jacobs directed staff to ensure excused absences are clearly noted in future agendas and minutes.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Comments and Adjournment to Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter reported on a General Assembly law taking effect December 1 and follow-up with the Sheriff's Office regarding approximately 20 detainees in the jail, slated for the January work session. The Board then voted 5-0 (moved by Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by James Hill) to adjourn to closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss economic development incentives and business location or expansion.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-11-27 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 27, 2017 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved the November 13 regular session minutes (5-0) and Consent Agenda Items 17-0512 through 17-0543 (5-0). Announcements highlighted Durham Parks and Recreation's 46th Annual Senior Holiday Party, winter fire safety, the December 15 ACA open enrollment deadline, and the deployment of 300 dockless shared bikes by LimeBike and Spin. In a ceremonial presentation, Duke Energy representative Casey Furr joined Durham Soil and Water Conservation District officials to recognize a $26,500 Water Resources Grant supporting a summer youth stormwater and environmental internship program with Durham Public Schools and Durham YouthWorks. The Board also appointed members by ballot to the Farmland Protection Advisory Board and the Women's Commission before voting unanimously 5-0 to adjourn into closed session for personnel matters under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting at 7:01 PM, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Announcements covered the December 12 Senior Holiday Party, winter candle and heating fire safety, the December 15 ACA health insurance deadline, LimeBike and Spin deploying 300 dockless bikes in Durham, and a tribute to Dr. Franklin's literacy tutoring.

agenda_items.title: Approval of November 13, 2017 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered the minutes for the November 13, 2017 Regular Session. Moved by Ellen W. Reckhow and seconded by Brenda A. Howerton, the minutes passed unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognition: Duke Energy Water Resources Grant ($26,500) to Soil and Water Conservation District
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Duke Energy's Casey Furr presented a $26,500 Water Resources Grant check to Durham Soil and Water Conservation District officials Eddie Culberson, Mike Dupree, and Daniel Adams. Matched by $35,000 from DPS Career and Technical Education and $16,000 from Durham YouthWorks, the grant funds a six-week summer internship for 10 students and six teachers to install 15-20 stormwater best management practices, building on prior projects at Birchwood Heights Community Center.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 17-0512 through 17-0543)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered Consent Agenda Items 17-0512 through 17-0543 (transcribed '15-0512-17-0543'). Moved by Ellen W. Reckhow and seconded by Brenda A. Howerton, the consent agenda passed unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After verifying incumbent status for Nicole Connolly, the Board completed ballot voting for two advisory bodies. Results were announced electing Kenyawn Browning and Nicole Connolly to the Farmland Protection Advisory Board, and Tamika McRae and Brianna Van Deelenburg (transcribed 'Bon, Declan Berg') to the Women's Commission.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Adjourn to Closed Session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board was requested to adjourn to closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider personnel qualifications, performance, appointment conditions, or complaints. The motion passed unanimously 5-0.

meetings.executive_summary: At the November 13, 2017 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved the October 23 regular session minutes (5-0) and Consent Agenda Items 17-0445 through 17-0507 (5-0). Ceremonial items centered on the Department of Social Services, welcoming new DSS Director William Ben Rose and recognizing Interim Director Catherine Williamson-Hardy for guiding the FY 2017-18 budget and delivering the fastest single audit in 16 years. Chair Jacobs also proclaimed November 2017 as Adoption Awareness Month and highlighted the shortened six-week Affordable Care Act open enrollment period ending December 15. The Board concluded by voting unanimously 5-0 to adjourn into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6), (a)(1), and (a)(4) for personnel, privileged information, and economic development matters.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting at 7:01 PM, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Announcements emphasized the shortened six-week ACA open enrollment window (Nov 1 to Dec 15, 2017) with navigator support at DSS and Lincoln Community Health Center, plus the November 30 'Forward Together' Women's Commission luncheon.

agenda_items.title: Approval of October 23, 2017 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed the minutes for the October 23, 2017 Regular Session. Moved by Ellen W. Reckhow and seconded by Brenda A. Howerton, the minutes were unanimously approved 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Introduction of New Social Services Director William Ben Rose
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager introduced William Ben Rose as Durham County's new Director of Social Services, having started October 9 after serving eight years as Human Services Director in Cabarrus County and 18 years as Social Services Director in Chowan County.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Interim Social Services Director Catherine Williamson-Hardy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners, the County Manager, and the Board of Social Services honored Catherine Williamson-Hardy for serving as Interim DSS Director from April through October 2017 following Michael Becketts' resignation. Speakers cited her leadership on the FY 2017-18 budget and CFO George Quick's commendation that the 2017 single audit was the best in 16 years, finishing two to three weeks ahead of schedule.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: November 2017 as Adoption Awareness Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs read a proclamation declaring November 2017 as Adoption Awareness Month in Durham County and recognized the Social Services Department staff in attendance.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 17-0445 through 17-0507)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: No items were pulled from Consent Agenda Items 17-0445 through 17-0507, and Commissioner Heidi Carter thanked staff for attending the prior work session to answer questions in advance. Moved by Ellen W. Reckhow and seconded by Brenda A. Howerton, the consent agenda passed unanimously 5-0.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-11-06 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 6, 2017 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, citizen commenters addressed transit-area affordable housing UDO density incentives (urging Alternative A at 60% AMI), the Sutherland Springs mass shooting, and Confederate monuments. Workforce development leadership briefed the Board on regional NCWorks postings, employer labor shortages, IBM apprenticeships, Made in Durham, Housing Authority employment efforts, and WIOA employment metrics. After a middle section omitted from the digest, commissioners discussed alternatives to jailing residents over unpaid court or traffic fines, gun policy, housing task force messaging across AMI tiers, and Chair Jacobs' draft Confederate monument public-input commission. The Board unanimously suspended the rules (5-0) and granted Vice Chair James Hill an excused absence for January (5-0), then reviewed upcoming consent items including school capital accounting, quarterly budget snapshots, detention center elevators, the Museum of Durham History contract, EMS Station #1 architectural design, and an annexation lost-revenue interlocal agreement with the City of Durham.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the work session at 9:08 AM and read the public charge. Becky Winders of the Coalition for Affordable Housing and Transit urged support for Alternative A (Option 1) in the proposed UDO affordable housing density bonus requiring 15% of units at 60% AMI in transit areas; John Tarantino commented on the Sutherland Springs mass shooting, and another resident spoke on historical monuments.

agenda_items.title: Workforce Development Board and Regional Apprenticeship Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A workforce development presenter reviewed regional NCWorks job postings across Raleigh-Durham-Chapel Hill, noting growth in lower-wage retail and security jobs alongside healthcare and industry labor shortages. The briefing highlighted IBM's new work-based apprenticeship programs, Made in Durham partnerships with Durham Public Schools, Housing Authority workforce initiatives, and WIOA second-quarter unsubsidized employment performance metrics.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Comments (Pretrial Fines, Gun Violence, Affordable Housing, and Monument Commission)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle portion omitted from the transcript digest, commissioners discussed exploring ankle-bracelet or non-custodial alternatives to jailing people over unpaid traffic/court fines and reviewed reactions to the Sutherland Springs mass shooting. Commissioners also discussed housing task force leadership (Heidi Carter co-chairing) and clarifying 30%/50%/80% AMI messaging, as well as Chair Jacobs' revised draft for a community stakeholder commission on Confederate monuments.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence for Vice Chair James Hill (January Meeting)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously 5-0 to suspend the rules at the work session to take action on an absence request. Commissioners then voted 5-0 to grant Vice Chair James Hill an excused absence for the January meeting.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (Items 17-0445 through 17-0480 and Annexation Interlocal Agreement)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners and staff walked through upcoming consent agenda items, including County Attorney item 445, school capital project accounting forms, quarterly red/yellow/green budget reports, library items, a detention center elevator contract, public health CC4C budget carryforwards, the Museum of Durham History contract (noting its 2020 city lease expiration), Sheriff's Office mutual aid in Chapel Hill/Carrboro, EMS Station #1 architectural design (updating a 2009 RFP), and an interlocal agreement with the City of Durham on annexation lost revenues and fees.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-10-23 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 23, 2017 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved all five formal actions on the agenda. Following approval of the June 14 budget work session and October 9 regular session minutes (5-0), the Board approved a cost-share Memorandum of Agreement with GoTriangle for the Major Investment Study and specialized rail-track modeling of a commuter rail corridor connecting Durham County, RTP, NC State, and Wake County (5-0). The Board also adopted Consent Agenda Items 17-0451 through 17-0489 (5-0) after a question regarding why a Criminal Justice Advisory Committee appointment was listed separately, and approved the FY19 Section 5311 Community Transportation Grant local match and authorizing resolutions after a public hearing with no speakers (5-0). Following a second public hearing, the Board unanimously adopted the 2016 Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) of the Durham Comprehensive Plan and an associated Future Land Use Map amendment near Stadium Drive (5-0), and made six advisory board appointments by ballot while deferring RTP Service District appointments due to outdated applications.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order at 7:02 PM, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Announcements covered early voting for the November 7 municipal election, Open Space Matching Grants, and the November 9 Veterans Day recognition program.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (June 14, 2017 Budget Work Session and October 9, 2017 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before approving the June 14 budget work session and October 9 regular session minutes, a commissioner noted the June minutes referenced Senate Bill 155's potential impact on ABC boards and requested a staff follow-up once absent staff returned. Moved by Ellen W. Reckhow and seconded by Brenda A. Howerton, both sets of minutes passed unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 17-0487/17-0472: Commuter Rail Study Cost-Share Memorandum of Agreement (GoTriangle)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Willie Darby and GoTriangle's John Tallmadge presented the cost-share MOA (two-thirds/one-third split) for a commuter rail Major Investment Study (MIS) connecting Durham County, RTP, NC State, and Wake County/downtown Raleigh, noting specialized rail track modeling would require an amendment. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow questioned why a new MIS was needed after an earlier capacity study, technical comparisons with BRT, and schedule clarity. Moved by Ellen W. Reckhow and seconded by Brenda A. Howerton, the agreement passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 17-0451 through 17-0489)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A commissioner asked why a Criminal Justice Advisory Committee appointment appeared on the consent agenda without an application separate from regular board appointments, without pulling the item. Moved by Brenda A. Howerton and seconded by Ellen W. Reckhow, Consent Agenda Items 17-0451 through 17-0489 passed 5-0, and Chair Jacobs thanked staff and Commissioner Heidi Carter for updating the TEFRA policy.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Approval of FY19 Section 5311 Community Transportation Grant
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff outlined federal Title VI and operational requirements for the FY19 Section 5311 Community Transportation Grant application and local match. After opening and closing the public hearing with no speakers, the Board voted 5-0 (moved by Brenda A. Howerton, seconded by Ellen W. Reckhow) to approve the local match and authorizing resolutions.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Approval of 2016 Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) of the Durham Comprehensive Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Laura Woods and Patrick Young presented the 2016 EAR, incorporating the revised Urban Open Space Plan adopted September 11 and one Future Land Use Map amendment near Stadium Drive requested by the Ellerbe Creek Watershed Association for conservation easements. Commissioners discussed UDO updates (adopted 2006), school capacity analyses in rezonings, and land-use/zoning consistency; after a public hearing with no speakers, the Board unanimously approved the report and resolutions 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs recommended holding off on RTP Service District appointments because several applications dated back to 2010 and needed updated contact information. By ballot vote, the Board appointed Tom Kreger (Historic Preservation Commission), Cameron Phillips (Juvenile Crime Prevention Council), James Miller (Public Health Board), Calvin Bonaparte (Transportation Advisory Board), Olivia Horton (Women's Commission), and a candidate to the Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau.

Ceremonial items and community recognitions featured an energy efficiency and weatherization update serving roughly 1,850 customers, a proclamation honoring domestic workers, and a proclamation declaring October 2017 as Community Planning Month. Planning Director Patrick Young highlighted the Planning Department's expanded Planning Academy and urban design charrettes for potential reuse of the Durham Police Department headquarters, alongside remarks from the PEACH lead-safe housing program and the Long-Term Care Ombudsman program. agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (September 25, 2017 Regular Session and September 5, 2017 Work Session)

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-10-02 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 2, 2017 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, no substantive policy votes occurred aside from routine adjournment. During citizen comments, PAC 1 representative James Chavis criticized City-County Planning Department outreach to neighborhood PACs and disputed email statements by Planning Director Patrick Young, while commissioners noted PAC 1 could subscribe to electronic rezoning notices. Transit planners then briefed the Board on the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit (DOLRT) engineering phase, covering property acquisition and zoning steps for the Rail Operations and Maintenance Facility (ROMF), two-car station platform cost savings, Gateway Station transit-oriented development, and staying within the $2.47 billion federal budget cap. Following a middle segment omitted from the digest, the County Manager and commissioners reviewed aligning nonprofit contracts for the Greater Durham Chamber of Commerce and Downtown Durham Inc. (DDI) with Managing for Results (MFR) metrics, discussing NC Chamber Work Ready Community goals, data disaggregation, and new work-session agenda review timelines.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Citizen Comments (PAC 1 Planning Outreach)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the work session and read the public charge. Citizen commenter James Chavis of PAC 1 requested that senior Planning Department leaders attend PAC meetings and disputed an email from Planning Director Patrick Young; commissioners advised PAC 1 to set up an email address to receive automatic rezoning notices.

agenda_items.title: Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit (DOLRT) Engineering and Cost Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transit officials briefed commissioners on advancing DOLRT engineering toward a Full Funding Grant Agreement (September 2019/January 2020), initiating property acquisition, rezoning, and annexation for the Rail Operations and Maintenance Facility (ROMF), and adopting shorter two-car platforms for cost savings. Presenters also discussed shifting Gateway Station to unlock 2.1 million square feet of transit-oriented development, moving parking away from historic properties and the WASP pump station, and keeping added Durham station costs offset within the $2.47 billion federal project cap.

agenda_items.title: Healthy Durham 2020 and Regional Development Context
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In a brief pre-truncation segment, speakers acknowledged staff support by Diane Pleasure, referenced large-scale innovation real estate management (Cambridge/Boston and Georgia Tech Technology Square), and noted the Johns Hopkins president's keynote at Healthy Durham 2020.

agenda_items.title: Managing for Results (MFR) Contract Alignment: Greater Durham Chamber of Commerce and Downtown Durham Inc. (DDI)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle portion omitted from the transcript digest, staff reviewed aligning Chamber and DDI nonprofit contracts with the County's Managing for Results framework. Commissioners questioned website/portal duplication with County economic development staff, proposed adding NC Chamber 'Work Ready Community' benchmarks, flagged 2016 date errors on contract attachments, and agreed to address DDI scope updates during upcoming board goal-setting and the spring budget cycle.

agenda_items.title: Worksession Process Review and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager and commissioners discussed how moving work sessions to the start of the month affects consent agenda pacing, Thursday noon agenda packet posting, and pulling items if needed. Because the meeting reached 2:10 PM, the Board dispensed with commissioner comments and voted to adjourn.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-09-25 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 25, 2017 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved minutes from three spring budget work sessions (May 25, May 30, June 30) and the September 11 regular session (5-0), requesting staff to cross-reference budget directives, highlight the strategic plan in future budget books, and align nonprofits under relevant departments. Ceremonial proclamations recognized Rail Safety Week (Sept 24-30) with North Carolina Operation Lifesaver and Minority Enterprise Development Week (Oct 2-6) highlighting the County's MWBE ordinance. The Board unanimously adopted Consent Agenda Items 17-0396 through 17-0440 (5-0), with Chair Jacobs highlighting a new farmland conservation easement on the Amey Tilly farm abutting Falls Lake to protect water quality. Following ballot appointments to eight county boards and commissions, the Board voted unanimously 5-0 to adjourn into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with the County Attorney.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and Announcements (Big Sweep, DOLRT, and Durham Reads Together)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting at 7:01 PM, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Announcements covered Durham Big Sweep (Oct 7) and Hurricane Matthew flood-resiliency recommendations on keeping storm drains and streams clear of debris/leaves, GoTriangle's Sept 26 DOLRT info session, October 10 election early voting, and Durham County Library's 'Durham Reads Together' selection of the U.S. Constitution.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (May 25, May 30, June 30, 2017 Budget Work Sessions and September 11, 2017 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed verifying completion of directives recorded in the spring budget work session minutes, placing the refreshed strategic plan prominently in the upcoming budget document, and organizing nonprofit allocations under corresponding departments. Moved by Heidi Carter and seconded by Brenda A. Howerton, the minutes passed unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Rail Safety Week (September 24-30, 2017)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs read a proclamation declaring September 24-30, 2017 as Rail Safety Week in partnership with North Carolina Operation Lifesaver (Margaret Cannell) to prevent highway-rail grade crossing crashes and pedestrian trespassing incidents.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Minority Enterprise Development Week (October 2-6, 2017)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read a proclamation declaring October 2-6, 2017 as Minority Enterprise Development Week, citing Durham County's MWBE Ordinance Section 8-132 and N.C.G.S. 143-128. MWBE management team members outlined vendor outreach events at the Durham Armory and Golf Day.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 17-0396 through 17-0440)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled, Consent Agenda Items 17-0396 through 17-0440 were moved by Brenda A. Howerton, seconded by Ellen W. Reckhow, and approved unanimously 5-0. Chair Jacobs commended the approval of another farmland conservation easement on the Amey Tilly farm abutting Falls Lake to support local food production and water quality protection.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ballot voting results were announced for eight advisory bodies: Amanda Borer (Adult Care Home CAC), Manuel Ross (Audit Oversight Committee), Christina Lott, Judy Mack, Charles Wood, and Gregory Pigrow (Community Child Protection / Child Fatality Prevention Team), Joseph Jones (Historic Preservation Commission), Jessica Jones (Juvenile Crime Prevention Council), Paige Wingfield (Nursing Home CAC), Michael Brewer (Triangle J Water Resource Committee), and Stephanie Freeman and Vivian Slade (Women's Commission).

agenda_items.title: Motion to Adjourn to Closed Session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a five-minute recess, the Board considered a motion to adjourn to closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to preserve attorney-client privilege. The motion passed unanimously 5-0.

votes.notes: Ellen W. Reckhow deferred seconding to Brenda A. Howerton.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve the May 25, May 30, and June 30, 2017 Budget Work Session minutes and September 11, 2017 Regular Session minutes.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-09-11 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 11, 2017 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board reconvened from closed session and voted unanimously 5-0 to set the salary for the incoming Social Services Director at $145,000, followed by unanimous approval of prior minutes (5-0). Ceremonial items featured a joint resolution with Durham City Council supporting continuation of the federal DACA program and passage of the DREAM Act, alongside an NCACC/LGFCU Innovation Award honoring Durham County EMS for improving ambulance unit-hour production by 17% and response times by 22 seconds without additional funding. During consent agenda review, commissioners discussed a CT Wilson Administration Building contract amendment and requested future work-session review of contractor workforce demographics alongside MWBE ownership, before unanimously passing Consent Agenda Items 17-0369 through 17-0449 (5-0), including Item 17-0429 making Durham the first North Carolina county to adopt a CEDAW resolution and EMS Community Paramedicine software. Following a public hearing with supportive testimony from the Ellerbe Creek Watershed Association, the Board voted 5-0 to adopt the revised Urban Open Space Plan with minor implementation edits.

agenda_items.title: Report from Closed Session and Approval of New DSS Director Salary ($145,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reconvening from closed session, Chair Wendy Jacobs reported the Board had given the County Manager direction on his work plan and agreed to set the salary for the new Department of Social Services Director candidate at $145,000. On formal motion, the $145,000 salary passed unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, 9/11 & First Responders Remarks, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read the public charge, led the Pledge of Allegiance, and marked the 16th anniversary of September 11 by honoring first responders amid Hurricanes Harvey and Irma, the Duke Life Flight helicopter crash, recent gun violence, and civil unrest. Announcements included CAMPO/DCHC MPO project social media links and community distribution of U.S. Constitution copies.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (August 28, 2017; August 14, 2017; and March 13, 2007 Regular Sessions)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered minutes from the August 28, 2017, August 14, 2017, and March 13, 2007 Regular Sessions. Moved by Brenda A. Howerton and seconded by Ellen W. Reckhow, the minutes were unanimously approved 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Resolution: Support for Continuation of Federal DACA Program and DREAM Act
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read a resolution developed in partnership with the Durham City Council opposing federal rescission of DACA and urging North Carolina's congressional delegation to pass the bipartisan DREAM Act, noting 30,000 DACA recipients in North Carolina and $1.2 billion in projected state GDP impact. Commissioners discussed working with Durham Public Schools to include local youth stories when transmitting the resolution to federal officials.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Presentation: NCACC/LGFCU Innovation Awards (Durham County EMS)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Darlene Jacobs of the Local Government Federal Credit Union presented the NCACC Innovation Award recognizing Durham County EMS. The program increased ambulance unit-hour production by 17% and reduced overall response time by 22 seconds without additional funding.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 17-0369 through 17-0449, including CT Wilson Amendment and CEDAW Resolution 17-0429)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed an amendment to CT Wilson Construction's competitively bid contract for unforeseen deterioration at the County Administration Building (noting a woman-owned restoration subcontractor and a diverse site workforce) and agreed to revisit contractor workforce demographics tracking at a future work session. Chair Jacobs also requested summer parking deck revenue comparisons and highlighted Item 17-0429 (CEDAW resolution, making Durham the first county in North Carolina to pass it) and EMS Community Paramedicine software before the Board unanimously approved Items 17-0369 through 17-0449 (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Approval of the Urban Open Space Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Scott Whiteman and Patrick Young presented revisions to the Urban Open Space Plan incorporating county matching grant recipient mapping, joint-use agreements, low-impact street design, and shopping center green-infrastructure retrofits. Following supportive public hearing remarks from Chris Dreps of the Ellerbe Creek Watershed Association, the Board voted 5-0 (moved by Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by Heidi Carter) to adopt the plan with two typo corrections and by adding multi-agency and county matching grants as responsible parties on page 58.

votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest; Chair Jacobs announced unanimous approval.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion following closed session to set the salary for the new Social Services Director candidate at $145,000.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (August 28, 2017; August 14, 2017; and March 13, 2007 Regular Sessions)
votes.notes: Chair Jacobs announced unanimous approval.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve the minutes of the August 28, 2017, August 14, 2017, and March 13, 2007 Regular Sessions.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Urban Open Space Plan with Page 58 Amendments
votes.notes: Chair Jacobs announced the plan was unanimously approved.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the public hearing, motion to approve the Urban Open Space Plan with corrections on page 58, Objective 1, Item 9 ('innovative' and 'recreation' typos) and adding 'multi-agency and the county matching grants' to responsible parties.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-09-05 9:00 AM - Worksession (Tuesday Meeting)
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 5, 2017 Board of County Commissioners work session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, with Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow excused and Vice Chair James Hill noted as arriving late, the Board opened by voting unanimously 3-0 to suspend its rules and remove James Burnham from the Historic Preservation Commission due to unaddressed absences. The Durham County Women's Commission, chaired by Zion Tankard alongside Beth C. of WomenNC, presented a proposed CEDAW (Counties for the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women) resolution backed by roughly 150 petition signatures; commissioners voiced support for CEDAW's equity principles—citing county paid family leave and a $15/hour minimum wage—while raising procedural questions about staff procurement, gender-analysis execution, and oversight roles. Later in the session, the My Brother's Keeper (MBK) Allies presented 24 recommendations across three pre-K-through-postsecondary milestones aimed at addressing racial disparities in education, health, employment, and criminal justice, prompting commissioners to call for broader community visibility and coordination with Durham Public Schools and local partners such as NCCU. During commissioner comments, members discussed NCACC child well-being initiatives, Durham's expanding reentry and expungement clinics (citing Senator Floyd McKissick's dismissed-charge erasure legislation), the Highway 98 corridor study, racial equity training, and emergency preparations ahead of Hurricane Irma and Tropical Storm Jose before adjourning unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Attendance, and Citizen Comment Period
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the Tuesday morning work session and read the public charge. She announced that Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow had an excused absence and Vice Chair James Hill had notified the Board he would arrive late. No citizens signed up to speak during the citizen comment period.

agenda_items.title: Suspension of Rules and Removal of Historic Preservation Commission Member
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs introduced a request from the Clerk's Office, following notification from the Historic Preservation Commission, regarding board member James Burnham's two absences and failure to respond to outreach. On motions by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Heidi Carter, the Board voted 3-0 to suspend the rules and then 3-0 to remove Burnham from the Historic Preservation Commission.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Women's Commission Presentation on CEDAW Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Women's Commission Chair Zion Tankard and Beth C. of WomenNC presented a proposal for Durham County to adopt a CEDAW resolution modeled on cities such as San Francisco, citing local gender wage gaps ($14,000+ higher average earnings for men ages 25-34), poverty, and youth sexual assault rates alongside ~150 petition signatures from the August 26 women's march. Commissioners expressed strong alignment with CEDAW's goals—pointing to Durham County's paid family leave and $15/hour minimum wage—while questioning how departmental gender analyses, Women's Commission oversight, and county study procurement processes would be structured before formal adoption.

agenda_items.title: My Brother's Keeper (MBK) Allies Presentation and Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presenters from the My Brother's Keeper Allies outlined 24 recommendations organized across three milestones—school readiness, high school graduation (with health, education, and community engagement actions), and postsecondary/career stability—supported by local disparity data on homicide, incarceration, poverty, unemployment, and earnings by race. They highlighted alignment with the Pre-K Task Force, Durham Public Schools' racial equity work, corporate internships, and NCCU coding programs. Commissioners urged wider community outreach and concrete implementation partnerships.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Comments, Reentry Update, Highway 98 Study, and Hurricane Preparedness
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed NCACC children's initiatives across all 100 counties, Durham's reentry efforts serving roughly 700 returning residents per month, and free Legal Aid clinics leveraging new legislation sponsored by Senator Floyd McKissick to expunge dismissed charges. Members also noted a September 21 CAMPO/DCHC MPO/NCDOT Highway 98 corridor public meeting at Eastway Elementary, scheduling Phase 1 racial equity training, and emergency management preparations for Category 5 Hurricane Irma and Tropical Storm Jose before adjourning.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend the Rules to Consider Board Member Removal
votes.notes: Chair Jacobs announced at 00:00:54 that Ellen W. Reckhow had an excused absence and James Hill was arriving late; only the three present commissioners voted.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to suspend the Board's rules to act on removing Historic Preservation Commission member James Burnham for poor attendance.

votes.item_title: Removal of James Burnham from the Historic Preservation Commission
votes.notes: Ellen W. Reckhow had an excused absence and James Hill was noted as arriving late; motion approved unanimously by the three commissioners present.
votes.discussion_detail: Removal of James Burnham from the Historic Preservation Commission due to two absences and lack of response to Clerk's Office outreach.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-08-28 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 28, 2017 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, the Board approved the August 7, 2017 work session minutes 5-0 and presented ceremonial proclamations for National Recovery Month (with Recovery Community of Durham representatives Randy Tucker and Robert Thomas), the Together for Resilient Youth (TRY) Plan for Zero Initiative, and a 10th-place National Association of Counties (NACo) Digital Counties Award earned by the Durham County IT Department. On the consent agenda (Items 17-0341 through 17-0402), Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow highlighted Item 17-0402 showing a record-pace 99.78% property tax collection rate, and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton inquired about an $8,500 state grant reduction for Triple P training before the Board approved the full consent agenda 5-0. In board and commission appointments, the Board voted 5-0 on Item 17-0350 to appoint Andy Miller as Chair of the ABC Board and announced ballot selections for five citizen boards under Item 17-0399, before initiating a motion to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(4) as the recording concluded.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of August 7, 2017 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting, read the public charge, and announced the September 16 Kickoff to College and Career fair as well as FY 2017-18 property tax billing deadlines (due September 1, delinquent after January 5, 2018). The Board unanimously approved the August 7, 2017 work session minutes 5-0, with Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow noting several directives in those minutes needed attention.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations: National Recovery Month and Together for Resilient Youth (TRY) Plan for Zero
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read a proclamation celebrating National Recovery Month (September 2017), highlighting national opioid overdose statistics and thanking Randy Tucker and Robert Thomas of Recovery Community of Durham, who announced a September 30 recovery celebration at Durham Central Park. Chair Jacobs also read the proclamation recognizing August 28, 2017 as the Together for Resilient Youth (TRY) Plan for Zero Initiative in Wanda Boone's absence.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Durham County IT Department NACo Digital Counties Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recognized Durham County IT leadership (including Greg Marrow and Steve Barton) for winning a 10th-place NACo / Center for Digital Government Digital Counties Award in the 250,000-to-499,999 population tier. IT staff highlighted countywide technology initiatives supporting departments such as Public Health, Social Services, and citizen service requests.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 17-0341 through 17-0402)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow commended the Tax Administrator and staff on Item 17-0402, noting a 99.78% property tax collection rate that may be the highest in county history. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton asked about a Triple P funding decrease, and staff confirmed an $8,500 state grant loss would slightly reduce training capacity while leaving a significant program budget intact. The Board approved the entire consent agenda 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments (Items 17-0399 and 17-0350)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Under Item 17-0350, the Board voted unanimously 5-0 on a motion by Commissioner Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Heidi Carter to appoint Andy Miller as Chair of the ABC Board for the upcoming year. For Item 17-0399, the Clerk announced ballot voting selections: Beverly Thorpe (ABC Board), Amanda D. Hope (Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission), Tony Amos (Jury Commission), Melissa Kimathi (Library Board of Trustees), and Cecilia Polanco (Women's Commission).

agenda_items.title: Request for Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read a request to adjourn to closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) regarding business or industry location/expansion and N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel in Marquita Welton v. Durham County Board of County Commissioners, Wendell Davis, and Kathy Everett-Perry. The transcript recording ends immediately as a motion was being initiated.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-08-14 7:00 PM - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 14, 2017 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, the Board unanimously approved the July 31, 2017 regular session and May 23, 2017 budget work session minutes (5-0) and adopted all unpulled consent agenda items (5-0), including a farmland conservation easement for Douglas Day. On pulled consent Item 17-0360 regarding the Access Transportation Program delegation of authority, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton questioned naming the Chair personally rather than by office title, leading to a unanimous 5-0 vote to designate the Board Chair as authorizing official while asking staff to check whether the wording can be generalized. During public comment on pulled Item 17-0364 (psychiatric services contract renewal), speakers raised concerns about Sheriff's deputy pay versus detention officer raises, and Chair Jacobs clarified that $414,000 in retroactive raises had been approved for 194 detention officers alongside a countywide salary benchmark study for Sheriff's Office and county employees. In public hearings, the Board voted 5-0 to continue the Urban Open Space Plan update for two cycles to September 11 to incorporate open-space matching grant properties, adopted UDO text amendment TC1700001 (Item 17-0374) on two 5-0 votes, and appointed Emily Page as Chair of the ABC Board (Item 17-053) 5-0 before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Approval of July 31, 2017 Regular Session and May 23, 2017 Budget Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered the minutes from the July 31, 2017 regular session and May 23, 2017 budget work session. On a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, the minutes were approved unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda and Approval of Non-Pulled Items (Including Farmland Easement)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs clarified public speaker sign-ups across Items 17-0364 and 17-0376 (Board of Adjustment annual report) and noted that Items 17-0360, 17-0364, and 17-0376 were pulled for discussion. The Board approved all remaining consent agenda items 5-0, with Chair Jacobs highlighting the farmland conservation easement for Douglas Day and open space matching grant leveraging.

agenda_items.title: Item 17-0360: Access Transportation Program Delegation of Authority
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton questioned why the state-provided delegation of authority document named the Board Chair personally rather than referring generically to the office of the Chair, which would force re-execution whenever leadership changes. Staff explained grant documents due in September require naming the authorizing official. Commissioner Heidi Carter moved, seconded by Commissioner Reckhow, to designate the Board Chair as authorizing official while requesting staff verify if the resolution text can be generalized and returned at the next meeting; the motion passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 17-0364: Psychiatric Services Contract Renewal and Sheriff's Office Pay Clarification
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speakers Ada Glenn, Marcella Thompson, and Andy Miller addressed Item 17-0364, with Glenn criticizing that detention officers received raises while street deputies had not and questioning an $80,000 pay study. Chair Jacobs clarified that all Sheriff's Office staff are eligible for the countywide 2-3% raise, that $414,000 had been approved retroactively to January 2017 for 194 detention staff, and that a comprehensive salary benchmark study covering all Sheriff's Office and county employees was budgeted for implementation before year-end (noting over $8 million in added Sheriff's funding since 2011). The middle portion of the transcript digest following Miller's remarks is truncated.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Urban Open Space Plan Update (Two-Cycle Continuance)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Patrick Young and Scott Whiteman presented updates to the Urban Open Space Plan to incorporate properties preserved through the County Open Space Matching Grant program and prior work-session feedback, requesting a two-cycle continuance to September 11 for final adoption. After E.L. Allison spoke during the public hearing, Chair Jacobs reopened the hearing and the Board voted 5-0 to defer/continue action for two cycles.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Item 17-0374 (UDO Text Amendment Omnibus Changes 10, TC1700001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Michael Stock presented UDO Text Amendment TC1700001 containing technical revisions and minor policy updates across Articles 2-10 and 12-16, including clarified rules for recreational vehicle parking in residential, townhouse, and apartment developments (addressed in response to a question from Commissioner Carter). With no public speakers, the Board closed the hearing and voted 5-0 to adopt the consistency statement and 5-0 to adopt the amending ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments: Item 17-053 (ABC Board Chair) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following ballot voting in which the Board selected Emily Page for the ABC Board, Commissioner Reckhow moved under Item 17-053, seconded by Commissioner Carter, to appoint Emily Page as Chair of the Durham County ABC Board, citing her extensive leadership experience. The motion passed 5-0, and the Board adjourned unanimously.
