meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-06-26 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 26, 2017 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, the Board granted Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow an excused absence for the rescheduled July 31 meeting (5-0) and approved the June 12 and May 22 regular session minutes (5-0). On the consent agenda, the Board approved all unpulled items 5-0—while Reckhow flagged equity questions for staff follow-up on the Rougemont water system (Item 17-0318)—and then separately approved the FY 2017-18 Budget Ordinance (Item 17-0290) 5-0 after Commissioner Heidi Carter detailed how the budget provided roughly $3.3 million above the superintendent's base continuation request to protect 24 teachers, 8 assistant principals, and AIG/ESL services while avoiding a full 3-cent property tax hike. On pulled Item 17-0295, commissioners declined to eliminate six public audience seats for a chambers desk/podium reconfiguration and voted 5-0 to sever that $47,000 portion for an August work session while approving $447,194 for the chambers audio upgrade. The Board also held a public hearing and voted 5-0 to name the Durham County Memorial Stadium press box after longtime Stadium Authority member Tommy Hunt (Item 17-0226), appointed Ellen W. Reckhow to the Durham Tech Board of Trustees (5-0), announced ballot board appointments (Item 17-0299), and entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, and Excused Absence for July 31 Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order and read the public charge. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow requested an excused absence for the rescheduled July 31, 2017 meeting due to a prior family commitment, which the Board approved 5-0. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton added a commissioner appointment to the Durham Tech Board of Trustees to the Boards and Commissions agenda section, and announcements covered an automated outreach reminder campaign.

agenda_items.title: Item 17-0217: Approval of June 12, 2017 and May 22, 2017 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed Item 17-0217 covering the regular session minutes of June 12, 2017 and May 22, 2017. On a motion by Commissioner Howerton seconded by Commissioner Reckhow, the minutes were approved 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Unpulled Items and Rougemont Water System Comments on 17-0318)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Reckhow commented on Item 17-0318 (Rougemont water system) without pulling it, supporting the outlined approach while requesting staff research on equity questions. Commissioners pulled Items 17-0290 (FY 2017-18 budget ordinance) and 17-0295 (chambers audio/seating contract) for separate discussion and voted 5-0 to approve all remaining consent agenda items.

agenda_items.title: Item 17-0290: Adoption of FY 2017-18 Budget Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter outlined the FY 2017-18 school funding package, praising County Manager Wendell Davis's initial $4.7 million local current expense increase and the Board's subsequent work-session addition of ~$1.3 million (including $400,000 in sales tax revenue), delivering ~$3.3 million above the base request to preserve 24 teaching positions, 8 assistant principals, and ~$1 million in AIG/ESL needs without imposing a full 3-cent tax increase on lower-income residents. Following the truncated middle remarks, Commissioner Reckhow moved and Commissioner Howerton seconded adoption of Item 17-0290, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 17-0295: Chambers Audio Upgrade Contract (Severing $47,000 Seating Reconfiguration)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed Item 17-0295, objecting to a proposed $47,000 staff-desk extension and podium shift for ADA compliance that would eliminate six audience chairs in the front two rows. Commissioners agreed to sever the $47,000 reconfiguration for an August work session and voted 5-0 on a motion by Commissioner Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Carter to approve $447,194 for the chambers audio upgrade.

agenda_items.title: Item 17-0226: Public Hearing to Name Memorial Stadium Press Box After Tommy Hunt
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Stadium Manager Rico Chavis presented the Stadium Authority's recommendation under the county naming policy to name the Durham County Memorial Stadium press box in honor of Tommy Hunt for nearly 30 years of Stadium Authority service. With no public speakers signed up, Commissioner Reckhow praised Hunt's legacy on the stadium rebuild and moved approval, seconded by Commissioner Howerton, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments (Item 17-0299 and Durham Tech Board of Trustees)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs noted a correction adding Rawlins Clark to the BPAC candidate list before ballot voting on Item 17-0299 (with the Clerk later announcing selections including Michael Donback and Jesse Pickett Williams). Separately, on a motion by Commissioner Howerton seconded by Commissioner Carter, the Board voted 5-0 to appoint Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow to the Durham Tech Board of Trustees effective June 30.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously 5-0 to adjourn into closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with its attorney and preserve attorney-client privilege.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-06-12 7:00 PM - Budget Public Hearing
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 12, 2017 Budget Public Hearing presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, the Board unanimously approved four sets of prior minutes (Item 17-0281, 5-0) and ceremonially welcomed new Board of Elections Director Derek Bowens, introduced by Board of Elections Chair Bill Bryan. During the public hearing on the FY 2017-18 Recommended Budget (Item 17-0300), 46 speakers signed up to testify—primarily urging full funding of Durham Public Schools' budget request to protect teachers, assistant principals, and arts programs alongside GED, housing wraparound, and youth safety services—followed by three speakers (Scott Barish, Patrick McHugh, and E.L. Allison) on the draft Strategic Plan refresh. On the consent agenda, the Board approved all unpulled items 5-0, then heard staff explanations on pulled Item 17-0279 (the Main Library renovation Construction Manager at Risk GMP-1 contract, covering its 3.25% contingency and separate state sales-tax rebate accounting) before approving it 5-0. Finally, after Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow requested clearer language on city-versus-county jurisdiction and requiring prior site-plan/Board of Adjustment approvals on pulled Item 17-0304 (educational project TEFRA bond policy affecting the Hill Center), the Board voted 5-0 to defer Item 17-0304 to its August work session and adjourned.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Item 17-0281 Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the budget public hearing meeting, emphasized observance of the public charge given the large crowd, and shared announcements including upcoming VA town hall forums. Under Item 17-0281, the Board voted 5-0 on a motion by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow to approve minutes from May 8, April 24, May 1 (work session), and April 15 (PAC 1).

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Welcome of New Board of Elections Director Derek Bowens
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board of Elections Chair Bill Bryan introduced newly appointed Board of Elections Director Derek Bowens to the Board and the public. Chair Jacobs welcomed Bowens and underscored the universal importance of election administration to all Durham County residents.

agenda_items.title: Item 17-0300: Public Hearing on FY 2017-18 Recommended Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With 46 speakers signed up at two minutes each, community members, parents, educators, and advocates—including Ira Knight, Alex Protsman (Life Skills Foundation), Alan Bradley, Ann Reback, Teresa Del Dado, Alexis Tyler, Katie Bauman, and Jerome Graham—addressed the recommended budget. Speakers overwhelmingly urged commissioners to fully fund Durham Public Schools' budget request (even if requiring a modest tax increase) to preserve teacher, assistant principal, and arts positions, while also supporting GED programs, supportive housing, and youth violence-prevention spaces.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Draft Refresh of the Durham County Strategic Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Three residents—Scott Barish, Patrick McHugh, and E.L. Allison—offered public comment on the draft Strategic Plan refresh. Allison urged that implementation of the strategic plan be guided by equity and attentiveness to impacts on the African-American community.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Unpulled Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Howerton pulled Item 17-0304 and Chair Jacobs pulled Item 17-0279 for separate discussion. On a motion by Commissioner Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Howerton, the Board voted 5-0 to approve all remaining consent agenda items (including 17-0185, 17-0259, 17-0261, 17-0263, 17-0264, 17-0268, 17-0274, and 17-0276).

agenda_items.title: Item 17-0279: Main Library Renovation CMAR GMP-1 Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs questioned the 3.25% contingency and separate sales-tax billing language in the Main Library renovation Construction Manager at Risk GMP-1 contract (covering demolition/abatement, general trades, temporary fencing, and elevators across four planned GMP packages). Staff explained the contingency was budgeted and that separate sales-tax accounting enables semiannual state Department of Revenue tax rebates; the Board then approved Item 17-0279 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 17-0304: Educational Project / TEFRA Bond Policy (Deferral to August Work Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners Howerton and Reckhow raised clarity concerns on the draft TEFRA/educational project policy (noting an impending application for the Hill Center, a non-charter educational facility), recommending explicit language requiring prior site-plan or Board of Adjustment approvals and clarifying city-versus-county review roles. Following brief remarks by Dr. E.L. Allison, the Board voted 5-0 on a motion by Commissioner Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Heidi Carter to defer Item 17-0304 to the August work session before adjourning.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-06-05 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 5, 2017 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs (with Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton previously excused at the May 22 meeting), Jacobs opened with remarks mourning the fatal shooting of a seven-year-old child on Guess Road the previous day, followed by citizen comment from satirist John Tarantino. Downtown Durham Inc. (DDI) leaders Nicole Thompson and Matt Gladick delivered an economic development briefing reporting 30 new street-level businesses since early 2016, 1.2 million square feet of upcoming downtown office space (including Durham Innovation District and Chesterfield), a 1-3% Class A vacancy rate, DDI's ~$1.1-1.2 million budget (including an anticipated $160,000 county contract), minority business partnerships, parking management, and EMS/CPR coordination. Later in the session, staff briefed commissioners on upcoming consent items including a Judicial Building Annex renovation capital amendment via LOBS financing, a budgeted Cherwell IT Service Management system upgrade, a $2,000 Veterans Services grant supporting the June 16-17 claims clinic, renewing the City of Durham fire apparatus repair contract with $21,000 reallocated within the service district budget, and the Strategic Plan refresh schedule ahead of June 12 public comment and June 26 adoption. The Board voted 4-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) before returning to open session and adjourning unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks, Public Charge, and Citizen Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the work session by noting the fatal shooting of a seven-year-old child on Guess Road the prior day and urging continued community effort, then read the public charge. John Tarantino delivered topical satire during the citizen comment period.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Durham Inc. (DDI) Downtown Development and Budget Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DDI President Nicole Thompson and Policy/Planning Director Matt Gladick reviewed downtown retail and commercial growth—highlighting 30 new street-level businesses since 2016, 11 opened in 2017, 14 opening within six months, 350,000 sq ft at Durham Innovation District, and 274,000 sq ft at Chesterfield alongside a 1-3% Class A vacancy rate. They outlined DDI's ~$1.1-1.2M budget (including an ~$803,000 BID request and $160,000 county economic development contract), minority small-business partnerships (NCIMED, SBTDC), evening/weekend parking lot promotion, and upcoming CPR/EMS training.

agenda_items.title: Budget Amendments, Capital Projects, IT System, Veterans Grant, Fire Apparatus, and Strategic Plan Preview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff previewed consent items for the upcoming business meeting: a Judicial Building Annex (Board of Elections building) renovation capital amendment funded via LOBS financing, a budgeted Cherwell IT Service Management upgrade replacing a 2006 platform, a $2,000 Veterans Services grant for the June 16-17 claims clinic (highlighting $6M in annual VA cash benefits secured locally), and renewing the City of Durham fire apparatus maintenance contract with $21,000 reallocated inside the service district fire rescue fund. Staff also previewed the Strategic Plan refresh schedule (June 12 public comment, June 26 adoption alongside the FY 2017-18 budget).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4)) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Vice Chair James Hill, the Board voted 4-0 to adjourn to closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss business or industry location or expansion. After returning to open session at 06:55:48, the Board adjourned unanimously.

votes.notes: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton was excused from the June 5 work session by Board vote on May 22, 2017 and is not recorded present in the transcript; the four seated commissioners present voted Aye.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-05-22 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 22, 2017 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, the Board held a moment of silence for community leaders Chuck Davis and Ralph Hunt, approved the May 9 and April 3 minutes (5-0), honored Acting EMS Director Kevin Underhill and EMS staff for National EMS Week, and reaffirmed support for House Bill 280 (the Juvenile Justice Reinvestment Act) to raise the age of juvenile jurisdiction from 16 to 18 (noting Senate efforts to restrict the reform to misdemeanors). Following a truncated middle segment covering the FY 2017-18 recommended budget presentation, the Board conducted two UDO public hearings and voted 5-0 on both consistency statements and ordinances amending Articles 4 and 16 as well as Item 17-0237 (TC1600006, revising mass grading buffers in City jurisdiction per state statute while directing planning staff to explore vegetation-retention incentives in the county). Under board and commission appointments (Item 17-0234), commissioners discussed single-applicant vetting and Open Meetings limits on offline candidate discussions, approved an excused absence for Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton for the June 5 work session (5-0), announced six citizen-board appointments, and voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Moment of Silence, and Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs announced that the County Manager would present the proposed FY 2017-18 budget ahead of the June 12 public hearing, highlighted the May 29 Memorial Day ceremony and weekend community events (including the Bimbé Festival and Dementia Inclusive Durham conference), and led a moment of silence for Chuck Davis and Ralph Hunt. The Board approved the May 9 and April 3, 2017 minutes 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation for National EMS Week and Resolution Supporting House Bill 280 (Raise the Age)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented a proclamation honoring National Emergency Medical Services Week to Acting EMS Director Kevin Underhill and EMS staff. Commissioner Heidi Carter read a resolution reaffirming support for House Bill 280 (Juvenile Justice Reinvestment Act) to raise juvenile jurisdiction from age 16 to 18 (excluding Class A-E felonies and traffic offenses); Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow and Brenda A. Howerton urged residents to lobby legislators so low-level felonies remain covered rather than only misdemeanors.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment (Articles 4 and 16)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the truncated middle portion of the transcript (which included the FY 2017-18 budget presentation), the Board held a public hearing on a UDO text amendment presented by Planning staff Michael Stock affecting Article 4 (Zoning Districts) and Article 16 (Definitions). With no public speakers signed up, the Board voted 5-0 to adopt the statement of consistency and 5-0 to adopt the amending ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Item 17-0237 (UDO Mass Grading Buffers Text Amendment, TC1600006)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock presented TC1600006 amending UDO Section 9.5 and Article 16.3 per state enabling legislation to expand mass grading buffers (65 ft adjacent to developed property/right-of-way and 32 ft adjacent to undeveloped property), remove supplemental vegetation mandates, and restrict applicability to City jurisdiction (already approved by City Council and recommended 13-0 by Planning Commission). In response to Commissioner Carter's concern about county buffers, Planning Director Patrick Young noted staff would bring a June 7 white paper to JCCPC on incentives to retain existing vegetation; the Board voted 5-0 on both the consistency statement and ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Item 17-0234: Board and Commission Appointments and Excused Absence for June 5
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners raised concerns about appointment procedures when a single applicant is not strong and discussed Open Meetings constraints on discussing nominees offline, agreeing to revisit appointment procedures at the June work session. The Board voted 5-0 to excuse Commissioner Howerton from the June 5 work session and announced ballot selections: Stephanie Strickland (City-County Appearance Commission), Keith Bryant (DOST), Tyler Stilman (Farmland Protection Advisory Board), James Burnham (Historic Preservation Commission), Larry Dixon (Memorial Stadium Authority), and Jennifer Piotrowski (Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Commissioner Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Howerton, the Board voted 5-0 to adjourn to closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) regarding personnel qualifications, performance, or complaints.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-05-08 6:30 PM - Special Meeting - 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 8, 2017 Special Meeting presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, County Manager Wendell Davis and Strategic Initiatives Manager Michael Davis presented the draft refresh of the 2012 Durham County Strategic Plan tied to the Managing for Results (MFR) performance framework, executive portfolio alignment across five general managers, an upcoming public performance dashboard, June 12 public comment, and June 26 adoption alongside the FY 2017-18 budget. After announcements on OpenDurham historic inventory workshops and emergency alert text-preference settings, the Board began considering minutes and heard a Drug Court presentation praising treatment alternatives and Lincoln Community Health Center's grant-funded substance use partnership. On the consent agenda, commissioners reviewed Item 17-0218 expanding the Homeless Services Advisory Committee (HSAC) by five seats and voted 5-0 to approve the consent agenda with clarifying language specifying that HSAC itself makes those five additional appointments. Commissioners also urged routing future consent items through work sessions first and scheduling a June work-session review of the building served by a boiler retrofit (Item 17-0222 area), announced five Durham County Hospital Corporation board appointments, and voted 5-0 to adjourn into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6).

agenda_items.title: Special Session Presentation: Draft Refresh of the Durham County Strategic Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis and Strategic Initiatives Manager Michael Davis presented the first refresh of the 2012 Strategic Plan following 10 months of community and staff engagement. Michael Davis outlined alignment with the Managing for Results (MFR) budgeting and performance-measurement system, the five general manager portfolios (including Goal 3 Safe Community led by Jody Miller and Goal 5 Accountable/Efficient Government), departmental work plans, a planned public dashboard, June 12 public comment, and June 26 adoption.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Consideration of March 6 and April 11 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Announcements covered drop-in community workshops for the OpenDurham architectural and historic inventory and subscriber preferences for emergency/Silver Alert text messages versus phone calls. Consideration of the March 6 work session and April 11 regular session minutes began at 00:34:59 before a truncated gap in the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Drug Court and Substance Abuse Treatment Partnership Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated presentation on Drug Court, commissioners praised Drug Court leadership and staff for transforming lives and offering treatment-based alternatives to incarceration and the war on drugs. Chair Jacobs highlighted Durham County's grant-funded partnership with Lincoln Community Health Center to expand medication and treatment access.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Including Item 17-0218 HSAC Interlocal Amendment Clarification)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed Item 17-0218 amending the interlocal agreement for the Homeless Services Advisory Committee (HSAC) to add five specialized seats (such as victim service and youth homeless housing providers) and clarified that HSAC itself will appoint those five seats, aligning with City Council's May 15 review. A commissioner also asked that future consent items be previewed at work sessions and requested a June work-session discussion on the building served by a boiler retrofit; the Board approved the consent agenda 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointments (Durham County Hospital Corporation) and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: While awaiting ballot tallies, commissioners noted staff investigation of Senior Center parking complaints. The Clerk announced ballot appointments to the Durham County Hospital Corporation: Rosemary Jackson, Gail Belted and Robert Newman, and Katrina Avery and Jay Kim. The Board then voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6).

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to adjourn to closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider personnel qualifications, performance, appointment conditions, or complaints.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-05-01 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 1, 2017 Work Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, the Board heard citizen comments from James Chavis Jr., Elizabeth Barber of the Threshold clubhouse (highlighting mental health services and a transitional employment partnership with Durham County Library), and satirist John Tarantino. Representatives of the Durham Charter School Collaborative presented their annual update—noting roughly 20% of Durham students attend charter schools and over 90% of funding comes from state, local, and federal allotments—while commissioners requested future side-by-side comparisons against Durham Public Schools and state averages on special-needs acuity (noting Voyager Academy's ~13% special-needs rate and high-cost self-contained programs), English language learners, and free/reduced breakfast participation. Later in the work session, commissioners reviewed a draft remote participation policy, reaching consensus to broaden acceptable absence categories to include out-of-town official conferences and family obligations/emergencies, require advance notice, exclude closed sessions, and note chamber audio constraints ahead of placing the policy on the next consent agenda. Under commissioner comments, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow requested a fiscal-impact analysis of General Assembly crossover bills—including a Senate-passed sales tax redistribution estimated to cost Durham County ~$3 million—before the Board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and later adjourned unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the work session and read the public charge. During citizen comments, James Chavis Jr. spoke, Elizabeth Barber presented on the Threshold clubhouse serving East Durham adults with severe mental illness and its transitional employment placement at Durham County Library, and John Tarantino performed Durham satire.

agenda_items.title: Durham Charter School Collaborative Annual Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presenters from the Durham Charter School Collaborative reported that roughly 20% of Durham students attend charter schools and that over 90% of charter revenue comes from state, local, and federal allotments, reviewing per-pupil spending, special-needs services, and ELL outcomes. Commissioners requested comparative DPS and state benchmarks on special-needs acuity, free/reduced breakfast participation, and ELL performance, while Voyager Academy's representative noted ~13% students with disabilities costing up to $20,000 per high-need student.

agenda_items.title: Draft Remote Participation Policy Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle section, commissioners debated revisions to the draft remote participation policy (referencing Mayor Bill Bell's symbolic remote GoTriangle vote), agreeing to expand eligibility to out-of-town official conferences/meetings and family obligations or emergencies, require advance notice, exclude closed sessions, and evaluate annual usage caps and chamber audio upgrades. The revised draft was slated for the next consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Comments and Legislative Fiscal Impact Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow requested a preliminary staff and NCACC fiscal-impact assessment of General Assembly crossover bills—specifically a Senate-passed sales tax redistribution estimated to cost Durham County ~$3 million and changes to economic development tiers/incentives—so the Board could brief the local House delegation. Staff confirmed tax and budget impact numbers would be shared with lawmakers.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)), Report Out, and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Vice Chair James Hill, the Board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel. Upon reconvening at 04:51:05, Chair Jacobs reported that direction was given to staff and the Board adjourned unanimously.

votes.item_title: Motion to Adjourn into Closed Session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; upon returning at 04:51:05, Chair Jacobs reported direction was given to staff before adjourning.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to adjourn to closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with an attorney and preserve attorney-client privilege.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-04-24 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 24, 2017 Regular Session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, the Board added a Week of the Young Child recognition for Laura Benson (Durham's Partnership for Children, previewing the Pre-K Task Force initial report), celebrated Durham County's Golden Leaf Award for Sustainability for the Human Services Building, and adopted proclamations and resolutions honoring Families and Children's Mental Health, Autism Awareness, the NCCU Men's Basketball Team (2017 MEAC Champions and NCAA Tournament berth under Coach LeVelle Moton), and the Duke University Men's Basketball Team (2017 ACC Tournament Champions). Following a truncated middle section, commissioners finalized review of the Durham County Transit Plan—highlighting commuter rail allocations ($175-$350 million), bus service expansions, TIFIA debt through 2062, and two-county arbitration rules—and voted 5-0 to adopt the plan with two amendments adding the Research Triangle Park tax service district on page 37 and cross-referencing Chart 4.7.1 funding assumptions in the cash-flow appendices. The Board then voted 5-0 to approve the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Interlocal Cost-Sharing Agreement with Orange County and GoTriangle, announced ballot board appointments, and voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(4).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustment, Announcements, and Ceremonial Proclamations/Resolutions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting, added Laura Benson (Week of the Young Child) to the agenda, and announced the State of Young Children report and the Human Services Building's Golden Leaf Sustainability Award. Commissioners presented proclamations/resolutions for Families and Children's Mental Health (Heidi Carter), the NCCU Men's Basketball Team's MEAC Championship (Brenda A. Howerton, joined by Coach LeVelle Moton and players), Autism Awareness (James Hill), the Duke Men's Basketball Team's ACC Championship (Ellen W. Reckhow), and the Week of the Young Child (Laura Benson previewing the Pre-K Task Force initial report).

agenda_items.title: Durham County Transit Plan Adoption (As Amended)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reviewing the Durham County Transit Plan, commissioners noted $175-$350M allocated for commuter rail transit, major bus service improvements, TIFIA loan repayment extending to 2062, and impasse arbitration provisions with Orange County. On a motion by Commissioner Reckhow (incorporating Chair Jacobs's addition) seconded by Commissioner Howerton, the Board voted 5-0 to adopt the Transit Plan with two amendments: adding 'and the Research Triangle Park service district' on page 37 and referencing Chart 4.7.1 funding assumptions on both Durham and Orange County cash-flow appendix pages.

agenda_items.title: Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Interlocal Cost-Sharing Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following adoption of the Transit Plan, Commissioner Howerton moved and Commissioner Reckhow seconded approval of the Interlocal Agreement for Cost Sharing for the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Project among Orange County, Durham County, and GoTriangle (Research Triangle Regional Public Transportation Authority). The agreement passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(4))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk announced ballot appointment results including Marlon Terry Kyle. On a motion by Commissioner Carter seconded by Commissioner Howerton, the Board voted 5-0 to adjourn into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) regarding Alonzo Green v. County of Durham Office of the Sheriff's Department et al. and N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) regarding business or industry location/expansion.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Durham County Transit Plan (As Amended)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Adoption of the Durham County Transit Plan with two incorporated amendments: (1) adding 'and the Research Triangle Park service district' after Research Triangle Park Foundation on page 37, and (2) adding a cross-reference to Chart 4.7.1 underlying funding assumptions on each page of the Durham and Orange County cash-flow appendices.

votes.item_title: Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Interlocal Cost-Sharing Agreement
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approval of the cost-share interlocal agreement among Orange County, Durham County, and GoTriangle (Research Triangle Regional Public Transportation Authority) for the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Project.

votes.item_title: Motion to Adjourn into Closed Session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(4)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation in Alonzo Green v. County of Durham Office of the Sheriff's Department et al. and N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) regarding business/industry location or expansion.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-04-11 7:00 PM - (Tuesday Meeting)
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 11, 2017 regular Tuesday meeting presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Durham County Board of Commissioners approved meeting minutes unanimously 5-0 and adopted proclamations for Parkinson's Disease Awareness Month alongside a resolution honoring outgoing Department of Social Services Director Michael Becketts upon his appointment as Assistant Secretary of Human Services at NC DHHS. GoTriangle staff presented an update on the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit project ahead of its upcoming Federal Transit Administration submission, followed by extensive public comment debating regional rail alignment, airport connectivity, cost, and long-term mobility ahead of a scheduled April 24 public hearing and vote. On the consent agenda, the Board unanimously approved eight items (including a Duke University fiber-optic network agreement, Vincent Valuations contract, 9-1-1 facility limited obligation bonds, Museum of Life and Science general obligation bond appropriations, detention center HVAC upgrades, and finance policy updates) 5-0 while pulling Item 17-0169 on the My Brother's Keeper Durham and Public Allies partnership. After County Manager Wendell Davis clarified an addendum extending two Public Allies positions through June 30, 2017 for up to $39,000, the Board approved Item 17-0169 unanimously 5-0 and voted 5-0 to enter closed session regarding the Marquita Welton litigation.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting at 7:04 PM, read the public charge, led the Pledge of Allegiance, and confirmed there were no agenda adjustments. Announcements reminded property owners of the April 17, 2017 deadline to appeal real property tax values before the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns, highlighted City-County Planning and Preservation Durham community meetings for the Open Durham historic inventory, and promoted Cooperative Extension kitchen classes starting April 27.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered approval of prior meeting minutes. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved approval and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded, passing unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Parkinson's Disease Awareness Month Proclamation and Resolution Honoring DSS Director Michael Becketts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill read a proclamation declaring April 2017 Parkinson's Disease Awareness Month, recognizing Duke Department of Neurology and the Triangle National Parkinson's Foundation, followed by a second ceremonial proclamation. Chair Jacobs then read a resolution honoring Durham County DSS Director Michael Becketts—hired in 2012 after serving as deputy director in Baltimore—as he prepared to become Assistant Secretary of Human Services at NC DHHS; Becketts thanked the 504 DSS employees, co-located staff, and Board for their support.

agenda_items.title: Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Project Update and Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: GoTriangle staff briefed the Board on the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit project as Durham and Orange counties approached a Federal Transit Administration submission milestone. During public comments, proponents emphasized light rail as critical regional infrastructure for millennials, seniors, and congestion/environmental relief, while a speaker raised concerns over rising cost estimates, lack of direct airport rail service, and a circuitous Chapel Hill alignment. Chair Jacobs announced the item will return for a formal public hearing and vote on April 24, 2017.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 17-0121, 17-0145, 17-0160, 17-0161, 17-0162, 17-0163, 17-0173, 17-0175)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter pulled Item 17-0169 for clarification, leaving eight consent items: a Duke University fiber-optic network agreement (17-0121), Vincent Valuations contract (17-0145), 9-1-1 facility limited obligation bonds (17-0160), Museum of Life and Science general obligation bond appropriation (17-0161), tax/stamp overpayment refunds (17-0162), detention center HVAC upgrade (17-0163), TJCOG Economic Development District support resolution (17-0173), and Durham County finance policy updates (17-0175). Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved approval and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: My Brother's Keeper Durham and Public Allies of North Carolina Partnership
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis clarified a late addendum revising the agreement to fund two Public Allies from April 17 through the end of the fiscal year (June 30, 2017) for up to $39,000, while Public Allies funds a third position on its payroll ahead of a May work session report and FY 2017-18 budget recommendation. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow supported the extension but noted from Dion Hines's report that some Allies encountered institutional roadblocks requiring stronger local support.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) (Marquita Welton v. Durham County et al.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board was requested to adjourn into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to preserve attorney-client privilege regarding Marquita Welton v. Durham County, Durham Board of County Commissioners, Wendell Davis, and Kathy Everett Perry. Commissioner Heidi Carter moved approval and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded, passing unanimously.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote with all five commissioners present.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve prior meeting minutes with no opposed votes.

votes.item_title: Item 17-0169: My Brother's Keeper Durham and Public Allies of North Carolina Partnership Addendum
votes.notes: Chair announced item was unanimously approved.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved up to $39,000 to extend two Public Allies positions through June 30, 2017, with a third funded by Public Allies and a progress report scheduled for the May work session.

votes.item_title: Motion to Adjourn to Closed Session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)
votes.notes: Chair announced closed session was unanimously approved.
votes.discussion_detail: Adjourned to closed session for attorney-client consultation regarding Marquita Welton v. Durham County, Durham Board of County Commissioners, Wendell Davis, and Kathy Everett Perry.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-04-03 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 3, 2017 work session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, citizen commenters urged the Board to hold the Sheriff's Office accountable following a 17-year-old's death in the county jail and to oppose a planned GTL video visitation system, calling on commissioners to request the contract and consider budget conditions. Commissioners clarified that the County had not signed a GTL contract and lacked statutory supervision over Sheriff contracts, later directing staff to obtain any draft video visitation contract and debating whether to invite the Sheriff to a special 5:00 PM meeting. Under Item 17-0094, staff presented an update on the Durham County Transit Plan, detailing 30% engineering design for the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit project (targeted to open in 2029 with TIFIA financing through 2062) alongside bus expansion and upcoming April public meetings. Staff also updated the Board on the Nehemiah Christian Center interim day shelter (averaging 16 unique visitors weekly with armed security and meals), presenting options to waive the RFP requirement or extend the contract four months while issuing an RFP before July 1, while the Board deferred its Rules of Procedure item to June and took no formal votes.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge and Citizen Comments on Sheriff Accountability and Jail Video Visitation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the work session with the public charge and citizen comment rules. Daniela Hernandez-Blanco and additional speakers raised concerns about Sheriff's Office accountability, cited the death of a 17-year-old in the jail, opposed replacing in-person visits with GTL video visitation (noting a ~50% drop in jail visits and a 2015 study on visitation phase-outs), and urged commissioners to read contracts and condition Sheriff funding. Commissioners clarified the Board had not signed a GTL contract and that video visitation had previously been presented as an add-on rather than a replacement.

agenda_items.title: Update on the Durham County Transit Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated the Board on the Durham County Transit Plan, including the Durham-Orange Light Rail project reaching 30% engineering design with updated federal and state funding assumptions, a minimum 1.15 debt service coverage ratio, TIFIA loan repayment extending to 2062, and a projected 2029 opening. The update also covered Hillsborough train station funding (91% STIP) and future bus connections, noting April 10 and April 12 public information sessions and the April 11 BOCC public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Budget Work Session Scheduling Conflict (June 9 vs. Health Summit)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners noted that rescheduling a budget work session from June 8 to June 9 conflicted with the rescheduled Health Summit and a commissioner's weeklong training. The Board discussed moving the budget session to June 13 and agreed to resolve scheduling offline.

agenda_items.title: Nehemiah Christian Center Day Shelter Operations and Contract Options
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported that the Nehemiah Christian Center interim day shelter (established after Main Library closed) was averaging 16 unique visitors per week, mostly daily attendees, with ODS armed security, Nehemiah staff, and lunch/dinner service. With the contract expiring July 1 and Urban Ministries showing limited interest, staff presented two options: waive the RFP requirement to continue with Nehemiah, or approve a four-month contract extension while conducting a full RFP; commissioners discussed outreach to unhoused individuals and scheduling a facility walkthrough.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up on Jail Video Visitation Draft Contract and Board Governance Authority
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners requested staff follow up on whether a draft or unsigned GTL video visitation contract existed and obtain a copy. Commissioner Heidi Carter noted public frustration stems from residents lacking direct channels to the independently elected Sheriff, and commissioners debated holding a 5:00 PM special meeting with the Sheriff versus meeting directly with him, raising concerns about maintaining meeting civility.

agenda_items.title: Committee Meeting Scheduling and Deferral of Rules of Procedure
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners briefly reviewed external board meeting schedules (noting fourth-Wednesday regular dates versus November/December third-Wednesday shifts), agreed to move the Rules of Procedure item to the June work session, and adjourned.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-03-27 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 27, 2017 regular meeting presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board opened with a formal statement addressing March 13 protests over detention center video visitation, affirming support for in-person jail visits while clarifying that the Sheriff holds statutory operational authority and the County was not party to the GTL grant/contract for eight lobby video portals. During advance public comments on the FY 2017-18 budget (slated for presentation May 22 and adoption June 26), Dr. E.L. Allison urged holding presentations before public comment and hosting town hall meetings, prompting commissioners to discuss expanding budget outreach to PACs, Rougemont, Bahama, and cable TV. The Board presented ceremonial resolutions recognizing the Durham CROP Hunger Walk and the Pauli Murray Home's designation as a National Historic Landmark, approved the February 3 Legislative Agenda Breakfast minutes 5-0, and unanimously passed the consent agenda 5-0—including Project BUILD donations, tax releases, Board of Equalization and Review alternate appointments (17-0130), CJRC HVAC upgrades (17-0140), and W.G. Pearson/Student U capital funding (17-0144). Following advisory board appointments by ballot (including David Mansour to the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee), the Board voted unanimously 5-0 to enter closed session regarding the Marquita Welton litigation.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Board Statement on Detention Center Video Visitation, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting at 7:00 PM, read the public charge, and delivered a Board statement responding to March 13 video visitation protests: the Board supports maintaining in-person visitation, noted the Sheriff plans to add eight lobby video portals under a GTL grant that the County neither signed nor approved, and highlighted county-funded jail education, substance abuse, mental health, and diversion programs. Announcements noted the April 17 property tax appeal deadline and a Durham appointee joining NCDOT.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (February 3, 2017 Legislative Agenda Breakfast)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered minutes from the February 3, 2017 Legislative Agenda Breakfast. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved approval and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Advance Public Comments on FY 2017-18 Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs outlined the FY 2017-18 budget calendar (May 22 presentation, May 23–June 15 work sessions, June 12 public hearing, June 26 adoption). Dr. E.L. Allison recommended presenting budget context prior to taking public comment and hosting small-group and town-hall outreach with the School Board; commissioners discussed attending PACs, Rougemont Ruritan Club, and Bahama meetings, as well as airing a televised budget constraints overview in April.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations: Durham CROP Hunger Walk and Pauli Murray Home National Historic Landmark
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter read a proclamation honoring the Durham CROP Hunger Walk (the second-largest walk nationwide), with organizers Bob Nolan and Marge Clemons presenting NCCU-designed T-shirts and noting local beneficiaries such as Urban Ministries and Meals on Wheels amid proposed federal cuts. The Board also presented a proclamation celebrating the Pauli Murray Home's designation as a National Historic Landmark with Barbara Lau.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Including Items 17-0103, 17-0116, 17-0125, 17-0126, 17-0127, 17-0130, 17-0140, 17-0141, 17-0144)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. E.L. Allison raised questions on Items 17-0126 and 17-0127, and Public Health Director Gayle Harris explained staffing via the Public Health Alliance, pregnancy smoking-cessation evaluation, and state SNAP-Ed nutrition funds. Chair Jacobs highlighted a $522.73 Ekklesia CDC donation for Project BUILD (17-0103) alongside closed session minutes, Duke Community Health Assessment support, February tax releases (17-0116), reduced state HIV funds (17-0125), Board of Equalization and Review alternate appointments (17-0130), CJRC HVAC (17-0140), JCPC appointment (17-0141), and W.G. Pearson/Student U capital funding (17-0144). After the unanimous vote, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow confirmed with the Tax Administrator that the two new alternate members on the Board of Equalization and Review prevent costly quorum cancellations.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners voted by ballot on appointments to the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee, Durham Open Space and Trails Commission, Juvenile Crime Prevention Council, Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee, Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority, and Transportation Advisory Board. The County Attorney announced the ballot results, including the selection of David Mansour for the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1) and (a)(3) (Marquita Welton v. Durham County et al.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board moved into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1) to prevent disclosure of privileged/confidential records under Chapter 132 and (a)(3) for attorney-client consultation regarding Marquita Welton v. Durham County, Durham Board of County Commissioners, Wendell Davis, and Kathy Everett Perry. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved approval and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded, passing unanimously.

votes.notes: Chair announced minutes were approved unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve minutes from the February 3, 2017 Legislative Agenda Breakfast.

votes.item_title: Motion to Adjourn to Closed Session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1) and (a)(3)
votes.notes: Voice vote with no opposed votes.
votes.discussion_detail: Adjourned to closed session regarding confidential records and Marquita Welton v. Durham County, Durham Board of County Commissioners, Wendell Davis, and Kathy Everett Perry.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-03-13 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 13, 2017 meeting presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, Jacobs delivered a State of the County overview highlighting 1.56% projected revenue growth, $875.8 million in 2016 business investment, 22% child poverty, $134 million in annual education spending (with 18%+ going to charter schools), the Bull City United violence-prevention initiative, and the county's $15/hour living wage. The Board held a contentious public hearing on approving Public Finance Authority tax-exempt bonds for Discovery Charter School on Orange Factory Road, where commissioners split 3-2: Brenda A. Howerton, Wendy Jacobs, and Ellen W. Reckhow voted Aye—stating the Board could not overturn the Board of Adjustment's land-use approval and expressing reluctant legal obligation despite deep concerns over neighbor notification and the Little River Plan—while James Hill and Heidi Carter voted Nay, arguing the Board retained discretion to deny the bond financing. In a separate public hearing, the Board unanimously approved 5-0 a bond financing resolution for Durham Academy. The meeting concluded with a request to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(4) just prior to the 11:00 PM curfew, though the final closed-session vote tally was not captured before the recording ended.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Public Charge, and Chair's State of the County Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting, read the public charge, and delivered a comprehensive State of the County overview. She cited 4.4% unemployment (>5,500 unemployed residents), 1.56% projected revenue growth, 22% child poverty, 83%+ voter passage of the $170 million bond package, over $134 million in education spending (with >18% flowing to charter schools), Bull City United's Cure Violence model, 3,581+ acres of preserved farmland/open space, the AAA bond rating, 61% citizen survey satisfaction, strategic plan refresh, and the $15/hour living wage.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Resolution Approving Tax-Exempt Bonds for Discovery Charter School Foundation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public testimony opposing Discovery Charter School's Orange Factory Road site, commissioners questioned the County Attorney regarding the prior Board of Adjustment quasi-judicial approval and community concerns over neighbor notification, the Little River Plan, and the Scenic Byway designation. County counsel advised that land-use errors could only be appealed in court and that the sole issue before the Board was approving the Public Finance Authority bond issuance. On a 3-2 split vote, Brenda A. Howerton, Wendy Jacobs, and Ellen W. Reckhow voted Aye while James Hill and Heidi Carter voted Nay; afterward, Jacobs, Reckhow, and Carter called for establishing guiding principles before future charter school bond requests return.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Bond Resolution for Durham Academy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Jeff Foley presented a bond financing request on behalf of Durham Academy. During the public hearing, Sophie Suberman (1002 Arrowhead Road, Chapel Hill) spoke before the hearing closed. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved approval and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded, passing unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Request for Closed Session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read a request to adjourn into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client privilege and (a)(4) for business or industry location/expansion, noting the upcoming 11:00 PM curfew and reluctance to extend past 11:00 PM. The transcript ends before a completed vote tally is recorded.

votes.item_title: Resolution Approving Issuance of Bonds by Public Finance Authority and Plan of Finance for Discovery Charter School Foundation
votes.notes: Chair explicitly read the 3-2 split vote tally on the record: Commissioners Howerton, Jacobs, and Reckhow in the affirmative; Commissioners Hill and Carter opposed.
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded approval of the tax-exempt bond resolution, stating the BOCC could not overturn the Board of Adjustment's land-use ruling; Chair Wendy Jacobs reluctantly voted Aye while calling for future guiding principles and expressing serious concern over lack of neighbor notice and Little River Plan protections. Commissioners James Hill and Heidi Carter voted Nay, maintaining the Board had legal discretion to deny the bonds.

votes.item_title: Resolution Approving Bond Financing for Durham Academy
votes.notes: Voice vote announced as 'the ayes have it' with no opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved Durham Academy's tax-exempt bond request following a public hearing.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-03-13 7:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Approval of Public Finance Authority Tax-Exempt Bonds for Discovery Charter School Foundation
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 3-2 over whether to approve tax-exempt bond financing for Discovery Charter School on Orange Factory Road after residents objected that adjacent neighbors were not properly notified and that the Board of Adjustment approval conflicted with the Little River Plan and Scenic Byway protections.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the bond financing resolution on narrow legal/procedural grounds while urging court appeal of the Board of Adjustment decision and adopting future guiding principles
side_a_arguments: The Board of Adjustment's quasi-judicial UDO decision is legally separate and can only be overturned through a court appeal, not by the BOCC.
Denying the bonds would not stop the school from proceeding, and commissioners believed they had a legal obligation regarding the bond-only action.
Commissioners still criticized planning staff due diligence, lack of neighbor notice, and disregard for the Little River Plan and Scenic Byway, calling for guiding principles for future requests.
disagreements.side_b_position: Vote against approving the tax-exempt bonds because the Board retained legal discretion not to facilitate the financing
side_b_arguments: Approving the bonds was not legally obligatory; commissioners had discretion to vote no.
Facilitating tax-exempt bond financing under flawed local land-use review and investor-driven charter school concerns was unwarranted.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 3-2 (Howerton, Jacobs, Reckhow voting Aye; Hill, Carter voting Nay), with Board consensus to establish core guiding principles before similar requests return.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-03-06 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 6, 2017 work session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, citizen Jim Svara followed up on housing stabilization grants from the February 2 Joint City-County meeting, which the Board folded into a presentation by the Durham Home Repair Collaborative (Item 17-0092) proposing a centralized 'no wrong door' intake and shared database across repair and weatherization agencies ahead of FY 2017-18 budget decisions. On the sole action item, Item 17-0086, the Board voted unanimously 5-0 to suspend its rules and voted unanimously 5-0 to remove two unresponsive members from the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee under the August 2014 attendance policy. Commissioners also reviewed a draft resolution advocating for restored state mental health funding and highlighting deinstitutionalization and the opioid epidemic, scheduling it for formal action at next month's regular meeting. The session concluded with updates on racial equity and My Brother's Keeper Alliance sessions, alarming federal budget/Medicaid/public-health proposals from a NACo briefing, and a review of the 60-day vetting and 30-day public hearing notice requirements under the county's facility naming policy.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge and Citizen Comments on Housing Stabilization Grants
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the work session with the public charge. Resident Jim Svara (1114 Woodburn Road) spoke on housing stabilization grants following the February 2 Joint City-County Committee meeting, and Chair Jacobs agreed to include staff's background report within the upcoming Home Repair Collaborative item.

agenda_items.title: Removal of Citizen Board Members Due to Poor Attendance (Adult Care Home Advisory Committee)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Under the Board's August 2014 attendance policy governing members missing more than 50% of meetings without responding to clerk outreach, the Board voted 5-0 to suspend the rules (moved by Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by Brenda A. Howerton). Following brief remarks by Heidi Carter noting the difficulty of volunteer committee service, the Board voted 5-0 to remove the two appointees from the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee (moved by Brenda A. Howerton, seconded by Ellen W. Reckhow).

agenda_items.title: Presentation from the Durham Home Repair Collaborative
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Representatives of the Durham Home Repair Collaborative proposed centralizing intake and assessment through a shared 'no wrong door' database to coordinate urgent repair, weatherization, and city/nonprofit rehab programs (noting the city's $9,600 cap and Rebuilding Together's single-family rehab work) and requested consideration of FY 2017-18 funding or redirected DSS emergency assistance. Commissioners noted the collaborative had not yet determined which organization would directly receive funds and requested a more strategic approach aligned with city efforts.

agenda_items.title: Draft Resolution Advocating for State Mental Health Funding and LME/MCO Support
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public remarks from a parent and LME/MCO representatives stressing predictable funding, low denial rates, and the risk of state cuts shifting costs onto counties, commissioners reviewed a draft mental health funding resolution. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow requested adding a clause on deinstitutionalization and fixing a grammatical error, another commissioner suggested adding a standalone clause on the opioid epidemic, and the Board agreed to place the amended resolution on next month's regular meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Commissioners' Updates: Racial Equity, My Brother's Keeper, NACo Federal Briefing, and Children's Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed racial equity training, National League of Cities / My Brother's Keeper Alliance sessions, and Aspen Institute two-generation strategies. Updates from a NACo legislative briefing flagged concerns over potential federal Medicaid capitation, repeal of the $1 billion Prevention and Public Health Fund, unfunded opioid authorizations, federal immigration directives, FAA air traffic control privatization, and gas tax indexing, alongside updates on the State of Durham Children report and veterans resources.

agenda_items.title: County Facility Naming Procedure Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff outlined the county's naming policy requiring 60 days for manager/staff vetting and background checks, Board acceptance of the recommendation, 30 days' written notice of a public hearing, and a post-hearing vote. Because staff had not yet completed the 60-day vetting, commissioners noted the matter would return by early May ahead of a possible June public hearing before adjourning.

meetings.executive_summary: At the February 13, 2017 regular meeting presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board unanimously approved the January 3 and January 23 meeting minutes 5-0 and heard presentations on consent items including Open Space matching grants ($77,200 leveraging over $140,000) and a MacArthur Foundation grant funding automated court-date text/phone reminders to reduce failure-to-appear jail stays. Following a public hearing with no speakers, the Board unanimously approved 5-0 Item 17-0071 authorizing $72.2 million in limited obligation bond anticipation notes, $50 million in voter-approved general obligation bond anticipation notes, and $3.8 million in taxable GO bonds for the Whitted School pre-K project, alongside a unanimous 5-0 deferral of an item captured in a truncated middle segment. The Board also unanimously approved all three items pulled from consent: Item 17-0057 (5-0) contracting with the UNC School of Government Development Finance Initiative for 300 and 500 East Main Street pre-development near the Dillard Street light rail station as amended; Item 17-0073 (5-0) contracting with O'Brien/Atkins Associates for Detention Center security modifications; and Item 17-0080 (5-0) adopting a Memorandum of Understanding with the Durham Public Schools Board of Education, before voting 5-0 to adjourn into closed session.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-02-06 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 6, 2017 work session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, no citizens signed up for public comment, and ETC Institute Senior Project Manager Jason Morado presented findings from the second annual City-County Resident Satisfaction Survey (Item 17-0036). The survey showed strong overall county service satisfaction across all census block groups and above-average ratings for Durham as a place to live and work, while identifying public schools, public communication effectiveness, Department of Social Services, and Sheriff protection as top county priorities alongside demand for animal control and bicycle facilities. Commissioners also discussed standardizing quarterly or semi-annual deliverables and staggered multi-year evaluations for outside nonprofit/agency contracts (including the Chamber of Commerce, Made in Durham, and Museum of Durham History) and reviewed the Comprehensive Transportation Plan memo. Commissioner Heidi Carter proposed reviewing routine contracts during work sessions ahead of regular consent agendas to surface questions on MWBE metrics and return on investment, while commissioners requested a March Workforce Development Board report on unemployed residents before adjourning with no formal votes taken.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge and Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the work session with the public charge and outlined the monthly 30-minute citizen comment guidelines. No citizens signed up to speak.

agenda_items.title: City-County Resident Satisfaction Survey Findings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Drew Cummings, Strategic Initiative Manager Michael Davis, and ETC Institute Senior Project Manager Jason Morado presented results from the fall 2016 joint resident survey. Residents across all census block groups reported high overall satisfaction with county services and rated Durham significantly above national benchmarks as a place to live and work, while top county priorities ranked public schools first, followed by public communication effectiveness, DSS, and Sheriff protection; staff noted survey findings will inform the strategic plan refresh, millennial outreach, and FY 2017-18 budget discussions.

agenda_items.title: Outside Agency Contract Deliverables and Multi-Year Funding Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners and staff discussed establishing consistent reporting formats (quarterly or twice-yearly deliverables) for funded partner organizations such as the Chamber of Commerce, Made in Durham, Art of Cool, and Museum of Durham History during the annual budget process. Participants also discussed staggering multi-year reviews across roughly one-third of long-term partner contracts each year in coordination with the City.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Transportation Plan (CTP) Memo and Work Session Contract Pre-Review Process
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners briefly referenced the Comprehensive Transportation Plan (CTP BOCC memo) before Commissioner Heidi Carter asked why routine contracts slated for regular consent agendas were not placed on work session agendas so questions—such as staff racial/MWBE demographics or return on investment for Chamber/Made in Durham agreements—could be addressed together. County Manager Wendell Davis and commissioners agreed to pilot interim attachments and ROI summaries for major partner contracts without moving routine operating deadlines earlier.

agenda_items.title: State of Durham Children, Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA), and Joint City-County Follow-Ups
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed the State of Durham Children initiative alongside North Carolina's draft Every Student Succeeds Act plan emphasizing early childhood (ages 0–8) and third-grade reading. Following up on Joint City-County items, County Manager Wendell Davis stated the Museum of Durham History capital request would be evaluated within the regular budget process, while commissioners agreed to revisit neighborhood stabilization grants and request a March report from the Workforce Development Board regarding 6,000+ unemployed residents before adjourning.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2017-01-23 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 23, 2017 regular meeting presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Board approved an expanded consent agenda unanimously 5-0—covering janitorial and utility locating contracts, public health grants, Lincoln Community Health Center Phase 2 funding ($1,191,000), Main Library renovation consulting and GO bond appropriations ($330,600), the Aim and Tilly Farm conservation easement, and initial bond resolutions—while pulling Item 17-0039 on the 2017 Legislative Agenda. Following a public hearing, the Board voted 5-0 to permanently close 220.66 linear feet of unopened Dickens Lane (Item 17-0012), reviewed a non-emergency ambulance franchise request for Jan-Care of McDowell County (Item 17-0018), voted 5-0 to expand Friday and Sunday open hours at Stanford L. Warren Library at zero additional cost, and voted 5-0 to authorize a six-month day-shelter service contract with Nehemiah Christian Center and ODS security adjustments (Item 17-0044) during the Main Library renovation. On Item 17-0039, Commissioner Heidi Carter objected to endorsing an NCACC proposal to repeal school boards' statutory right to sue counties over education funding (N.C.G.S. 115C-431(c)), leading the Board to vote 5-0 to remove that item from explicit County support while attaching the full NCACC list as an addendum. After announcing six advisory board appointments by ballot (Item 17-0032), the Board voted 5-0 to adjourn into closed session (Item 17-0049).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Item 17-0039)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Noting an expanded consent agenda resulting from the January 9 snow-day cancellation, commissioners requested stronger written backup for major contracts going forward and pulled Item 17-0039. The Board approved 5-0 Items 17-0005 (janitorial contracts), 17-0009 (utility locating RFP), 17-0013/17-0014/17-0020 (state public health/Zika/women's health grants), 17-0017 (business personal property listing extension), 17-0023 (Special Board of Equalization and Review resolution), 17-0024 (December tax releases), 17-0027/17-0028 (Lincoln Community Health Center Phase 2 design and $1,191,000 appropriation), 17-0033/17-0034 (Heery consulting, moving, and $330,600 GO bond funding for Main Library renovation), 17-0035 (Rules of Procedure), 17-0037 ($75,702 Fiscal Technology software), 17-0038 (April 11 meeting date change), 17-0040 (Aim and Tilly Farm easement), 17-0041 (SAP cloud amendment), and 17-0048 (initial GO/LOB bond resolutions).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Street Closing of 220.66 Linear Feet of Dickens Lane
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Kyle Taylor presented Robert Murphy's petition to permanently close 220.66 linear feet of dedicated, unopened Dickens Lane right-of-way north of Freeman Road (adjacent to a section already closed by the City of Durham). The Board voted 5-0 to open the public hearing (moved by Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by Brenda A. Howerton); after the sole registrant Robert Shump declined to speak, the Board voted 5-0 to adopt the closing order (moved by Reckhow, seconded by Howerton).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Ambulance Franchise Award to Jan-Care of McDowell County, Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County EMS representative Brandon Mitchell presented Jan-Care of McDowell County's franchise application for non-emergency/inter-facility BLS and ALS transport, mutual-aid backup, and special events coverage at no cost to the county. Answering Commissioner Heidi Carter, Mitchell explained private billing and noted the county lifted franchise caps after prior provider closures left Durham vulnerable; the transcript truncates before the subsequent public hearing and vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Vote not captured in truncated transcript

agenda_items.title: Library Summer Meals Partnership and Extension of Open Hours at Stanford L. Warren Library
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Library staff detailed a summer meals partnership with East Durham Children's Initiative during the Main Library renovation and recommended extending Friday hours (9:30 AM–6:00 PM) and adding Sunday hours (2:00 PM–6:00 PM) at Stanford L. Warren Library starting mid-March. Confirming zero additional budget cost because staff are already on site, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved approval (noting restoration of recession-era cuts) and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded, passing 5-0; staff confirmed Item 17-0042 was informational only.

agenda_items.title: Service Contract with Nehemiah Christian Center and ODS Security Adjustment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Drew Cummings presented a six-month service contract with Nehemiah Christian Center (Rev. Herbert Reynolds Davis) near downtown to serve daytime visitors displaced by the Main Library closure, along with corresponding ODS security adjustments. Commissioner Heidi Carter moved authorization and Vice Chair James Hill seconded, passing unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: 2017 Durham County Legislative Agenda (Amendment Removing NCACC Item #2)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by Commissioner Heidi Carter, who opposed endorsing NCACC Legislative Item #2 seeking repeal of N.C.G.S. 115C-431(c) (allowing local school boards to sue county commissioners over education appropriations), emphasizing that although Durham BOCC funds schools generously, statewide school boards need that statutory safeguard. After thanking Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton for advocating at NCACC, the Board voted 5-0 to amend the legislative agenda by removing Item #2 from explicit County support while attaching the NCACC items as an addendum.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Attorney announced ballot results for six boards: Ronaldo Jackson (Boxing and Wrestling Commission), Everett Harris (Firemen's Relief Fund Board of Trustees), Shauna Waller (Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee), Ferdinand Allison III, Marianne Fuchs, Dale Stewart, and Art Ferguson (Public Health Board), Joyce Spencer (Women's Commission), and Jeff Durham (Workforce Development Board).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(3)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously 5-0 (moved by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton) to adjourn into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) for business/industry location or expansion and (a)(3) for attorney-client consultation.
