meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-12-12 7:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 12, 2016 regular meeting presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs with all five commissioners present, the Board approved the November 14 and November 28, 2016 minutes (5-0), adopted ceremonial proclamations for Durham County Access Champions in Transportation Week (honoring Alana Bass and Charlotte Wood) and HIV Cure Research Day (with remarks from Dr. Allison Matthews of 2-Beat HIV), and introduced Mars White as interim Cooperative Extension director. Following a presentation by GoTriangle General Manager Jeff Mann on a state funding shortfall ahead of a December 30, 2016 federal Department of Transportation submission, the Board voted unanimously 5-0 on two motions moved by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow: first directing county staff to assess five long-term financial and planning issues with preliminary and final reports due April 1, 2017 and April 1, 2018, and second approving support for the GoTriangle light rail Memorandum of Understanding and Letter of Intent. Commissioners also voted 5-0 to excuse Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton from the December 13 joint meeting with the Board of Education due to a General Assembly commitment and made citizen appointments to advisory boards before adjourning with no split votes.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Tax Deadlines, and Approval of November 2016 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs announced the annual City-County Martin Luther King Jr. celebration on January 11, 2017 at First Presbyterian Church and reminded residents of the property tax payment deadline and the January 1–31, 2017 filing window for property tax exemptions (June 1, 2017 for elderly homestead and circuit breaker applications). The Board then approved the November 14 and November 28, 2016 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations: Champions in Transportation Week and HIV Cure Research Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff introduced Mars White as interim director for Cooperative Extension before Chair Wendy Jacobs read a proclamation declaring December 12–18, 2016 as Durham County Access Champions in Transportation Week. Vice Chair James Hill and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow read resolutions honoring Access Passenger of the Year Alana Bass and Outstanding Senior Citizen of the Year Charlotte Wood, respectively. The Board also proclaimed December 14, 2016 as HIV Cure Research Day, with remarks from 2-Beat HIV founder Dr. Allison Matthews.

agenda_items.title: GoTriangle Light Rail Transit Letter of Intent, MOU, and Staff Financial Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: GoTriangle's Jeff Mann requested a Letter of Intent/MOU by December 30, 2016 for federal DOT review to help address a local funding gap after the General Assembly reduced state light rail participation from 25% to 10%, noting key federal milestones in June 2018 and June 2019. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved a formal five-point staff direction requiring assessments of 10-year county financial impacts and competing long-term commitments, with a preliminary report due April 1, 2017 and a final report due April 1, 2018. Commissioners emphasized broad support for transit alongside affordable housing and transit-oriented development while stressing the need for clear funding plans.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Excused Absence for Joint BOCC/BOE Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recognized an attending North Carolina Central University student, briefly noted the Equalization and Review Board term-limit exemption and monthly appointment schedule, and voted to excuse Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton from the December 13 joint meeting with the Board of Education because she was scheduled to meet with the General Assembly. The County Attorney then announced ballot appointments to the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee, Farmland Protection Advisory Board, Durham Open Space and Trails Commission, and Transportation Advisory Committee.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (November 14 and November 28, 2016 Regular Sessions)
votes.notes: Approved unanimously by voice vote with no opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve the regular session minutes of November 14, 2016 and November 28, 2016.

votes.item_title: GoTriangle Light Rail Transit Staff Financial and Planning Review Directive
votes.notes: Chair Jacobs noted a motion and second were on the floor without naming the seconder; passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion directing county staff to work with GoTriangle and stakeholders to assess five issues—including 10-year county fiscal impact and capacity alongside other long-term county needs—and deliver a preliminary report by April 1, 2017 and a final report by April 1, 2018.

votes.item_title: Support for GoTriangle Light Rail Memorandum of Understanding / Letter of Intent
votes.notes: Approved unanimously by voice vote with no opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion supporting the MOU/Letter of Intent for GoTriangle's December 30, 2016 federal Department of Transportation light rail package.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton (December 13, 2016 Joint BOCC/BOE Meeting)
votes.notes: Approved unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to excuse Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton from the December 13, 2016 morning joint meeting with the Board of Education due to a scheduled General Assembly meeting.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2016-12-05 9:00 AM - Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 5, 2016 organizational meeting convened under N.C.G.S. 153A-39, County Attorney Lowell Siler presided initially as Durham County Board of Elections Chair Bill Bryan presented election certificates to all five county commissioners (Wendy Jacobs, Brenda A. Howerton, James Hill, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Heidi Carter), Soil and Water Conservation Supervisor Danielle Adams, Register of Deeds Sharon Davis, and a certified declaration that all four county bond referendums passed. Chief District Court Judge Marcia Morey administered the oaths of office, after which Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow declined a nomination for Chair and the Board elected Wendy Jacobs as Chair and James Hill as Vice Chair by voice votes. The Board then approved public official bonds unanimously (5-0), deferred action on the 2017 BOCC meeting calendar at the County Manager's advisement, and closed with remarks from commissioners highlighting universal pre-K, affordable housing, regional transit, workforce development, and strategic planning.

agenda_items.title: Board of Elections Presentation of Certificates and Swearing-In of Elected Officials
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board of Elections Chair Bill Bryan and interim director Kate Cosner noted that over 156,000 Durham County residents voted and commended weekend recount volunteers before delivering Certificates of Election to Commissioners Wendy Jacobs, Brenda A. Howerton, James Hill, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Heidi Carter, Soil and Water Supervisor Danielle Adams, and Register of Deeds Sharon Davis, along with certification of all four bond referendums. Chief District Court Judge Marcia Morey administered the oaths of office.

agenda_items.title: Election of Board Chair and Vice Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Lowell Siler opened nominations for Chair; Ellen W. Reckhow was nominated first and declined, after which Wendy Jacobs was elected Chair by voice vote. Newly seated Chair Jacobs opened nominations for Vice Chair, and James Hill was nominated and elected Vice Chair by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Public Official Bonds and Deferral of 2017 Meeting Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At County Attorney Lowell Siler's request, the Board approved public official bonds to be recorded in the Register of Deeds office and filed with the Clerk of Superior Court. On the next item—suspending rules to adopt the 2017 BOCC meeting calendar—Chair Jacobs announced that no action would be taken at the County Manager's advisement.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Bonds passed 5-0; 2017 calendar deferred / No vote

agenda_items.title: Commissioner and County Manager Term-Opening Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs, Commissioners Heidi Carter, Ellen W. Reckhow, James Hill, Brenda A. Howerton, and the County Manager delivered opening remarks outlining term priorities including universal pre-K, affordable housing, transportation planning, workforce development, and strategic plan updates. Commissioners also recognized Durham Public Schools Board of Education Chair Mike Lee and Vice Chair Natalie Beyer in attendance.

votes.item_title: Election of Board Chair (Wendy Jacobs)
votes.notes: County Attorney Siler called the voice vote and announced 'The ayes have it'; individual mover/seconder not named in transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Following Ellen W. Reckhow declining nomination for Chair, the Board elected Wendy Jacobs as Chair of the Board of County Commissioners.

votes.item_title: Election of Board Vice Chair (James Hill)
votes.notes: Nominator was not named in the transcript digest; Chair Jacobs announced 'The ayes have it' with no opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Nomination and voice vote electing Commissioner James Hill as Vice Chair of the Board of County Commissioners.

votes.item_title: Approval of Public Official Bonds
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not identified by name in the transcript digest; approved unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve statutory public official bonds presented by County Attorney Lowell Siler for recording with the Register of Deeds and safekeeping by the Clerk of Superior Court.
